

                                                                       Office of the President of the Republic
                                                                                       Civil House
                                                                 Special Secretariat for Legal Affairs

                                                       COMPLEMENTARY LAW No. 214, OF JANUARY 16, 2025

  Veto message

  Production of effects

  Production of effects                                                                  Institutes the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS), the Social
                                                                                       Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS) and the Selective Tax (IS); creates the
  (Promulgation of vetoed parts)                                                         IBS Management Committee and amends the
                                                                                       tax legislation.

  Compiled text

  (See Decree No. 12,955, of 2026)

        THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC Hereby makes known that the National Congress decrees and I sanction the following Complementary Law:

                                                                                      BOOK I

                              ON THE TAX ON GOODS AND SERVICES (IBS) AND THE SOCIAL CONTRIBUTION ON GOODS AND SERVICES (CBS)

                                                                                      TITLE I

                                                                    ON THE GENERAL RULES OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

                                                                                    CHAPTER I

                                                                          PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS

        Art. 1 The following are hereby instituted:

        I - the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS), of shared competence among States, Municipalities and the Federal District, as provided in art. 156-A of the Federal
  Constitution; and

        II - the Social Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS), of competence of the Union, as provided in item V of the caput of art. 195 of the Federal Constitution.

        Art. 2 The IBS and the CBS are informed by the principle of neutrality, according to which these taxes must avoid distorting consumption decisions and the
  organization of economic activity, observed the exceptions provided in the Federal Constitution and in this Complementary Law.

        Art. 3 For the purposes of this Complementary Law, the following are considered:

        I - operations with:

        a) goods, any and all that involve movable or immovable property, tangible or intangible, including rights;

        b) services, all others that are not classified as operations with goods under item "a" of this item;

        II - supply:

        a) delivery or making available of tangible goods;

        b) institution, transfer, assignment, grant, licensing or making available of intangible goods, including rights;

        c) provision or making available of a service;

        III - supplier: a natural or legal person who, resident or domiciled in the Country or abroad, carries out the supply;

        IV - acquirer:

        a) the person obligated to payment or any other form of consideration for the supply of goods or services;

       b) in cases of payment or any other form of consideration on behalf of and in the name of third parties, the person on whose account or in whose
  name the obligation to pay or any other form of consideration for the supply of goods or services arises; and

        V - recipient: the person to whom the goods or services are supplied, who may or may not be the acquirer itself.

        § 1 For the purposes of this Complementary Law, energies with economic value are treated as tangible goods.

       § 2 Included in the concept of supplier under item III of the caput of this article are entities without legal personality, including an unincorporated
  common company, an undisclosed partnership (sociedade em conta de participação), a consortium, a condominium and an investment fund.

         § 3 Included in the operations under item "a" of item I of the caput of this article are the leasing, letting and temporary assignment of the property.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                    CHAPTER II

                                                       ON THE IBS AND THE CBS ON OPERATIONS WITH GOODS AND SERVICES

                                                                                       Section I

                                                                           On the Hypotheses of Incidence

        Art. 4 The IBS and the CBS are levied on onerous operations with goods or services.

        § 1 Non-onerous operations with goods or services will be taxed in the hypotheses expressly provided in this Complementary Law.

        § 2 For the purposes of the provisions of this article, an onerous operation with goods or services is considered to be any supply with consideration, including that
  arising from:

          I - purchase and sale, exchange or barter, payment in kind (dação em pagamento) and other forms of transfer;

          II - leasing (locação);

          III - licensing, grant, assignment;

          IV - onerous loan (mútuo oneroso);

          V - donation with consideration in favor of the donor;

          VI - onerous constitution of rights in rem;

          VII - leasing (arrendamento), including finance leasing; and

          VIII - provision of services.

          § 3 The following are irrelevant to the characterization of the operations covered by this article:

          I - the legal title under which the goods are held in the possession of the supplier;

          II - the kind, type or legal form, the legal validity and the effects of the acts or legal transactions;

          III - the obtainment of profit from the operation; and

          IV - compliance with legal, regulatory or administrative requirements.

         § 4 The IBS and the CBS are levied on any operation with goods or services carried out by the taxpayer, including those carried out with non-current
  assets or in the exercise of non-habitual economic activity, observed the provisions of § 4 of art. 57 of this Complementary Law.

         § 4 The IBS and the CBS are levied on any operation with goods or services carried out by the taxpayer, including those carried out with non-current
  assets or in the exercise of non-habitual economic activity. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 5 The incidence of the IBS and the CBS on the operations covered by the caput of this article does not alter the tax base of the:

        I - Tax on the Transmission Causa Mortis and Donation of Any Goods or Rights (ITCD), provided in item I of the caput of art. 155 of the Federal
  Constitution;

        II - Tax on the Inter Vivos Transmission of Real Property and Related Rights (ITBI), provided in item II of the caput of art. 156 of the Federal
  Constitution.

         § 6 The acquisition and supply, by a natural person characterized as a taxpayer, of goods and services not related to the development of their
  economic activity are subject to the same rules applicable to non-taxpayers. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 5 The IBS and the CBS also apply to the following operations:

          I - non-onerous supply or supply at a value below market value of goods and services, in the hypotheses provided in this Complementary Law;

          I - non-onerous supply or supply at a value below market value of goods and services:          (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) acquired by the taxpayer, that have permitted the appropriation of IBS and CBS credits, for:              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

          1. the taxpayer itself, if the taxpayer is a natural person;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        2. the natural persons who are partners, shareholders, administrators and members of boards of directors and audit boards and advisory committees of the
  board of directors of the taxpayer provided for by law; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          3. the employees of the taxpayer; and        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         4. the spouses, partners or relatives, by blood or by affinity, up to the third degree, of the natural persons referred to in items 1 to 3 of this item;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) produced or provided by the taxpayer for:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          1. the natural persons referred to in items 2 and 3 of item "a" of this item; and       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        2. the spouses, partners or relatives, by blood or by affinity, up to the third degree, of the natural persons referred to in item 1 of this item; and         (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          c) in the other hypotheses provided in this Complementary Law;           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - supply of gifts and bonuses (brindes e bonificações);

         III - transmission, by the taxpayer, to a partner or shareholder that is not a taxpayer under the regular regime, by return of capital, dividends in kind or in
  another form, of goods whose acquisition permitted the appropriation of credits by the taxpayer, including in production; and

          IV - other non-onerous supplies or supplies at a value below market value of goods and services by a taxpayer to a related party.

          § 1 The provisions of item II of the caput of this article:

          I - do not apply to bonuses that are stated on the respective tax document and that do not depend on a subsequent event; and

          II - apply to goods given as a bonus subject to a specific rate per unit of measure, including in the hypothesis of item I of this paragraph.

        § 2 For the purposes of this Complementary Law, parties are considered related when at least one of them is subject to influence, exercised
  directly or indirectly by another party, that could lead to the establishment of terms and conditions in their transactions that diverge from those that would be
  established between unrelated parties in comparable transactions.

          § 3 The following are considered related parties, without prejudice to other hypotheses that fall under the provisions of § 2 of this article:

          I - the controlling party and its controlled companies;

          II - affiliated companies (coligadas);



         III - entities included in consolidated financial statements or that would be included if the final controlling party of the multinational group of which they are
  part prepared such statements if its capital were traded on the securities markets of its jurisdiction of residence;

        IV - entities, when one of them has the right to receive, directly or indirectly, at least 25% (twenty-five percent) of the profits of the other or of
  its assets in the event of liquidation;

        V - entities that are, directly or indirectly, under common control or in which the same partner, shareholder or holder holds 20% (twenty percent) or
  more of the capital stock of each one;

         VI - entities in which the same partners or shareholders, or their spouses, partners, relatives, by blood or by affinity, up to the third degree,
  hold at least 20% (twenty percent) of the capital stock of each one; and

         VII - the entity and the natural person who is a spouse, partner or relative, by blood or by affinity, up to the third degree, of a director, of an officer or of a
  controlling party of that entity.

        § 4 For purposes of the definition of related parties, the term "entity" comprises natural and legal persons and entities without legal personality.

        § 5 For purposes of § 3 of this article, a control relationship is characterized when an entity:

         I - holds, directly or indirectly, alone or jointly with other entities, including due to the existence of voting agreements, rights that
  assure it preponderance in corporate resolutions or the power to elect or remove the majority of the administrators of another entity;

        II - participates, directly or indirectly, in more than 50% (fifty percent) of the capital stock of another entity; or

        III - holds or exercises the power to administer or manage, directly or indirectly, the activities of another entity.

         § 6 For purposes of item II of § 3 of this article, an affiliated company (coligada) is considered to be an entity that holds significant influence over another entity, as
  provided in §§ 1, 4 and 5 of art. 243 of Law No. 6,404, of December 15, 1976.

         § 7 The regulation may relax the requirement to verify market value under item IV of the caput of this article in operations between related
  parties, provided that such operations are not subject to a prohibition on the appropriation of credits, within the scope of tax compliance programs.

          § 8 The provisions of items "a" and "b" of item I of the caput of this article do not apply to the supply to the natural persons referred to therein of goods and services
  predominantly used in the taxpayer's economic activity, according to the criteria provided in items IV and V of § 3 of art. 57 of this Complementary
  Law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 9 The non-onerous supply or supply at a value below market value of the goods and services in the hypotheses under items "a" and "b" of item I of the caput
  of this article will be taxed in an amount equivalent to the IBS and the CBS levied on the market value of the goods or service. (Included by Complementary Law
  No. 227, of 2026)

        § 10. The regulation will provide for simplified and optional criteria for the taxation of the supply of goods and services in the hypotheses under the
  items "a" and "b" of item I of the caput of this article for temporary use by the natural persons referred to therein. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        Art. 6 The IBS and the CBS are not levied on:

        I - supply of services by natural persons as a result of:

        a) an employment relationship with the taxpayer; or

         b) their role as administrators or members of boards of directors and audit boards and advisory committees of the board of directors of the
  taxpayer provided for by law;

         II - transfer of goods between establishments belonging to the same taxpayer, observed the obligation to issue an electronic tax document,
  under item II of § 2 of art. 60 of this Complementary Law;

       III - write-off, liquidation and transmission, including disposal, of an equity interest, except as provided in item III of the caput of art. 5 of this Complementary
  Law;

         IV - transmission of goods as a result of merger, spin-off and incorporation and of paid-in capital and return of capital, except as provided in item III of the caput
  of art. 5 of this Complementary Law;

        V - financial income, except when included in the tax base under the specific regime for financial services covered by Chapter II of Title V
  of this Book and the tax-base calculation rule provided in item II of § 1 of art. 12 of this Complementary Law;

         VI - receipt of dividends and interest on equity, of interest or remuneration on capital paid by cooperatives and the results of valuation of
  equity interests, except as provided in item III of the caput of art. 5 of this Complementary Law;

         VII - other operations with securities, except as provided for such operations under the specific regime for financial services covered by
  Section III of Chapter II of Title V of this Book, under the terms of that regime and of the other situations expressly provided in this Complementary Law;

        VIII - donations without consideration in favor of the donor;

        IX - transfers of public funds and other public assets to civil society organizations organized as non-profit legal entities
  in the Country, by means of fostering agreements (termos de fomento), collaboration agreements, cooperation agreements, partnership agreements, decentralized execution agreements, management
  contracts, transfer agreements, subsidies, covenants and other instruments entered into by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations;

        X - allocation of resources by a cooperative society to the funds provided in art. 28 of Law No. 5,764, of December 16, 1971, and the reversion of the
  resources of such reserves; and

          XI - the pass-through by the cooperative to its members of amounts arising from the operations provided in the caput of art. 271 of this Complementary Law and the
  distribution in cash of surpluses (sobras) by a cooperative society to its members, calculated in the statement of income for the year, except as provided in item
  III of the caput of art. 5 of this Complementary Law.

        XII - statutory associative contributions, of a non-consideration nature and intended for the maintenance of civil associations without economic purposes
  that meet the requirements set forth in art. 14 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 (National Tax Code).     (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

         § 1 The IBS and the CBS are levied on the set of acts or legal transactions involving the hypotheses provided in items III to VII of the caput of this article that
  constitute, in essence, an onerous operation with goods or services.

        § 2 If the donations under item VIII of the caput of this article have as their object goods or services that permitted the appropriation of credits by the
  donor, including in production:

        I - the donation will be taxed based on the market value of the goods or service donated; or
          II - at the taxpayer's option, the credits will be canceled.

        Art. 7 In the case of the supply of different goods and services in a single operation, it will be mandatory to specify each supply and its
  respective value, except if:

          I - all the supplies are subject to the same tax treatment; or

         II - one of the supplies can be considered principal and the others its ancillary items, in which case a single supply will be deemed to occur,
  applying to it the tax treatment corresponding to the principal supply.

        § 1 For purposes of item I of the caput of this article, there is distinct tax treatment when the supplies are subject to different rules regarding
  incidence, taxation regimes, exemption, the moment of occurrence of the taxable event, the place of the operation, the rate, taxable-person status and non-cumulativity.

         § 2 For purposes of item II of the caput of this article, ancillary supplies are considered to be those that are a condition or means for the
  principal supply.

         § 3 If there is unified billing for different supplies in disagreement with the provisions of this article, each supply will be considered independent
  for all purposes and the tax base corresponding to each will be assessed (arbitrada) under art. 13 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 7-A. If it is possible to apply more than one of the following mechanisms to the same operation, the following order of application will prevail:
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - reduction of the rate to zero;    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - suspension with conversion into a zero rate;        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - exemption;   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          IV - deferral; and   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          V - a rate reduction distinct from that under item I.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Sole paragraph. If it is possible to apply more than one rate reduction to the same operation:                 (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

          I - the cumulative application of the reductions will only occur if expressly provided for; and           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - if there is no provision for accumulation, the greater reduction will prevail.          (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                         Section II

                                                                                      On Immunities

          Art. 8 Exports of goods and services are immune from the IBS and the CBS, under the terms of Chapter V of this Title.

          Art. 9 Also immune from the IBS and the CBS are supplies:

          I - carried out by the Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities;

          II - carried out by religious entities and temples of any faith, including their welfare and charitable organizations;

         III - carried out by political parties, including their institutes and foundations, workers' union entities and non-profit educational and social
  assistance institutions;

          IV - of books, newspapers, periodicals and the paper intended for their printing;

         V - of phonograms and music videograms produced in Brazil containing musical or literary-musical works by Brazilian authors and/or works generally
  performed by Brazilian artists, as well as the physical media or digital files containing them, except at the stage of industrial replication of laser-read optical media;

          VI - of communication services in the modalities of free and unrestricted-reception radio and television broadcasting; and

          VII - of gold, when defined by law as a financial asset or foreign-exchange instrument.

         § 1 The immunity provided in item I of the caput of this article extends to autarchies and to foundations instituted and maintained by public authorities and to the
  public company providing postal services, as well as:

          I - it comprises only operations related to their essential purposes or those arising therefrom;

        II - it does not apply to operations related to the exploitation of economic activities governed by the rules applicable to private enterprises or in
  which there is consideration or payment of prices or tariffs by the user; and

          III - it does not exempt the prospective buyer from the obligation to pay tax with respect to real property.

          § 2 For the purposes of item II of the caput of this article, the following are considered:

          I - a religious entity and temple of any faith, a private-law non-profit legal entity whose objectives are to profess religious faith and practice
  religion; and

        II - a welfare and charitable organization, a private-law non-profit legal entity linked to and maintained by a religious entity and temple of
  any faith, that supplies goods and services in the area of social assistance, without discrimination against or requirements of any kind imposed on those assisted.

       § 3 The immunity provided in item III of the caput of this article applies exclusively to non-profit legal entities that cumulatively meet
  the requirements set forth in art. 14 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 (National Tax Code).

         § 4 The immunities of the entities provided in items I to III of the caput of this article do not apply to their acquisitions of tangible and intangible goods, including
  rights, and services.

                                                                                         Section III

                                                                    On the Moment of Occurrence of the Taxable Event

        Art. 10. The taxable event of the IBS and the CBS is deemed to occur at the moment of supply in operations with goods or services, even if of
  continuous or fractional performance.


        § 1 For purposes of the caput of this article, supply is deemed to occur at the moment:

        I - of the start of transport, in the provision of a transport service initiated in the Country;

        II - of the end of transport, in the provision of a cargo-transport service when initiated abroad;

        III - of the end of the supply, in the case of other services;

        IV - at which goods are found without valid tax documentation; and

        V - of the acquisition of goods in the hypotheses of:

        a) an auction (licitação) held by public authorities of seized or abandoned goods; or

        b) a judicial auction.

        § 2 In acquisitions of goods and services by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations, that are subject to art. 473
  of this Complementary Law, the taxable event is deemed to occur at the moment payment is made.

         § 3 In operations of continuous or fractional performance in which it is not possible to identify the moment of delivery or making available of the goods or the
  end of the supply of the service, such as those relating to water supply, basic sanitation, piped gas, telecommunications services, internet services
  and electric energy, the taxable event is deemed to occur at the moment payment becomes due.

        § 3 In operations of continuous or fractional performance, the taxable event is deemed to occur upon the first of the following occurrences:            (Wording
  given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - when the portion of the consideration corresponding to each payment becomes enforceable; or          (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - payment of the obligation arising from the supply.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 4 For purposes of the caput of this article, if payment, in full or in part, occurs before the supply:

        I - on the date of payment of each installment:

        a) advance taxes will be required, calculated as follows:

        1. the tax base will correspond to the value of each installment paid;

        2. the rates will be those in force on the date of payment of each installment;

        2. the rates will be those in force and applicable to the operation on the date of issuance of the electronic tax document corresponding to the payment or on the
  date of payment, whichever occurs first; (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        b) the advances under item "a" of this item will be recorded as debits in the assessment;

        II - on the date of supply:

        a) the final amounts of the taxes will be calculated as follows:

        1. the tax base will be the total value of the operation, including installments paid in advance;

        2. the rates will be those in force on the date of supply;

        b) if the amounts of the advances are lower than the final amounts, the differences will be recorded as debits in the assessment; and

        c) if the amounts of the advances are higher than the final amounts, the differences will be recorded as credits in the assessment.

        c) if the amounts of the advances are higher than the final amounts, the rules applicable to undue or excess payment will apply.          (Wording
  given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 5 In the case of § 4 of this article, if the supply to which the payment refers does not occur, including as a result of a rescission (distrato), the supplier may
  appropriate credits based on the value of the installments of the advances returned.

        § 5 In the case of § 4 of this article, if the supply to which the payment refers does not occur, including as a result of a rescission (distrato), the rules
  applicable to cancellation will apply. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 6 The extinguishment of the debits under § 4 will allow the acquirer to appropriate credits under the terms of arts. 47 to 57 of this Complementary Law.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 7 The regulation will establish hypotheses in which, observed the maximum period of 5 (five) days between the advance payment and the date of supply,
  the advances under item "a" of item I of § 4 of this article may be recorded as debits in the assessment period of the supply. (Included by the
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                      Section IV

                                                                              On the Place of the Operation

        Art. 11. The place of the operation is considered to be, for:

        I - tangible movable goods, the place of delivery or making available of the goods to the recipient;

        II - real property, intangible movable goods, including rights, related to real property, a service physically provided on real property and a service of
  administration and intermediation of real property, the place where the real property is located;

        III - a service physically provided on a natural person or enjoyed in person by a natural person, the place of provision of the service;

         IV - a service of planning, organization and administration of fairs, exhibitions, congresses, shows, exhibits and similar events, the place of the event to which
  the service refers;

        V - a service physically provided on tangible movable goods and port services, the place of provision of the service;

        VI - a passenger-transport service, the place where the transport begins;

        VII - a cargo-transport service, the place of delivery or making available of the goods to the recipient stated in the tax document;


        VIII - a service of exploitation of a route (via), through the charging of a value under any title, including tariffs, tolls and any other forms of charge, the territory
  of each Municipality and State, or of the Federal District, proportionally to the corresponding length of the route exploited;

        IX - fixed telephony service and other communication services provided by means of cables, wires, fibers and similar media, the place of installation of the terminal; and

        X - other services and other intangible movable goods, including rights, the place of the principal domicile of the:

        X - goods or a service not covered by the other items of this article:        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        a) acquirer, in onerous operations;

        a) if the operation is onerous:     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        1. the place of the principal domicile of the acquirer resident or domiciled in the Country; or      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        2. the place of the principal domicile of the recipient resident or domiciled in the Country, if the acquirer is not resident or domiciled in the Country.         (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        b) recipient, in non-onerous operations.

        b) if the operation is non-onerous, the place of the principal domicile of the recipient resident or domiciled in the Country.        (Wording given by Complementary Law
  No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1 For purposes of item I of the caput of this article:

        I - in an operation carried out remotely (não presencial), understood as one in which the delivery or making available does not occur in the presence of the acquirer or
  recipient at the establishment of the supplier, the place of delivery or making available of the goods to the recipient is considered to be the final destination indicated by the acquirer:

        a) to the supplier, if the transport service is the supplier's responsibility; or

        b) to the third party responsible for the transport, if the transport service is the acquirer's responsibility;

        II - the operation is considered to occur at the place of the principal domicile of the recipient, in the acquisition of a land, water or air motor vehicle;

        III - the operation is considered to occur at the place where the tangible movable goods are located:

        a) in the acquisition of goods in the hypotheses of:

        1. an auction (licitação) held by public authorities of seized or abandoned goods; or

        2. a judicial auction; and

        b) upon the finding of an irregularity due to the lack of tax documentation or coverage by invalid documentation.

        § 2 For purposes of item II of the caput of this article, if the real property is located in more than one Municipality, the place of the property is considered to be the
  Municipality where the largest part of its area is located.

        § 3 For purposes of this Complementary Law, the place of the principal domicile of the acquirer or, as the case may be, of the recipient is considered to be:

        I - the place stated in the registry with unique identification under art. 59 of this Complementary Law, which must take into account:

        a) for natural persons, the place of their permanent residence or, in the absence of, or in case of more than one, permanent residence, the place where their
  economic relations are most significant; and

         b) for legal persons and entities without legal personality, as applicable, the place of each establishment to which the goods or
  service is supplied;

          II - in the case of an acquirer or recipient not duly registered, whatever results from the combination of at least 2 (two) non-conflicting criteria, at
  the supplier's choice, among the following:

        a) the address declared to the supplier;

        b) the address obtained by collecting other commercially relevant information in the course of the operation;

        c) the address of the acquirer stated in the registry of the payment arrangement used for payment of the operation; and

        d) the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the device used to contract the operation or obtained by using a geolocation method;

        III - if it is not possible to comply with item II of this paragraph, the address declared to the supplier will be considered.

        § 4 In acquisitions carried out centrally by a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime who has more than one establishment and that
  are not subject to a prohibition on the appropriation of credits:

        I - the services under item IX of the caput of this article will be considered provided at the acquirer's principal domicile; and

        I - the services under item IX of the caput of this article and the leasing (locação) of tangible movable goods will be considered supplied at the principal domicile of the
  acquirer; and (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - for purposes of item X of the caput of this article and item I of this paragraph, the acquirer's principal domicile is considered to be the place of its
  head-office establishment.

        § 5 The provisions of item X of the caput of this article apply to the services under item III of the caput of this article that are provided remotely,
  even if only partially.

       § 6 If the tax authority finds that the information provided by the acquirer under § 3 of this article is incorrect and results in
  underpayment of the IBS and the CBS, the difference will be assessed against the acquirer, with statutory additions.

        § 7 In operations involving water supply, piped gas and electric energy, the place of the operation is considered to be:

        I - the place of delivery or making available, in operations intended for consumption;

        II - the place of the acquirer's principal establishment, defined under § 4 of this article:

       II - the place of the acquirer's principal establishment, defined under § 4 of this article, in operations that do not involve effective consumption:
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)
        a) in the supply of electric-energy transmission services; and

        b) in other operations, including in the hypotheses of generation, distribution or commercialization of electric energy.

        § 8 In the case under item X of the caput of this article, if the acquirer is resident or domiciled abroad and the recipient is resident or
  domiciled in the Country, the recipient's domicile is considered the place of the operation.  (Revoked by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 8 (Revoked).      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 9 In acquisitions of electric energy carried out on a multilateral basis, the place of the operation is considered to be that of the establishment or domicile of the
  agent that is in a debtor position in the energy balance.

        § 9 In acquisitions of electric energy carried out on a multilateral basis, the place of the operation is considered to be that of the establishment of the agent or of its
  represented parties that are in the debtor position of the financial settlement determined by the Electric Energy Trading Chamber (Câmara de Comercialização de
  Energia Elétrica). (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 10. In pipeline-transport operations of natural gas, the place of the operation will be that of the principal establishment of the:

        I - supplier, in the contracting of natural-gas entry capacity of the pipeline, under applicable legislation; and

        II - acquirer, in the contracting of natural-gas exit capacity from the pipeline.

        § 11. The provisions of item X of the caput of this article apply to operations involving the assignment of space for the provision of advertising services.

                                                                                      Section V

                                                                                 On the Tax Base

         Art. 12. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS is the value of the operation, except as otherwise provided in this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The value of the operation comprises the entire amount charged by the supplier under any title, including amounts corresponding to:

        I - increases arising from adjustments to the value of the operation;

        II - interest, penalties, additions and charges;

        III - discounts granted subject to a condition;

        IV - the value of transport charged as part of the value of the operation, in transport performed by the supplier itself or by transport on its behalf;

        V - taxes and public prices, including tariffs, levied on the operation or borne by the supplier, except those provided in § 2 of this article; and

        VI - other amounts charged or received as part of the value of the operation, including insurance and fees.

        § 2 The following are not included in the tax base of the IBS and the CBS:

        I - the amount of the IBS and the CBS levied on the operation;

        II - the amount of the Tax on Industrialized Products (IPI);

        III - unconditional discounts;

       IV - reimbursements received for amounts paid relating to operations on behalf of or in the name of third parties, provided that the
  tax documentation relating to such operations is issued in the name of the third party; and

         V - the amount levied on the operation of the taxes referred to in item II of the caput of art. 155, item III of the caput of art. 156 and item "b" of item I and
  item IV of the caput of art. 195 of the Federal Constitution, and of the Contribution to the Social Integration Programs and the Public Servant Asset Formation Program
  (Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep) referred to in art. 239 of the Federal Constitution, from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2032;

        VI - the contribution provided in art. 149-A of the Federal Constitution.

         § 3 For purposes of item III of § 2 of this article, an unconditional discount is considered to be the portion reducing the price of the operation that appears on the
  respective tax document and does not depend on a subsequent event, including if granted through a loyalty program provided on a non-onerous basis by the
  supplier itself.

         § 4 The tax base will correspond to the market value of the goods or services, understood as the value practiced in comparable operations between unrelated
  parties, in the following hypotheses:

        I - absence of the value of the operation;

        II - an operation with no determined value;

        III - a value of the operation not represented in money; and

        IV - an operation between related parties, under item IV of the caput of art. 5, observed §§ 2 to 7 thereof.

        § 5 If the value of the operation is expressed in foreign currency, it will be converted into national currency at an exchange rate determined by the Central
  Bank of Brazil, in accordance with the regulation.

        § 6 If the taxpayer contracts derivative financial instruments outside market conditions and that conceal, partially or fully, the value of the
  operation, the gain on the derivative will make up the tax base of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 7 The tax base relating to a return or cancellation will be the same as that used in the original operation.

        § 8 In international passenger transport, if outbound and return legs are sold together, the tax base will be half the value charged.

       § 9 In acquisitions of electric energy carried out on a multilateral basis, the tax base is the value of the financial settlement determined by the Electric Energy
  Trading Chamber, observed the proportional participation of the establishments of the agent or of its
  represented parties.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 13. The value of the operation will be assessed (arbitrado) by the tax administration when:

        I - the elements necessary to prove the value of the operation are not presented to the tax authorities upon inspection, including under an allegation of loss,
  misplacement, disappearance or accident, in cases in which:


        a) the operation is carried out without issuance of a tax document or is covered by invalid documentation; or

        b) a value notoriously lower than the market value of the operation is declared in the tax document;

         II - in any other hypothesis in which the declarations, information or documents presented by the taxable person or by a third party legally obligated
  are omitted, conflicting or unreliable.

        Sole paragraph. For purposes of the assessment (arbitramento) under this article, the tax base of the IBS and the CBS will be:

        I - the market value of the goods or services supplied, understood as the value practiced in comparable operations between unrelated parties; or

        II - when the value under item I of this paragraph is not available, that calculated:

       a) based on the cost of the goods or service, plus the expenses indispensable to the maintenance of the taxable person's activities or the gross profit determined
  based on accounting or tax records; or

        b) by the value fixed by a competent body, by the final consumer price suggested by the manufacturer or importer or by the price published or provided by
  entities representing the respective sectors, as the case may be.

                                                                                       Section VI

                                                                                   On Rates

                                                                                      Subsection I

                                                                               On Standard Rates

        Art. 14. The rates of the CBS and the IBS will be set by specific law of the respective federative entity, as follows:

        I - the Union will set the CBS rate;

        II - each State will set its IBS rate;

        III - each Municipality will set its IBS rate; and

        IV - the Federal District will exercise the state and municipal competences in setting its rates.

        § 1 For purposes of item III of the caput of this article, the State of Pernambuco will exercise the municipal competence relating to operations carried out
  in the Fernando de Noronha State District, under art. 15 of the Act of Transitional Constitutional Provisions (ADCT).

        § 2 When setting its rate, each federative entity may:

        I - link it to the reference rate of the respective federative sphere, under art. 18 of this Complementary Law, by means of an increase or decrease in
  percentage points; or

        II - set it without linkage to the reference rate of the respective federative sphere.

        § 3 In the absence of a specific law establishing the federative entity's rate, the reference rate of the respective federative sphere will apply.

        § 4 References in this Complementary Law to standard rates must be understood as references to the rates set by each federative entity under the
  terms of this article.

        Art. 15. The IBS rate levied on each operation will correspond to:

        I - the sum:

        a) of the rate of the destination State of the operation; and

        b) of the rate of the destination Municipality of the operation; or

        II - the rate of the Federal District, when it is the destination of the operation.

       Sole paragraph. For purposes of this article, the destination of the operation is the place where the operation occurs, defined under art. 11 of this Complementary
  Law.

         Art. 16. The rate set by each federative entity under art. 14 of this Complementary Law will be the same for all operations with goods or with
  services, except as provided in the hypotheses in this Complementary Law.

        Sole paragraph. Rate reductions established under the differentiated regimes covered by Title IV of this Book will be applied to the rate of
  each federative entity.

        Sole paragraph. Rate reductions established under the differentiated and specific regimes covered by Titles IV and V of this Book will be
  applied to the rate of each federative entity, except in cases where a nationally uniform rate applies. (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 17. The rate applied for purposes of a return or cancellation of the operation will be the same as that charged in the original operation.

                                                                                      Subsection II

                                                                            On Reference Rates

         Art. 18. Reference rates will be set by resolution of the Federal Senate:

        I - for the CBS, from 2027 to 2035, under arts. 353 to 359, 366, 368 and 369 of this Complementary Law;

        II - for the IBS, from 2029 to 2035, under arts. 361 to 366 and 369 of this Complementary Law;

        III - for the IBS and the CBS, after 2035, those in force in the previous year.

        Art. 19. Any change in federal legislation that reduces or increases the collection of the IBS or the CBS:

        I - must be offset by an increase or reduction, by the Federal Senate, of the CBS reference rate and of the state and
  municipal IBS reference rates, so as to preserve the revenue collection of the federative spheres;

        II - will only take effect with the start of the production of effects of the adjustment of the reference rates under item I of this caput.
        § 1 For purposes of the caput of this article:

        I - any change in federal legislation that reduces or increases the collection of the IBS or the CBS must be taken into account, including, among others:

        a) changes to the criteria relating to the general refund of IBS and CBS to natural persons, covered by Chapter I of Title III of this Book;

        b) changes to the differentiated, specific or favored taxation regimes provided in this Complementary Law, including as a result of the five-year
  review under Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law; and

       c) changes to the favored taxation regime of the Unified Special Regime for the Collection of Taxes and Contributions owed by Microenterprises and
  Small Businesses (Simples Nacional) and of the Individual Micro-Entrepreneur (MEI), covered by Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006;

        II - the following will not be taken into account:

        a) changes to the CBS rate, under item I of the caput and § 2 of art. 14 of this Complementary Law; and

        b) changes to the amount of the specific CBS refund to natural persons under federal legislation, covered by Chapter I of Title III of this Book;

        III - the adjustment of the reference rates must be established by resolution of the Federal Senate, based on calculations prepared by the IBS Management
  Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union and approved by the Federal Court of Accounts (Tribunal de Contas da União), observed the ninety-day advance-notice rule (anterioridade nonagesimal) provided
  in item "c" of item III of the caput of art. 150 of the Federal Constitution and, for the IBS, also the annual advance-notice rule (anterioridade anual) provided in item "b" of item III of the
  caput of art. 150 of the Federal Constitution.

        § 2 For purposes of item III of § 1 of this article:

       I - the calculations must be sent to the Federal Court of Accounts, accompanied by the respective methodology, within 60 (sixty)
  days after the promulgation of the law that reduces or increases the collection of the IBS or the CBS:

        a) by the IBS Management Committee, in the case of legal changes that affect only IBS revenue;

        b) by the Executive Branch of the Union, in the case of legal changes that affect only CBS revenue; or

        c) jointly by the IBS Management Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union, in the case of legal changes that affect both IBS and CBS revenue;

        II - the Federal Court of Accounts may request adjustments to the methodology or the calculations, within 60 (sixty) days after receiving them;

        III - the IBS Management Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union will have up to 30 (thirty) days to adjust the methodology or the calculations;

        IV - the Federal Court of Accounts will decide definitively with respect to the calculations and will forward them to the Federal Senate, within 30 (thirty) days; and

        V - the Federal Senate will establish the adjustment of the reference rates, within 30 (thirty) days.

       Art. 20. Complementary bill proposals that reduce or increase the collection of the IBS or the CBS, under art. 19, will only be considered by the
  National Congress if accompanied by an estimate of the impact on the reference rates of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 1 The impact estimate under the caput of this article, accompanied by the respective methodology, will be prepared:

        I - by the Executive Branch of the Union, for bills of its own initiative, with a statement from the IBS Management Committee within up to 30 (thirty) days; or

       II - by the author and the rapporteur of the bill before the body responsible for issuing an opinion on the financial and budgetary aspects of the bill, in the
  other cases.

        § 2 For purposes of item II of § 1 of this article, the Chamber of Deputies, the Federal Senate, or any of their Committees, may consult the
  Executive Branch of the Union, the IBS Management Committee or the Federal Court of Accounts, which must present the impact estimate within 60 (sixty)
  days.

                                                                                     Section VII

                                                                               On Tax Liability

        Art. 21. The following are taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS:

        I - the supplier that carries out operations:

        a) in the development of an economic activity;

        b) on a habitual basis or in a volume that characterizes an economic activity; or

        c) on a professional basis, even if the profession is not regulated;

        II - the acquirer, even if not covered by item I of this caput, in the acquisition of goods:

        a) seized or abandoned, in an auction (licitação) held by public authorities; or

        b) at a judicial auction;

        III - the importer;

        IV - the person expressly provided for in other hypotheses in this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The taxpayer under the caput of this article is required to register in the records relating to the IBS and the CBS.

         § 2 A supplier resident or domiciled abroad is required to register as a taxpayer if it carries out operations in the Country or as a tax
  liable party in the case of imports, observed the definition of the place of the operation provided in art. 11 and the provisions of art. 23 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3 The regulation may also require registration in the records relating to the IBS and the CBS of the parties responsible for compliance with principal or
  ancillary obligations provided in this Complementary Law.

         § 4 In the importation of tangible goods, the provisions of § 2 of this article apply only to international shipments subject to a simplified taxation regime
  under art. 95.

         Art. 22. Digital platforms, even if domiciled abroad, are liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS relating to the transactions and imports
  carried out through their intermediation, in the following cases:

        I - jointly and severally with the acquirer or recipient and in substitution for the supplier, should the latter be resident or domiciled abroad; and


        II - jointly and severally with the supplier, should the latter:

        II - jointly and severally with the supplier resident and domiciled in the Country, should:      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) be resident or domiciled in the Country;

        a) the digital platform not provide the information set forth in § 5 of this article; or     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) be a taxpayer, even if not registered under the terms of § 1 of art. 21 of this Complementary Law; and

        b) the supplier:        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        1. be a taxpayer, even if not registered under the terms of § 1 of art. 21 of this Complementary Law; and       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        2. not issue an electronic tax document for the value of the transaction carried out through the platform.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        c) not register the transaction in an electronic tax document.

        § 1 A digital platform is considered to be one that:

        I - acts as an intermediary between suppliers and acquirers in transactions and imports carried out on a non face-to-face basis or electronically; and

        II - controls one or more of the following elements essential to the transaction:

        a) charging/billing;

        b) payment;

        c) definition of terms and conditions; or

        d) delivery.

        § 2 A platform that carries out only one of the following activities is not considered a digital platform:

        I - provision of internet access;

        II - payment services provided by institutions authorized to operate by the Central Bank of Brazil;

        III - advertising; or

        IV - search for or comparison of suppliers, provided it does not charge for the service based on sales made.

         § 3 In the case dealt with in item I of the caput of this article, the supplier resident or domiciled abroad is exempted from the registration referred to in § 2
  of art. 21 of this Complementary Law if it carries out transactions exclusively through a digital platform registered in the IBS and CBS registry under the regular regime.

         § 4 For purposes of applying the provision of item II of the caput of this article, it is incumbent upon the IBS Management Committee and the Special Secretariat of the Federal Revenue of
  Brazil (RFB) to inform the digital platform of the taxpayer status of the supplier resident or domiciled in the Country who is not registered in the registry.

       § 5 The digital platform shall submit to the IBS Management Committee and to the RFB, in the manner set forth in the regulations, information on the transactions and imports involving goods or
  services carried out through its intermediation, including identifying the supplier, even if it is not a taxpayer.

        § 6 In the case in which the payment process for the transaction or import is initiated by the digital platform, it shall submit the information
  necessary for the segregation and collection of the IBS and CBS amounts owed by the supplier at the financial settlement of the transaction (split payment), when
  available, including under the simplified procedure, under the terms of arts. 31 to 35 of this Complementary Law.

        § 7 A digital platform that complies with §§ 5 and 6 of this article shall not be liable for payment of any differences between the amounts of
  IBS and CBS collected and those owed on the transaction by the supplier resident or domiciled in the Country.

        § 7 The digital platform shall not be liable for payment of any differences between the amounts of IBS and CBS collected and those owed on the
  transaction by the supplier resident and domiciled in the Country if: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         I - it is possible to carry out the split payment at the financial settlement of the transaction and the digital platform submits the information referred to in § 6 of this
  article; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the digital platform submits the information referred to in § 5 of this article.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 8 In the case in which the supplier is resident or domiciled in the Country and the payment process for the transaction is not initiated by the digital platform,
  the platform shall not be tax liable if it complies with § 5 and the supplier issues an electronic tax document for the value of the transaction carried out through the
  platform.    (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8 (Repealed).        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 9 The provision of § 8 also applies if the payment process for the transaction is initiated by the digital platform and the split
  payment is not carried out. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 9 (Repealed).        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 10. In the cases in which the digital platform is liable, under the terms of items I and II of the caput of this article:

         I - the platform shall be jointly and severally liable for the IBS and CBS debts of the supplier relating to the transaction, in accordance with the tax rules
  applicable to it, if the supplier is resident or domiciled in the Country and is registered as a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS, under the regular regime or a favored regime; and

        II - in other cases, the IBS and CBS debts shall be calculated under the rules of the regular regime, including as to rates, differentiated regimes and
  specific regimes applicable to the goods and services.

         § 11. The digital platform shall not be tax liable in relation to transactions in which it does not control any of the essential elements, under the terms of
  item II of § 1 of this article.

        § 12. The digital platform may opt, with the consent of the supplier resident or domiciled in the Country, subject to the criteria established in the regulations:

        I - to issue electronic tax documents on behalf of the supplier, including on a consolidated basis; and

        II - to pay the IBS and the CBS, based on the value and other information of the transaction intermediated by the platform, with the supplier's obligation
  maintained in relation to any differences.


        § 13. The digital platform may opt, with the consent of the supplier, in the manner established in the regulations, to be a tax substitute in relation to the
  transactions it intermediates for a supplier resident or domiciled in the Country, in which case it shall: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       I - issue electronic tax documents relating to the transactions of the substituted supplier, including on a consolidated basis;                   (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

         II - assess the IBS and the CBS arising from the said transactions in accordance with the provisions of items I or II of § 10 of this article, as applicable; and
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - pay the IBS and the CBS based on the value and other information of the transaction intermediated by the platform, with the supplier's obligation
  maintained in relation to any differences. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 14. In the case referred to in item "b" of item II of the caput of this article, if the platform issues the tax document within 30 (thirty) days counted from the date
  on which the supplier should have issued it and pays the IBS and the CBS as set forth in the regulations, based on the value and other information of the transaction
  intermediated by it, the surcharges referred to in § 2 of art. 29 of this Complementary Law and the penalty for failure to issue the tax document shall be required
  exclusively from the supplier.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 15. In the cases of §§ 12, 13 and 14 of this article, the digital platform is authorized to calculate the IBS and CBS debits at the reference rates
  in the event of unavailability of information regarding the tax rules applicable to the supplier, and any difference in the IBS and CBS owed on the transaction
  shall be:   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - paid by the supplier, if the applicable rates are higher than the reference rates; or            (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

          II - refunded if the applicable rates are lower than the reference rates.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 23. The digital platform, including one domiciled abroad, shall register in the IBS and CBS registry under the regular regime for purposes of compliance
  with the provisions of art. 22.

        Sole paragraph. If the supplier or the digital platform resident or domiciled abroad does not register in the IBS and CBS registry under the regular
  regime referred to in the caput of this article:

        I - the IBS and the CBS shall be segregated and collected, at the reference rates, on remittances to the supplier or the platform, by the institution that carries out the
  exchange transaction, subject to the criteria established in the regulations; and

          II - any difference in the IBS and CBS owed on the transaction or import shall be:

          a) paid by the acquirer or importer, if the applicable rates are higher than the reference rates; or

          b) refunded to the acquirer or importer, if the applicable rates are lower than the reference rates.

         Art. 24. Without prejudice to the other cases provided for in Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 (National Tax Code) and in civil legislation, jointly and severally
  liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS are:

         I - the person or entity without legal personality that, under any title, acquires, imports, receives, causes the entry or exit of, or holds in deposit, goods, or takes
  a service, not covered by a valid tax document;

          II - the carrier, including a postal service or express delivery company:

          a) in relation to goods transported without a valid tax document;

          b) when it delivers goods to a location other than that indicated on the tax document;

          III - the auctioneer, for the IBS and the CBS owed on the transaction carried out at auction;

        IV - the developers or suppliers of programs or applications used to record transactions with goods or services that contain functions
  or commands inserted for the purpose of failing to comply with tax legislation;

        V - any individual, legal entity or entity without legal personality that contributes, through its acts and omissions, to the failure to comply with
  tax obligations, by means of:

          a) concealment of the occurrence or value of the transaction; or

          b) abuse of legal personality, characterized by deviation of purpose or commingling of assets; and

          VI - the bonded warehouse, the customs area or an establishment equivalent to it, the depositary or the customs broker, in relation to the goods:

          a) intended for export without corresponding tax documentation;

          b) received for export and not exported;

          c) intended for a person or entity without legal personality different from the one that imported or acquired it at auction; or

          d) imported and delivered without due authorization from the competent tax administrations.

        § 1 The immunity referred to in § 1 of art. 9 of this Complementary Law does not exempt the public company providing postal services from joint and several liability
  in the cases provided for in item II of the caput of this article.

          § 2 The liability referred to in item "a" of item V of the caput of this article is limited to the concealed value of the transaction.

         § 3 The mere existence of an economic group, in the absence of any action or omission that falls within the provisions
  of item V of the caput of this article, does not give rise to joint and several liability.

       § 4 Re-refiners or collectors authorized by the National Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANP) are jointly and severally liable for
  payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on the acquisition of used or contaminated lubricating oil from a taxpayer subject to the regular regime.

        § 5 In the case of § 4, the issuance of the electronic tax document relating to the transaction shall be carried out by the re-refiners or collectors, in the manner established
  in the regulations, which may provide, including, that the issuance occur periodically, encompassing the transactions carried out in the period.

         Art. 25. The liabilities referred to in this Complementary Law comprise the obligation for payment of the IBS and the CBS, plus monetary correction and
  adjustment, late-payment penalty, punitive fines and other charges.

          Art. 26. The following are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS, except as provided in item II of § 1 of art. 156-A of the Federal Constitution:

          I - condominium (edilícia - building condominium);
        II - consortium referred to in art. 278 of Law No. 6,404, of December 15, 1976;

        III - a silent partnership (sociedade em conta de participação);

       IV - nanoentrepreneur, understood as the individual who has earned gross revenue lower than 50% (fifty percent) of the limit established for
  joining the MEI (Individual Microentrepreneur) regime provided for in § 1 of art. 18-A, also observing the provisions of §§ 4 and 4-B of the said article of Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14,
  2006, and who has not joined that regime; and

        V - (VETOED);
        V - investment funds, subject to the provisions of §§ 5 to 8 of this article; (Promulgation of vetoed parts)

        V - investment funds, subject to the provisions of §§ 5-A to 8-A of this article;        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        VI - rural producer referred to in art. 164 of this Complementary Law;

        VII - self-employed cargo carrier referred to in art. 169 of this Complementary Law;

        VIII - an entity or unit of an economic-accounting nature, non-profit, that provides health care plan services under the self-management modality;

        IX - closed supplementary pension entities, established in accordance with Complementary Law No. 109, of May 29, 2001; and

        X - (VETOED).

        X - endowment funds established under the terms of Law No. 13,800, of January 4, 2019.     (Promulgation of vetoed parts)

        § 1 The following may opt for the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, subject to the provisions of § 6 of art. 41 of this Complementary Law:

        I - the entities without legal personality referred to in items I to III of the caput of this article;

        II - the individual referred to in item IV of the caput of this article; and

        III - (VETOED);

        IV - the rural producer referred to in item VI of the caput of this article, in the manner set forth in art. 165 of this Complementary Law; and

        V - the self-employed cargo carrier referred to in item VII of the caput of this article.

        § 2 In relation to the building condominium referred to in item I of the caput of this article:

       I - if it exercises the option for the regular regime referred to in § 1 of this article, the IBS and the CBS shall be levied on all fees and other amounts charged by the
  condominium to its unit owners and to third parties; and

       I - if it exercises the option for the regular regime, under the terms of § 1 of this article, the IBS and the CBS shall be levied on all fees and other amounts charged by the
  condominium to its unit owners and to third parties; and (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - if it does not exercise the option for the regular regime and provided that the fees and other condominium amounts charged to its unit owners represent less than
  80% (eighty percent) of the condominium's total revenue:

        a) it shall be subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS on the transactions with goods and services that it carries out in accordance with the provisions of item I of the caput of art.
  21 of this Complementary Law; and

       b) it shall appropriate credits in proportion to the revenue arising from the transactions taxed in the manner of item "a" of this item, in relation to the total revenue of the
  condominium.

        § 3 If the consortium referred to in item II of the caput does not exercise the option for the regular regime referred to in § 1 of this article, the members of the consortium shall
  be liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS regarding the transactions carried out by the consortium, in proportion to their respective interests.

         § 4 If the silent partnership referred to in item III of the caput does not exercise the option for the regular regime referred to in § 1 of this article, the
  managing partner shall be liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS regarding the transactions carried out by the partnership, with the exclusion of amounts owed to silent
  partners being prohibited.

        § 5 (VETOED).

        § 5-A. For purposes of the provisions of item V of the caput of this article, the following are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - Real Estate Investment Funds (FII) and Agribusiness Production Chain Investment Funds (Fiagro), referred to in Law No. 8,668, of
  June 25, 1993, that carry out transactions with real property, including transactions with real rights over real property, and that, cumulatively: (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         a) have their units admitted to trading exclusively on stock exchanges or organized over-the-counter markets and have at least 100 (one hundred)
  unit holders; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) do not have:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        1. an individual unit holder holding units that represent 20% (twenty percent) or more of the total units issued by the FII or the Fiagro, or whose units
  entitle it to receive income greater than 20% (twenty percent) of total income; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

        2. a group of related individual unit holders, understood as relatives up to the second degree, holding units that represent 40% (forty
  percent) or more of the total units issued by the FII or the Fiagro, or whose units entitle them to receive income greater than 40%
  (forty percent) of the total income earned by the fund; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        3. legal entity unit holders that, individually or together with unit holders that are their controlling shareholders or their subsidiaries and affiliates, hold
  more than 50% (fifty percent) of the units of the fund, except when the unit holder is a closed pension entity;   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

         II - the FII and the Fiagro that carry out transactions with real property, including transactions with real rights over real property, and that do not meet the
  conditions established in item I of this paragraph, whose units are held, directly or indirectly, in more than 95% (ninety-five percent), by:
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) a FII or Fiagro that meets the provisions of item I of this paragraph; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) an investment fund established in the Country exclusively to receive resources from supplementary pension benefit plans and from
  personal insurance plans, regulated and supervised by the competent governmental bodies; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
       c) pension entities and pension funds in the Country, regulated and supervised by the competent governmental bodies; or                   (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        d) an investment fund that, although not established as a FII or Fiagro, meets the requirements set forth in items "a" and "b" of item I of this paragraph;
  and    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          III - other investment funds whose assets consist exclusively of investments in equity interests, certificates, rights,
  securities and other financial assets permitted by the Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM), subject to the provisions of § 6-A and § 8-A of this article.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 5-B. Temporary possession by the investment fund of assets obtained as a result of judicial or extrajudicial proceedings relating to the recovery of assets forming part of its
  portfolio does not undermine compliance with the requirements referred to in the items of § 5-A of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

        § 6 (VETOED).

        § 6-A. The following are taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime:        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       I - the FII and the Fiagro that carry out transactions with real property, including transactions with real rights over real property, that:                 (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) do not meet the conditions established in item I or item II of § 5-A of this article; or         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) are subject to the taxation applicable to legal entities, under the terms of the legislation in force; and       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - Receivables Investment Funds (FIDC) and other investment funds that prepay receivables, not
  characterized as investment entities, under the terms provided for in art. 193, § 5, or art. 219, § 6, both of this Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7 The following are taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime: investment funds that prepay receivables, under the terms provided for in art.
  193 or art. 219 of this Complementary Law. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7 (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7-A. The FII and the Fiagro referred to in items I and II of § 5-A of this article may opt, at any time, irrevocably, for the regular regime
  of the IBS and the CBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8 (VETOED).

         § 8-A. If, after the date of publication of this Complementary Law, it becomes permitted, in accordance with regulations to be issued by the
  governmental bodies that make up the National Financial System, for new transactions with goods or services subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS
  to be carried out by an investment fund, that fund shall be considered a taxpayer under the regular regime. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 9 The entities and units of an economic-accounting nature referred to in items VIII and IX of the caput of this article shall be taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS if
  they fail to meet the requirements set forth in art. 14 of the National Tax Code.

        § 9-A. In the case in which investment funds are taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime, when the unit holder is subject to taxation
  under the specific regime for financial services, under the terms of Chapter II of Title V of this Book, the portion of the income received by the unit holder
  corresponding to the transactions taxed at the fund level shall not be included in the tax base of the specific regime for financial services.               (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 10. For purposes of classification as a nanoentrepreneur, under the terms of item IV of the caput of this article, the gross revenue of the individual
  providing private individual passenger transport services or goods delivery services intermediated by digital platforms shall be considered to be 25% (twenty-five percent)
  of the gross monthly amount received.

         § 10. For purposes of classification as a nanoentrepreneur under the terms of item IV of the caput of this article, the gross revenue of the individual
  providing private individual passenger transport services or goods delivery, including in the case in which there is intermediation by
  digital platforms, shall be considered to be 25% (twenty-five percent) of the gross monthly amount received. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 11. The regulations may establish simplified ancillary obligations for the persons and entities without legal personality and the units of an
  economic-accounting nature referred to in this article.

                                                                                     Section VIII

                                                                   On the Methods of Extinguishing Debts
