                                                                                    Subsection I

                                                                               General Provisions

        Art. 27. Debts of the IBS and the CBS arising from the levy on transactions with goods or services shall be extinguished by the following methods:

        I - offset with credits, respectively, of IBS and CBS appropriated by the taxpayer, under the terms of arts. 47 to 56 and the other provisions of this
  Complementary Law;

        II - payment by the taxpayer;

        III - collection at the financial settlement of the transaction (split payment), under the terms of arts. 31 to 35 of this Complementary Law;

        IV - collection by the acquirer, under the terms of art. 36 of this Complementary Law; or

        V - payment by the party to which this Complementary Law assigns liability.

        Sole paragraph. The extinction of debts referred to in the caput of this article:

         I - in the cases of items I and II of the caput of this article, shall be applied to the amounts of unextinguished debts of the IBS and the CBS levied on transactions
  occurring in the assessment period in chronological order of the tax document, according to criteria established in the regulations;

        II - in the cases of items III and IV of the caput of this article, shall be linked to the respective transaction; and

        III - in the case of item V of the caput of this article, shall be linked to the specific transaction to which it refers or, if it does not refer to a specific transaction, shall be
  applied in the manner of item I of this paragraph.

         Art. 28. In transactions with electric energy or with rights related to it, collection of the IBS and the CBS relating to generation, commercialization and
  distribution and transmission shall be carried out exclusively:
         I - by the electric energy distributor, if the sale is made to an acquirer served in the regulated contracting environment;
         II - by the seller of electric energy, in the case of acquisition in the free contracting environment of energy for the acquirer's own consumption or when the
  acquirer is not subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS;
         III - by the acquirer, in the capacity of liable party, of electric energy if intended for consumption in the acquisition of electric energy carried out in a
  multilateral manner; or
         IV - by the electric energy transmitter, in the provision of electric energy transmission service to a consumer connected directly to the basic
  transmission network.

       Art. 28. In transactions with electric energy or with rights related to it, collection of the IBS and the CBS relating to import, generation,
  commercialization, distribution and transmission shall be carried out exclusively: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - by the electric energy distributor, in cases of supply to an acquirer served in the regulated contracting environment or of charging for the
  use of distribution systems for consumers served in the free contracting environment; (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         II - by the seller, in the case of acquisition in the free contracting environment of energy for the acquirer's own consumption or when the acquirer is not
  subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS; (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          III - in the case of acquisition for consumption, carried out in a multilateral manner:      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          a) by the retail trader, in relation to the consumption of the represented consuming units; or              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

          b) in other cases, by the consuming establishment;         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       IV - by the electric energy transmitter, in the provision of electric energy transmission service and of connection to the transmission system to a
  consumer connected directly to the basic transmission network. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 1 Collection of the IBS and the CBS levied on transactions with electric energy, or with rights related to it, relating to generation, commercialization,
  distribution and transmission shall occur only upon supply:

       § 1 Collection of the IBS and the CBS levied on transactions with electric energy, or with rights related to it, relating to import, generation,
  commercialization, distribution and transmission shall occur only upon supply: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - for consumption; or

          II - to a taxpayer not subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS.

         § 2 In the electric energy transmission service, the supply is deemed to have occurred at the moment when payment relating to the transmission
  service becomes due, under the terms of the applicable legislation.

        § 2 In the electric energy transmission service and connection to transmission systems, the supply is deemed to have occurred at the moment defined
  under the terms of § 3 of art. 10 of this Complementary Law. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3 Excluded from the tax base of the CBS and the IBS is the electric energy supplied by the distributor to the consuming unit, in the quantity corresponding to the
  energy injected into the distribution grid by that same consuming unit, plus the electric energy credits originated by the same consuming unit in the
  same month, in prior months, or in another consuming unit of the same holder.

          § 4 The exclusion referred to in § 3 of this article:

          I - applies only to consumers participating in the Electric Energy Compensation System, referred to in Law No. 14,300, of January 6, 2022;

         II - applies only to the offsetting of electric energy produced by microgeneration and minigeneration, whose installed capacity is, respectively, less than or
  equal to 75 kW and greater than 75 kW and less than or equal to 1 MW; and

       III - does not apply to the availability cost, reactive energy, power demand, connection charges or use of the distribution system, non-energy-related
  tariff components, and any other amounts charged by the distributor.

                                                                                      Subsection II

                                                                          On Payment by the Taxpayer

          Art. 29. The taxpayer shall, by the due date, make payment of the balance payable referred to in art. 45 of this Complementary Law.

         § 1 If the payment made by the taxpayer is greater than the balance payable, the excess portion, up to the amount of the debts of the assessment period
  that have been extinguished by the methods provided for in items III to V of the caput of art. 27 of this Complementary Law between the end of the assessment period and
  the business day preceding the taxpayer's payment, shall be transferred to the taxpayer within 3 (three) business days.

        § 1 If the payment made by the taxpayer is greater than the balance payable, the excess portion, up to the amount of the debts of the assessment
  period that have been extinguished by the methods provided for in items III to V of the caput of art. 27 of this Complementary Law between the end of the
  assessment period and the processing of the payment made by the taxpayer, shall be transferred to the taxpayer within 3 (three) business days.   (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 2 Payment made after the due date shall be increased by:

          I - a late-payment penalty, calculated at a rate of 0.33% (thirty-three hundredths percent) per day of delay; and

        II - late-payment interest, calculated at the reference rate of the Special Settlement and Custody System (Selic), from the first day of the month following the
  due date of the term until the month prior to that of payment, plus 1% (one percent) in the month of payment.

       § 3 The penalty referred to in item I of § 2 of this article shall be calculated from the first day following the due date of the term set for
  payment of the tax until the day on which payment occurs.

          § 4 The percentage of the penalty referred to in item I of § 2 of this article is limited to 20% (twenty percent).

        § 5 Late-payment interest, under the terms of item II of § 2 of this article, applies to unpaid punitive fines.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

       Art. 30. The IBS Management Committee and the RFB may offer, as an option to the taxpayer, an automated payment mechanism, respectively, for the IBS and
  the CBS.

          § 1 Use of the mechanism provided for in the caput of this article by the taxpayer is conditioned on prior authorization by the taxpayer.

          § 2 The automated mechanism referred to in the caput of this article shall permit the withdrawal and deposit of amounts in deposit accounts and payment accounts
  held by the taxpayer.


                                                                                  Subsection III

                                                        On Collection at Financial Settlement (Split Payment)

        Art. 31. In payment transactions relating to transactions with goods or services, providers of electronic payment services and institutions
  operating payment systems shall segregate and collect, to the IBS Management Committee and the RFB, at the time of financial settlement of the transaction (split
  payment), the amounts of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Subsection.

        § 1 The split payment procedures provided for in this Subsection shall comprise the linking between:
        I - the electronic tax documents relating to transactions with goods or services; and
        II - the payment transaction of the respective transactions.

        § 1 The split payment procedures provided for in this Subsection comprise:             (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - the standard procedure, referred to in art. 32 of this Complementary Law; and      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the simplified procedure, referred to in art. 33 of this Complementary Law.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1-A. For purposes of the provisions of this Subsection, the following definitions apply:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - originator of the payment transaction: the party that initiates the transaction with the payment arrangement, which may be the payer or the receiver of the
  funds; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - payment transactions initiated by the receiver: those originated by means of an instruction or instrument issued by the receiver of the funds, which
  defines the payment amount, with the payer being responsible only for making the payment, even if partial; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - payment transactions initiated by the payer: those originated by the payer, who defines the payment amount, without prior intervention by the
  receiver of the funds with the payment arrangement. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 2 Joint acts of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB shall regulate the provisions of this Subsection, including as to the duties of the providers of
  electronic payment services and the institutions operating payment systems, considering the characteristics of each payment arrangement and of the
  transactions with goods and services.

         § 3 The provisions of this Subsection apply to all providers of electronic payment services referred to in the caput of this article, participants in
  payment arrangements, open and closed, public and private, including participants and arrangements not subject to regulation by the Central Bank of Brazil.

        Art. 32. The standard split payment procedure shall comply with the provisions of this article.

        § 1 The supplier is required to include in the electronic tax document information that allows for:
        I - the linking of the transactions with the payment transaction; and
        II - the identification of the amounts of the IBS and CBS debits levied on the transactions.

        § 1 The originator of the payment transaction shall transmit to the payment service provider information that allows for:                (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - the linking of the transactions with the payment transaction; and        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the identification of the amounts of the IBS and the CBS levied on the transactions.      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2 The information provided for in § 1 of this article shall be transmitted to the payment service providers:

       § 2 The information provided for in § 1 of this article shall be transmitted to the payment service providers:                    (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - by the supplier;

        I - by the supplier or by the acquirer, in cases in which they initiate the payment transaction;         (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - by the digital platform, in relation to the transactions and imports carried out through its intermediation, under the terms of art. 22 of this Complementary Law; or

        III - by another person or entity without legal personality that receives the payment.

       III - by another person or entity without legal personality, in cases in which they initiate the payment transaction.                     (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2-A. In payment transactions initiated by the receiver, the receiver may opt not to transmit to the payment service provider the information
  referred to in item I of § 1 of this article, in which case the supplier or the digital platform shall include in the electronic tax document information that
  allows for the linking of the transaction with the payment transaction. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 3 Before making funds available to the supplier, the payment service provider or the institution operating the payment system shall,
  based on the information received, consult the system of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB regarding the amounts to be segregated and collected, which shall correspond to the
  positive difference between:

        I - the amounts of the IBS and CBS debits levied on the transaction, shown separately in the electronic tax document; and

        II - the portions of the debits referred to in item I of this paragraph already extinguished by any of the methods provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law.

        § 4 If the query cannot be carried out under the terms of § 3 of this article, the following procedure shall be adopted:

        I - the payment service provider or the institution operating the payment system shall segregate and collect, to the IBS Management Committee and the RFB, the amount
  of the IBS and CBS debits levied on the transactions linked to the payment transaction, based on the information received; and

        II - the IBS Management Committee and the RFB:

        a) shall calculate the amounts of the IBS and CBS debits of the transactions linked to the payment transaction, with the deduction of the portions already extinguished
  by any of the methods provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law; and

        b) shall transfer to the supplier, within 3 (three) business days, the amounts received that exceed the amount referred to in item "a" of this item.

       Art. 33. The taxpayer may opt for the simplified split payment procedure for all transactions in which the acquirer is not a taxpayer of the IBS and the
  CBS under the regular regime.

        Art. 33. The simplified split payment procedure shall be optional and shall comply with the provisions of this article.       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)


       § 1 In the simplified procedure referred to in the caput of this article, the amounts of the IBS and the CBS to be segregated and collected by the payment service
  provider or by the institution operating the payment system shall be calculated based on a pre-established percentage of the value of the transactions.

        § 2 The percentage referred to in § 1 of this article:

        I - shall be established by the IBS Management Committee, for the IBS, and by the RFB, for the CBS, with the application of the simplified procedure to only one
  of these taxes being prohibited;

        II - may be differentiated by economic sector or by taxpayer, based on calculations grounded on a previously disclosed uniform methodology, including
  data on the average rate levied on the transactions and the history of use of credits; and

        III - shall bear no relation to the amount of the IBS and CBS debits actually levied on the transaction.

         § 2-A. The origination of a payment transaction relating to a transaction with goods or services without the identification of the amounts of the IBS and the CBS, under the terms
  of item II of § 1 of art. 32 of this Complementary Law, implies opting for the simplified procedure referred to in this article. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

          § 3 The amounts of the IBS and the CBS collected through the simplified procedure referred to in the caput shall be used for payment of the unextinguished
  debts of the taxpayer arising from the transactions referred to in the caput occurring in the assessment period, in chronological order of the tax document, according to
  criteria established in the regulations.

        § 3 The amounts of the IBS and the CBS collected through the simplified procedure referred to in this article shall be used for payment, in chronological
  order of the tax document: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       I - of unextinguished debts of the taxpayer arising from transactions occurring in the assessment period in which the acquirer is not a taxpayer of the IBS and
  the CBS under the regular regime; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - of other unextinguished debts of the taxpayer, at the end of the assessment period, if amounts not used under the terms of item I of § 3
  of this article remain. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 4 The IBS Management Committee and the RFB shall:
         I - calculate the balance of the IBS and CBS debits of the transactions referred to in the caput of this article, after deduction of the portions already extinguished by
  any of the methods provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law, in the assessment period; and
         II - transfer to the supplier, within 3 (three) business days counted from the conclusion of the assessment, the amounts received that exceed the amount referred to in
  item I of this paragraph.

        § 4 The IBS Management Committee (CGIBS) and the RFB shall transfer to the supplier, within 3 (three) business days counted from the conclusion of the assessment, the amounts of the IBS
  and the CBS collected through the simplified procedure in the assessment period and not used under the terms of § 3 of this article. (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 5 The option referred to in the caput of this article shall be irrevocable for the entire assessment period.   (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 5 (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 6 A joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB may determine the use of the simplified procedure referred to in this article for the transactions
  referred to in the caput, while the standard procedure described in art. 32 is not operating at an adequate level for the main electronic
  payment instruments used in those transactions.

        § 6 A joint act of the CGIBS and the RFB may determine the use of the simplified procedure referred to in this article for transactions in which the
  acquirer is not a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime, while the standard procedure described in art. 32 is not operating at an adequate
  level for the main electronic payment instruments used in those transactions. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7 Collection of the IBS and the CBS through the simplified procedure referred to in this article:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - ensures the extinction of the taxpayer's debts exclusively under the terms of § 3 of this article; and     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - does not give rise to any right, for the acquirer that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime, to appropriate credit for the amount segregated and
  collected.         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 34. The following rules must also be observed for split payment:

        I - the segregation and collection of the IBS and the CBS shall occur on the date of financial settlement of the payment transaction, subject to the payment flows
  established between the participants in the arrangement;

        II - in transactions with goods or services with payment made in installments by the supplier, the segregation and collection of the IBS and the CBS shall be
  carried out, proportionally, at the financial settlement of all installments;

        III - the early settlement of receivables does not alter the obligation to segregate and collect the IBS and the CBS in the manner of items I and II of this caput;

      IV - the provisions of this Subsection do not remove the liability of the taxpayer for payment of any balance payable of the IBS and the CBS, observing the
  moment of occurrence of the taxable event and the due date of the taxes; and

        V - the providers of payment services and the institutions operating payment systems:

        a) shall be liable for segregating and collecting the amounts of the IBS and the CBS in accordance with the provisions of this Subsection; and

       a) shall be liable for segregating and collecting the amounts of the IBS and the CBS in accordance with the provisions of this Subsection; and                    (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) shall not be tax liable for the IBS and the CBS levied on transactions with goods and services whose payments they settle.

        Art. 35. The Executive Branch of the Union and the IBS Management Committee shall approve a budget for the development, implementation, operation and maintenance of the
  split payment system.  Effects to take place [Produção de efeitos]

        § 1 Split payment shall come into operation simultaneously, in transactions with acquirers that are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS under the
  regular regime, for the main electronic payment instruments used in those transactions.

        § 2 A joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB:

        I - shall establish the gradual implementation of split payment; and

        II - may provide for cases in which the adoption of split payment shall be optional.

        § 3 The main electronic payment instruments, for purposes of the provisions of § 1 of this article, are those predominantly used in the retail sector.


                                                                                      Subsection IV

                                                                          On Collection by the Acquirer

        Art. 36. The acquirer of goods or services that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime may pay the IBS and the CBS levied on the
  transaction if payment to the supplier is made using a payment instrument that does not permit segregation and collection under the
  terms of arts. 32 and 33 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The option referred to in the caput of this article shall be exercised exclusively through collection, by the acquirer, of the IBS and the CBS levied on the
  transaction.

           § 2 (VETOED).

           § 3 The amount collected in the manner of this article:

           I - shall be used exclusively for payment of the amounts of unextinguished debits of the IBS and the CBS relating to the respective transactions; and

           II - when in excess of the amount used under the terms of item I of this paragraph, shall be transferred to the taxpayer within 3 (three) business days.

           § 4 The IBS Management Committee and the RFB shall establish a mechanism for monitoring, by the supplier, of collection by the acquirer.

                                                                                       Subsection V

                                                                           On Payment by the Liable Party

          Art. 37. The provisions of art. 29 of this Complementary Law apply, as applicable, to payment of the IBS and the CBS by the party to which this Complementary Law
  assigns the status of liable party.

                                                                                        Section IX

                                                                          On Undue or Excess Payment

           Art. 38. In the case of undue or excess payment, refund of the IBS and the CBS shall be due to the taxpayer only in the case in which:

           I - the transaction has not generated a credit for the acquirer of the goods or services; and

           II - the provisions of art. 166 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 (National Tax Code), have been observed.

                                                                                         Section X

                                                                                   On Reimbursement

         Art. 39. The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS that assesses a recoverable balance under the terms of art. 45 at the end of the assessment period may request its
  reimbursement, in full or in part.

        § 1 If the reimbursement is not requested or the request is partial, the remaining amount of the recoverable balance shall constitute a credit of the taxpayer, which
  may be used for offsetting or reimbursed in subsequent periods.

           § 2 The reimbursement request referred to in this article shall be assessed by the IBS Management Committee, in relation to the IBS, and by the RFB, in relation to the CBS.

           § 3 The time period for assessment of the reimbursement request shall be:

        I - up to 30 (thirty) days counted from the date of the request referred to in the caput of this article, for reimbursement requests from taxpayers enrolled in
  compliance programs developed by the IBS Management Committee and the RFB that meet the provisions of art. 40 of this Complementary Law;

        II - up to 60 (sixty) days counted from the date of the request referred to in the caput of this article, for reimbursement requests that meet the provisions of art. 40
  of this Complementary Law, except for the case provided for in item I of this paragraph; or

           III - up to 180 (one hundred eighty) days counted from the date of the request referred to in the caput of this article, in other cases.

        § 4 If there is no response from the IBS Management Committee or the RFB within the periods provided for in § 3 of this article, the credit shall be reimbursed to the taxpayer within the
  15 (fifteen) subsequent days.

           § 5 If an audit procedure relating to the reimbursement request is initiated before the end of the periods established in § 3 of this article,
  the following shall occur:

           I - the periods shall be suspended; and

           II - the approved credits shall be reimbursed within 15 (fifteen) days counted from the conclusion of the audit.

           § 6 The audit procedure referred to in § 5 of this article may not extend for more than 360 (three hundred sixty) days.

         § 7 If the audit procedure is not concluded within the period referred to in § 6 of this article, the credit shall be reimbursed to the taxpayer within the 15 (fifteen)
  subsequent days.

        § 8 Reimbursement made under the terms of this article does not preclude the possibility of a subsequent audit of the reimbursed credits, nor does it prejudice the conclusion
  of the procedure referred to in § 6 of this article.

         § 9 The amount of credit balances whose reimbursement has been requested under the terms of this article shall be adjusted, if payment occurs from the first
  day of the second month following the request, at the Selic rate accrued monthly from that date until the month prior to payment, plus 1% (one
  percent) in the month of payment.

           § 10. The periods referred to in § 3 shall be suspended, for up to 5 (five) years, with § 9 of this article not applying, if the taxpayer exercises the option:

           I - for Simples Nacional or for MEI, except in the case referred to in § 3 of art. 41 of this Complementary Law; or

           II - to not be a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS, in the cases authorized in this Complementary Law.

         § 11. In the event of non-compliance with the periods provided for in §§ 3 to 5 of this article, the amount of the credit balance shall be adjusted daily at the Selic rate from
  the first day of the start of the period for assessment of the request until the day before that of reimbursement.

           Art. 40. The reimbursement periods provided for in items I or II of § 3 of art. 39 of this Complementary Law shall apply to:

           I - the appropriated credits of the IBS and the CBS relating to the acquisition of goods and services incorporated into the taxpayer's fixed assets;


        II - reimbursement requests whose amount is equal to or less than 150% (one hundred fifty percent) of the average monthly value of the difference between:

        a) the credits of the IBS and the CBS appropriated by the taxpayer; and

        b) the debits of the IBS and the CBS levied on the taxpayer's transactions.

         § 1 The calculation of the average monthly value referred to in item II of the caput shall be carried out based on information relating to the 24 (twenty-four) months
  preceding the assessment period, excluding from the calculation the credits appropriated under the terms of item I of the caput of this article.

        § 2 The regulations shall govern the manner of application of the provisions of this article, including as to:

       I - the use of estimates for the amounts referred to in items "a" and "b" of item II of the caput of this article, during the initial years of collection of the IBS and
  the CBS, while the information referred to in those items is not available;

        II - the possibility of adjustment in the calculation referred to in item II of the caput of this article, as a result of the increase in the IBS rate between 2029 and 2033.

        § 3 The value calculated under the terms of item II of the caput of this article may be adjusted, under the terms of the regulations, so as to take into account seasonal variations
  in the value of the taxpayer's transactions and acquisitions and variations arising from the expansion or establishment of an economic undertaking by the taxpayer.

         § 4 For purposes of the provisions of item I of the caput of this article, also considered as goods and services incorporated into fixed assets shall be those
  of the same nature that, as a result of applicable accounting standards, are recorded by public service concessionaires as a contract asset,
  intangible asset or financial asset.

                                                                                      Section XI

                                                                            On Assessment Regimes

         Art. 41. The regular regime of the IBS and the CBS comprises all rules of levy and assessment provided for in this Complementary Law, including those
  applicable to the differentiated regimes and to the specific regimes.

        § 1 A taxpayer that does not exercise the option for Simples Nacional or for MEI, referred to in Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006, is subject to the regular
  regime of the IBS and the CBS referred to in this Complementary Law.

        § 2 Taxpayers opting for Simples Nacional or for MEI are subject to the rules of those regimes.

        § 3 Those opting for Simples Nacional may exercise the option to assess and collect the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime, in which case the IBS and the CBS
  shall be assessed and collected in accordance with the provisions of this Complementary Law.

        § 4 The option referred to in § 3 shall be exercised under the terms of Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006.

        § 5 A taxpayer under Simples Nacional, or a taxpayer that comes to opt for that regime, is prohibited from withdrawing from the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS
  if it has received reimbursement of credits of those taxes in the current or prior calendar year, under the terms of art. 39 of this Complementary Law.

        § 6 The provisions of § 5 of this article apply, in relation to the other cases in which an individual, legal entity or entity without legal personality
  exercises the optional election for taxpayer status subject to the regular regime, in the cases provided for in this Complementary Law.
        Art. 42. The assessment relating to the IBS and the CBS shall consolidate the operations carried out by all establishments of the taxpayer.

        § 1º Payment of the IBS and the CBS and the request for reimbursement shall be centralized in a single establishment.

        § 2º The assessment shall consolidate all debits and credits of the taxpayer under the regular regime, including those arising from the assessment of the differentiated
  and specific regimes, except in the cases expressly provided for in this Complementary Law.

        Art. 43. The assessment period for the IBS and the CBS shall be monthly.

        Art. 44. The regulation shall establish:

        I - the deadline for completion of the assessment; and

        II - the due date of the taxes.

        Art. 45. For each assessment period, the taxpayer shall assess, separately, the balance of the IBS and the CBS, which shall correspond to the difference between the
  values:

        I - of the IBS and CBS debits arising from taxable events occurring in the assessment period;

          II - of the credits appropriated in the same period, including presumed credits, plus the balance to be recovered from prior period or periods not
  used for offsetting or reimbursement.

        § 1º The taxpayer may make positive or negative adjustments to the balance assessed under the caput of this article, under the terms set forth in the regulation.

        § 2º Among the adjustments referred to in § 1º of this article is included the reversal of a credit appropriated in a prior assessment period, applying the increases referred to
  in §§ 2º to 4º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law from the date on which the improper appropriation of the credit occurred.

         § 3º From the balance assessed under the caput and § 1º of this article, the amounts extinguished by the modalities provided for in items III to V of the caput of
  art. 27 shall be deducted, resulting in:

        I - when positive, a balance payable that must be paid by the taxpayer; and

        II - when negative, a balance to be recovered that may be used for reimbursement or offsetting as provided for in this Complementary Law.

        § 4º The assessment carried out under the terms of this article implies a confession of debt by the taxpayer and constitutes the tax credit.

        § 5º The confession of debt referred to in § 4º is a suitable and sufficient instrument for demanding the amount of the IBS and the CBS levied on the operations therein
  recorded.

         § 6º The assessment referred to in this article must be carried out and delivered to the IBS Management Committee and to the RFB within the deadline for completion of the assessment, referred to
  in item I of the caput of art. 44 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 46. The IBS Management Committee and the RFB may, respectively, present to the taxable person an assisted assessment of the balance of the IBS and the CBS for the assessment
  period.

        § 1º The balance of the assessment referred to in the caput of this article shall be calculated under the terms of the caput of art. 45 of this Complementary Law and shall be based on:

        I - electronic tax documents;
        II - information relating to the extinction of IBS and CBS debits by any of the modalities provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law; and

        III - other information provided by the taxpayer or relating to the taxpayer.

       § 2º If the assisted assessment referred to in the caput of this article is presented, the assessment by the taxpayer referred to in art. 45 of this Complementary
  Law may only be carried out by means of adjustments to the assisted assessment.

         § 3º The assisted assessment carried out under the terms of this article, if the taxpayer confirms it or makes adjustments to it, implies a confession of debt and constitutes the
  tax credit.

        § 4º In the absence of a statement by the taxpayer on the assisted assessment within the deadline for completion of the assessment referred to in item I of the caput of art. 44
  of this Complementary Law, the assessed balance is presumed correct and the tax credit is deemed constituted.

        § 5º The confession of debt and the assisted assessment referred to, respectively, in §§ 3º and 4º of this article are suitable and sufficient instruments for
  demanding the amounts of the IBS and the CBS levied on the operations recorded therein.

         § 6º The balance resulting from the assessment referred to in this article shall constitute a balance payable or a balance to be recovered, as the case may be, applying the provisions of § 3º of
  art. 45 of this Complementary Law.

        § 7º The provisions of this article do not preclude the prerogative of an ex officio assessment of a tax credit relating to differences subsequently verified by the
  tax administration.

        § 8º The assisted assessment referred to in the caput of this article must be uniform and synchronized for the IBS and the CBS.

                                                                                     Section XII

                                                                              Of Non-Cumulativity

         Art. 47. A taxpayer subject to the regular regime may appropriate IBS and CBS credits when the extinction, by any of the modalities provided for
  in art. 27, occurs of the debits relating to the operations in which it is the acquirer, excluding exclusively those considered to be for personal use or consumption, under the terms of
  art. 57 of this Complementary Law, and the other cases provided for in this Complementary Law.

        § 1º The appropriation of the credits referred to in the caput of this article:

       I - shall be carried out separately for the IBS and for the CBS, it being prohibited, under any circumstances, to offset IBS credits against amounts owed of
  CBS and to offset CBS credits against amounts owed of IBS; and

        II - is conditioned on proof of the operation by means of a valid electronic tax document.

        § 2º The amounts of the IBS and CBS credits appropriated shall correspond to:

        I - the amounts of the debits, respectively, of the IBS and the CBS that have been indicated on the tax document of acquisition and extinguished by any of the
  modalities provided for in art. 27; or

        II - the amounts of presumed credit, in the cases provided for in this Complementary Law.

        § 3º The provisions of this article apply, including, to acquisitions of goods or services supplied by a party opting for the Simples Nacional.

        § 4º In operations in which the taxpayer is the acquirer of fuels taxed under the specific regime referred to in Chapter I of Title V of this Book, proof of extinction of the IBS and CBS debits is
  waived for the appropriation of credits.

        § 5º In the case referred to in § 4º, the credits shall be equivalent to the amounts of the IBS and the CBS recorded on a valid electronic tax document.

        § 6º The acquirer must reverse the appropriated credit if the acquired good is destroyed, deteriorates, or is the subject of robbery, theft, or misplacement.

          § 7º In the case of robbery or theft of a fixed asset, the reversal of credit referred to in § 6º of this article shall be made proportionally to the useful life period
  and to the depreciation rates defined in the regulation.

         § 8º In the return and cancellation of operations by an acquirer that is not a taxpayer under the regular regime, the supplier subject to the regular regime may appropriate
  credits based on the amounts of the debits levied on the returned or cancelled operation.

        § 8º In the return and cancellation of operations in which the acquirer is not a taxpayer under the regular regime, the supplier subject to the regular regime
  may appropriate credits or reverse debits based on the amounts of the debits levied on the returned or cancelled operation. (Wording given by Complementary Law
  No. 227 of 2026)

         § 9º In the case where payment of the IBS and the CBS is made through the Simples Nacional, when the option for the regular regime referred to in
  § 3º of art. 41 of this Complementary Law is not exercised:

        I - the appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the party opting for the Simples Nacional shall not be permitted; and

         II - the taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS shall be permitted to appropriate IBS and CBS credits corresponding to the amounts of those
  taxes paid on the acquisition of goods and services from a party opting for the Simples Nacional, in an amount equivalent to that owed under that regime.

         § 10. The carrying out of operations subject to a reduced rate shall not result in the reversal, in whole or in part, of the credits appropriated by the taxpayer in its
  acquisitions, except when expressly provided for in this Complementary Law.

        § 11. The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime may take credit for the amounts of the extinguished debits relating to supplies of goods and services not
  paid by an acquirer whose bankruptcy has been declared, under the terms of Law No. 11.101, of February 9, 2005, provided that:

        I - the acquisition of the good or service did not permit the appropriation of credits by the acquirer;

        II - the operation has been recorded in the taxpayer's accounting since the assessment period in which the taxable event of the IBS and the CBS occurred; and

        III - the payment of the creditors of the bankrupt acquirer has been definitively concluded.

        § 12. In cases of return and cancellation of operations in which the acquirer is a taxpayer under the regular regime, the regulation shall govern the
  procedures and requirements to be observed, which may consist of: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - for the acquirer, the establishment of a debit or reversal of credit; and     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - for the supplier, appropriation of credit or reversal of debit.       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 13. In the return and cancellation of operations whose IBS and CBS debit has been extinguished, in whole or in part, by reason of payment through the
  financial settlement carried out under the terms of arts. 31 to 34 of this Complementary Law (split payment), the regulation may provide for the total or partial transfer to the
  supplier of the amount paid, observing the following:     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
        I - the transfer must be carried out within a period of up to 3 (three) business days counted from the date of the reversal of the debit or from the date on which the
  appropriation of credit by the supplier would have been permitted; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the amount transferred may not be appropriated as credit by the supplier.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 48. The requirement of extinction of the debits for purposes of appropriation of the credits referred to in the caput of art. 47 of this Complementary Law shall be waived,
  exclusively, if none of the following modalities of extinction has been implemented:

        I - payment through the financial settlement of the operation (split payment), under the terms of arts. 31 and 32 of this Complementary Law; or

        II - payment by the acquirer, under the terms of art. 36 of this Complementary Law.

       Sole paragraph. In the case referred to in the caput of this article, the appropriation of the credits shall be conditioned on the correct amounts of the IBS and the
  CBS being indicated on the electronic tax document relating to the acquisition.

        Art. 49. Operations that are immune, exempt, or subject to a zero rate, deferral, or suspension shall not permit the appropriation of credits by the acquirers of the
  goods and services.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of the caput of this article do not prevent the appropriation of the presumed credits expressly provided for in this Complementary Law.

        Art. 50. In cases of suspension, if the suspended credit is demanded, the appropriation of the credits shall only be permitted at the time of the extinction
  of the debits by any of the modalities provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law, it being prohibited to appropriate credits with respect to statutory increases.

        Art. 51. Immunity and exemption shall result in the cancellation of the credits relating to prior operations.

         § 1º The cancellation of the credits referred to in the caput of this article shall be proportional to the value of the immune and exempt operations relative to the value of all
  operations of the supplier.

        § 2º The provisions of the caput and § 1º of this article do not apply to:

        I - exports; and

        II - operations referred to in items IV and VI of the caput of art. 9º of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 52. In the case of operations subject to a zero rate, the credits relating to prior operations shall be maintained.

        Art. 53. IBS and CBS credits appropriated in each assessment period may be used, in the following order, by means of:

         I - offsetting against the balance payable of the IBS and the CBS that is due, not extinguished, and not recorded as outstanding tax debt relating to prior assessment periods,
  including statutory increases; and

         II - offsetting against the IBS and CBS debits arising from taxable events of the same assessment period, observing the chronological order referred to
  in item I of the sole paragraph of art. 27 of this Complementary Law; and

       III - offsetting, respectively, against the IBS and CBS debits arising from taxable events of subsequent assessment periods, observing the
  chronological order referred to in item I of the sole paragraph of art. 27 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1º As an alternative to the provisions of item III, the taxpayer may request reimbursement, under the terms of Section X of this Chapter.

         § 2º IBS and CBS credits shall be appropriated and offset or reimbursed at their nominal value, monetary correction or adjustment being prohibited, without
  prejudice to the cases of interest increases relating to reimbursement expressly provided for in this Complementary Law.

         Art. 54. The right to use the credits shall be extinguished after a period of 5 (five) years, counted from the first day of the period following that of the assessment in
  which the appropriation of the credit occurred.

        Art. 55. The transfer, under any title, to another person or entity without legal personality, of IBS and CBS credits is prohibited.

        Sole paragraph. In the case of merger, spin-off, or incorporation, credits appropriated and not yet used may be transferred to the successor
  legal entity, the original date of appropriation of the credits being preserved for purposes of counting the period referred to in art. 54 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 56. The provisions of this Section apply to all cases of appropriation and use of IBS and CBS credits provided for in this Complementary Law.

                                                                                    Section XIII

                                                                  Of Goods and Services for Personal Use or Consumption

        Art. 57. The following are considered to be for personal use or consumption:

        I - the following goods and services:

        a) jewelry, precious stones and metals;

        b) works of art and antiques of historical or archaeological value;

        c) alcoholic beverages;

        d) tobacco products;

        e) weapons and ammunition;

        f) recreational, sports, and aesthetic goods and services;

        g) goods and services related to the acquisition or maintenance of the goods referred to in this item;        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - goods and services acquired or produced by the taxpayer and supplied free of charge or at a value below market value to:

       II - goods and services acquired by the taxpayer and supplied free of charge or at a value below market value to:           (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) the taxpayer itself, when it is a natural person;

        b) natural persons who are partners, shareholders, officers, and members of boards of administration and audit and of advisory committees of the
  board of administration of the taxpayer provided for by law;

        c) the employees of the taxpayers referred to in items "a" and "b" of this item; and
        c) the employees of the taxpayer; and       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        d) spouses, partners, or relatives, by blood or affinity, up to the third degree, of the natural persons referred to in items "a", "b", and "c" of this item.

        § 1º For purposes of item II of the caput of this article, goods and services for personal use or consumption include, among others:

        I - residential real property and other goods and services related to its acquisition and maintenance; and

        II - a vehicle and other goods and services related to its acquisition and maintenance, including insurance and fuel.

        § 2º In the case of a company whose main activity is the management of assets of the natural persons referred to in item II of the caput of this article and of the
  financial assets of such natural persons (family office), the goods and services related to such management shall be considered to be for personal use and consumption.

       § 3º Goods and services predominantly used in the economic activity of the taxpayer shall not be considered goods and services for personal use or consumption, in accordance
  with the following criteria:

       I - the goods provided for in items "a" to "d" of item I of the caput of this article that are marketed or used for the manufacture of goods to be
  marketed;

        II - the goods provided for in item "e" of item I of the caput of this article that meet the provisions of item I of this paragraph or are used by
  security companies;

        III - the goods provided for in item "f" of item I of the caput of this article that meet the provisions of item I of this paragraph or are used exclusively at a
  physical establishment by its customers;

        IV - the goods and services provided for in item II of the caput of this article that consist of:

        a) uniforms and work clothing;

        b) personal protective equipment;

         c) food and non-alcoholic beverages made available at the taxpayer's establishment to its employees and officers during the workday;

        d) health services made available at the taxpayer's establishment to its employees and officers during the workday;

        e) daycare services made available at the taxpayer's establishment to its employees and officers during the workday;

        f) health care plan services and the provision of transportation vouchers, meal vouchers, and food vouchers intended for employees and their
  dependents pursuant to a collective bargaining agreement or convention, the credits on the acquisition of these services being equivalent to the respective debits of the
  supplier assessed and extinguished in accordance with the provisions of the specific regimes for health care plans and financial services;

        f) health care plan services intended for employees and their dependents pursuant to a collective bargaining agreement or convention,
  the credits on the acquisition of these services being equivalent to the respective debits of the supplier assessed and extinguished in accordance with the provisions of the specific
  regime for health care plans; (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        g) educational benefits to its employees and dependents pursuant to a collective bargaining agreement or convention, including through the granting of
  scholarships or discounts on tuition, provided that these benefits are offered to all employees, differentiation in favor of
  lower-income employees or those with larger households being authorized; and

        h) provision of transportation vouchers, meal vouchers, and food vouchers, the credits on the acquisition of these services being equivalent to the respective debits
  of the supplier assessed and extinguished in accordance with the provisions of the specific regime for financial services, observing the rules applicable to payment
  arrangements; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        V - other goods and services that meet criteria established in the regulation.

        § 4º Goods and services not related to the pursuit of economic activity by a natural person characterized as a taxpayer of the
  regular regime shall be considered to be for personal use or consumption. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 4º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 5º With respect to goods and services for personal use or consumption referred to in this article, the appropriation of credits is prohibited.

        § 6º If credits have been appropriated on the acquisition of goods or services for personal use or consumption, debits shall be required in amounts
  equivalent to those of the credits, with the statutory increases referred to in § 2º of art. 29, calculated from the date of appropriation. (Repealed by Complementary Law
  No. 227 of 2026)

        § 6º (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 7º In the case of the supply of a good of the taxpayer for temporary use by the natural persons referred to in item II of the caput of this article, debits shall be
  required in amounts equivalent to those of the credits, calculated proportionally to the useful life period of the good in relation to the time used by the
  taxpayer, with the statutory increases referred to in § 2º of art. 29, as set forth in the regulation. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7º (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8º The regulation shall provide for the manner of identifying the natural person recipient of the goods and services referred to in this article.

         § 9º In the case of disposal of a good that did not permit the appropriation of credit when it was acquired, under the terms of § 5º of this article, the
  taxpayer may exclude from the tax base the acquisition value of the good, up to the limit of the disposal value, provided that unambiguous identification
  of the good is possible. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                  CHAPTER III

                                                                OF THE OPERATIONALIZATION OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

                                                                                    Section I

                                                                              General Provisions

         Art. 58. The IBS Management Committee and the RFB shall act jointly to implement integrated solutions for the administration of the IBS and the CBS, without
  prejudice to their respective legal competencies. Effects to take place

         § 1º The taxpayer shall access information on the assessment and payment of the IBS and the CBS on a unified electronic platform, with shared management
  between the IBS Management Committee and the RFB.


        § 2º The unified electronic platform referred to in § 1º of this article shall make available a taxpayer service channel for resolving problems
  relating to the operation of assessment and payment of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 3º Without prejudice to the provisions of §§ 1º and 2º of this article, the IBS Management Committee and the RFB may maintain their own systems for administration of the IBS
  and the CBS.

       § 4º The taxpayer is guaranteed free access to the systemic integration mechanisms for sending and receiving minimum data and transactions
  intended for the assessment and compliance with ancillary obligations relating to the IBS and the CBS, made available, respectively, by the CGIBS and by the
  RFB. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 5º The CGIBS and the RFB may provide, upon reimbursement of costs, automated transactions that go beyond the minimum necessary for
  assessment and compliance with ancillary obligations, as defined in the regulation. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                      Section II

                                                                       Of the Registry with Unique Identification

          Art. 59. Natural and legal persons and entities without legal personality subject to the IBS and the CBS are required to register in a registry with
  unique identification, observing the provisions of items "a" and "b" of item I of § 3º of art. 11 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1º For purposes of the caput of this article, the following registries administered by the RFB shall be considered:

        I - for natural persons, the Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas (CPF - Individual Taxpayer Registry);

        II - for legal persons and entities without legal personality, the Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica (CNPJ - National Registry of Legal Entities); and

        III - for rural and urban real property, the Cadastro Imobiliário Brasileiro (CIB - Brazilian Real Property Registry).

        § 2º Registry information shall have mandatory and timely integration, synchronization, cooperation, and sharing in a national data environment among
  the federal, state, Federal District, and municipal tax administrations.

        § 3º The national environment for sharing and integrating registry information shall have shared management through the Comitê para Gestão da Rede
  Nacional para Simplificação do Registro e da Legalização de Empresas e Negócios (CGSIM) referred to in item III of the caput of art. 2º of Complementary Law No. 123,
  of December 14, 2006.

        § 4º The federal, state, Federal District, and municipal tax administrations may process supplementary data and specific attributes for the tax management of the
  IBS and the CBS, observing the provisions of § 2º of this article.

         § 5º The Domicílio Tributário Eletrônico (DTE - Electronic Tax Domicile) provided for in art. 332 of this Complementary Law shall be unified and mandatory for all
  entities and other legal persons subject to registration with the CNPJ.

        § 5º The Domicílio Tributário Eletrônico (DTE) provided for in art. 332 of this Complementary Law shall be unified, within the scope of the IBS, and mandatory for all
  entities and other legal persons subject to registration with the CNPJ. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                      Section III

                                                                          Of the Electronic Tax Document

          Art. 60. The taxable person of the IBS and the CBS, when carrying out operations with goods or services, including exports and imports, must issue an electronic tax
  document.

       § 1º The information provided by the taxable person under the terms of this article has a declaratory nature and constitutes a confession of the amount owed of IBS and
  CBS recorded in the tax document.

        § 2º The obligation to issue electronic tax documents applies including to:

        I - operations that are immune, exempt, or covered by a zero rate or suspension;

        II - the transfer of goods between establishments belonging to the same taxpayer; and

        III - other cases provided for in the regulation.

       § 3º For purposes of the assessment of the IBS and the CBS, the IBS Management Committee and the tax administrations responsible for authorizing or receiving
  electronic tax documents shall observe the form, content, and deadlines provided for in a joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB. Effects to take place

      § 4º Electronic tax documents relating to operations with goods or services must be shared with all federative entities at the
  time of authorization or receipt, using uniform technical standards.

        § 5º The regulation may require the taxable person to submit supplementary information necessary for the assessment of the IBS and the CBS.

       § 6º A valid tax document is considered to be the record of information that meets the requirements established in the regulation, observing the provisions of this Complementary
  Law.

        § 7º For purposes of simplification, the joint act referred to in § 3º of this article must permit the issuance of consolidated tax documents.         (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                      Section IV

                                                                 Of Programs to Encourage Fiscal Citizenship

        Art. 61. The IBS Management Committee and the RFB may establish programs to encourage fiscal citizenship by means of encouraging consumers to demand the
  issuance of tax documents.

        § 1º The programs referred to in the caput of this article may be financed by an amount equivalent to up to 0.05% (five hundredths of one percent) of the
  IBS and CBS revenue collection.

          § 2º The regulation may provide for cases in which the information submitted under the terms of item I of § 1º of art. 32 of this Complementary Law may
  be used to identify the acquirer who is not a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS in the respective electronic tax documents, the acquirer's option
  for another form of identification being guaranteed.

                                                                                      Section V

                                                                              Transitional Provisions

        Art. 62. The Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities are required to:       Effects to take place
        I - adapt the current authorizing systems and applications for simplified issuance of electronic tax documents for use of a standardized layout,
  that allows taxpayers to provide the data relating to the IBS and the CBS necessary for the assessment of these taxes; and

        II - share the electronic tax documents, after receipt, validation, and authorization, with the national common-use environment of the IBS Management
  Committee and the tax administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities.

        § 1º For purposes of the caput of this article, the Municipalities and the Federal District are required, as of January 1, 2026, to:

        I - authorize their taxpayers to issue the national-standard Nota Fiscal de Serviços Eletrônica (NFS-e) in the national environment or, in the case of
  having their own issuing system, share the electronic tax documents generated, in accordance with a standardized layout, with the national data environment of the NFS-e; and

        II - share the content of other forms of electronic declaration, in accordance with a standardized layout defined in the regulation, with the national data
  environment of the NFS-e.

        § 2º The provisions of § 1º of this article apply until December 31, 2032.

        § 3º The data of the national centralizing environment of the NFS-e must be immediately shared in the national environment under the terms of item II of § 1º
  of this article.

        § 4º The standard and layout referred to in items I and II of § 1º of this article are those defined in an agreement entered into between the tax administration of the
  Union, the Federal District, and the Municipalities that established the NFS-e, developed and managed by the Comitê Gestor da Nota Fiscal de Serviços Eletrônica de padrão
  nacional (CGNFS-e - National Standard Electronic Service Invoice Management Committee).

          § 5º The national data environment of the NFS-e is the repository that ensures the integrity and availability of the information contained in the shared
  tax documents.

         § 6º The IBS Management Committee and the RFB may define alternative solutions to the NFS-e platform, subject to adoption of the national standard NFS-e layout
  for purposes of sharing in the national environment.

        § 7º Failure to comply with the provisions of the caput of this article shall result in the temporary suspension of voluntary transfers.

                                                                                   CHAPTER IV

                                                                    OF THE IBS AND THE CBS ON IMPORTS

                                                                                      Section I

                                                                            Of the Taxable Event

         Art. 63. The IBS and the CBS shall be levied on the import of goods or services from abroad carried out by a natural or legal person or entity without legal
  personality, even if not registered or required to register under the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, for whatever purpose.

        Sole paragraph. Except as specifically provided for in this Chapter, the rules relating to onerous operations referred to in Chapter II of this Title shall apply to the
  import referred to in the caput of this article.

                                                                                      Section II

                                                                 Of the Import of Intangible Goods and Services

         Art. 64. For purposes of art. 63 of this Complementary Law, an import of a service or of an intangible good, including rights, is considered to be the supply
  made by a party resident or domiciled abroad whose consumption occurs in the Country, even if the supply is made abroad.

        § 1º Consumption of intangible goods and services is considered to be use, exploitation, enjoyment, fruition, or access.

       § 1º Consumption in the Country of a service or of an intangible good, including rights, is considered to be the supply made by a party resident or domiciled abroad:
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - whose place of the operation is in the Country, under the terms of items II to IX of the caput of art. 11 of this Complementary Law; or         (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

        II - in which the acquirer or the recipient is resident or domiciled in the Country, in the other cases.         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2º The provision by a party resident or domiciled abroad is also considered to be an import of a service:

        I - carried out in the Country;

        II - related to real or personal property located in the Country; or

        III - related to personal property that is sent abroad for the provision of the service and returns to the Country after its completion.

        § 3º In the case of consumption of services or intangible goods, including rights, occurring concurrently in national territory and abroad, only the
  portion whose consumption occurs in the Country shall be considered an import.

       § 4º Intangible goods, including rights, and services whose value is included in the customs value of imported material goods under the terms of art. 69 of this
  Complementary Law shall be subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS in accordance with Section III of this Chapter.

        § 5º In the import of intangible goods or of services referred to in the caput of this article:

        I - the taxable event of the IBS and the CBS shall be deemed to have occurred:

        a) at the time defined in accordance with the provisions of art. 10 of this Complementary Law;

        b) at the place defined in accordance with the provisions of art. 11 of this Complementary Law;      (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) (repealed);    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the tax base is the value of the operation under the terms of art. 12 of this Complementary Law;

         III - the rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on each import of an intangible good or of a service are the same as those levied on the supply of the same intangible
  good or service in the Country, observing the specific provisions relating to the setting of rates on imports of intangible goods or of services subject to
  specific regimes of taxation;

        IV - for purposes of determining the state, Federal District, and municipal rates of the IBS, the place of the import is the destination of the operation defined under the terms of art. 11
  of this Complementary Law;


       IV - for purposes of determining the state, Federal District, and municipal rates of the IBS, the import is considered to have occurred in the place:       (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) of the operation defined under the terms of items II to IX of the caput of art. 11 of this Complementary Law; or      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) of the principal domicile of the acquirer or of the recipient, in the other cases;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         V - the acquirer is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS on acquisitions of intangible goods, including rights, and services from a supplier resident or domiciled
  abroad;

         VI - if the acquirer is resident or domiciled abroad, the recipient is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS on acquisitions of intangible goods, including
  rights, and services from a supplier resident or domiciled abroad;

        VII - the acquirer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS may appropriate and use credit as provided for in arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law;

         VIII - the supplier resident or domiciled abroad is jointly and severally liable, together with the taxpayer, for payment of the IBS and the CBS, observing the provisions
  of arts. 21 and 23 of this Complementary Law;

        IX - digital platforms, even if resident and domiciled abroad, shall be liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS on imports carried out
  through them, observing the provisions of arts. 22 and 23 of this Complementary Law.

        § 6º The specific rules provided for in Title V of this Book shall also apply to imports of goods and services that are the subject of specific regimes.

       § 7º Occasional consumption by a non-resident natural person temporarily present in the Country shall not be considered an import of a service or of an intangible
  good, including rights, under the terms of the regulation. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7º (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                     Section III

                                                                       Of the Import of Material Goods

                                                                                   Subsection I

                                                                                 Of the Taxable Event

        Art. 65. For purposes of art. 63 of this Complementary Law, the taxable event of the import of material goods is the entry of goods of foreign
  origin into national territory.

         Sole paragraph. For purposes of the caput of this article, goods that are recorded as having been imported and whose misplacement comes to be verified by the
  customs authority shall be presumed to have entered national territory, except with respect to baggage and international postal shipments.

        Art. 66. The following material goods do not constitute taxable events of the IBS and the CBS on imports:

        I - those that return to the Country in the following cases:

        a) sent on consignment and not sold within the authorized period;

        b) returned due to technical defect, for repair, or for replacement;

        c) due to changes in the import system by the importing country;

        d) due to war or public calamity; or

        e) due to other factors beyond the exporter's control;

        II - those that, correctly described in the transport documents, arrive in the Country due to unmistakable or proven shipping error and that are redirected
  or returned abroad;

         III - those that are identical, in equal quantity and value, and intended to replace others previously imported that have proven, after their
  release by the customs authority, to be defective or unfit for the purpose for which they were intended, under the terms of the regulation;

        IV - those that have been subject to a penalty of forfeiture prior to their release by the customs authority;

        V - those that have been returned abroad prior to registration of the import declaration;

        VI - those considered to be fish caught outside the territorial waters of the Country by a company located in its territory, provided that the
  requirements governing fishing activity are met;

        VII - those to which the temporary export regime has been applied;

        VIII - those that are in customs transit, accidentally destroyed; and

        IX - those that have been destroyed under customs control, at no cost to the public authorities, prior to their release by the customs authority.

                                                                                   Subsection II

                                                                           Of the Moment of Assessment

        Art. 67. For purposes of calculating the IBS and the CBS, the taxable event of the IBS and the CBS on the import of material goods is deemed to have occurred:

        I - upon release of goods submitted to clearance for consumption;

        II - upon release of goods submitted to the special customs regime of temporary admission for economic use;

        III - upon assessment of the corresponding tax credit, in the case of:

        a) goods included in the concept of baggage, accompanied or unaccompanied;

        b) goods listed in a manifest or in other declarations of equivalent effect, whose misplacement has been verified by the customs authority; or

        c) imported goods that have not been the subject of an import declaration.

        § 1º For purposes of item I of the caput of this article, clearance for consumption on import means the customs clearance to which goods
  imported on a definitive basis are submitted.
        § 2º The provisions of item I of the caput of this article apply, including, in the case of clearance for consumption of goods under a suspensive taxation regime and of
  goods contained in an international shipment or carried by a traveler, subject to the ordinary taxation regime.

                                                                                   Subsection III

                                                                  Of the Place of Import of Material Goods

        Art. 68. For purposes of the IBS and the CBS levied on imports of material goods, the place of import of material goods corresponds to:

        I - the place of delivery of the goods to the final recipient, under the terms of art. 11 of this Complementary Law, including in an international shipment;

        II - the principal domicile of the acquirer of bonded goods; or

        III - the place where the misplacement was characterized.

                                                                                   Subsection IV

                                                                                Of the Tax Base

        Art. 69. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS on the import of material goods is the customs value plus:

        I - the Import Tax;

        II - the Selective Tax (IS);

        III - the fee for use of the Sistema Integrado do Comércio Exterior (Siscomex - Integrated Foreign Trade System);

        IV - the Adicional ao Frete para a Renovação da Marinha Mercante (AFRMM - Merchant Marine Renewal Freight Surcharge);

        V - the Contribuição de Intervenção no Domínio Econômico levied on the import and marketing of petroleum and its derivatives, natural gas and its
  derivatives, and combustible ethyl alcohol (Cide-Combustíveis);

        VI - antidumping duties;

        VII - countervailing duties;

        VIII - safeguard measures; and

        IX - any other taxes, fees, contributions, or duties levied on the imported goods up to their release.

         § 1º The tax base of the IBS and the CBS in the case referred to in § 2º of art. 71 of this Complementary Law shall be the value that serves or would serve as the basis for
  calculating the Import Tax plus the amounts referred to in the caput, except as provided for in § 2º of this article.
