        § 2º The following shall not form part of the tax base of the IBS and the CBS:

        I - the Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI - Tax on Industrialized Products), provided for in item IV of the caput of art. 153 of the Federal Constitution;

      II - the Imposto sobre operações relativas à Circulação de Mercadorias e sobre prestações de Serviços de Transporte Interestadual e Intermunicipal e de
  Comunicação (ICMS - Tax on the Circulation of Goods and on Interstate and Intermunicipal Transportation and Communication Services), provided for in item II of the caput of art. 155 of the Federal Constitution; and

        III - the Imposto sobre Serviços de Qualquer Natureza (ISS - municipal service tax), provided for in item III of the caput of art. 156 of the Federal Constitution.

       Art. 70. For purposes of assessing the tax base, amounts expressed in foreign currency must be converted into national currency at the exchange
  rate used for calculating the Import Tax, without any subsequent adjustment arising from any exchange rate variation.

         Sole paragraph. In the case where the Import Tax is not owed, the exchange rate that would be used should taxation apply
  shall be used.

                                                                                   Subsection V

                                                                                    Of the Rate

         Art. 71. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on each import of a material good are the same as those levied on the acquisition of the respective good in the
  Country, observing the specific provisions relating to the setting of rates on imports of goods subject to specific regimes of taxation.

        Art. 71. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on each import of a material good are the same as those levied on the acquisition of the respective good
  in the Country, observing the specific provisions relating to the setting of rates on imports of goods subject to specific regimes of taxation and
  except as provided for in § 6º of art. 126 of this Complementary Law. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1º For purposes of determining the state, Federal District, and municipal rates of the IBS, the destination of the operation is the place of import, defined under the terms of art.
  68 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º Where it is not possible to identify the material good imported, due to its misplacement or consumption, and to a generic description in the
  commercial and transport documents available, the standard rates of the destination of the operation shall be applied for purposes of determining the IBS and the CBS
  levied on the import.

                                                                                   Subsection VI

                                                                                Of Tax Liability

        Art. 72. The following is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS on the import of material goods:

        I - the importer, considered as such any person or entity without legal personality that causes the entry of material goods of foreign
  origin into national territory; and

        II - the acquirer of bonded goods.

        Sole paragraph. In an import on account and order of a third party, the person that causes the entry of material goods of foreign origin into national territory is the
  acquirer of the goods abroad.

        Art. 73. The following is liable for the IBS and the CBS on the import of material goods, in substitution for the taxpayer:

        I - the carrier, with respect to goods of foreign origin, or under customs control, that it transports, when misplacement is found up to the completion of the
  unloading of the goods at the customs-bonded place or facility;


        II - the depositary, with respect to goods of foreign origin that are under customs control and under its custody, when misplacement is found
  after completion of the unloading at the customs-bonded place or facility;

        III - the beneficiary of a special customs regime who has not caused the entry of foreign goods into national territory; and

        IV - the beneficiary who causes non-compliance with the application of a suspensive customs regime intended for processing for export, in the case of
  admission of goods into the regime by another beneficiary, with its consent, with a view to carrying out a stage of the industrial chain of the product to be exported.

         Sole paragraph. In the cases of items I and II of the caput of this article, liability shall be excluded in cases of fortuitous event or force majeure.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 74. The following is jointly and severally liable for the IBS and the CBS on the import of material goods:

        I - the person that registers, in its own name, the import declaration of goods of foreign origin acquired abroad by another person;

        II - the predetermined orderer that acquires goods of foreign origin from an importing legal entity;

        III - the representative, in the Country, of the foreign carrier;

        IV - the shipper, the multimodal transport operator, or any subcontractor for carrying out the multimodal transport; and

       V - the recipient of the service or the party contracting the charter of a vessel or aircraft, under an international contract, with respect to goods admitted under a
  special customs regime by a third party.

        Art. 75. The taxable persons referred to in arts. 72 to 74 of this Complementary Law must register for compliance with the obligations relating to the IBS
  and the CBS on imports, under the terms of the regulation.

                                                                                  Subsection VII

                                                                                 Of Payment

        Art. 76. The IBS and the CBS owed on the import of material goods must be paid by the time of delivery of the goods submitted to clearance for consumption, even if
  this occurs before release of the goods by the customs authority.

        § 1º The taxable person may opt to anticipate payment of the IBS and the CBS to the time of registration of the import declaration.

         § 2º Any difference in taxes generated by the anticipation of payment shall be charged to the taxable person on the date of occurrence of the taxable event for purposes
  of calculating the IBS and the CBS, without the levy of late-payment increases.

         § 3º The regulation may establish cases in which payment of the IBS and the CBS may occur at a time later than that defined in the caput of this
  article, for taxable persons certified under the Programa Brasileiro de Operador Econômico Autorizado (Programa OEA - Brazilian Authorized Economic Operator Program) established under
  specific legislation.

         § 3º The regulation may establish cases in which payment of the IBS and the CBS may occur at a time later than that defined in the caput of this
  article, for taxable persons certified under the Programa Brasileiro de Operador Econômico Autorizado (Programa OEA) established under specific
  legislation and for goods of international shipments to which the Regime de Tributação Simplificada (RTS - Simplified Taxation Regime) has been applied.            (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 4º Payment of the IBS and the CBS is a condition for delivery of the goods, observing the provisions of § 3º of this article.

        § 5º The IBS and the CBS owed on import shall be extinguished exclusively by payment by the taxable person.

        Art. 77. Percentage differences in bulk goods that, due to their nature or handling conditions, are subject to breakage, decrease, or increase,
  assessed by the customs authority, shall not be considered for purposes of demanding the IBS and the CBS, up to the percentage limit to be defined in the regulation, which
  may be differentiated by type of good.

                                                                                  Subsection VIII

                                                                            Of Non-Cumulativity

        Art. 78. When subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, the taxpayers referred to in art. 72 and the acquirers of goods taxed under the regime
  of international shipments referred to in art. 95 may appropriate and use credits corresponding to the amounts of the IBS and the CBS actually paid on the import
  of material goods, observing the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                  CHAPTER V

                                                                   OF THE IBS AND THE CBS ON EXPORTS

                                                                                     Section I

                                                                              General Provisions

         Art. 79. Exports of goods and services abroad are immune from the IBS and the CBS, under the terms of art. 8º of this Complementary Law, the exporter being
  guaranteed the appropriation and use of the credits relating to the operations in which it is the acquirer of a good or a service, observing the prohibitions on crediting
  provided for in arts. 49 and 51, the other provisions of arts. 47 and 52 to 57 of this Complementary Law, and the provisions of this Chapter.

                                                                                     Section II

                                                               Of Exports of Intangible Goods and Services

         Art. 80. For purposes of art. 79 of this Complementary Law, an export of a service or of an intangible good, including rights, is considered to be the supply
  to a party resident or domiciled abroad and consumption abroad.

        § 1º The following are also considered to be exports:

        I - the provision of a service to a party resident or domiciled abroad related to:

        a) real property located abroad;

        b) personal property that enters the Country for the provision of the service and returns abroad after its completion, observing the period established in the regulation; and

        II - the provision of the following services, provided that they are directly and exclusively linked to the export of material goods or associated with the delivery abroad of
  material goods:



        II - the supply of the following goods and services, provided that they are directly and exclusively linked to the export of material goods or associated with the delivery
  abroad of material goods: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          a) intermediation in the distribution of goods abroad (agent's commission);

          b) cargo insurance;

          c) customs clearance;

          d) warehousing of goods;

          e) road, rail, air, waterway, or multimodal freight transport;

          f) cargo handling;

          g) container handling;

          h) unitization or deunitization of cargo;

          i) documentary consolidation or deconsolidation of cargo;

          j) freight forwarding of cargo;

          k) express shipments;

          l) weighing and measuring of cargo;

          m) refrigeration of cargo;

          n) operating lease or rental of containers;

          o) installation and assembly of exported goods; and

          p) training for the use of exported goods.

          § 1º-A. Consumption abroad of a service or of an intangible good, including rights, is considered to be the supply:     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

       I - whose place of the operation is not in the Country, under the terms of items II to IX of the caput of art. 11 of this Complementary Law; or                    (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          II - in which the acquirer and the recipient are resident or domiciled abroad, in the other cases.       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

       § 2º If it is not possible for the national supplier to identify the place of consumption from the conditions and characteristics of the supply, the place of the
  consumption shall be presumed to be the place of domicile of the acquirer abroad. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 2º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 3º If the consumption referred to in § 2º occurs in the Country, it shall be considered an import of a service or intangible good, including a right, observing the provisions of
  art. 64 of this Complementary Law. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 3º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 4º A person who does not carry out the export of the material goods referred to in item II of § 1º shall be required to pay the IBS and the CBS, plus interest and
  late-payment penalty, in accordance with § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, counted from the date of occurrence of the operation, in the capacity of a responsible party.

        § 5º In the case of the supply of services or of intangible goods, including rights, occurring concurrently in national territory and abroad, only the
  portion whose execution or consumption occurs abroad shall be considered an export.

         § 6º The provisions of § 1º of art. 64 of this Complementary Law apply for purposes of defining consumption abroad of services or of intangible goods, including
  rights. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 6º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 7º The specific rules provided for in Title V of this Book shall also apply to exports of goods and services that are the subject of specific regimes.

                                                                                       Section III

                                                                        Of Exports of Material Goods

        Art. 81. The immunity of the IBS and the CBS on the export of material goods referred to in art. 79 of this Complementary Law applies to exports without
  departure from national territory, in the manner governed by the regulation, when the exported goods are:

       I - fully incorporated into a good that is temporarily in the Country, owned by the foreign buyer, including under a regime of temporary
  admission under the responsibility of a third party;

         II - delivered to a body of the direct, autonomous agency, or foundation administration of the Union, the States, the Federal District, or the Municipalities, in fulfillment of
  a contract arising from an international bidding process;

          III - delivered in the Country to a body of the Ministry of Defense, to be incorporated into a product of interest to national defense under construction or manufacture in
  national territory, as a result of an international agreement;

          IV - delivered to a national company authorized to operate the duty-free shop regime;

        V - sold to a company based abroad, in the case of an aircraft manufactured in the Country and delivered to a regular air transport service provider
  based in national territory;

         VI - delivered in the Country to be incorporated into a vessel or platform under construction or conversion contracted by a company based abroad or into its
  modules, with subsequent allocation to the activities of exploration, development, and production of petroleum, natural gas, and other fluid hydrocarbons
  provided for in specific legislation; and

         VII - intended exclusively for the activities of exploration, development, and production of petroleum, natural gas, and other fluid hydrocarbons
  provided for in specific legislation, when sold to a company based abroad and as defined in specific legislation, even if carried out through a third party
  based in the Country.
        Art. 81-A. The export of material goods, including in cases where there is no physical departure from national territory as referred to in art. 81, shall be proven
  by means of registration by the competent body or documentation and procedures established in customs legislation, under the terms of the regulation. (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 1º After the period of 180 (one hundred eighty) days, counted from the issuance of the electronic tax document, without proof of the export, an
  onerous operation shall be deemed to have occurred and the CBS and the IBS levied on the operation shall be required from the exporter, with the applicable increases, including those relating to
  the operations referred to in item II of § 1º of art. 80. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2º The regulation may provide for cases extending the period provided for in § 1º of this article.          (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
        Art. 82. Payment of the IBS and the CBS may be suspended on the supply of material goods for the specific purpose of export to a trading
  export company that cumulatively meets the following requirements:

        I - be certified under the OEA Program (Authorized Economic Operator);

        II - hold net equity equal to or greater than the highest of the following amounts:

        a) R$ 1,000,000.00 (one million reais); and

        b) once the total value of the suspended taxes;

        III - opt for the DTE (Electronic Tax Domicile), in the manner set out in specific legislation;

        IV - maintain accounting records and present them in digital format; and

        V - be in a situation of tax compliance before the federal, state or municipal tax administrations of its domicile.

        § 1º For the purposes of this article's caput, the trading export company must be authorized by joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB (Federal Revenue of Brazil).

        § 2º For purposes of the suspension of payment of the IBS, the certification referred to in item I of this article's caput shall be conditioned on the consent of the
  state and municipal tax administrations of the company's domicile.

        § 3º Goods sent for export shipment or to bonded facilities, on behalf of and by order of the trading export company, without any other commercial or industrial operation occurring
  in that interval, are considered acquired for the specific purpose of export.

        § 4º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput converts into a zero rate after the actual export of the goods, provided that the
  time limit set out in item I of § 5º of this article is observed.

       § 5º The trading export company is responsible for payment of the IBS and the CBS that were suspended on the supply of goods to the trading
  export company, in the following cases:

        I - if 180 (one hundred and eighty) days have elapsed from the date of issuance of the invoice by the supplier and the export has not been completed;

        II - if the goods are redirected to the domestic market;

        III - if the goods are subjected to a manufacturing process; or

        IV - if destruction, loss, theft or robbery occurs before the actual export of the goods.

        § 6º For purposes of § 5º of this article, the IBS and the CBS are considered due at the moment the taxable event occurs, as defined in art.
  10 of this Complementary Law.

         § 7º In the cases of § 5º of this article, amounts paid voluntarily shall be subject to the incidence of penalty and default interest, as set out in § 2º
  of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

         § 8º The amount set in item II of this article's caput shall be updated by the Broad National Consumer Price Index (IPCA), at intervals of no less than
  12 (twelve) months, by joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB, which shall set the initial and final terms of the update.

        § 9º The regulation shall establish:

        I - the specific requirements for the authorization procedure referred to in § 1º of this article;

        II - the frequency for presenting the accounting records referred to in item IV of this article's caput;

        III - cases in which the goods may be sent to locations other than those set out in § 3º of this article, without this undermining the specific purpose
  of export; and

         IV - requirements and conditions for carrying out transshipment, ferrying, unloading or storage operations during the shipment referred to in § 3º
  of this article.

        § 10. The regulation may set an extended time limit for application of the provision in item I of § 5º of this article, based on the type of good.

       § 11. Payment of the IBS and the CBS is also suspended on the supply of fresh (in natura) agricultural and livestock products to a taxpayer under the regular regime that
  carries out manufacturing for export abroad:

        I - whose gross revenue from export abroad, in the 3 (three) calendar years immediately preceding the acquisition, was greater than
  50% (fifty percent) of its total gross revenue from the sale of goods and services in the same period, after excluding taxes levied on the sale; and

       I - whose gross revenue from export abroad, in the 3 (three) calendar years immediately preceding the acquisition, was greater than
  30% (thirty percent) of its total gross revenue from the sale of goods and services in the same period, after excluding taxes levied on the sale; and
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 235 of 2026)

        II - that complies with the provisions of items II to V of this article's caput.

       § 12. The acquirer referred to in § 11 is responsible for payment of the suspended IBS and CBS, with the additions set out in § 2º of art. 29 of this
  Complementary Law, if, within 180 (one hundred and eighty) days counted from the date of issuance of the invoice by the supplier:

        I - the fresh (in natura) agricultural product acquired with suspension is not used for manufacturing; or

        II - the manufactured product resulting from fresh (in natura) agricultural products acquired with suspension:

        a) is not exported abroad; or

        b) is not sold on the domestic market, with the corresponding taxation.


        § 13. The regulation may establish:

          I - criteria for classification under the provisions of this article for a taxpayer starting activities or that began its activities less than 3
  (three) years ago; and

        II - cases in which the time limit referred to in § 12 of this article may be extended.

        Art. 83. The authorization referred to in § 1º of art. 82 of this Complementary Law may be cancelled in the following cases:

        I - failure to meet the requirements set out in items I to V of the caput of art. 82 of this Complementary Law; or

        II - outstanding payment referred to in § 5º of art. 82 of this Complementary Law.

       § 1º Cancellation of the authorization shall be carried out by the tax authority of the RFB or of the state, district or municipal tax administration of the domicile of the
  trading export company.

       § 2º In the cases set out in the caput of this article, a cancellation proceeding for the authorization shall be opened, supported by a finding report, and the
  trading export company shall be notified to regularize its situation or file an objection within 30 (thirty) business days, counted from the date of notice of the notification.

       § 3º The notification referred to in § 2º of this article shall preferably be made electronically, by sending it to the electronic tax domicile of the
  trading export company.

        § 4º If the trading export company regularizes its situation by fulfilling all the requirements and conditions set out in the caput of art. 82, and
  provided there is no outstanding payment relating to the cases referred to in § 5º of art. 82 of this Complementary Law, the cancellation proceeding referred to in §
  2º of this article shall be extinguished.

        § 5º Default shall be deemed to occur, and the cancellation proceeding shall continue, if the trading export company does not regularize its situation in the
  manner of § 4º nor file the objection referred to in § 2º of this article.

        § 6º Once the objection referred to in § 2º of this article has been filed, the preparing authority shall have a period of 15 (fifteen) days to forward the proceeding for
  judgment.

        § 7º An appeal against the decision cancelling the authorization shall be admissible, to be filed within 20 (twenty) business days, counted from the date of notice of the decision, to the
  IBS Management Committee or to the RFB, according to the tax authority that carried out the cancellation of the authorization under § 1º of this article.

        § 8º The regulation may provide for additional procedural acts complementing the provisions of this article.

                                                                                   TITLE II

                OF SPECIAL CUSTOMS REGIMES AND OF THE REGIMES FOR BAGGAGE, INTERNATIONAL SHIPMENTS AND THE SUPPLY OF
                                        FUEL FOR AIRCRAFT IN INTERNATIONAL TRAFFIC

                                                                                  CHAPTER I

                                                                  OF SPECIAL CUSTOMS REGIMES

                                                                                    Section I

                                                                            Of the Transit Regime

        Art. 84. Payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on import is suspended while material goods are subject to the special customs
  regime of customs transit, in any of its forms, observing the discipline set out in customs legislation.

                                                                                    Section II

                                                                          Of the Warehousing Regimes

        Art. 85. Payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on import is suspended while material goods are subject to the special customs regime
  of warehousing, observing the discipline set out in customs legislation.

        Sole paragraph. The regulation shall specify the types of special customs warehousing regimes.

          Art. 86. The provision in the caput of art. 85 of this Complementary Law does not apply to goods admitted under the special customs regime of certified
  bonded warehousing.

        Sole paragraph. Goods admitted under the special customs regime of certified bonded warehousing are considered exported, under the terms of the regulation.

       Art. 87. Payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on import and on acquisition in the domestic market of material goods subject to the special
  customs regime of duty-free shops is suspended, observing the discipline set out in customs legislation.

        Sole paragraph. The regime provided for in the caput applies to the supply of material goods intended for use or on-board consumption, on aircraft
  exclusively in international traffic bound for abroad and delivered in a bonded primary zone or bonded organized port area.

                                                                                   Section III

                                                                 Of the Temporary Stay Regimes

        Art. 88. Payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on import is suspended while material goods are subject to the special customs regime
  of temporary stay in the Country or temporary departure from the Country, observing the discipline set out in customs legislation.

        Sole paragraph. The regulation shall specify the types of special customs regimes for temporary stay.

        Art. 89. In the case of goods temporarily admitted into the Country for economic use, the suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS shall be partial,
  and the IBS and the CBS must be paid proportionally to the length of stay of the goods in the Country.

         § 1º The proportionality referred to in the caput of this article shall be obtained by applying the percentage of 0.033% (thirty-three thousandths of one percent),
  for each day within the period for which the regime is granted, on the amount of the IBS and the CBS originally due.

        § 2º In the event of payment after the date on which it would be due, as set out in item II of the caput of art. 67 of this Complementary Law, the IBS and the CBS
  shall be adjusted by the Selic rate, calculated from that date, without prejudice to the other additions set out in the legislation.

        § 3º The provision in the caput of this article does not apply:

        I - until December 31, 2040:


        a) to goods intended for exploration, development and production activities of oil and natural gas, whose stay in the Country is of a
  temporary nature, listed in a schedule specified in the regulation; and

        b) to goods intended for the transport, handling, transfer, storage or regasification activities of liquefied natural gas,
  listed in a schedule specified in the regulation; and

        II - until the date established by art. 92-A of the Transitional Constitutional Provisions Act, to goods temporarily imported for
  economic use by companies that fall under the provisions of Decree-Law No. 288 of February 28, 1967, during the period of their stay in the Manaus
  Free Trade Zone, which shall be subject to the temporary admission regime with total suspension of payment of the taxes.

        § 4º In the event that the temporary import of aircraft is carried out by a taxpayer under the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS by means of a
  leasing agreement:

       § 4º In the event that the temporary import of aircraft, their components and engines, is carried out by a taxpayer under the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS
  by means of a leasing agreement: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - payment of the IBS and the CBS on the import of the aircraft shall be waived; and

        I - payment of the IBS and the CBS shall be waived; and         (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         II - the IBS and the CBS shall be levied on the payment of the leasing consideration in accordance with the specific regime for
  financial services on imports.

                                                                                    Section IV

                                                                      Of the Improvement Regimes

        Art. 90. Payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on import is suspended while material goods are subject to the special customs regime
  of improvement, observing the discipline set out in customs legislation.

        § 1º The regulation shall specify the types of special customs improvement regimes.

        § 2º The suspension referred to in the caput of this article may extend to material goods that are imported and to those acquired in the domestic market.

        § 3º The regulation shall establish the requirements and conditions for the admission of material goods and services under the special customs regime of drawback, in the
  suspension modality.

        § 4º Material goods subject to the special customs regime of drawback, in the suspension modality, that, in whole or in part:

        I - cease to be used or consumed in the production process of exported final goods, as established in the granting act; or

         II - are used in a manner not in accordance with the granting act, if intended for the domestic market, in the state in which they were imported or acquired or,
  further, incorporated into the aforementioned final goods,

  are subject to payment of the IBS and the CBS.

         § 5º In the case set out in § 4º, if the destination for the domestic market occurs more than 30 (thirty) days after the deadline set for export, the amounts of the
  taxes due shall be increased by penalty and default interest under § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

       § 6º For purposes of the provisions of this Section, the Special Customs Regime of Industrial Bonded Warehouse under Computerized Control (Recof) is considered a special
  customs improvement regime.

        Art. 91. The exemption and refund modalities of the special customs drawback regime do not apply to the IBS and the CBS.

       Art. 92. In the case of national or nationalized goods leaving the Country temporarily for a transformation, processing, finishing or
  assembly operation, or for a repair, maintenance or restoration process, the IBS and the CBS due upon the return of the goods to the Country shall be calculated:

         I - on the difference between the value of the IBS and the CBS levied on the product of the transformation, processing, finishing or assembly operation and the
  value of the IBS and the CBS that would be levied, on the same date, on the goods that left the country, if they were being imported from the same country in which the
  temporary export operation took place; or

        II - on the value of the goods and services used in the repair, maintenance or restoration process.

        Sole paragraph. The regulation may establish other manufacturing operations to which the provisions of the caput of this article apply.

                                                                                     Section V

                                              Of the Special Customs Regime Applicable to the Oil and Gas Sector (Repetro)

        Art. 93. Observing the discipline set out in customs legislation, payment of the IBS and the CBS is suspended in the following operations:

         I - import of goods intended for exploration, development and production activities of oil, natural gas and other fluid hydrocarbons
  provided for in specific legislation, whose stay in the Country is of a temporary nature, listed in a schedule specified in the regulation (Repetro-
  Temporário);

        II - import of goods intended for the transport, handling, transfer, storage or regasification activities of liquefied natural gas
  listed in a schedule specified in the regulation (GNL-Temporário);

        III - import of goods listed in a schedule specified in the regulation whose stay in the Country is definitive and that are intended for the activities referred to
  in item I of this caput (Repetro-Permanente);

        IV - import or acquisition in the domestic market of raw materials, intermediate products and packaging materials to be used entirely in the
  production process of a final product to be supplied to a company that allocates it to the activities referred to in item I of this caput (Repetro-Industrialização);

        V - acquisition of the final product referred to in item IV of this caput (Repetro-Nacional); and

         VI - import or acquisition in the domestic market of goods listed in a schedule specified in the regulation, for the conversion or construction of other goods in
  the Country, contracted by a company based abroad, whose final product must be intended for the activities referred to in item I of this caput (Repetro-Entreposto).

       § 1º The suspension provided for in item III of the caput of this article is prohibited for the import of vessels intended for cabotage navigation and for
  national-route inland navigation, as well as for port support navigation and maritime support navigation, under the terms of specific legislation.

        § 2º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in item III of the caput of this article converts into a zero rate after 5 (five) years have elapsed,
  counted from the date of registration of the import declaration.



         § 3º The beneficiary that carries out an import with suspension of payment under item III of the caput of this article and does not allocate the goods in the manner
  provided for therein within the period of 3 (three) years, counted from the date of registration of the import declaration, is obliged to pay the IBS and the CBS not paid as a result of the
  suspension enjoyed, plus penalty and default interest under § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, calculated from the date the
  respective taxable events occurred.

          § 4º Payment of the IBS and the CBS is also suspended on the import or acquisition of goods in the domestic market by a company called an intermediate
  manufacturer for the manufacturing of an intermediate product to be supplied to a company that uses it in the production process referred to in item IV of the caput of this
  article.

        § 5º Once the supply of the final product has been completed, the suspensions referred to in item IV of the caput and in § 4º of this article convert into a zero rate.

        § 6º Once the allocation of the final product has been completed, the suspension referred to in item V of the caput of this article converts into a zero rate.

         § 7º The beneficiary that carries out the acquisition in the domestic market with suspension of payment under item V of the caput and does not allocate the good to the
  activities referred to in item I of the caput of this article within the period of 3 (three) years, counted from the date of acquisition, is obliged to pay the IBS and the CBS not paid as a result of
  the suspension enjoyed, plus default penalty and adjusted by the Selic rate, calculated from the date the respective taxable
  events occurred.

        § 8º The suspensions of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput of this article shall only apply to taxable events occurring until December 31, 2040.

                                                                                        Section VI

                                                           Of the Baggage and International Shipments Regimes

        Art. 94. Exempt from payment of the IBS and the CBS on import of material goods are:

        I - baggage of travelers and crew members, accompanied or unaccompanied; and

        II - international shipments, provided that:

        a) they are exempt from the Import Tax;

        b) the sender and the recipient are natural persons; and

        c) there was no intermediation by a digital platform.

        Art. 95. In an international shipment in which the simplified taxation regime is applied, under the terms of customs legislation, the supplier of material
  goods of foreign origin, even if resident or domiciled abroad, is jointly and severally liable for the IBS and the CBS and is required to register under the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS,
  observing the provisions of § 2º of art. 21, § 3º of art. 22 and art. 23 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 96. The digital platform, even if domiciled abroad, is responsible for payment of the IBS and the CBS relating to material goods that are the subject of an international
  shipment whose operation or import was carried out through its intermediation, observing the provisions of arts. 22 and 23 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 97. In the cases of arts. 95 and 96 of this Complementary Law, the recipient of an international shipment, even if not the importer, is jointly and severally
  responsible for payment of the IBS and the CBS relating to material goods that are the subject of an international shipment if:

        I - the supplier resident or domiciled abroad is not registered; or

        II - the taxes have not been paid by the supplier resident or domiciled abroad, even if registered, or by a digital platform.

                                                                                        Section VII

                                           Of the Regime for the Supply of Fuel to Aircraft in International Traffic

         Art. 98. The supply of fuel or lubricant for refueling aircraft in international traffic bound for
  abroad is considered an export.

        Sole paragraph. The provision in this article applies only to the refueling of fuel or lubricant carried out exclusively in a bonded primary
  zone or bonded organized port area.

                                                                                    Section VIII
                                                                (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                 Final Provisions

        Art. 98-A. The regulation may provide for cases in which the special customs regimes referred to in arts. 84, 85, 88 and 90 of this Complementary Law
  shall be applied to material goods bound for abroad, including in the case of temporary departure from the Country. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

        Art. 98-B. The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS resulting from the application of a special customs regime converts into a zero rate in the case
  in which the material good is destroyed, under customs control and at the expense of the interested party, as a measure for terminating the application of the regime. (Wording
  given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                    CHAPTER II

                                                             OF EXPORT PROCESSING ZONES

         Art. 99. Imports or acquisitions in the domestic market of machinery, apparatus, instruments and equipment carried out by a company
  authorized to operate in export processing zones shall be carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 1º The suspension referred to in the caput of this article applies only to goods, new or used, necessary for the activities of the company authorized to operate in
  export processing zones, for incorporation into its fixed assets.

       § 2º In the case of import of used goods, the suspension referred to in the caput of this article shall apply when it is an industrial complex that is an
  constitutive element of the paying-up of the company's share capital.

         § 3º In the case of use of goods imported or acquired in the domestic market with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS not in accordance with the
  provisions of §§ 1º and 2º, or of resale of the goods before the conversion of the suspension into a zero rate occurs, in the manner set out in § 4º of this article, the company
  authorized to operate in export processing zones is obliged to pay the IBS and the CBS whose payment remains suspended, plus
  penalty and default interest under § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, calculated from the date the respective taxable events occurred, in the capacity
  of:

        I - taxpayer, with regard to import operations; or

        II - person liable, with regard to acquisitions in the domestic market.
        § 4º If the cases set out in § 3º do not occur, the suspension referred to in the caput of this article shall convert into a zero rate, once the period of 2 (two)
  years has elapsed, counted from the date the taxable event occurred.

         § 5º If payment of the IBS and the CBS is not made in the manner of § 3º of this article, the amounts shall be demanded through an ex officio proceeding, adjusted
  by the Selic rate, and the applicable penalties shall be due.

       Art. 100. Imports or acquisitions in the domestic market of raw materials, intermediate products and packaging materials carried out by
  a company authorized to operate in export processing zones shall be carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 1º The raw materials, intermediate products and packaging materials referred to in the caput of this article must be used entirely in the
  production process of the final product to be exported, without prejudice to the provisions of art. 101 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The suspension referred to in the caput of this article shall convert into a zero rate upon the export of the final product or the provision of services supplied
  or intended exclusively for abroad, observing the provisions of § 4º.

         § 3º Electric energy from renewable generation sources used by companies established in Export Processing Zones is considered a raw
  material for purposes of the caput.

        § 4º Electric energy from renewable generation sources used by service-providing companies established in export processing
  zones shall receive treatment equivalent to that established in the caput for raw materials, intermediate products and packaging materials.

        Art. 101. Manufactured products or products acquired for manufacturing by a company authorized to operate in export processing zones may
  be sold on the domestic market, provided that the legal entity makes payment of:

        I - the IBS and the CBS, as taxpayer, whose payment on imports remains suspended due to the provisions of arts. 99 and 100
  of this Complementary Law, plus default penalty and adjusted by the Selic rate, calculated from the date the respective taxable events occurred;

        II - the IBS and the CBS, as person liable, whose payment relating to acquisitions in the domestic market remains suspended due to the
  provisions of arts. 99 and 100 of this Complementary Law, plus default penalty and adjusted by the Selic rate, calculated from the date the
  respective taxable events occurred;

        III - the IBS and the CBS normally levied on the sale operation.

        Art. 102. The treatment established in arts. 99 and 100 of this Complementary Law applies to acquisitions of machinery, apparatus, instruments,
  equipment, raw materials, intermediate products and packaging materials carried out between companies authorized to operate in export
  processing zones.

        Art. 103. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on transport services are reduced to zero:

        I - for the goods referred to in arts. 99 and 100 of this Complementary Law, up to the export processing zones; and

        II - for goods exported from the export processing zones.

        Art. 104. The provisions of this Chapter shall observe the discipline set out in customs legislation for export processing zones.

                                                                                 CHAPTER III

                                                                   OF THE CAPITAL GOODS REGIMES

                                                                                    Section I

                                    Of the Tax Regime to Incentivize the Modernization and Expansion of Port Infrastructure (Reporto)

         Art. 105. Observing the discipline set out in specific legislation, imports and acquisitions in the domestic market of machinery, equipment, spare parts and other goods
  carried out directly by beneficiaries of the Tax Regime to Incentivize the Modernization and Expansion of Port Infrastructure (Reporto), and intended for their fixed
  assets for exclusive use in the performance of services of:

        I - loading, unloading, storage and handling of merchandise and products, including when carried out in a bonded facility in a secondary zone;

        II - supplementary operational support systems;

        III - environmental protection;

        IV - security and monitoring systems for the flow of people, merchandise, products, vehicles and vessels;

        V - dredging; and

        VI - training and education of workers, including in the establishment of Professional Training Centers,

  shall be carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS.

         § 1º The provision in the caput of this article also applies to goods used in the performance of merchandise transport services by rail, classified
  under headings 86.01, 86.02 and 86.06 of the Mercosur Common Nomenclature based on the Harmonized System (NCM/SH), and to rails and other railway track
  elements, classified under heading 73.02 of the NCM/SH.

        § 2º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput of this article converts into a zero rate after 5 (five) years have elapsed, counted from the date
  the respective taxable events occurred.

        § 3º The transfer, on any grounds, of ownership of goods imported or acquired in the domestic market under Reporto, within the period of 5 (five)
  years, counted from the date the respective taxable events occurred, must be preceded by authorization of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB and by payment of the
  IBS and the CBS whose payment was suspended, plus penalty and default interest under § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

         § 4º The transfer referred to in § 3º of this article, previously authorized by the IBS Management Committee and the RFB, to another Reporto beneficiary shall be
  carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS, provided that the acquirer assumes responsibility, from the moment the respective taxable events
  occurred, for the IBS and the CBS whose payment was suspended.

        § 5º The goods benefiting from the suspension referred to in the caput and in § 1º of this article shall be listed in the regulation.

        § 6º The spare parts referred to in the caput must have a value equal to or greater than 20% (twenty percent) of the value of the machine or equipment to which they
  are intended, according to the respective import declaration or invoice.

        § 7º Reporto beneficiaries may carry out imports and acquisitions in the domestic market covered by the regime until December 31, 2028.

        § 8º Legal entities opting for Simples Nacional may not join Reporto.

                                                                                    Section II


                                             Of the Special Incentive Regime for the Development of Infrastructure (Reidi)

         Art. 106. Observing the discipline set out in specific legislation, imports and acquisitions in the domestic market of new machinery, apparatus, instruments and
  equipment, and of construction materials, carried out directly by beneficiaries of the Special Incentive Regime for the Development of Infrastructure (Reidi) for use or
  incorporation into infrastructure works intended for fixed assets, shall be carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 1º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput of this article also applies to:

        I - the import of services intended for infrastructure works for incorporation into fixed assets;

        II - the acquisition in the domestic market of services intended for infrastructure works for incorporation into fixed assets; and

        III - the lease of machinery, apparatus, instruments and equipment intended for infrastructure works for incorporation into fixed assets.

        § 2º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput and in § 1º of this article converts into a zero rate after the use or incorporation of the
  good, construction material or service into the infrastructure work.

        § 3º A Reidi beneficiary that does not use or incorporate the good, construction material or service into the infrastructure work is obliged to pay the IBS and the
  CBS whose payment remains suspended, plus penalty and default interest under § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, calculated from
  the date the respective taxable events occurred, in the capacity of:

        I - taxpayer, with regard to import operations of material goods; or

        II - person liable, with regard to services, leases or acquisitions of material goods in the domestic market.

         § 4º The benefits provided for in this article also apply in the event that, in accordance with applicable accounting standards, the revenues of legal entities
  holding public service concession contracts, recognized during the execution of infrastructure works eligible for Reidi, have as counterpart a contract asset, an intangible asset
  representing a right of exploration, or a financial asset representing an unconditional contractual right to receive cash or another financial asset, extending, including,
  to ongoing projects already authorized before the RFB.

        § 5º The benefits provided for in this article may be enjoyed for imports and acquisitions in the domestic market carried out within a period of 5 (five) years,
  counted from the date of authorization under Reidi of the legal entity holding the infrastructure project.

        § 6º Legal entities opting for Simples Nacional may not join Reidi.

         § 7º The tax benefits of the special regime dealt with in this article also apply to beneficiaries of the Special Incentive Regime for the
  Production of Low Carbon Emission Hydrogen (Rehidro), established by Law No. 14,948 of August 2, 2024, observing the discipline set out in
  specific legislation. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                      Section III

                                                       Of the Tax Regime to Incentivize Naval Activity - Renaval

       Art. 107. The Tax Regime to Incentivize Naval Economic Activity - Renaval allows previously authorized beneficiaries to suspend the
  payment of IBS and CBS:

         I - on the supply of vessels registered or pre-registered in the Special Brazilian Registry - REB established by art. 11 of Law No. 9,432 of January
  8, 1997, for incorporation into the fixed assets of an acquirer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS;

        II - on imports and acquisitions in the domestic market of machinery, equipment and vehicles intended for use in the activities referred to in item III,
  carried out for incorporation into their fixed assets; and

        III - on imports and acquisitions in the domestic market of raw materials, intermediate products, parts, pieces and components for use in the
  construction, maintenance, modernization and repair of vessels pre-registered or registered in the REB.

        § 1º Only taxpayers subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS that primarily carry out the activities of construction, maintenance, modernization
  and repair of vessels may be authorized as Renaval beneficiaries, under the terms of the regulation.

        § 2º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput of this article converts into a zero rate after:

        I - 12 (twelve) months of the good remaining in the fixed assets of the acquirer, in the case of item I of the caput;

        II - 5 (five) years of the good remaining in the fixed assets of the acquirer, in the case of item II of the caput; and

        III - incorporation or consumption in the activities referred to in item III of the caput.

        § 3º A Renaval beneficiary that does not meet the condition established in items I to III of the caput is obliged to pay the suspended IBS and CBS, with the
  additions referred to in § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, calculated from the date the respective taxable events occurred, in the capacity of:

        I - taxpayer, with regard to import operations of material goods; or

        II - person liable, with regard to operations in the domestic market.

       § 4º The provision in § 3º applies to a beneficiary that transfers, on any grounds, ownership of goods imported or acquired in the domestic market under
  the coverage of Renaval before conversion into a zero rate.

        § 5º For purposes of this article, goods and services of the same nature that, as a result of applicable accounting standards, are recorded by
  public service concessionaires as a contract, intangible or financial asset shall also be considered as goods incorporated into fixed assets.

                                                                                      Section IV

                                                               Of the Relief from Taxation on the Acquisition of Capital Goods

        Art. 108. Full and immediate credit of the IBS and the CBS is assured, in the manner set out in arts. 47 to 56, on the acquisition of capital goods.

        Art. 109. A joint act of the Federal Executive Branch and the IBS Management Committee may define cases in which imports and acquisitions in the domestic market
  of capital goods by a taxpayer under the regular regime shall be carried out with suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS, in which case the provision of art. 108 of this
  Complementary Law does not apply.

        § 1º The joint act referred to in the caput of this article shall specify the goods covered and the term of the benefit.

        § 2º The suspension of payment of the IBS and the CBS provided for in the caput of this article converts into a zero rate after the incorporation of the good into the fixed
  assets of the acquirer, observing the term referred to in § 1º of this article.
        § 3º A beneficiary that does not incorporate the good into its fixed assets is obliged to pay the IBS and the CBS whose payment remains suspended,
  plus penalty and default interest in the manner of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, calculated from the date the respective taxable events occurred,
  in the capacity of:

        I - taxpayer, with regard to imports; or

        II - person liable, with regard to acquisitions in the domestic market.

       § 4º The provision in this article also applies to legal entities opting for Simples Nacional registered under the regular regime referred to in this
  Complementary Law.

        Art. 110. The rates of the IBS and the CBS are reduced to zero on the supply and import:

        I - of tractors, machinery and agricultural implements, intended for a non-taxpayer rural producer referred to in art. 164; and

        II - of cargo transport vehicles intended for a self-employed natural-person cargo carrier who is a non-taxpayer, referred to in art. 169.

        Sole paragraph. The provision in this article applies to the capital goods listed in the regulation.

       Art. 111. For purposes of this Section, goods of the same nature that, as a result of applicable accounting standards, are recorded by
  public service concessionaires as a contract, intangible or financial asset shall also be considered as goods incorporated into fixed assets.

                                                                                      TITLE III

                            OF THE PERSONALIZED REFUND OF THE IBS AND THE CBS (CASHBACK) AND OF THE NATIONAL BASIC FOOD BASKET

                                                                                      CHAPTER I

                                                       OF THE PERSONALIZED REFUND OF THE IBS AND THE CBS (CASHBACK)

        Art. 112. The following shall be refunded, under the terms and limits set out in this Chapter, to natural persons who are members of low-income
  families:

        I - the CBS, by the Union; and

        II - the IBS, by the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities.

        Art. 113. The recipient of the refunds provided for in this Chapter shall be the person responsible for a family unit of a low-income family registered in the
  Single Registry for Federal Government Social Programs (CadÚnico), under art. 6º-F of Law No. 8,742 of December 7, 1993, or an equivalent rule
  that supersedes it, and who cumulatively meets the following requirements:

        I - have a monthly per capita family income of up to half the national minimum wage;

        II - reside in national territory; and

        III - hold a registration in regular status in the CPF (individual taxpayer registry).

        § 1º The recipient shall be automatically included in the refund system, and may, at any time, request their exclusion.

        § 2º Personal data collected under the refund system shall be processed in the manner set out in Law No. 13,709 of August 14, 2018 (General Personal Data
  Protection Law), and art. 198 of Law No. 5,172 of October 25, 1966 (National Tax Code), and may only be used or transferred to public
  administration bodies or, in anonymized form, to research institutes for the execution of actions related to the refunds.

        Art. 114. The refund of the CBS referred to in item I of the caput of art. 112 of this Complementary Law shall be managed by the RFB, which shall be responsible for:

        I - regulating, coordinating, controlling and supervising its execution;

        II - defining the procedures for determining the amount and the system for payment of the refunded amounts;

        III - preparing management and accountability reports relating to the refunded amounts; and

        IV - adopting other actions and initiatives necessary for operationalizing the refund.

        § 1º The regulation referred to in item I of the caput of this article shall define, in particular:

        I - the assessment period for the refund;

        II - the calendar and frequency of payment;

        III - the forms of crediting to the recipient natural persons;

        IV - the manner of reimbursement of amounts wrongly received by natural persons;

        V - the mechanisms for mitigating fraud or errors;

        VI - the treatment in relation to indications of irregularities;

        VII - the forms of transparency relating to the distribution of the refunds; and

        VIII - the deadline for use of the refunds, which may not exceed 24 (twenty-four) months.

          § 2º The procedures adopted for payment of the refunds shall prioritize mechanisms that encourage the formalization of consumption by the
  recipient families, by means of the issuance of tax documents, so as to encourage tax citizenship and mitigate informality in economic activities, tax
  evasion and unfair competition.

         Art. 115. The refund of the IBS referred to in item II of the caput of art. 112 shall be managed by the IBS Management Committee, which shall have the powers set out
  in art. 114 of this Complementary Law, respecting the specificities.

        Art. 116. The tax refunds provided for in this Chapter shall be granted at the time defined in the regulation.

         § 1º In the case of household supply of electric energy, water supply, sanitary sewage and piped gas, and of the supply of
  telecommunications services, the refunds shall be granted at the time of billing.

      § 2º In the case of the supply of goods or services subject to billing at a fixed frequency, the refunds shall preferably be granted at the
  time of billing.


         § 3º The amounts shall be made available to the financial agent within a maximum period of 15 (fifteen) days after the assessment, observing the provision in item I of § 1º
  of art. 114 and in art. 115 of this Complementary Law.

        § 4º The financial agent must transfer the amounts to the recipient families within 10 (ten) days after the amounts are made available, as referred to in § 3º of this article.

        § 5º (VETOED).      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 117. The refunds provided for in this Chapter shall be calculated by applying a percentage to the value of the tax relating to consumption, formalized
  by means of the issuance of tax documents.

         § 1º The regulation shall establish refund rules by recipient family unit and by refund assessment period, so that the refund
  is compatible with the family's disposable income.

        § 2º To determine the tax to be refunded to natural persons, under the terms of the caput and § 1º of this article, the following shall be considered:

       I - the total consumption of products by the recipient families, excluding products subject to the Selective Tax, referred to in Book II of this
  Complementary Law;

        I - the total consumption of goods and services by the recipient families, excluding goods and services subject to the Selective Tax, referred to in Book II of this
  Complementary Law;      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - data extracted from tax documents linked to the CPF of members of the family unit, covering acquisition operations of goods or services
  exclusively for household consumption;

         III - the disposable monthly family income, understood as that resulting from the sum of the income declared in CadÚnico plus amounts received as
  conditional cash transfer;

        IV - data extracted from official publications relating to the consumption structure of families;

        V - the tax rules for goods and services set out in the legislation.

        Art. 118. The percentage to be applied under art. 117 of this Complementary Law shall be:

        I - 100% (one hundred percent) for the CBS and 20% (twenty percent) for the IBS on the acquisition of a bottle of up to 13 kg (thirteen kilograms) of liquefied
  petroleum gas, in household supply operations of electric energy, water supply, sanitary sewage and piped gas, and in telecommunications
  supply operations; and

        II - 20% (twenty percent) for the CBS and the IBS, in the other cases.

        § 1º The Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities may, by specific law, set refund percentages for their share of the CBS or the IBS
  higher than those set out in items I and II of the caput, which may be differentiated:

        I - according to the family income of the recipients, observing the provision in art. 113 of this Complementary Law;

        II - between the cases set out in items I and II of the caput.

        § 2º In the absence of the setting of own percentages, the refunds provided for in this Chapter shall be calculated by applying the percentages referred to
  in items I and II of the caput.

        § 3º The provision in § 1º of this article does not apply to the CBS refund percentage referred to in item I of the caput.

       Art. 119. Exceptionally, in localities with operational difficulties that compromise the effectiveness of the tax refund under art. 117 of this
  Complementary Law, simplified procedures may be adopted for calculating the refunds.

         § 1º The simplified procedure referred to in this article does not apply to refunds granted at the time of billing of the operation, under the terms of §§ 1º
  and 2º of art. 116 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º For purposes of the provision in the caput of this article, the following sequence of calculations shall be observed, respecting the income brackets of the
  recipient families:

         I - determination of the tax burden borne in the different income brackets, understood as the product of the estimated monthly consumption of goods and
  services by the corresponding rates;

        II - determination of the tax pressure in the different income brackets, obtained by the ratio between the tax burden borne, under
  item I of this paragraph, and the estimated average monthly income, expressed as a percentage;

         III - determination of the tax burden borne at the family unit level in the different income brackets, which consists of the multiplication of the tax
  pressure of the income bracket by the disposable monthly income of the recipient family, under item III of § 2º of art. 117 of this Complementary Law;

         IV - determination of the monthly refund amount at the family unit level, which results from the multiplication of the tax burden borne at the family unit
  level by the refund percentage set under art. 118 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3º Data relating to consumption of goods and services and average income referred to, respectively, in items I and II of § 2º of this article, shall
  be estimated based on the information from the most recent Household Budget Survey (POF), produced by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics Foundation (IBGE),
  based on a methodology defined in the regulation.

          § 4º The definition of localities with operational difficulties referred to in the caput of this article shall take into account the degree of effectiveness of the tax
  refund, by means of an evaluation methodology defined in the regulation.

         Art. 120. Under no circumstances may the portion credited individually to the beneficiary family under this Chapter exceed the tax burden borne
  relating to the CBS, in the case of the refund referred to in item I of the caput of art. 112, and the tax burden borne relating to the IBS, in the case of the refund referred to
  in item II of the caput of art. 112 of this Complementary Law, levied on the families' consumption.

       Sole paragraph. For purposes of the provision in the caput of this article, the tax burden borne by the recipient families may be assessed based on
  tax documents issued or by the calculation procedures detailed in art. 119 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 121. Refunds of taxes to natural persons referred to in this Chapter shall be deducted from tax collection, by means of cancellation of the corresponding revenue.

         Art. 122. The Union, through the RFB, and the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities, through the IBS Management Committee, may implement
  integrated solutions for the administration of a system that enables unified refund of the portions referred to in items I and II of the caput of art. 112 of this
  Complementary Law.

        Sole paragraph. Integrated administration includes the exercise of the powers set out in arts. 114 and 115 of this Complementary Law, under the terms of a specific
  agreement for that purpose.


        Art. 123. The refunds provided for in art. 112 of this Complementary Law shall be calculated based on family consumption carried out as of:

        I - January 2027, for the CBS; and

        II - January 2029, for the IBS.

        Art. 124. For the purposes of this Complementary Law, the following are understood as:

       I - general refund to natural persons of the IBS or the CBS, the amount determined by applying the percentages established in art. 118 of this
  Complementary Law;

        II - specific refund to natural persons of the IBS or the CBS, the difference between the amount determined by applying the percentages set by the
  federative entities under art. 118 of this Complementary Law and the amount referred to in item I of this caput.

         Sole paragraph. The general refund referred to in item I of the caput of this article shall be taken into account for purposes of calculating the reference rates, with
  a view to rebalancing the tax collection of the respective federative spheres.

                                                                                   CHAPTER II

                                                                 OF THE NATIONAL BASIC FOOD BASKET

        Art. 125. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on sales of products intended for human consumption listed in
  Annex I of this Complementary Law, with the specification of the corresponding NCM/SH classifications, that make up the National Basic Food Basket, created under the
  terms of art. 8º of Constitutional Amendment No. 132 of December 20, 2023, are reduced to zero.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of §§ 1º and 2º of art. 126 of this Complementary Law apply to the rate reductions referred to in the caput of this article.

                                                                                    TITLE IV

                                                              OF THE DIFFERENTIATED REGIMES OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

                                                                                   CHAPTER I

                                                                             GENERAL PROVISIONS

         Art. 126. Differentiated regimes of the IBS and the CBS are hereby established, uniformly throughout the national territory, as set out in this Title, with
  the application of reduced rates or the granting of presumed credits, ensuring the corresponding adjustments to the reference rates of the IBS and the CBS,
  with a view to rebalancing tax collection.

         § 1º Provided the applicable requirements are met, the differentiated regimes referred to in this Chapter apply, as applicable, to the import of the goods and services
  provided for therein.

        § 2º The alteration of operations with goods or services benefited by the differentiated regimes referred to in this Chapter, by means of addition, exclusion
  or substitution, shall only take effect after compliance with the provisions of §§ 9º and 11 of art. 156-A of the Federal Constitution.

        § 3º The provision in § 2º of this article does not apply to the cases dealt with in § 2º of art. 131, § 2º of art. 132, art. 134, § 10 of art. 138, § 2º of art.
  144, § 2º of art. 145 and § 3º of art. 146 of this Complementary Law, provided that their effects, considered jointly for each review period, do not result in an
  increase of more than 0.02 (two hundredths) of a percentage point in the reference rate of the CBS, the state reference rate of the IBS or the
  municipal reference rate of the IBS.

         § 4º The rate reductions referred to in this Title shall be applied to the standard rates of the IBS and the CBS of each federative entity, set under the
  terms of art. 14 of this Complementary Law.

        § 5º The appropriation of the presumed credits provided for in this Title is conditioned on:

        I - the issuance of an electronic tax document relating to the operation by the acquirer, identifying the respective supplier; and

        II - actual payment to the supplier.

        § 6º The provision in § 1º of this article does not apply to international shipments subject to the Simplified Taxation Regime (RTS), except in the case of
  finished products belonging to classes of medicines imported by a natural person for their own or individual use. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

                                                                                   CHAPTER II

                                                   OF THE THIRTY PERCENT REDUCTION OF THE RATES OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

        Art. 127. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on the provision of services by the following professionals, who carry out intellectual activities of a
  scientific, literary or artistic nature, subject to oversight by a professional council, are reduced by 30% (thirty percent):

        I - administrators;

        II - lawyers;

        III - architects and urban planners;

        IV - social workers;

        V - librarians;

        VI - biologists;

        VII - accountants;

        VIII - economists;

        IX - home economists;

        X - physical education professionals;

        XI - engineers and agronomists;

        XII - statisticians;

        XIII - veterinarians and animal scientists;
        XIV - museologists;

        XV - chemists;

        XVI - public relations professionals;

        XVII - industrial technicians; and

        XVIII - agricultural technicians.

        § 1º The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies to the provision of services carried out by:

        I - a natural person, provided that the services rendered are linked to the professional's qualification; and

        II - a legal entity that cumulatively meets the following requirements:

         a) the partners hold professional qualifications directly related to the corporate purpose and are subject to oversight by a professional
  council;

        b) does not have a legal entity as a partner;

        c) is not a partner of another legal entity;

        d) does not carry out activity other than the professional qualifications of the partners; and

        e) the services related to the core activity are rendered directly by the partners, with the assistance of aides or collaborators being permitted.

        § 2º For purposes of item II of § 1º of this article, the following do not prevent the rate reduction referred to in this article:

        I - the legal form of the company;

         II - the union of different professionals referred to in items I to XVIII of the caput of this article, provided that each partner's activity is within their professional
  qualification; and

        III - the manner of distribution of profits.

        § 3º §§ 1º and 2º of this article do not apply to the provision of services related to the profession in item X of the caput of this article carried out by a legal entity,
  provided it is subject to oversight by a professional council.

                                                                                    CHAPTER III

                                                   OF THE SIXTY PERCENT REDUCTION OF THE RATES OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

                                                                                       Section I

                                                                                General Provisions

        Art. 128. Provided the definitions and other provisions of this Chapter are observed, the rates of the IBS and the
  CBS levied on operations involving the following are reduced by 60% (sixty percent):

        I - education services;

        II - health services;

        III - medical devices;

        IV - accessibility devices for persons with disabilities;

        V - medicines;

        VI - foods intended for human consumption;

        VII - personal hygiene and cleaning products predominantly consumed by low-income families;

        VIII - fresh (in natura) agricultural, aquaculture, fishing, forestry and plant extractivism products;

        IX - agricultural and aquaculture inputs;

        X - national artistic, cultural, event, journalistic and audiovisual productions;

        XI - institutional communication;

        XII - sports activities; and

        XIII - goods and services related to sovereignty and national security, information security and cybersecurity.

                                                                                       Section II

                                                                            Of Education Services

        Art. 129. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the education services listed
  in Annex II to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective classifications under the Brazilian Nomenclature of Services, Intangibles and Other Transactions that
  Produce Changes in Net Worth (NBS).

        Sole paragraph. The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article:

        I - applies only to the amounts owed as consideration for the services listed in Annex II to this Complementary Law; and

        II - does not apply to other transactions that may occur within the schools, institutions or establishments of the service supplier.

                                                                                       Section III
