                                                                              Health Services



       Art. 130. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the health services listed in
  Annex III to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NBS classifications.

       Sole paragraph. Amounts disallowed by the medical audit of health assistance plans and not paid do not form part of the IBS and CBS tax base for the health services referred to in the caput of this article.

                                                                                    Section IV

                                                                          Medical Devices

        Art. 131. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the medical devices listed
  in Annex IV to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies only to the devices listed in Annex IV to this Complementary Law that are regularized
  before the National Health Surveillance Agency (Anvisa).

        § 2 Without prejudice to the five-year review referred to in Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law, the Minister of State for Finance and the
  IBS Management Committee, after consulting the Ministry of Health, shall review, every 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, by joint act, the list referred to in Annex IV to this Complementary
  Law, solely for the purpose of including medical devices that did not exist on the date of publication of the previous review and that serve the same purposes
  as those already included in that annex.

                                                                                    Section V

                                                Accessibility Devices for Persons with Disabilities

         Art. 132. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of accessibility devices
  for persons with disabilities listed in Annex V to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies only to the accessibility devices listed in Annex V to this Complementary Law
  that meet the requirements set out in a rule issued by the competent public agency.

          § 2 Without prejudice to the five-year review referred to in Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law, the Minister of State for Finance and the
  IBS Management Committee, after consulting the competent public agency, shall review, every 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, by joint act, the list referred to in Annex V to this
  Complementary Law, solely for the purpose of including accessibility devices that did not exist on the date of publication of the previous review and that serve the same
  purposes as those already included in that annex.

                                                                                    Section VI

                                                                              Medicines

        Art. 133. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of medicines registered with
  Anvisa or produced by compounding pharmacies are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), except for medicines subject to the zero rate referred to in art. 146 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article also applies to transactions involving the supply of formulations for enteral and parenteral nutrition,
  special formulations and nutritional formulas intended for persons with inborn errors of metabolism listed in Annex VI to this Complementary Law, with the
  specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

         § 2 In order to ensure that the reduction in tax burden is passed through to prices, the reduction referred to in this article applies only to medicines
  industrialized or imported by legal entities that have entered into a conduct adjustment agreement with the Federal Government and the IBS Management Committee, or that
  comply with the system established by the Drug Market Regulation Chamber (CMED), as provided by law.

          Art. 134. Without prejudice to the five-year review referred to in Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law, the Minister of State for Finance and the
  IBS Management Committee, after consulting the Ministry of Health, shall review, every 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, by joint act, the list referred to in Annex VI, solely
  for the purpose of including formulations referred to in § 1 of art. 133 of this Complementary Law that did not exist on the date of publication of the previous review and that serve the same
  purposes as those already covered.

                                                                                   Section VII

                                                              Food Intended for Human Consumption

       Art. 135. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of food intended for human
  consumption listed in Annex VII to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

                                                                                   Section VIII

                                Personal Hygiene and Cleaning Products Predominantly Consumed by Low-Income Families

        Art. 136. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the personal hygiene and
  cleaning products listed in Annex VIII to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

                                                                                    Section IX

                                    Agricultural, Aquaculture, Fishing, Forestry and Plant Extractive Products In Natura

       Art. 137. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of agricultural, aquaculture,
  fishing, forestry and plant extractive products in natura are reduced by 60% (sixty percent).

        § 1 A product is considered in natura when it is in the state in which it is found in nature, has not undergone any industrialization process nor
  been packaged for presentation, and does not lose that status merely by having undergone:

        I - drying, cleaning, threshing of grains or de-stoning; and

        II - freezing, cooling or simple packaging, when such procedures are intended solely for transport, storage or
  display for sale.

        § 2 The regulation shall provide for products that will not lose their in natura status when they require packaging in preservation packaging,
  with the addition of concentrates or preservatives to maintain the integrity and characteristics of the product.

        § 3 For the purposes of this article's caput, the supply of a forestry product is deemed to include the supply of environmental services of
  conservation or recovery of native vegetation, even when supplied in the form of sustainable management of agricultural, agroforestry and
  agrosilvopastoral systems, in accordance with the definitions and requirements of specific legislation.

                                                                                    Section X

                                                                  Agricultural and Aquaculture Inputs
         Art. 138. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the agricultural and aquaculture inputs
  listed in Annex IX to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH and NBS classifications.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies only to the products referred to in Annex IX to this Complementary Law that, when required,
  are registered as agricultural or aquaculture inputs with the competent agency of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock.

        § 2 Payment of the IBS and CBS levied on the following transactions with agricultural and aquaculture inputs referred to in the caput is deferred:

        I - supply made by a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime to:

        a) a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime; and

         b) a rural producer that is not an IBS and CBS taxpayer who uses the inputs in the production of goods sold to acquirers entitled to appropriate the
  presumed credits established by art. 168 of this Complementary Law; and

        II - importation carried out by:

        a) a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime; and

         b) a rural producer that is not an IBS and CBS taxpayer who uses the inputs in the production of goods sold to acquirers entitled to appropriate the
  presumed credits established by art. 168 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3 The deferral referred to in item "b" of item I and item "b" of item II, both of § 2, shall apply only to the portion of inputs used
  by the rural producer that is not an IBS and CBS taxpayer in the production of goods sold to acquirers entitled to appropriate the presumed credits
  established by art. 168 of this Complementary Law.

        § 4 (VETOED).

        § 5 In the cases provided for in item "a" of item I and item "a" of item II, both of § 2 of this article, the deferral shall end if:

        I - the supply of the agricultural or aquaculture input, or of the product resulting therefrom:

        a) is not covered by the deferral; or

        b) is exempt, not taxed, including by reason of suspension of payment, or subject to a zero rate; or

        II - the transaction is carried out without issuance of the tax document.

        § 6 Payment of the IBS and CBS relating to the deferral shall be made by the taxpayer that carries out the transaction that ends the deferral phase,
  even if not taxed, as provided in §§ 7 and 8 of this article.

        § 7 In the case referred to in item "a" of item I of § 5 of this article, the incidence of the IBS and CBS shall follow the rules applicable to the taxed transaction.

        § 8 In the case referred to in item "b" of item I of § 5 of this article, payment of the IBS and CBS is waived if credit appropriation is permitted,
  under the terms provided in arts. 47 to 56.

        § 9 In the cases provided for in item "b" of item I and item "b" of item II, both of § 2 of this article, the deferral shall end by means of:

        I - the reduction of the amount of the IBS and CBS presumed credits established by art. 168, as provided in § 3 of that article; or

        II - (VETOED).

         § 10. Without prejudice to the five-year review referred to in Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law, the Minister of State for Finance and the
  IBS Management Committee, after consulting the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, shall review, every 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, by joint act, the list referred to in Annex
  IX, solely for the purpose of including inputs referred to in the caput of this article that serve the same purposes as those already covered and products intended for
  exclusive use in the manufacture of agricultural pesticides.

                                                                                          Section XI

                                           National Artistic, Cultural, Event, Journalistic and Audiovisual Productions

          Art. 139. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the goods and services listed in Annex X
  to this Complementary Law are reduced by 60% (sixty percent), with the specification of the respective NCM/SH and NBS classifications, in cases related to the following national
  artistic, cultural, event, journalistic and audiovisual productions:

        I - theatrical, circus and dance performances;

        II - musical shows;

        III - carnival or folk parades;

        IV - academic and scientific events, such as congresses, conferences and symposiums;

        V - trade fairs;

        VI - exhibitions, fairs, galleries and cultural, artistic and literary shows;

        VII - talk shows or news programs, films, documentaries, series, soap operas, interviews and music videos; and

        VIII - works of art.

          § 1 The provisions of items I, II, III and VII of the caput of this article apply only to productions made in the country that predominantly contain
  artistic, musical, literary or journalistic works by Brazilian authors or performed predominantly by Brazilian artists.

        § 2 In the case of cinematographic or video-phonographic works referred to in item VII of the caput of this article, a national production is considered to be one that
  meets the requirements for national audiovisual works defined in specific legislation.

        § 3 The supply of works of art referred to in item VIII of the caput of this article covers only those produced by Brazilian artists.

                                                                                          Section XII

                                                                             Institutional Communication

          Art. 140. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the following institutional
  communication services to the direct public administration, government agencies and public foundations are reduced by 60% (sixty percent):
          I - services aimed at the planning, creation, programming and maintenance of public administration webpages, at monitoring and managing
  its social media, and at optimizing pages and digital channels for search engines and producing messages, infographics, interactive panels and
  institutional content;

         II - press relations services, which bring together organizational strategies to promote and reinforce communication between the contracting bodies and entities
  and their target audiences, through interaction with press professionals; and

        III - public relations services, which comprise the planned, cohesive and continuous communication effort aimed at establishing an adequate
  perception of the institutional actions and objectives, through the promotion of mutual understanding and the maintenance of relationship standards and
  information flows between the contracting bodies and entities and their target audiences, in the country and abroad.

       Sole paragraph. Suppliers of institutional communication services are subject to the standard rate in relation to services supplied to acquirers
  not mentioned in the caput of this article.

                                                                                      Section XIII

                                                                           Sports Activities

        Art. 141. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the following transactions related to sports
  activities are reduced by 60% (sixty percent):

        I - supply of sports education services, classified under NBS code 1.2205.12.00;

         II - management and operation of sport by associations and sports clubs affiliated with the state or federal agency responsible for coordinating sports,
  including through the sale of tickets to sporting events, the supply, whether for consideration or not, of goods and services, including tickets, through fan
  membership programs, the assignment of athletes' sporting rights, and the transfer of athletes to another sporting entity or their return to activity at another sporting
  entity.

                                                                                      Section XIV

                                     Sovereignty and National Security, Information Security and Cybersecurity

        Art. 142. The IBS and CBS rates on the following are reduced by 60% (sixty percent):

        I - supply to the direct public administration, government agencies and public foundations of the services and goods relating to sovereignty and national
  security, information security and cybersecurity listed in Annex XI to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NBS and
  NCM/SH classifications; and

        II - transactions and provision of information security and cybersecurity services developed by a company with a Brazilian partner holding a
  minimum of 20% (twenty percent) of its share capital, listed in Annex XI to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NBS
  and NCM/SH classifications.

       II - supply of information security and cybersecurity services developed by a company with a Brazilian partner holding a minimum of
  20% (twenty percent) of its share capital, listed in Annex XI to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NBS classifications.
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                     CHAPTER IV

                                                           REDUCTION TO ZERO OF THE IBS AND CBS RATES

                                                                                       Section I

                                                                                General Provisions

        Art. 143. Provided the definitions and other provisions of this Chapter are observed, the IBS and CBS rates levied on
  transactions with the following goods and services are reduced to zero:

        I - medical devices;

        II - accessibility devices for persons with disabilities;

        III - medicines;

        IV - basic menstrual health care products;

        V - vegetables, fruit and eggs;

        VI - passenger automobiles acquired by persons with disabilities or with autism spectrum disorder;

        VII - passenger automobiles acquired by professional drivers who dedicate the automobile to use in the rental category (taxi); and

        VIII - services provided by a non-profit Scientific, Technological and Innovation Institution (ICT).

                                                                                       Section II

                                                                            Medical Devices

        Art. 144. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the medical devices listed below are reduced to zero:

        I - in Annex XII to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications; and

        II - in Annex IV to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications, when acquired by:

        a) direct public administration bodies, government agencies and public foundations; and

        b) health entities immune to the IBS and CBS that hold a Charitable Social Assistance Entity Certificate (CEBAS) for proving the
  provision of services to the SUS (Unified Health System), under the terms of arts. 9 to 11 of Complementary Law No. 187 of December 16, 2021.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies only to the devices listed in Annexes IV and XII to this Complementary Law that
  meet the requirements set out in an Anvisa rule.

        § 2 The provisions of § 2 of art. 131 of this Complementary Law apply to the products covered by this Section.

       § 3 In the event of a public health emergency recognized by the competent federal, state, Federal District or municipal Legislative Branch, a joint act of the Minister
  of State for Finance and the IBS Management Committee may be issued, at any time, to include devices not listed in Annex XII to this
  Complementary Law, with the validity of the benefit limited to the period and locality of the public health emergency.

  disabilities listed below are reduced to zero:

          II - in Annex V to this Complementary Law, with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications, when acquired by:

          a) direct public administration bodies, government agencies and public foundations; and

       b) health entities immune to the IBS and CBS that hold CEBAS for proving the provision of services to the SUS, under the terms of arts. 9 to 11 of Complementary
  Law No. 187 of 2021.

       § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies only to the accessibility devices listed in Annexes V and XIII to this
  Complementary Law that meet the requirements set out in a rule issued by the competent public agency.

          § 2 The provisions of § 2 of art. 132 of this Complementary Law apply to the products covered by this Section.

                                                                                      Section IV

         Art. 146. The IBS and CBS rates on the supply of the medicines listed in Annex XIV to this Complementary Law,
  with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications, are reduced to zero.
         § 1 The IBS and CBS rates on the supply of medicines registered with Anvisa are also reduced to zero when acquired by:
         I - direct public administration bodies, government agencies and public foundations; and
         II - health entities immune to the IBS and CBS that hold CEBAS for proving the provision of services to the SUS, under the terms of arts. 9 to 11 of Complementary
  Law No. 187 of 2021.
         § 2 The rate reduction referred to in the caput of this article also applies to the supply of formulations for enteral and parenteral nutrition,
  special formulations and nutritional formulas intended for persons with inborn errors of metabolism listed in Annex VI to this Complementary Law, with the
  specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications, when acquired by the bodies and entities mentioned in the items of § 1 of this article.
         § 3 Without prejudice to the five-year review referred to in Chapter I of Title III of Book III of this Complementary Law, the head of the Federal Executive Branch and the
  IBS Management Committee, after consulting the Ministry of Health, may issue a joint act annually to review the list referred to in Annex XIV to this Complementary Law,
  solely for the purpose of including medicines that did not exist on the date of publication of the previous review and that serve the same purposes as those
  included in that annex and whose price limits have already been established by CMED.
         § 4 In the event of a public health emergency recognized by the competent federal, state, Federal District or municipal Legislative Branch, a joint act of the Minister
  of State for Finance and the IBS Management Committee may be issued, at any time, to include medicines not listed in Annex XIV to this
  Complementary Law, with the validity of the benefit limited to the period and locality of the public health emergency.

        Art. 146. The IBS and CBS rates on the supply of medicines registered with Anvisa are reduced to zero, provided they are intended,
  according to the health registration, for:   (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - rare diseases;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          II - neglected diseases;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          III - oncology;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          IV - diabetes;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          V - HIV/AIDS and other sexually transmitted infections (STIs);       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          VI - cardiovascular diseases; and      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          VII - the Popular Pharmacy Program of Brazil or equivalent.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1 The IBS and CBS rates on the supply of medicines registered with Anvisa are also reduced to zero when:               (Wording given
  by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - acquired by direct public administration bodies, government agencies and public foundations;          (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

         II - acquired by health entities immune to the IBS and CBS that hold Cebas for proving the provision of services to the SUS, under the terms of
  arts. 9 to 11 of Complementary Law No. 187 of December 16, 2021; or (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          III - classified as serums or vaccines, in accordance with specific health regulations.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2 The rate reduction referred to in the caput of this article also applies to the supply of formulations for enteral and parenteral nutrition,
  special formulations and nutritional formulas intended for persons with inborn errors of metabolism listed in Annex VI to this Complementary Law, with the
  specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications, when acquired by bodies and entities mentioned in items I and II of § 1 of this article.
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3 A joint act of the Ministry of Finance and the CGIBS, after consulting the Ministry of Health, shall disclose, every 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, the list of medicines
  entitled to the zero rate of the IBS and CBS, as provided in the caput of this article and in item III of § 1 of this article.        (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 4 In the event of a public health emergency recognized by the competent federal, state, Federal District or municipal Legislative Branch, a joint act of the
  Minister of Finance, the Ministry of Health and the CGIBS may be issued, at any time, solely to include medicines and lines of care
  not covered by the rate reduction referred to in this article, with the validity of the benefit limited to the period of the respective public health emergency.
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

  the requirements set out in an Anvisa rule.

       Art. 148. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the supply of the vegetables, fruit and eggs listed in Annex
  XV to this Complementary Law are reduced to zero, with the specification of the respective NCM/SH classifications.

        Sole paragraph. The products mentioned in the caput of this article, in accordance with the NCM/SH classification rules, may be presented whole, cut
  into slices or pieces, grated, turned, peeled, defoliated, washed, sanitized, packaged, fresh, chilled or frozen, even if
  mixed.

                                                                                   Section VII

        Passenger Automobiles Acquired by Persons with Disabilities or with Autism Spectrum Disorder and by Professional Drivers who
                                          Dedicate the Automobile to Use in the Rental Category (Taxi)

        Art. 149. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the sale of nationally manufactured passenger automobiles with at least
  4 (four) doors, including the trunk access door, are reduced to zero when acquired by:

          I - professional drivers who demonstrably carry out, in an automobile they own, the activity of independent passenger driver, as
  holder of a public authorization, permit or concession, and who dedicate the automobile to use in the rental category (taxi);

        II - persons with:

        a) physical, visual or hearing disability;

        b) severe or profound intellectual disability; or

         c) autism spectrum disorder, with impairments in social communication and in restricted or repetitive patterns of behavior of moderate or severe
  level, under the terms of legislation on the subject.

        § 1 A person with a disability is considered to be one with a long-term impairment of a physical, mental, intellectual or sensory nature that, in interaction with
  one or more barriers, may obstruct their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others, in accordance with the criteria for
  recognition of disability status set out in art. 150 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2 The rate reductions referred to in the caput of this article apply only:

        I - in the case of item I of the caput of this article, to an electric passenger automobile or one equipped with an engine of no more than 2,000 cm³ (two thousand
  cubic centimeters) displacement powered by fuel of renewable origin, reversible combustion system or hybrid; and

        II - in the case of item II of the caput of this article, to an automobile whose sale price to the consumer, including taxes that would be levied if the
  reductions did not exist and not including the costs necessary for the adaptation referred to in § 3 of this article, is not more than R$ 200,000.00 (two hundred thousand reais),
  with the benefit limited to a transaction value of up to R$ 70,000.00 (seventy thousand reais).

         II - in the case of item II of the caput of this article, to an automobile whose sale price to the consumer, including taxes that would be levied if the
  reductions did not exist and not including the costs necessary for the adaptation referred to in § 3 of this article, is not more than R$ 200,000.00 (two hundred thousand reais),
  with the benefit limited to a transaction value of up to R$ 100,000.00 (one hundred thousand reais).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3 In the case of item "a" of item II of the caput of this article, when the person is physically able to drive, the benefit shall cover only automobiles
  that are adapted, adaptations being considered those necessary to enable driving and not offered to the general public. (Repealed by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

        § 3 (Repealed).       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 4 In the case of item II of the caput of this article, passenger automobiles shall be acquired directly by persons who have full legal
  capacity or through their legal representative or attorney-in-fact.

        § 5 The legal representative or attorney-in-fact referred to in § 4 of this article shall be jointly and severally liable for any tax that goes unpaid as a result of the
  rate reductions referred to in this Section.

        § 6 The limits set out in item II of § 2 of this article shall be updated annually, on January 1, solely for the purpose of increasing them, based on the
  variation in the average price of new automobiles falling within those limits on the Table of the Getúlio Vargas Economic Research Institute Foundation (Fipe Table), under the terms of a joint
  act of the Minister of State for Finance and the IBS Management Committee.

       Art. 150. For the purposes of recognizing the right to the rate reductions referred to in this Section, a person with a disability is considered to be one who
  falls into at least one of the following categories:

        I - physical disability: complete or partial alteration of one or more segments of the human body that impairs
  physical function, in the form of:

        a) paraplegia;

        b) paraparesis;

        c) monoplegia;

        d) monoparesis;

        e) tetraplegia;

        f) tetraparesis;

        g) triplegia;

        h) triparesis;

        i) hemiplegia;


        j) hemiparesis;

        k) ostomy;

        l) amputation or absence of a limb;

        m) cerebral palsy;

        n) dwarfism; or

        o) limbs with congenital or acquired deformity;

        II - hearing disability: bilateral, partial or total loss, of 41 dB (forty-one decibels) or more, measured by audiogram at frequencies of 500 Hz
  (five hundred hertz), 1,000 Hz (one thousand hertz), 2,000 Hz (two thousand hertz) and 3,000 Hz (three thousand hertz);

        III - visual disability:

        a) blindness, in which visual acuity is equal to or less than 0.05 (five hundredths) in the better eye, with the best optical correction;

        b) low vision, in which visual acuity is between 0.3 (three tenths) and 0.05 (five hundredths) in the better eye, with the best optical correction;

        c) cases in which the sum of the measurement of the visual field in both eyes is equal to or less than 60 (sixty) degrees;

        d) simultaneous occurrence of any of the conditions provided for in items "a", "b" and "c" of this item; or

        e) monocular vision, in which the person has vision equal to or less than 20% (twenty percent) in one eye, while maintaining normal vision in the other;

        IV - mental disability: intellectual functioning significantly below average, manifested before age 18 (eighteen) and limitations
  associated with two or more areas of adaptive skills, such as:

        a) communication;

        b) personal care;

        c) social skills;

        d) use of community resources;

        e) health and safety;

        f) academic skills;

        g) leisure; and

        h) work.

          § 1 The provisions of items I, II and III of the caput of this article apply to disabilities of moderate or severe degree, understood as those that cause
  partial or total impairment of the functions of the body segments involved in the safety of vehicle driving, resulting in impairment of physical
  function and total or partial inability to drive.

        § 2 Aesthetic deformities and those that do not cause difficulties in the performance of the person's locomotor functions are not included among physical
  disabilities.

        Art. 151. For purposes of granting the rate reductions referred to in this Section, proof of the disability and of the status of person with
  autism spectrum disorder shall be provided by means of an assessment report issued:

        I - by a public health service provider;

        II - by a contracted or accredited private health service provider that is part of the Unified Health System (SUS); or

        III - by the Department of Motor Vehicles (Detran) or its accredited clinics.

        § 1 The completion of the assessment report, under the terms of this article, shall comply with the provisions of a joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB (Federal Revenue Service).

       § 2 The accredited clinics referred to in item III of the caput of this article are jointly and severally liable for taxes that go unpaid,
  with the legal additions, if fraudulent issuance of an assessment report by their agents is proven.

        Art. 152. The rate reductions referred to in art. 149 of this Complementary Law may be enjoyed:

        I - in the case of item I of the caput of art. 149 of this Complementary Law, at intervals of not less than 2 (two) years;

        II - in the case of item II of the caput of art. 149 of this Complementary Law, at intervals of not less than 4 (four) years.

       II - in the case of item II of the caput of art. 149 of this Complementary Law, at intervals of not less than 3 (three) years.                (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. In cases of total loss or disappearance of the automobile due to theft or robbery, the rate reductions may be enjoyed at any
  time.

        Art. 153. The right to the rate reductions referred to in art. 149 of this Complementary Law shall be recognized by the state or Federal District tax administration
  of the applicant's domicile and by the RFB, upon prior verification that the acquirer meets the requirements set out in this Section.

        Art. 154. Taxes shall be levied normally on any optional accessories that are not original equipment of the automobile acquired.

         Art. 155. Disposal of the automobile acquired under this Section that occurs at intervals shorter than those defined in art. 152, counted from the date of its
  acquisition, to persons who have not had the right referred to in art. 153 of this Complementary Law recognized shall result in payment by the seller of the
  taxes waived, updated as provided in tax legislation.

        § 1 Early disposal referred to in this article shall also subject the seller to payment of fines and default interest provided for in legislation in force.

        § 2 The provisions of the caput of this article do not apply in cases of:

        I - transfer of the automobile acquired:

        a) to the insurer, in cases of total loss or disappearance due to theft or robbery;
        b) due to the death of the beneficiary;

        II - fiduciary assignment of the automobile as collateral.

                                                                                      Section VIII

                                  Services Provided by a Non-Profit Scientific, Technological and Innovation Institution (ICT)

         Art. 156. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the provision of research and development services by a non-profit
  Scientific, Technological and Innovation Institution (ICT) are reduced to zero for:

         Art. 156. The IBS and CBS rates levied on the provision of research and development services by a non-profit
  Scientific, Technological and Innovation Institution (ICT), as well as by support foundations accredited as provided by law, are reduced to zero for: (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the direct public administration, government agencies and public foundations; or

        II - a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime,

  are reduced to zero.

        Sole paragraph. The rate reduction provided for in the caput of this article applies to a non-profit ICT that, cumulatively:

        I - includes in its corporate or statutory purpose:

        a) basic or applied research of a scientific or technological nature; or

        b) the development of new products, services or processes;

        II - meets the conditions for enjoying the immunity provided for in item III of the caput of art. 9 of this Complementary Law for transactions carried out by non-profit
  education and social assistance institutions.

                                                                                    CHAPTER V

        URBAN, SEMI-URBAN AND METROPOLITAN ROAD AND RAIL PUBLIC COLLECTIVE PASSENGER TRANSPORT

        Art. 157. The supply of urban, semi-urban and metropolitan road and rail public collective
  passenger transport services, under a regime of public authorization, permit or concession, is exempt from the IBS and CBS.

        Sole paragraph. For the purposes of the caput of this article, the following are considered:

        I - public collective passenger transport service: one accessible to the entire population upon individualized payment, with routes and prices set
  by the public authorities;

        II - road transport: the land transport service carried out on urban and rural roads;

        III - rail transport: that carried out by means of railways, including urban trains, subways, light rail vehicles and monorails;

        IV - urban passenger transport: the service of an urban nature provided within the territory of the Municipality;

        V - semi-urban passenger transport: the intermunicipal, interstate or international travel service between nearby localities of an
  urban or metropolitan nature; and

        VI - metropolitan passenger transport: the service provided between municipalities belonging to the same metropolitan region.

                                                                                    CHAPTER VI

                  URBAN REHABILITATION OF HISTORIC ZONES AND CRITICAL AREAS FOR URBAN RECOVERY AND RECONVERSION

         Art. 158. Subject to the provisions of this Chapter, the IBS and CBS rates on transactions related to
  urban rehabilitation projects for historic zones and critical areas for urban recovery and reconversion of the Municipalities or the Federal District, to be
  delimited by municipal or district law, are reduced by 60% (sixty percent).

        Sole paragraph. In the case of leasing of properties provided for in item VI of the caput of art. 162 of this Complementary Law, the rate reduction referred to in the
  caput of this article shall be 80% (eighty percent).

        Art. 159. The urban rehabilitation of historic zones and critical areas for urban recovery and reconversion of the Municipalities has as its objective the preservation
  of heritage, the qualification of public spaces, the recovery of residential areas, the restoration of buildings and improvements to urban and mobility infrastructure.

         Sole paragraph. In using the resources of the fund referred to in art. 159-A of the Federal Constitution, the States and the Federal District shall take into consideration the
  objectives referred to in the caput of this article in relation to their historic zones and critical areas for urban recovery and reconversion, including through
  incentives for the establishment of businesses in the area and the development of economic activity.

          Art. 160. In order to obtain the benefit referred to in art. 158, the Municipalities must submit to the Tripartite Commission referred to in art. 161 of this
  Complementary Law economic and social development projects for the respective preservation, recovery, reconversion and urban rehabilitation areas and historic
  zones.

        Art. 161. The Tripartite Commission responsible for analyzing the projects referred to in art. 160 of this Complementary Law shall be composed of:

        I - 2 (two) representatives of the Ministry of Cities;

        II - 2 (two) representatives of the Ministry of Finance;

        III - 4 (four) representatives of the IBS Management Committee, of which 2 (two) shall represent the States or the Federal District and 2 (two) shall
  represent the Municipalities or the Federal District.

        Art. 162. The benefit referred to in art. 158 shall be restricted to projects approved under art. 163 of this Complementary Law and shall cover the following
  transactions:

         I - provision of services for the preparation of architectural, urban planning, landscape, environmental, ecological, engineering, infrastructure and
  risk mitigation projects and their corresponding executive projects;

         II - provision of construction management, coordination, general contracting or subcontracting services for all works and
  services related to buildings and urbanization, infrastructure and other similar works, including auxiliary or complementary services typical of civil construction;

        III - provision of repair, restoration, conservation and renovation services for properties;


        IV - provision of services relating to:

        a) engineering, surveying, digital mapping and scanning, digital modeling, scale models, soil surveys, foundations, geology, urban planning, maintenance,
  environmental performance, climate efficiency, cleaning, environment and sanitation; and

        b) complementary projects for electrical and hydraulic installations, fire prevention and fighting, and structural projects;

         V - first sale of properties located in rehabilitated zones made by the owner within a period of up to 5 (five) years, counted from the date of issuance of the
  occupancy permit;

        VI - leasing of properties located in rehabilitated zones, for a period of 5 (five) years, counted from the date of issuance of the occupancy permit.

        Sole paragraph. The services mentioned in items I to IV of the caput of this article shall be entitled to the benefit until the completion date provided for in the approved project.

        Art. 163. Federal ordinary law shall establish:

        I - the concepts of preservation, recovery, reconversion and urban rehabilitation;

        II - the institutional affiliation and powers of the Tripartite Commission;

        III - the criteria for approval of projects submitted to the Tripartite Commission; and

        IV - the governance to be adopted for receiving and evaluating projects.

                                                                                    CHAPTER VII

                                               RURAL PRODUCERS AND NON-TAXPAYER INTEGRATED RURAL PRODUCERS

        Art. 164. A rural producer, whether an individual or a legal entity, earning revenue of less than R$ 3,600,000.00 (three million six hundred thousand reais) in the calendar year, and an
  integrated rural producer shall not be considered IBS and CBS taxpayers.

         § 1 An integrated rural producer is considered to be an agro-silvo-pastoral producer, whether an individual or a legal entity, who, individually or in association,
  with or without the labor cooperation of employees, is bound to an integrator by means of a vertical integration contract, receiving goods or services for the production and
  supply of raw materials, intermediate goods or final consumption goods.

       § 2 If, during the calendar year, the rural producer exceeds the annual revenue limit provided for in the caput of this article, it shall become a taxpayer as of the
  second month following the occurrence of the excess.

        § 3 The effects provided for in § 2 shall take place in the following calendar year if the excess verified in relation to annual revenue is not more than 20% (twenty
  percent) of the limit referred to in the caput of this article.

         § 4 In the case of a new activity, the limit referred to in the caput of this article shall be proportional to the number of months in which the producer has carried out
  activity, with fractions of months counted as a whole month.

        § 5 For the purposes of the caput, a legal entity is also considered to include an association or cooperative of rural producers:

        I - whose revenue is less than R$ 3,600,000.00 (three million six hundred thousand reais) in the calendar year; and

        II - is made up exclusively of individual rural producers whose revenue is less than R$ 3,600,000.00 (three million six hundred thousand reais) in the calendar
  year.

         § 6 If a rural producer, whether an individual or a legal entity, holds an equity interest in another legal entity that carries out agricultural activity, the limit
  provided for in the caput of this article shall be verified in relation to the sum of the revenue earned in the calendar year by all such persons.

        Art. 165. A rural producer or integrated rural producer may opt, at any time, to register as an IBS and CBS taxpayer under the regular regime.

        § 1 The effects of the option provided for in the caput of this article shall begin on the first day of the month following the month in which the request was made.

        § 2 The option to register under the terms of the caput of this article shall be irrevocable for the entire calendar year and shall apply to subsequent calendar years,
  subject to the provisions of art. 166 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3 A rural producer that earned revenue equal to or greater than R$ 3,600,000.00 (three million six hundred thousand reais) in the calendar year prior to the
  entry into force of this Complementary Law shall be considered a taxpayer as of the beginning of the effects of this Complementary Law, regardless of
  any action taken.

         Art. 166. A rural producer or integrated rural producer may renounce the option referred to in art. 165 as provided in the regulation, subject to the provisions of §
  5 of art. 41 of this Complementary Law.

         Sole paragraph. In the case referred to in the caput of this article, the rural producer or integrated rural producer shall cease to be an IBS and CBS taxpayer as of the
  first day of the calendar year following the renunciation of the option, subject to the provisions of art. 164 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 167. The amount established in the caput of art. 164 of this Complementary Law shall be updated annually based on the variation of the IPCA.

         Art. 168. A taxpayer of IBS and CBS subject to the regular regime may appropriate presumed credits of such taxes relating to purchases of goods and
  services from a rural producer or integrated rural producer that is not a taxpayer, as referred to in art. 164 of this Complementary Law. Effects pending.

        § 1 The electronic tax document relating to the purchase shall itemize:

        I - the value of the transaction, corresponding to the amount paid to the supplier;

        II - the amount of the presumed credit; and

        III - the net amount for tax purposes, corresponding to the difference between the amounts itemized in items I and II of this paragraph.

       § 2 In the case of a good or service supplied by an integrated producer, the value of the transaction referred to in item I of § 1 of this article shall be the amount of the
  integrated producer's remuneration determined based on the integration contract.

        § 3 The amount of the presumed credit referred to in item II of § 1 of this article shall be the result of applying the percentages referred to in § 4 of this article
  to the value of the transaction referred to in item III of § 1 of this article.

        § 4 The percentages shall be defined and disclosed annually by September, by joint act of the Minister of State for Finance and the IBS Management
  Committee, and shall enter into force as of January 1 of the following year.

        § 5 The definition of the percentages referred to in § 4:


        I - shall be carried out, as provided in the regulation, based on available tax information;

        II - shall result from the proportion between:

        a) the amount of IBS and CBS charged in relation to the total value of goods and services acquired by non-taxpayer rural producers; and

        b) the total value of goods and services supplied by non-taxpayer rural producers referred to in item III of § 1 of this article; and

         III - shall be based on the average of the annual percentages relating to transactions carried out in the 5 (five) calendar years prior to that of the disclosure period
  provided for in § 4.

         § 6 The percentages referred to in § 4 of this article may be differentiated, in accordance with the categories established in the regulation, according to the good or
  service supplied by the rural producer or integrated rural producer.

        § 6 The percentages referred to in § 4 may be differentiated, in accordance with the categories established in the regulation, according to the good or service
  supplied by the rural producer or integrated rural producer, the level of annual revenue and the type of rural producer. (Wording given by Complementary Law
  No. 227 of 2026)

        § 7 For the purposes of § 5 of this article, purchases of goods and services referred to in item I of the caput of art. 57 of this Complementary
  Law shall not be considered, nor shall the purchase of goods and services intended for the personal use and consumption of the rural producer or of persons related to the producer, under the terms of item II
  of the caput of art. 57 of this Complementary Law.

       § 8 The IBS and CBS presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article may be used for deduction, respectively, from the amount of IBS and
  CBS owed by the taxpayer, with reimbursement permitted as provided in Section X of Chapter II of Title I of this Book.

         § 9 The right to appropriate and use the presumed credit referred to in this article also applies to a cooperative society in relation to the receipt
  of goods and services from its members that are not IBS and CBS taxpayers under art. 164 of this Complementary Law and are not opting for Simples Nacional,
  including in the case of opting for the specific regime referred to in art. 271 of this Complementary Law, except where the good is sent for
  processing at the cooperative and returned to the member.

        § 10. Exceptionally, from 2027 to 2031, the period referred to in item III of § 5 may be less than 5 (five) years, depending on the availability of
  information.

                                                                                   CHAPTER VIII

                                               INDEPENDENT INDIVIDUAL CARGO TRANSPORTER NOT A TAXPAYER

         Art. 169. A taxpayer of IBS and CBS subject to the regular regime may appropriate presumed credits of such taxes relating to the purchase of
  cargo transport services from an independent individual transporter who is not a taxpayer of such taxes or who is registered as a MEI (Individual Micro-Entrepreneur). Effects
  pending.

        § 1 The presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article:

        I - apply only to a taxpayer that acquires goods and services and bears the charge for the value of the cargo transport service;

        II - do not apply to a taxpayer that acquires goods and services and bears the charge for the value of the transport as part of the value of the transaction, even if
  specified separately in the documents relating to the purchase.

        § 2 The electronic tax document relating to the purchase shall itemize:

        I - the value of the transaction, corresponding to the amount paid to the supplier;

        II - the amount of the presumed credit; and

        III - the net amount for tax purposes, corresponding to the difference between the amounts itemized in items I and II of this paragraph.

        § 3 The amount of the presumed credit referred to in item II of § 2 of this article shall be the result of applying the percentages referred to in § 4 of this article
  to the value of the transaction referred to in item III of § 2 of this article.

        § 4 The percentages shall be defined and disclosed annually by September, by joint act of the Minister of State for Finance and the IBS Management
  Committee, and shall enter into force as of January 1 of the following year.

        § 5 The definition of the percentages referred to in § 4:

        I - shall be carried out, as provided in the regulation, based on available tax information;

        II - shall result from the proportion between:

        a) the amount of IBS and CBS charged in relation to the total value of purchases made by the transporters referred to in the caput of this article; and

        b) the total value referred to in item III of § 2 of this article in relation to the services supplied by the transporters referred to in the caput of this article; and

        III - shall be based on transactions carried out in the calendar year prior to that of the disclosure period provided for in § 4 of this article.

         § 6 For the purposes of § 5 of this article, purchases of goods and services for personal use and consumption referred to in item I of the caput of art. 57 shall
  not be considered, nor shall the purchase of goods and services intended for the personal use and consumption of the transporter or of persons related to the transporter, under the terms of
  item II of the caput of art. 57 of this Complementary Law.

        § 7 The IBS and CBS presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article may only be used for deduction, respectively, from the amount of IBS
  and CBS owed by the taxpayer.

        § 8 The right to appropriate and use the presumed credit referred to in this article also applies to a cooperative society in relation to the receipt
  of cargo transport services from its members that are independent individual transporters and are not IBS and CBS taxpayers, including in the case of
  opting for the specific regime referred to in art. 271 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                    CHAPTER IX

          WASTE AND OTHER MATERIALS INTENDED FOR RECYCLING, REUSE OR REVERSE LOGISTICS ACQUIRED FROM AN INDIVIDUAL,
                                        COOPERATIVE OR OTHER FORM OF GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATION

        Art. 170. A taxpayer of IBS and CBS subject to the regular regime may appropriate presumed credits of such taxes relating to purchases of
  solid waste from incentivized collectors for use in an environmentally appropriate final disposal process. Effects pending.

        § 1 For the purposes of the caput of this article, the following are considered:


        I - solid waste: material, substance, object or good discarded resulting from human activities in society, for which final disposal is carried out, proposed
  to be carried out or is required to be carried out, in solid or semi-solid states, as well as gases contained in containers and liquids whose particularities
  make it unviable for them to be discharged into the public sewage network or into bodies of water or that require technically or economically unviable solutions
  given the best available technology;

        II - incentivized collectors:

       a) an individual who carries out the collection or sorting of solid waste and sale to an IBS and CBS taxpayer that gives it environmentally
  appropriate final disposal;

        b) an association or cooperative of individuals that exclusively carries out the activity mentioned in item "a" of this item; and

        c) an association or cooperative that exclusively brings together the persons referred to in item "b" of this item;

        III - environmentally appropriate final disposal: disposal of solid waste for reuse, recycling, composting and recovery, as well as, as
  provided in the regulation, other forms of disposal permitted by the competent agencies, including final disposal.

        § 2 The presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article may only be used for deduction, respectively, from the amount of IBS and CBS
  owed by the taxpayer, and shall be calculated by applying the following percentages to the value of the purchase recorded in a document accepted by the
  tax administration as provided in the regulation:

        I - for the IBS presumed credit:

        a) in 2029, 1.3% (one point three percent);

        b) in 2030, 2.6% (two point six percent);

        c) in 2031, 3.9% (three point nine percent);

        d) in 2032, 5.2% (five point two percent);

        e) as of 2033, 13% (thirteen percent); and

        II - for the CBS presumed credit, 7% (seven percent).

        § 3 The IBS and CBS presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article shall not be granted for purchases of:

        I - agricultural pesticides, their residues and packaging;

        II - industrialized and compounded medicines for human home use and, subject to criteria established in the regulation, their packaging;

        III - batteries and cells;

        IV - tires;

        V - electronic products for domestic use and their components;

        VI - lubricating oils, their residues and packaging;

        VII - fluorescent, sodium vapor, mercury vapor and mixed light lamps; and

        VIII - copper scrap.

        § 4 The provisions of item VI of § 3 of this article do not apply to purchases of used or contaminated lubricating oil by a re-refiner or collector authorized
  by the National Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANP) to carry out collection, and the granting of IBS and CBS presumed credits
  as provided in this Chapter is permitted.

                                                                                  CHAPTER X

                                   USED MOVABLE GOODS ACQUIRED FROM A NON-TAXPAYER INDIVIDUAL FOR RESALE
        Art. 171. The taxpayer of IBS and CBS subject to the regular regime may appropriate presumed credits of the said taxes relative to acquisitions, for
  resale, of used movable property from a natural person who is not a taxpayer of the said taxes or who is registered as MEI. Effects to take place

         § 1º The presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article shall be calculated by applying the following percentages to the value of the acquisition
  recorded in a document accepted by the tax administration in the form of the regulation:

          I - for the IBS presumed credit, the percentage equivalent to the sum of the IBS rates applicable to operations with movable property referred to in the caput of this
  article, fixed by the Municipality and by the State where the establishment in which the acquisition was carried out is located, in effect:

        a) on the date of resale, for acquisitions made until December 31, 2032;

        b) on the date of acquisition, for acquisitions made as of January 1, 2033;

        II - for the CBS presumed credit, the CBS rate applicable to operations with the movable property referred to in the caput of this article, fixed by the Union and
  in effect:

        a) on the date of resale, for acquisitions made until December 31, 2026;

        b) on the date of acquisition, for acquisitions made as of January 1, 2027.

         § 2º The presumed credits referred to in the caput of this article may only be used to deduct, respectively, the IBS and the CBS owed by the
  taxpayer, upon resale of the used property on which the respective credits were calculated.

        § 3º The regulation shall govern the manner of appropriation of the presumed credits in the event that it is not possible to link such credits to the used
  property resold.

        § 4º For purposes of this article, used movable property is considered to be that which has been the object of supply for final consumption by a natural person and
  has returned to commercialization.

                                                                                    TITLE V

                                                                SPECIFIC REGIMES OF IBS AND CBS

                                                                                  CHAPTER I
                                                                              FUELS

                                                                                     Section I

                                                                              General Provisions

          Art. 172. IBS and CBS shall be levied only once on operations, even if initiated abroad, with the following fuels, regardless of their
  purpose:

        I - gasoline;

        I - gasoline and its streams;        (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - anhydrous fuel ethanol (EAC);

        III - diesel oil;

        III - diesel oil and its streams;     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        IV - biodiesel (B100);

        V - liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), including liquefied gas derived from natural gas (GLGN);

        VI - hydrated fuel ethanol (EHC);

        VII - aviation kerosene;

        VIII - fuel oil;

        IX - processed natural gas;

        X - biomethane;

        XI - vehicular natural gas (GNV); and

       XII - other fuels specified and authorized by the National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP), listed in a joint act
  of the IBS Management Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union.

         § 1º For purposes of items I and III of the caput of this article, "streams" are considered to be liquid hydrocarbons derived from petroleum and liquid
  hydrocarbons derived from natural gas used in mechanical blending for the production of gasoline or diesel, in accordance with the rules established by the
  ANP.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º A joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS shall provide for cases of suspension of the IBS and the CBS levied on operations with liquid hydrocarbons derived
  from non-fuel petroleum or from natural gas, including naphtha, provided that: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the acquirers are petrochemical central plants duly authorized by the ANP;         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - they are used as an input by the petrochemical industry; and     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        III - they comply with the criteria and conditions established in the said joint act.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 3º A joint act of the CGIBS and the Executive Branch of the Union may postpone the implementation of the specific regime for the fuels referred to in
  items IX, X and XI of the caput of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                     Section II

                                                                              Of the Tax Base

        Art. 173. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS shall be the quantity of fuel that is the object of the operation.

        § 1º The quantity of fuel shall be measured according to the unit of measurement proper to each fuel.

       § 2º The value of the IBS and the CBS, under the terms of this Chapter, shall correspond to the multiplication of the tax base by the specific rate applicable to each
  fuel.

                                                                                    Section III

                                                                                 Of the Rates

        Art. 174. The rates of the IBS and the CBS for the fuels referred to in art. 172 of this Complementary Law shall be:

        I - uniform throughout the national territory, specific per unit of measurement and differentiated by product;

         II - adjusted in the year prior to the year they take effect, observing, for their increase, the ninety-day advance notice period provided for in item "c" of item III of the caput
  of art. 150 of the Federal Constitution;

        III - disclosed:

        a) as to the IBS, by the IBS Management Committee;

        b) as to the CBS, by the head of the Executive Branch of the Union.

        § 1º The CBS rates in 2027 shall be fixed so as not to exceed the tax burden levied on fuels of the federal taxes extinguished or
  reduced by Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, calculated under the terms of § 2º of this article.

        § 2º In determining the tax burden referred to in § 1º of this article, the following shall be considered:

         I - the direct tax burden of the contributions provided for in item "b" of item I and in item IV of the caput of art. 195 of the Federal Constitution and of the Contribution
  to the PIS/Pasep referred to in art. 239 of the Federal Constitution, levied on the production, importation and commercialization of fuels, calculated as
  follows:

        a) the tax burden per unit of measurement of the contributions referred to in this item shall be determined for each of the months from July 2025 to June 2026;

        b) the values determined under item "a" of this item shall be adjusted to July 2026 prices, based on the variation of the IPCA, summed and divided
  by 12 (twelve);
         c) the value determined under item "b" of this item shall be updated to 2027 prices by adding a percentage equivalent to the target for
  inflation for 2027, set by the National Monetary Council, in effect in July 2026; and

         II - the indirect tax burden arising from the contributions referred to in item I of this paragraph, from the tax referred to in item IV of the caput of art. 153 of the
  Federal Constitution and from the tax referred to in item V of the caput of the same article on insurance operations, levied on inputs, services and capital
  goods used in the production, importation and commercialization of fuels and not recovered as credit, calculated as follows:

         a) the values shall be determined at 2025 prices and divided by the volume of the respective fuel consumed in the country in 2025, so as to result in the tax
  burden per unit of measurement;

        b) the values determined under item "a" of this item shall be adjusted to July 2026 prices, based on the variation of the IPCA;

         c) the value determined under item "b" of this item shall be updated to 2027 prices by adding a percentage equivalent to the target for
  inflation for 2027, set by the National Monetary Council, in effect in July 2026.

         § 3º For years subsequent to 2027, the CBS rates shall be fixed so as not to exceed the tax burden calculated under § 2º of this article,
  adjusted by a percentage equivalent to the variation of the weighted average sale price to the final consumer, obtained through research carried out by a
  competent agency or based on data from electronic sales invoices to the final consumer, between:

        I - the 12 (twelve) months prior to July of the year preceding the year for which the rate will be fixed; and

        II - the period from July 2025 to June 2026.

        § 4º The IBS rates shall be fixed:

        I - in 2029, so as not to exceed 10% (ten percent) of the tax burden levied on fuels of the state and municipal taxes extinguished or
  reduced by Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, calculated under the terms of § 5º of this article;

        II - in 2030, so as not to exceed 20% (twenty percent) of the tax burden calculated under § 5º, adjusted under § 6º of this article;

        III - in 2031, so as not to exceed 30% (thirty percent) of the tax burden calculated under § 5º, adjusted under § 6º of this article;

        IV - in 2032, so as not to exceed 40% (forty percent) of the tax burden calculated under § 5º, adjusted under § 6º of this article;

        V - as of 2033, so as not to exceed the tax burden calculated under § 5º, adjusted under § 6º of this article.

        § 5º In determining the tax burden referred to in items I to V of § 4º of this article, the following shall be considered:

        I - the direct tax burden of the tax referred to in item II of the caput of art. 155 of the Federal Constitution levied on the production, importation and commercialization
  of fuels, calculated as follows:

        a) the tax burden per unit of measurement of the tax referred to in this item shall be determined for each of the months from July 2027 to June 2028;

        b) the values determined under item "a" of this item shall be adjusted to July 2028 prices, based on the variation of the IPCA, summed and divided
  by 12 (twelve);

         c) the value determined under item "b" of this item shall be updated to 2029 prices by adding a percentage equivalent to the target for
  inflation for 2029, set by the National Monetary Council, in effect in July 2028; and

         II - the indirect tax burden arising from the taxes referred to in item II of the caput of art. 155 and item III of the caput of art. 156 of the Federal Constitution,
  levied on inputs, services and capital goods used in the production, importation and commercialization of fuels and not recovered as credit,
  calculated as follows:

         a) the values shall be determined at 2027 prices and divided by the volume of the respective fuel consumed in the country in 2027, so as to result in the tax
  burden per unit of measurement;

        b) the values determined under item "a" of this item shall be adjusted to July 2028 prices, based on the variation of the IPCA;

         c) the value determined under item "b" of this item shall be updated to 2029 prices by adding a percentage equivalent to the target for
  inflation for 2029, set by the National Monetary Council, in effect in July 2028.

         § 6º For years subsequent to 2029, the IBS rate shall be fixed so as not to exceed the tax burden calculated under § 5º of this article,
  adjusted by a percentage equivalent to the variation of the weighted average sale price to the final consumer, obtained through research carried out by a
  competent agency or based on data from electronic sales invoices to the final consumer, between:

        I - the 12 (twelve) months prior to July of the year preceding the year for which the rate will be fixed; and

        II - the period from July 2027 to June 2028.

        § 7º The methodology for calculating the tax burden for fixing the rates under §§ 1º and 4º of this article shall be approved by joint act of the Minister
  of State for Finance and the IBS Management Committee.

        § 8º The calculations for fixing the rates, based on the methodology referred to in § 7º of this article, shall be carried out, for the CBS, by the RFB and, for the IBS,
  by the IBS Management Committee.

         § 9º The Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities shall provide the IBS Management Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union the
  subsidies necessary for the calculation of the IBS and CBS rates on fuels, by sharing data and information.

        § 10. The IBS rate calculated under §§ 4º to 6º of this article shall be distributed between the state IBS rate and the municipal IBS rate
  proportionally to their respective reference rates.

        § 11. In relation to the fuels referred to in item XII of the caput of art. 172 of this Complementary Law, the same rate shall be applied as observed for the
  fuel with the closest purpose, among those provided for in items I to XI of the caput of the said article, weighted by the respective energy
  equivalence, observing, in the case of biofuels, the provisions of art. 175.

        § 12. In the case of the fuels listed in the items of the caput of art. 172 that have their rates reduced during the period from March to June
  2026, the rates in effect in February 2026 shall be considered, for purposes of determining the direct tax burden under item I of § 2º of this article, for the months in which
  there is a reduction. (Included by Complementary Law No. 235, of 2026)

        Art. 175. Biofuels and low carbon emission hydrogen are hereby assured taxation lower than that levied on fossil fuels, so
  as to guarantee the competitive differential established in item VIII of § 1º of art. 225 of the Federal Constitution.

         § 1º The IBS and CBS rates relative to biofuels and low carbon emission hydrogen may not be lower than 40% (forty
  percent) and may not exceed 90% (ninety percent) of the rates levied on the respective compared fossil fuels.


        § 2º The reduced taxation referred to in this article shall be established taking into account, under the terms of the regulation:

        I - the energy equivalence, market prices and units of measurement of the compared fuels;

        II - the potential for reduction of environmental impacts of biofuels or of low carbon emission hydrogen in relation to the fossil fuels
  which they replace or with which they are blended.

         § 3º In relation to hydrated fuel ethanol (EHC), the differential referred to in the caput of this article shall be, at a minimum, that existing between the direct and indirect
  tax burden defined in §§ 2º and 5º of art. 174 of this Complementary Law on the said fuel and on gasoline C in the period from July 1, 2023 to
  June 30, 2024, for the following taxes:

        I - Contribution to the PIS/Pasep and Contribution for the Financing of Social Security (Cofins), for the CBS; and

      II - Tax on Operations relative to the Circulation of Goods and on the Provision of Interstate and Intermunicipal Transportation and
  Communication Services (ICMS), for the IBS.

         § 4º The calculation of the tax burden referred to in § 3º of this article shall be carried out based on the rates in effect on July 1, 2024, weighted by the sales volume
  of the respective products in each unit of the Federation and taking into account the Weighted Average Price to the Final Consumer (PMPF) observed in the period
  between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024.

        § 5º The differential referred to in § 3º of this article shall be:

       I - in 2027, for the CBS, and in 2029, for the IBS, the difference in burden referred to in § 3º of this article in percentage and absolute terms per unit of
  measurement;

        II - in subsequent calendar years, updated in accordance with the system established for the IBS and CBS rates in art. 174 of this Complementary Law.

        § 6º An act of the Federal Executive Branch may reduce the specific rates per unit of measurement of the CBS for biodiesel (B100) produced with raw
  material acquired from family farming.

                                                                                    Section IV

                                                                              Of Tax Liability

        Art. 176. Taxpayers of the specific IBS and CBS regime referred to in this Chapter are:

        I - the domestic producer of biofuels;

        II - the petroleum refinery and its bases;

        III - the petrochemical raw material central (CPQ);

       IV - the natural gas processing unit (UPGN) and the producing and industrial establishment treated as equivalent to it, defined and authorized by a competent
  agency;

        V - the fuel formulator;

        VI - the importer; and

        VII - any producing agent not referred to in items I to VI of this caput, authorized by a competent agency.

        § 1º The provisions of this article also apply to the fuel distributor in its operations as importer.

        § 2º A cooperative of ethanol producers authorized by a competent agency is treated as equivalent to a domestic producer of biofuels.

        Art. 177. In operations carried out directly with the taxpayers referred to in art. 176 of this Complementary Law, the acquirer shall be jointly and severally
  liable for payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on the operation, under the terms provided for in this article.

        § 1º The liability referred to in the caput:

         I - does not apply in the event that the payment transaction has been settled by an electronic instrument that allows the collection of the IBS and the CBS at the
  financial settlement of the operation (split payment), under the terms of arts. 31 to 35 of this Complementary Law;

        II - is limited to the amount of the IBS and the CBS not extinguished by the taxpayer, in the manner of items I and II of the caput of art. 27 of this Complementary Law;

         III - extends to the other participants in the economic chain, not referred to in the caput, who carry out operations subsequent to the single-phase taxation
  referred to in this Chapter, if there is proof that they contributed to the non-payment of the IBS and the CBS owed by the taxpayer.

        § 2º For purposes of defining the amount referred to in item II of § 1º, the chronological order provided for in item I of the
  single paragraph of art. 27 of this Complementary Law shall be observed in each assessment period.

                                                                                    Section V

                                                             Of Operations with Anhydrous Fuel Ethanol (EAC)

        Art. 178. Responsibility for the withholding and collection of the IBS and the CBS levied on imports of EAC or on outflows from the EAC producing establishment
  is hereby attributed to the petroleum refinery or its bases, the CPQ, the fuel formulator and the importer, in relation to the percentage of
  biofuel used in the blend, in operations with gasoline A.

        Art. 179. In operations with EAC:

        I - the acquirer of EAC intended for blending with gasoline A who carries out the outflow of the biofuel for a different destination is required to collect the IBS and the
  CBS levied on the biofuel;
