        II - the fuel distributor that carries out blending of EAC with gasoline A in a percentage:

        a) higher than mandatory, shall be required to collect the IBS and the CBS referred to in art. 172 of this Complementary Law in relation to the volume of biofuel
  corresponding to the amount exceeding the mandatory blending percentage; and

        b) lower than mandatory, shall be entitled to reimbursement of the IBS and the CBS referred to in art. 172 of this Complementary Law in relation to the volume of
  biofuel corresponding to the amount blended less than the mandatory blending percentage.

                                                                                    Section VI

                                       Of Credits on the Acquisition of Fuels Subject to the Single-Phase Taxation Regime
         Art. 180. Appropriation of credits in relation to acquisitions of fuels subject to the single levy of the IBS and the CBS is prohibited, when
  intended for distribution, commercialization or resale.

         § 1º Except for the cases provided for in the caput of this article, the taxpayer under the regular regime may appropriate IBS and CBS credits in relation to the
  acquisition of fuels, under the terms of § 4º of art. 47 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The right to appropriate and use IBS and CBS credits relative to the acquisitions referred to in this Section, in the manner of § 1º of this article,
  is hereby assured to the fuel exporter.

                                                                                  CHAPTER II

                                                                        OF FINANCIAL SERVICES

                                                                                     Section I

                                                                              General Provisions

        Art. 181. Financial services are subject to a specific regime of levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

        Art. 182. For purposes of this Complementary Law, the following are considered financial services:

         I - credit operations, including fund-raising and on-lending operations, advances, loans, financing, discounting of instruments, recovery of
  credits and provision of guarantees, with the exception of securitization, factoring and early settlement of receivables of payment arrangements, referred to,
  respectively, in items IV, V and IX of the caput of this article;

        II - foreign exchange operations;

        III - operations with securities, including acquisition, trading, settlement, custody, brokerage, distribution and other forms of
  intermediation, as well as the activity of investment advisor and securities consultant;

        IV - securitization operations;

        V - factoring operations;

         VI - leasing, operating or financial, of any goods, including the assignment of rights and obligations, substitution of guarantee,
  amendment, cancellation and registration of contract and other services related to leasing;

        VII - consortium administration;

        VIII - management and administration of resources, including investment funds;

        IX - payment arrangements, including operations of the arrangement instituting entities and the payment institutions and the early settlement of receivables of these arrangements;

         IX - payment arrangements, including operations of the arrangement instituting entities and the payment institutions, the early settlement of receivables of these
  arrangements and the administration of loyalty programs; (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        X - activities of entities administering organized markets, market infrastructures and central depositories;

        XI - insurance operations, with the exception of health insurance referred to in Chapter III of this Title;

        XII - reinsurance operations;

        XIII - private pension, composed of administration and management operations of open and closed supplementary pension plans;

        XIV - capitalization operations;

        XV - intermediation of consortiums, insurance, reinsurance, supplementary pension and capitalization; and

        XVI - virtual asset services.

        XVII - mutual asset protection operations.      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Single paragraph. This specific regime applies to the entirety of the consideration for the financial services provided for in items I to XVI of the caput
  of this article, regardless of their nomenclature.

        Art. 183. Financial services are subject to the specific regime of this Chapter when provided by natural and legal persons supervised
  by the government agencies that make up the National Financial System and by the other suppliers referred to in this article, subject to the provisions of art. 184.

        § 1º The natural and legal persons supervised referred to in the caput of this article, at the date of publication of this Complementary Law, are the following:

        I - banks of any kind;

        II - savings banks (caixas econômicas);

        III - credit cooperatives;

        IV - foreign exchange brokers;

        V - securities brokers;

        VI - securities distributors;

        VII - administrators and managers of securities portfolios, including investment funds;

        VIII - investment advisors;

        IX - securities consultants;

        X - correspondents registered with the Central Bank of Brazil;

        XI - consortium administrators;

        XII - brokers and other consortium intermediaries;

        XIII - direct credit companies;
        XIV - person-to-person lending companies;

        XV - development agencies;

        XVI - savings and loan associations;

        XVII - mortgage companies;

        XVIII - credit, financing and investment companies;

        XIX - real estate credit companies;

        XX - leasing companies;

        XXI - credit companies for microentrepreneurs and small businesses;

        XXII - payment institutions;

         XXIII - entities administering organized securities markets, including stock exchange and organized over-the-counter markets, clearing and
  settlement entities, central depositories and other financial market infrastructure entities;

        XXIV - insurance companies;

        XXV - reinsurers, including local reinsurers, admitted reinsurers and occasional reinsurers;

        XXVI - open supplementary pension entities and closed entities that do not meet the requirements mentioned in art. 26, § 9o, of this Complementary Law;

        XXVII - capitalization companies;

        XXVIII - insurance brokers, reinsurance brokers and other intermediaries of insurance, reinsurance, supplementary pension and capitalization; and

        XXIX - virtual asset service providers.

        § 2º Also included among the suppliers referred to in the caput of this article, even if not supervised by the government agencies that make up the
  National Financial System, are:

        I - participants in payment arrangements that are not payment institutions;

        I - participants in payment arrangements and entities that administer loyalty programs that are not payment institutions;
     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - companies whose purpose is the securitization of credits;

        III - factoring companies;

        IV - simple credit companies;

        V - correspondents registered with the Central Bank of Brazil; and

        VI - other suppliers that provide financial services:

        a) in the development of an economic activity;

        b) in a habitual manner or in a volume that characterizes an economic activity; or

        c) in a professional manner, even if the profession is not regulated.

        § 3º The provisions of this Chapter apply to suppliers that:

        I - come to be supervised by the government agencies referred to in the caput of this article after the date of publication of this Complementary Law; or

        II - come to carry out the operations referred to in items I to XVI of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, under the terms of item VI of § 2º of this article,
  even if not supervised by the government agencies referred to in the caput of this article.

        § 4º (VETOED).

         Art. 184. Services that, by regulatory provision, may only be provided by banking financial institutions and are remunerated by fees and
  commissions, including services of opening, maintaining and closing of demand deposit accounts and savings accounts, provision of checks, of withdrawal and of
  transfer of funds, are subject to the general rules of levy of the IBS and the CBS provided for in Title I of this Book.

         § 1º For purposes of the caput of this article, banking financial institutions are considered to be banks of any kind and savings banks, referred
  to in items I and II of § 1º of art. 183 of this Complementary Law.

          § 2º Services for maintaining and closing prepaid and postpaid payment accounts provided by payment institutions and remunerated by a
  fee and commission are also subject to the general rules of levy of the IBS and the CBS provided for in Title I of this Book.

         § 3o Also subject to the general rules of levy of the IBS and the CBS provided for in Title I of this Book and, if applicable, to the differentiated regimes referred to
  in Title IV of this Book, and not subject to the specific regime of this Chapter, are the other services provided by the suppliers referred to
  in art. 183 that are not defined as financial services in art. 182 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                   Section II

                                                               Common Provisions for Financial Services

         Art. 185. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS under the specific regime for financial services shall consist of the revenues of the operations, with the deductions
  provided for in this Chapter.

        Art. 186. Revenues from reversal of provisions and from recovery of credits written off as a loss shall make up the tax base of the IBS and the CBS, provided that
  the respective provision or write-off was deducted from the tax base.

         Art. 187. The deductions from the tax base provided for in this Chapter are limited to operations authorized by a government agency, provided that they are carried out within the
  operational limits provided for in the relevant legislation, with the deduction of any administrative expense being prohibited.



         Art. 188. Cooperative societies that provide financial services and exercise the option referred to in art. 271 of this Complementary Law shall
  reverse the effect of the tax base deductions provided for in this Chapter proportionally to the value that the operations benefited by a reduction to zero of the
  IBS and CBS rates represent of the total operations of the cooperative.

        Art. 189. Unless otherwise provided for in this Chapter, the IBS and CBS rates levied on financial services shall be:

        I - from 2027 to 2033, those fixed in accordance with the rules provided for in art. 233 of this Complementary Law; and

        II - as of 2034, those fixed for 2033.

        § 1º The rates referred to in the caput of this article shall be nationally uniform.

         § 2º The CBS rate and the state, district and municipal IBS rates shall be fixed so as to maintain the proportion between their respective
  reference rates.

        Art. 190. IBS and CBS credits on the acquisition of financial services, in the cases provided for in this Chapter, shall be appropriated based on the
  information provided by the suppliers to the IBS Management Committee and to the RFB, in the manner of the regulation, and shall be subject to the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this
  Complementary Law.

        Art. 191. Entities that carry out the operations with financial services referred to in this Chapter must provide, as an ancillary obligation, in the manner
  of the regulation, information on the operations carried out, without prejudice to a minimum set of information provided for in this Complementary Law.

                                                                                      Section III

                               Of Credit, Foreign Exchange, Securities, Securitization and Factoring Operations

         Art. 192. In credit, foreign exchange, and securities operations, referred to in items I to III of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law,
  for purposes of determining the tax base, the revenues of these operations shall be considered, with the deduction of:

        I - financial expenses with fund-raising;

        II - foreign exchange expenses relative to the operations referred to in item II of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law;

        III - losses in operations with securities referred to in item III of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law;

       IV - financial charges recognized as expenses, even if recorded in shareholders' equity, relative to debt instruments issued by the
  legal entity;

        V - losses incurred in the receipt of credits arising from the activities of financial institutions and other institutions authorized to operate by the
  Central Bank of Brazil in operations with financial services referred to in items I to V of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, and losses on the assignment
  of these credits and on the granting of discounts, provided that they are carried out at market value, also observing, in all cases, the same rules of
  deductibility of the income tax legislation applicable to such losses for assessment periods beginning as of January 1, 2027; and

        V - losses incurred in the receipt of credits arising from the activities of financial institutions and other institutions authorized to operate
  by the Central Bank of Brazil in operations with financial services referred to in items I to III of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, and losses on the
  assignment of these credits and on the granting of discounts, provided that they are carried out at market value, also observing, in all cases, the same rules
  of deductibility of the income tax legislation applicable to such losses for assessment periods beginning as of January 1, 2027; and
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        VI - expenses with investment advisors, securities consultants and correspondents registered with the Central Bank of Brazil, relative to the
  operations referred to in items I to III of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, provided that these services were not rendered by employees or
  officers of the company.

        § 1o The concept of revenues of the operations:

        I - does not include the value of the principal, in the case of credit operations;

        II - corresponds to the difference between the disposal value of the asset and its acquisition cost, in the case of disposal of securities.

        § 2o Financial expenses with fund-raising do not include payment of the principal.

         § 3º In the event of a reversal for any reason, offsetting the shareholders' equity account referred to in item IV of the caput of this article, the values
  previously deducted must be added to the tax base.

        § 4º The provisions of item IV of the caput of this article do not apply to equity instruments, such as shares, share deposit certificates and subscription
  warrants.

       § 5º The revenues and expenses computed in the tax base referred to in the caput of this article include monetary variations due to the exchange rate,
  when the result of the operations varies according to the quotation of foreign currency.

         § 6º Revenues and expenses recognized in offsetting fair value measurement, to the extent that they exceed the yield produced in the operations referred to in
  item III of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, must be disclosed in a subaccount and computed in the tax base at the time of the
  realization of the respective asset or liability.

        § 7º Revenues and expenses with derivative financial instruments contracted by the entities that carry out the operations provided for in this article shall also
  be computed in the tax base.

        § 8º Revenues from the services referred to in the caput of this article do not include, with the deduction of the respective fund-raising financial expenses being prohibited for purposes of
  determining the tax base, those earned in credit operations carried out between the cooperative and the member:

        I - with the cooperative's own resources or those of the members; or

        II - with public resources, earmarked, equalized or from official or constitutional funds.

         Art. 193. Securitization and factoring operations referred to in items IV and V of the caput of art. 182 are subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS at the rate provided for
  in this Section.

        § 1º The tax base of the IBS and the CBS shall correspond to the discount applied at early settlement, with the deduction of:

        I - financial expenses with fund-raising;

        II - securitization expenses, consisting of issuance, distribution, custody, bookkeeping, registration, preparation and formalization of documents, administration
  of the segregated assets and activity of fiduciary agents, collection agents and risk classification agents, provided that these services were not rendered by
  employees or officers of the company.

        § 2º The losses incurred in the receipt of credits and the losses on the assignment of these credits and on the granting of discounts may be deducted from the tax base referred to in § 1º,
  provided that they are carried out at market value.

        § 3º The losses referred to in § 2º that cannot be fully deducted from the tax base of a given assessment period, because they exceed the
  taxable values in such period, may be deducted in subsequent periods.

       § 4º The National Monetary Council and the Central Bank of Brazil, within their respective competencies, shall regulate the rules for qualification and
  disqualification with respect to the requirements provided for in this article.

        § 5o The provisions of this article apply to the Receivables Investment Fund (FIDC) that early settles commercial receivables through
  discounting of trade notes, promissory notes, checks and other commercial instruments, as defined in regulation to be issued by the National Monetary
  Council, if not classified as an investment entity, in accordance with the provisions of art. 23 of Law No. 14,754, of December 12, 2023, and its
  regulation.

        § 6o Quotaholders of the funds referred to in § 5º of this article are not subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS.

         Art. 194. Taxpayers under the regular regime who are not subject to the specific regime of this Section and are takers of credit operations referred to
  in item I of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law may appropriate IBS and CBS credits at the same rate owed on such credit
  operations, applied to the financial expenses relative to such operations actually paid, on a cash basis, and calculated from the following deductions
  from the amount of each installment, after the date of its payment:

        I - the amount corresponding to the value of the principal contained in each installment, in accordance with the amortization rules provided for in the contract; and

       II - the amount corresponding to the application of the Selic rate on the principal, calculated based on the average interest rate practiced in
  repo operations with federal government securities with a maturity of 1 (one) business day.

        Art. 195. Taxpayers under the regular regime who are not subject to the specific regime of this Section and issue debt instruments, including debentures and
  commercial notes, may appropriate credits in the manner of art. 194, during the period in which the instrument or security is held by a taxpayer under the specific regime
  of this Section.

         § 1º In the case referred to in the caput of this article, when the debt instrument is the object of a public offering, in the manner regulated by the Securities and
  Exchange Commission:

        I - the creditor under the specific regime referred to in this Section shall exclude from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS the amount corresponding to the portion of the interest and
  yield produced by the debt instrument that exceeds the SELIC rate; and

        II - the debtor shall not appropriate credits.

        § 2º The system referred to in § 1º of this article shall also apply to the creditor under the specific regime referred to in this Section that holds the debt instruments
  through an exclusive investment fund, whose portfolio is composed of at least 95% (ninety-five percent) of such instruments.

         Art. 196. The taker of the services of assignment of receivables, advance, discount, securitization and factoring referred to in items I, IV and V of
  the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law who is a taxpayer under the regular regime and is not subject to the specific regime of this Section may appropriate credits
  in these operations, in relation to the portion of the discount applied, at the time of early settlement of the receivable, on a cash basis, that exceeds the DI future
  interest rate curve, for the term of the advance.

        Art. 197. Members that are takers of credit operations with cooperative societies that provide financial services and exercise the option referred to in art. 271
  of this Complementary Law may not appropriate credits in the manner provided for in arts. 194 to 196.

        Art. 197. The following may not appropriate credits in the manner provided for in arts. 194 to 196 of this Complementary Law:           (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

          I - members that are takers of credit operations with cooperative societies that provide financial services and exercise the option referred to
  in art. 271 of this Complementary Law; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - takers of credit operations referenced in foreign currency and issuers of debt instruments referenced in foreign currency,
  subject to the provisions of art. 198 of this Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 198. Taxpayers under the regular regime who are not subject to the specific regime of this Section may appropriate IBS and CBS credits, based on
  the amounts paid by the supplier, on the fees and commissions relative to the operations referred to in items I to V of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law.

        Single paragraph. The provisions of the caput of this article also apply to acquisitions made by entities subject to the specific regime of this Section, provided
  that the respective expense is not deducted from the tax base.

        Art. 199. Appropriation of IBS and CBS credits on the acquisition of financial services referred to in items I to V of the caput of art. 182 of this
  Complementary Law that are not expressly permitted in arts. 194 to 198 is hereby prohibited.

         Art. 200. In the disposal of movable or immovable property that has been the object of a guarantee constituted in favor of a creditor subject to the specific regime of this Section,
  whose ownership has been consolidated by or transferred to it in payment of the debt, the following shall be observed:

        I - the consolidation of ownership of the property by the creditor shall not be subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS; and

        II - in the disposal of the property by the creditor:

        a) there shall be no levy of the IBS and the CBS, if the guarantee provider is not a taxpayer of these taxes; or

        b) there shall be levy of the IBS and the CBS under the same assessment rules that would be applicable if the disposal had been carried out directly by the
  guarantee provider, if the latter is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 1º The same rules relative to the IBS and the CBS that would be applicable if the disposal had been carried out by the guarantee provider shall apply to the acquirer.

         § 2º For purposes of any refund by the creditor to the guarantee provider of the amount of the disposal in excess of the debt, the disposal value of the
  property net of the IBS and the CBS shall be considered.

                                                                                     Section IV

                                                                          Of Leasing

        Art. 201. For purposes of determining the tax base, in leasing referred to in item VI of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law:

        I - service revenues shall be subject, to the extent of receipt, on a cash basis:

        a) in relation to installments of the consideration for operating leasing, at the following rates:


        1. in the case of immovable property, at the rate applicable to leasing/rental, under the respective specific regime; and

        2. in the case of other goods, at the rate applicable to the rental of the good;

        b) in relation to the disposal of a good that is the object of operating leasing, at the following rates:

        1. in the case of immovable property, at the rate applicable to sale, under the respective specific regime; and

        2. in the case of other goods, at the rate applicable to the sale of the good;

        c) in relation to installments of the consideration for financial leasing, at the rate provided for in art. 189 of this Complementary Law;

        d) in relation to the residual value of the leased good, the guaranteed residual value, even if paid in installments, agreed in the financial leasing contract,
  paid upon the effective exercise of the purchase option, at the following rates:

        1. in the case of immovable property, at the rate applicable to sale, under the respective specific regime; and

        2. in the case of other goods, at the rate provided for in the general levy rules referred to in Title I of this Book applicable to the sale of the good;

        II - the deduction shall be allowed, in proportion to the share of revenues obtained in operations that do not generate IBS and CBS credits for the lessee
  in relation to the total revenues from leasing operations:

        a) of financial expenses with fund-raising used in leasing operations;

        b) of leasing expenses;

        c) of provisions for doubtful debts relative to leasing operations, subject to the provisions of item V of the caput of art. 192
  of this Complementary Law. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Single paragraph. For purposes of the levy of the IBS and the CBS on financial leasing:

         I - the consideration taxed under item "c" of item I of the caput of this article must be measured taking into account the effects of the present value adjustments
  of the payment flow of the leasing contract, at the rate equivalent to the financial charges, duly disclosed in accounting accounts;

        II - the portion taxed under item "d" of item I of the caput shall correspond, at a minimum, to the acquisition cost of the leased good or service,
  regardless of the amount provided for in the contract, the same rule applying if the good is sold to a third party;

        III - the sum of the installments taxed under items "c" and "d" of item I of the caput of this article must correspond to the total amount received by the
  lessor for the financial leasing and sale of the good, during the entire term of the operation.

       Art. 202. If the legal entity records revenues from financial services referred to in items I to VI of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, the
  fund-raising financial expenses shall be deducted from the tax base in proportion to the revenues of each type.

        Art. 203. The party to a leasing contract that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime and is not subject to the specific regime
  of this Section may use credits of these taxes based on the amount of the installments of the leasing consideration and the residual value of the good,
  to the extent of actual payment, on a cash basis, at the same rate owed on these services.

                                                                                   Section V

                                                                       Of Consortium Administration

         Art. 204. In consortium administration referred to in item VII of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, for purposes of determining the tax base,
  the service revenues comprise all fees, commissions and charges, as well as the respective surcharges, penalties and interest, arising from a contract of
  participation in a consortium group, actually paid, on a cash basis.

         § 1º The consortium administrator may deduct from the tax base the amounts referring to the intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of
  art. 182 of this Complementary Law.

         § 2º Acquisitions of goods and services by a consortium member with a consortium credit letter are subject to the rules provided for in the general levy rules
  referred to in Title I of this Book, except in the case of immovable property, which is subject to the respective specific regime, and other goods or services subject to a
  differentiated or specific regime, under the terms of this Complementary Law, with the consortium administrator not being liable for these taxes.

        § 3º In the execution of a guarantee of a consortium member, with receipt of the amounts by the consortium group, the following shall be observed:

        I - the consolidation of ownership of the good by the consortium group shall not be subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS;

        II - in the disposal of the good by the consortium group:

        a) there shall be no levy of the IBS and the CBS, if the consortium member is not a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS;

        b) there shall be levy of the IBS and the CBS under the same rules that would be applicable if the disposal had been carried out by the consortium member, if the latter is a taxpayer
  of the IBS and the CBS;

        III - the same rules relative to the IBS and the CBS that would be applicable if the disposal had been carried out by the consortium member shall apply to the acquirer; and

        IV - the consortium administrator shall be subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS on the remuneration for the service rendered and shall not be liable for the taxes
  owed by the consortium member under item "b" of item II of this paragraph.

        Art. 205. The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime that acquires consortium administration services may appropriate IBS and CBS credits based
  on the amounts paid to the supplier for these services.

       Art. 206. Consortium intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law shall be subject to the levy of the IBS and
  the CBS on the value of the operation, at the same rates applicable to consortium administration services.

        § 1º Providers of consortium intermediation services that are Simples Nacional participants:

        I - shall remain taxed in accordance with the Simples Nacional rules, when they do not exercise the option for the regular IBS and CBS regime; and

        II - shall be subject to the same IBS and CBS rates applicable to consortium administration services, when they exercise the option for the
  regular IBS and CBS regime.

         § 2º Credits on intermediation operations may be used by acquirers that are taxpayers under the regular regime, provided that the
  intermediation supplier identifies the destination acquirers, based on the amounts of the IBS and the CBS paid by the intermediary and applying the provisions of
  arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.
                                                                                        Section VI

                                                 Of the Management and Administration of Resources, including Investment Funds

       Art. 207. The management and administration of resources referred to in item VIII of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law are subject to the levy of the IBS and the
  CBS under a specific regime, in accordance with the provisions of this Section.

         Art. 208. The IBS and CBS rates on services provided to investment funds that are not financial services referred to in art. 182
  of this Complementary Law shall follow the general levy rules of the IBS and the CBS provided for in Title I of this Book and, if applicable, the
  differentiated regimes referred to in Title IV of this Book.

         Art. 209. The investment fund and its quotaholders may not use IBS and CBS credits owed by the suppliers of any goods or
  services to the fund, except as provided for in the single paragraph of this article.

         Single paragraph. If the investment fund is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime, the fund may appropriate credits on its
  acquisitions of goods and services, subject to the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 210. The investment fund administrator and the distributor acting on behalf of and for the account of quotas of an investment fund must submit, in the manner
  of the regulation, as an ancillary obligation, information on the investment fund and each quotaholder, or on the distributor acting on behalf of and for the account of, or on the central depository
  if the quota is traded on a stock exchange, and the value of its quotas, without prejudice to other information that the regulation may require.

       Single paragraph. The IBS Management Committee may enter into an agreement with public administration agencies to have access to the information provided for in the caput,
  and may, in such case, exempt the administrator and the distributor from the ancillary obligation referred to in the caput of this article.

         Art. 211. Management and administration of resources services provided to the investor and not to the investment fund, as in the management of
  managed portfolios, are subject to the IBS and the CBS at the rates provided for in art. 189 of this Complementary Law, with the IBS and CBS credit being prohibited for the acquirer of the
  services.

                                                                                        Section VII

                         Of the Severance Indemnity Fund (FGTS) and other Guarantee Funds and Public Policy Executing Funds

        Art. 212. Operations related to the Severance Indemnity Fund (FGTS) are subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS, at a
  nationally uniform rate, to be fixed so as to maintain the tax burden levied on these operations.

        Art. 212. Operations related to the Severance Indemnity Fund (FGTS) are subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS, at
  nationally uniform rates, calculated under the terms of item II of § 1º of art. 10 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023. (Wording given
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 1º The FGTS is not a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS.

          § 2º Operations related to the FGTS are those necessary for the application of Law No. 8,036, of May 11, 1990, carried out:

          I - by the FGTS operating agent;

          II - by the FGTS financial agents; and

          III - by the other banking establishments.

          § 3º The following are subject to:

          I - a zero rate of the IBS and the CBS, the operations provided for in item I of § 2º of this article;

          I - in the case of the operations provided for in item I of § 2º of this article, a zero rate of the IBS and the CBS;          (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

          II - the rates necessary to maintain the tax burden, the operations provided for in items II and III of § 2º of this article.

        II - in the case of the operations provided for in items II and III of § 2º of this article, the IBS and CBS rates that shall be fixed so that the sum of the
  rates corresponds to: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) in 2027, to 1.0% (one percent);      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) in 2028, to 1.0% (one percent);      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          c) in 2029, to 1.2% (one point two percent);       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          d) in 2030, to 1.4% (one point four percent);        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          e) in 2031, to 1.6% (one point six percent);       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          f) in 2032, to 1.8% (one point eight percent); and      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          g) as of 2033, to 3.0% (three percent).   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 4º Observing, each year, the proportion between the CBS and IBS rates under the terms of § 2º of art. 189 of this Complementary Law, the CBS
  and IBS rates shall be fixed so that the sum of the rates corresponds to the percentage fixed in the items of item II of § 3º of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

        § 5º The provisions of Section III of this Chapter II apply to the operations referred to in items II and III of § 2º of this article, insofar as they are not
  contrary thereto. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 6º The provisions of § 6º of art. 233 apply to the rates referred to in item II of § 3º of this article.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 7º The rates referred to in item II of § 3º of this article shall be levied on the value of the financial services related to the FGTS, excluding:         (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - the IBS and the CBS; and   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - the tax referred to in art. 156, item III, of the Federal Constitution.   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)
         Art. 213. Operations related to other guarantee and public-policy-executing funds are not subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS,
  including housing and regional development funds, provided for by law.



        § 1º Operations related to the guarantee and executing funds referred to in the caput of this article include administration and
  operationalization services provided to the fund.

        § 2º The funds referred to in the caput of this article are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS.

       § 3º The provisions of this article also apply to the funds referred to in the caput that come to be constituted after the date of publication of this Complementary
  Law.

         § 4º It shall be incumbent on a joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the RFB to list the guarantee and public-policy-executing funds provided for by law as of the date of the
  publication of this Complementary Law and to update the list with funds of the same nature that come to be constituted subsequently.

                                                                                   Section VIII

                                                                         Of Payment Arrangements

       Art. 214. The payment arrangement services referred to in item IX of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law are subject to the incidence of the IBS and the
  CBS under a specific regime, in accordance with the provisions of this Section.

        § 1º The services referred to in the caput of this article comprise all of those related to the accreditation, capture, processing and settlement of
  payment transactions and to the other goods and services supplied to the accredited party, to another recipient of the arrangement, and among participants of the arrangement, including:

        I - the arrangement services remunerated by the accredited party by means of a discount fee on payment transactions;

        II - the leasing of electronic terminals and the supply of computer programs (software) that enable the functioning of payment arrangements; and

         III - goods and services supplied by the founders of payment arrangements to the other participants of the arrangement, even if the charge is not linked to
  each payment transaction;

        IV - goods and services imported from card brands by founders and participants of payment arrangements.

         § 2º The legal relationship between the issuer and the holder of the payment instrument is subject to the rules provided for in the general incidence rules referred to in
  Title I of this Book, except for the credit operations referred to in item I of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law, which are subject to their respective specific
  regime.

        § 3º The tax base of the IBS and the CBS owed by taxpayers subject to the specific regime of this Section shall correspond to the gross value of the remuneration
  received directly from the accredited party, plus the amounts received from other participants of the payment arrangement and minus the amounts paid to them.

         § 3º The tax base of the IBS and the CBS owed by taxpayers subject to the specific regime of this Section shall correspond to the gross value of the
  remuneration effectively received from the accredited party, from the founder of the arrangement, or from other participants, guaranteeing the right to the credit corresponding to the amounts
  paid to them, provided that the IBS and CBS debits have been duly extinguished. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 4º The provisions of § 3º of this article apply for purposes of determining the tax base of the participants of the arrangements referred to in the caput of art. 216 of this
  Complementary Law.

         § 5º The income earned as a result of the
  investment of funds available in payment accounts, in accordance with the regulation of the Central Bank of Brazil and the National Monetary Council, also form part of the tax base of the services referred to in the caput of art. 216 of this Complementary Law, minus the
  amounts of income paid in favor of the holders of such accounts.

         § 6º The provisions of § 3º do not imply recognition of the existence of a contracting or subcontracting relationship between the founder of the arrangement and other
  participants, nor the inclusion of the amounts passed on to other participants or to the founder in the tax base of the taxes that will be extinguished as provided for in
  Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         Art. 215. The accredited party shall be considered the recipient of the payment arrangement services related to accreditation, capture, processing and
  settlement of payment transactions.

        Art. 216. The recipient of the service shall be considered the recipient of the services in the case of payment arrangements not provided for in art. 215
  of this Complementary Law.

          Art. 217. Without prejudice to other information required by regulation, participants in payment arrangements shall submit, in the manner provided by the
  regulation, as an ancillary obligation, the following information: (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
          I - in the case of the accrediting entity, the identification of the accredited parties, the gross amounts of remuneration of each accredited party and the amounts passed on to each of the
  other participants of the arrangement; and
          II - in the case of the other participants of the arrangement, the gross amounts of remuneration received from recipients or other participants of the arrangement and the
  amounts paid to other participants of the arrangement.
          Sole paragraph. In the case of a sub-accrediting entity and other companies that come to participate in payment arrangements and are not provided for in items I
  and II of the caput of this article, the form of the ancillary obligations shall be set out in the regulation.

        Art. 218. The accredited party or another recipient of an arrangement that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime may appropriate credits of the IBS and the
  CBS calculated on the basis of the gross amounts of remuneration owed to the accrediting entity or another participant of the arrangement, in the same amounts of the IBS and the CBS
  paid by the participants of the payment arrangement levied on the operations.

        Art. 218-A. To enable the operationalization of the provisions of § 3º of art. 214, the regulation shall:     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         I - provide for specific payment deadlines for the founder and the different participants of the arrangement, including shorter deadlines than those applicable to the
  participants of the arrangement that settle amounts directly to the accredited parties and other recipients of the arrangement; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - establish:   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) cases of withholding of the IBS and the CBS, which shall observe the provisions of art. 36 of this Complementary Law;           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        b) the case in which the founder of the arrangement and the other participants that initiate the financial flow to another participant of the arrangement, including through a
  clearing or settlement chamber, carry out the early extinguishment of the taxes levied on the amount of their own remuneration, by any of the
  methods provided for in art. 27 of this Complementary Law; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        c) that, in cases in which the regulation permits the consolidated recording of operations, the collection document relating to the payment referred to in
  item "a" of this item must identify it. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 1º The taxpayer that settles amounts directly to the accredited parties shall provide the information necessary to attribute to them the IBS and CBS credits
  referred to in art. 218 of this Complementary Law, as well as for the allocation of the proceeds of the collection, in the manner provided by the regulation, exempting the founder of the
  arrangement and the other participants from this obligation. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 2º The regulation of the procedures provided for in this article shall seek to avoid altering the financial and operational flows of the founders and
  other participants of the arrangement. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)


        Art. 219. The early settlement of receivables of payment arrangements shall be taxed by the IBS and the CBS in the manner set out in this article.

         § 1º The tax base of the IBS and the CBS shall correspond to the discount applied in the early settlement, with the deduction of an amount corresponding to the future interest rate curve
  of the DI rate, for the anticipation period.

        § 2º Losses incurred in the receipt of credits and losses on the assignment of such credits and on the
  granting of discounts may be deducted from the tax base referred to in § 1º, provided they are carried out at market value.

        § 3º Losses referred to in § 2º that cannot be fully deducted from the tax base of a given assessment period, because they exceed the
  taxable amounts in such period, may be deducted in subsequent periods.

        § 4º The rate of the IBS and the CBS levied on the operations referred to in the caput of this article shall be equal to the rate applied to the other payment arrangement
  services.

         § 5º The recipient of the early settlement services for receivables of payment arrangements that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime
  may take credit for the IBS and the CBS on such operations, in relation to the portion of the discount applied, at the time of early settlement, on a cash basis, that
  is greater than the future interest rate curve of the DI rate, for the anticipation period.

        § 6º The provisions of this article also apply to the FIDC and other investment funds that early-settle receivables of payment
  arrangements, which shall be considered taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS if they are not classified as investment entities, in accordance with the provisions of art.
  23 of Law No. 14,754, of December 12, 2023, and its regulation.

        § 7º Unit holders of the funds referred to in § 6º of this article are not subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS.

        Art. 219-A. The administration of loyalty programs shall be taxed in the manner set out in this article, in which case:         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        I - the tax base of the IBS and the CBS shall correspond, in each assessment period, to the value of the points issued, minus the amounts paid upon redemption
  of the points and those reimbursed for points not used computed as revenue; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the acquirer of the points shall not be entitled to the IBS and CBS credit.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         Sole paragraph. The specific regime referred to in this article also applies to the issuer's own loyalty programs in which the points are used
  as consideration in the supply of goods and services by the issuer of the points itself, in which case the points used as consideration will be
  deducted from the tax base based on the value considered in setting the tax base of the IBS and the CBS in the operation, under the terms of item III of § 4º of
  art. 12 of this Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                    Section IX

                     Of the Activities of Entities Administering Organized Markets, Market Infrastructures and Central Depositories

        Art. 220. The activities of entities administering organized markets, market infrastructures and central depositories referred to in item X of the
  caput of art. 182 are subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS on the value of the service supply operation, at the rates provided for in art. 189 of this Complementary
  Law.

        Art. 221. The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime that acquires services from entities administering organized markets, market infrastructures
  and central depositories referred to in item X of the caput of art. 182 may appropriate credits of these taxes, based on the amounts paid to the
  supplier.

        Art. 222. Entities administering organized markets, market infrastructures and central depositories shall provide, as an ancillary
  obligation, in the manner provided by the regulation, information on the acquirers of the services and the amounts paid by each one.

                                                                                    Section X

                                                   Of Insurance, Reinsurance, Supplementary Pension Plans and Capitalization

         Art. 223. For purposes of determining the tax base, in insurance and reinsurance operations referred to, respectively, in items XI and XII of the caput
  of art. 182 of this Complementary Law:

        I - the service revenues comprise the following, to the extent effectively received, on a cash basis:

        a) those earned from insurance premiums, accepted coinsurance, reinsurance and retrocession; and

       b) the financial revenues of the financial assets guaranteeing technical provisions, in proportion to the revenues referred to in item "a" in operations that do not
  generate IBS and CBS credits for the acquirers, and the total revenues referred to in item "a" of this item, observing criteria established in the regulation;

        II - the following shall be deducted:

         a) indemnity expenses relating to insurance for elementary lines and for persons without survival coverage, exclusively when relating to
  insured natural or legal persons that are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime, corresponding to claims,
  effectively paid, occurring in insurance operations, after subtracting salvage and other reimbursements;

        b) amounts paid relating to premium refunds that have been computed as revenue, including upon cancellation; and

        c) amounts paid relating to insurance and reinsurance intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law;

        d) amounts paid relating to the premium of ceded coinsurance operations;

        e) the portions of premiums allocated to the constitution of technical provisions or reserves relating to redeemable insurance.

       § 1º The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime that acquires and is the insured party of insurance and reinsurance services may appropriate credits of IBS and
  CBS on the premiums, in the amount of taxes paid on such services.

         § 2º The receipt of the indemnities referred to in item "a" of item II of the caput of this article is not subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS and does not give the right to
  IBS and CBS credit.

         § 3º The portion of the reversal of technical provisions or reserves that is retained by the entity as its own revenue forms part of the tax base referred to in this article
  .

        § 4º Reinsurance and retrocession operations are subject to a zero rate, including when reinsurance and retrocession premiums are
  ceded abroad.

       Art. 224. For purposes of determining the tax base, in supplementary pension plans, open and closed, referred to in item XIII of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary
  Law, and in life insurance with survival coverage:


        I - the service revenues comprise, to the extent effectively received, on a cash basis:

        a) contributions to supplementary pension plans;

        b) premiums for life insurance with survival coverage; and

        c) the fund charge arising from structuring and maintaining supplementary pension plans and life insurance with survival coverage;

        II - the following shall be deducted:

        a) the portions of contributions and premiums allocated to the constitution of technical provisions or reserves;

        b) amounts paid relating to refunds of contributions and premiums that have been computed as revenue, including cancellations;

        c) amounts paid for supplementary pension plan intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law and for
  life insurance intermediation with survival coverage; and

        d) indemnity expenses relating to risk coverages, corresponding to benefits effectively paid, occurring in
  supplementary pension plan operations.

        § 1º The portion of the reversal of technical provisions or reserves retained by the entity as its own revenue forms part of the tax base referred to in this article.

        § 2º Income earned on the investment of financial resources intended for the payment of
  retirement, pension, lump-sum and redemption benefits does not form part of the tax base referred to in this article.

        § 3º The provisions of § 2º of this article apply to income:

        I - from financial investments provided by the assets guaranteeing technical provisions, such assets being limited to the amount of the said provisions; and

        II - from the financial assets guaranteeing the technical provisions of private insurance companies intended exclusively for pension benefit plans
  and for life insurance with survival coverage.

         § 4º Also not forming part of the tax base referred to in this article are the other financial investment income earned by entities that provide
  the activities set out in the caput of this article.

        Art. 225. For purposes of determining the tax base, in capitalization referred to in item XIV of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law:

        I - the service revenues comprise, to the extent effectively received, on a cash basis:

        a) collections from capitalization bonds; and

        b) revenues from lapses and penalties;

        II - the following shall be deducted:

        a) portions of contributions allocated to the constitution of technical provisions or reserves, including provisions for prizes payable;

        b) amounts paid relating to cancellations and refunds of bonds that have been computed as revenue; and

        c) amounts paid for capitalization intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1º The portion of the reversal of technical provisions or reserves retained by the entity as its own revenue forms part of the tax base referred to in this article.

          § 2º Income earned on financial investments intended for the payment of redemption of
  bonds and drawing prizes does not form part of the tax base referred to in this article.

         § 3º The provisions of § 2º of this article are restricted to income from financial investments provided by the assets guaranteeing technical provisions,
  such assets being limited to the amount of the said provisions.

         § 4º Also not forming part of the tax base referred to in this article are the other financial investment income earned by entities that provide
  the activities set out in the caput of this article.

         § 5º The taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime that acquires capitalization bonds may appropriate credits of IBS and CBS in the amount of the
  taxes paid on such service.

        Art. 226. Credit for the IBS and the CBS is prohibited on the acquisition of supplementary pension plan services.

        Art. 227. Without prejudice to other information required by regulation, insurance companies, reinsurers, open and closed supplementary
  pension entities and capitalization companies shall submit, in the manner provided by the regulation, as an ancillary obligation, the following information:

         I - insurance companies and reinsurers, the identification of the insured parties or, in cases where the insured parties are not identified in the insurance contract, of the
  policyholders and the premium amounts paid by each one;

        II - supplementary pension entities, the identification of the participants and the contribution amounts paid by each one; and

        III - capitalization companies, the identification of the holders, subscribers or distributors of the bonds and the amounts collected from the bonds.

        Art. 228. Insurance, reinsurance, supplementary pension plan and capitalization intermediation services referred to in item XV of the caput of art. 182 of this
  Complementary Law shall be subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS on the value of the operation, at the same rate applicable to insurance, reinsurance,
  supplementary pension plan and capitalization services.

        § 1º Providers of insurance, reinsurance, supplementary pension plan and capitalization intermediation services that opt for the Simples
  Nacional:

        I - shall remain taxed in accordance with the Simples Nacional rules, when they do not exercise the option for the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS; and

        II - shall be subject to the same rate of the IBS and the CBS applicable to insurance, reinsurance, supplementary pension plan and capitalization services, when
  they exercise the option for the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 2º Credits from intermediation operations may be used by insured acquirers of the respective insurance and reinsurance and by
  acquirers of capitalization bonds that are taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS in the regular regime, provided that the supplier of the intermediation identifies the
  acquirers and recipients, based on the amounts of the IBS and the CBS paid by the intermediary and applying the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                      Section XI


                                                                        Of Virtual Asset Services

         Art. 229. Virtual asset services referred to in item XVI of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law are subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS on
  the value of the virtual asset service provided.

          § 1º The virtual assets referred to in the caput of this article are digital representations of value that can be traded or transferred by electronic means
  and used to make payments or for investment purposes, under the terms of Law No. 14,478, of December 21, 2022, not including
  digital representations considered securities, which are subject to the provisions of Section III of this Chapter.

         § 2o The acquisition of goods and services with virtual assets is subject to the rules provided for in the general incidence rules referred to in Title I of this
  Book or to the respective differentiated or specific regime applicable to the good or service acquired, under the terms of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 230. The taxpayer in the regular regime that acquires virtual asset services may appropriate credits of the IBS and the CBS, based on the amounts paid to the
  supplier.

                                                                                    Section XII

                                                                    Of the Importation of Financial Services

        Art. 231. Financial services referred to in art. 182 of this Complementary Law, when considered imported, under the terms of Section II of Chapter
  IV of Title I of this Book, are subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS at the same rate applicable to the respective financial services acquired from suppliers
  domiciled in the Country.

        § 1º In the importation of financial services:

        I - the tax base shall be the amount corresponding to the revenue earned by the supplier as a result of the operation, with the application of a reduction factor to
  account for a presumed margin, to be provided for in the regulation, observing the limits established in this Chapter for the tax base deductions of the
  same financial services provided in the Country, when applicable;

         II - in cases where the importer of the financial services is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS subject to the regular regime and is entitled to appropriate
  credits of these taxes on the acquisition of the same financial service in the Country, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, a zero rate shall be applied on importation, and
  IBS and CBS credits shall not be appropriated; and

        III - (VETOED).

         IV - in cases where the importer of the financial services is a taxpayer that carries out the operations referred to in items I to V of the caput of
  art. 182, a zero rate shall be applied on importation, without prejudice to maintaining the right to deduct such expenses from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS,
  in accordance with the provisions of art. 192 of this Complementary Law.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2º The provisions of Chapter IV of Title I of this Book apply to importations of financial services, insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this article.

        § 3º The zero rate provided for in item IV of § 1º of this article does not apply in the case of the importation of financial services from a related party on the
  portion of the value of the operation that exceeds the prices and fees usually practiced under market conditions.              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

                                                                                    Section XIII

                                                                    Of the Exportation of Financial Services

        Art. 232. Financial services referred to in art. 182 of this Complementary Law, when provided to residents or persons domiciled abroad, shall be
  considered exported and shall be immune to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS, for purposes of the provisions of Chapter V of Title I of this Book.

        § 1º An entity that provides financial services in the Country and by way of exportation shall:

        I - in the operations referred to in items I to V of the caput of art. 182 of this Complementary Law:

        a) calculate the proportion of export revenue to total revenue with such financial services;

        b) reverse the effect of the tax base deductions permitted for such financial services in the same proportion referred to in this item; and

         II - in the other operations subject to the specific regime for financial services, make the same calculation provided for in item I of this paragraph,
  taking into account the revenues of operations of each nature, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, and, when applicable, the permission to deduct expenses from the tax
  base of the respective operations.

         § 2º Financial services provided to entities abroad that are branches, subsidiaries or investees, predominantly,
  of residents or persons domiciled in the Country that are not taxpayers of the IBS and the CBS in the regular regime, individually or together with
  related parties, as defined in §§ 2º to 6o of art. 5º of this Complementary Law, are not considered exported.

        § 3º In the case of operations carried out in the financial and capital markets under the terms of the regulation of the National Monetary Council, the provisions of §
  2º of this article shall apply exclusively in cases where information about the entity abroad being controlled or invested in, predominantly, by
  residents or persons domiciled in the Country, is indicated by the legal representative of such entity abroad, in the registry referred to in art. 59 of this Complementary Law,
  as provided for in the regulation.

                                                                                    Section XIV

                                                                            Transitional Provisions

       Art. 233. From 2027 to 2033, the rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on financial services referred to in art. 189 of this Complementary Law shall be set
  so as to maintain the tax burden levied on the credit operations of banking financial institutions.

         Art. 233. From 2027 to 2033, the sum of the rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on financial services referred to in art. 189 of this Complementary Law,
  calculated under the terms of item II of § 1º of art. 10 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, shall correspond to:         (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - in 2027 and 2028, 10.85% (ten point eighty-five percent);      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - in 2029, 11.00% (eleven percent); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - in 2030, 11.15% (eleven point fifteen percent); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        IV - in 2031, 11.30% (eleven point thirty percent); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        V - in 2032, 11.50% (eleven point fifty percent); and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)


          VI - in 2033, 12.50% (twelve point fifty percent). (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 1º The calculation of the rate referred to in the caput of this article shall be made in accordance with the following criteria:    (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)
         I - the proportion of the tax base of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and Cofins of banking financial institutions relating to:
         a) fees and commissions; and
         b) other revenues shall be calculated;
         II - the debits of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and Cofins of banking financial institutions on the other revenues referred to in
  item "b" of item I of this paragraph shall be calculated;
         III - the amounts of the IPI, the Tax on Services of Any Nature (ISS), the ICMS, the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and Cofins
  levied on acquisitions by banking financial institutions and not recovered as credits shall be calculated, in the proportion that the other revenues referred to in
  item "b" of item I of this paragraph represent of the total tax base of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and Cofins; and
         IV - the amount of the debits of the IBS and the CBS on the tax base of the financial services referred to in items I to III of the caput of art. 182 of this
  Complementary Law provided by banking financial institutions, without taking into account operations with debt securities subject to a public offering excluded
  from the tax base under the terms of §§ 1º and 2º of art. 195 of this Complementary Law, shall be equal to the sum of the amount of the debits of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep
  and Cofins referred to in item II and the amounts of taxes not recovered as credits referred to in item III of this paragraph.

          § 1º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 2º The calculation referred to in § 1º of this article shall be made based on data for the period from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2023.       (Repealed by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 2º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3º Observing, each year, the proportion between the rates of the CBS and the IBS under the terms of § 2º of art. 189 of this Complementary Law, the rates of the CBS and
  of the IBS shall be set so that the joint debit of the two taxes meets the provisions of item IV of § 1º of this article.

        § 3º Observing, each year, the proportion between the rates of the CBS and the IBS under the terms of § 2º of art. 189 of this Complementary Law, the rates of the CBS
  and of the IBS shall be set so that the sum of the rates corresponds to the percentage set out in the items of the caput of this article.        (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 4º The calculation methodology for setting the rates referred to in the caput of this article shall be approved by joint act of the Minister of State for Finance and
  the IBS Management Committee, after consultation and approval by the Federal Court of Accounts within a period not exceeding 180 (one hundred and eighty) days. (Repealed by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 4º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 5º The Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities shall provide the IBS Management Committee and the Executive Branch of the Union with the subsidies necessary for
  the calculation of the rates of the IBS and the CBS, by means of the sharing of data and information. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 5º (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 6º The rates of the CBS and the IBS shall be disclosed:

          I - as regards the IBS, by the States, the Municipalities and the Federal District, in a shared and integrated manner, by act of the IBS Management Committee; and

          II - as regards the CBS, by act of the head of the Executive Branch of the Union.

        § 7º For purposes of this article, banking financial institutions are considered to be banks of any kind and savings banks (caixas econômicas).        (Repealed
  by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 7º (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8º The rates set in accordance with the procedure established in this article, in relation to the provisions of item III of § 1º, shall be set taking into
  account the transition rule established in Title VIII of this Book, so that the respective impact on the rates of the IBS and the CBS is introduced
  proportionally to the reduction and elimination of the taxes that will be extinguished. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 8º (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 9º The rates referred to in the items of the caput of this article shall be levied on the value of financial services, excluding:                   (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - the IBS and the CBS; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          II - the tax referred to in art. 156, III, of the Federal Constitution. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 10. In the case of financial services on which the tax referred to in art. 156, III, of the Federal Constitution is levied, the sum of the rates provided
  for in the items of the caput of this article shall be reduced: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          I - in 2027 and 2028, by 2 p.p. (two percentage points); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          II - in 2029, by 1.8 p.p. (one point eight tenths of a percentage point); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          III - in 2030, by 1.6 p.p. (one point six tenths of a percentage point); (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          IV - in 2031, by 1.4 p.p. (one point four tenths of a percentage point); and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          V - in 2032, by 1.2 p.p. (one point two tenths of a percentage point). (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                   CHAPTER III

                                                                    OF HEALTH ASSISTANCE PLANS

        Art. 234. Health assistance plans are subject to a specific regime of incidence of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, in
  cases where such services are provided by:

          I - health insurers;

          II - benefits administrators;

          III - cooperatives operating health plans;

          IV - health insurance cooperatives; and

          V - other operators of health assistance plans.
        Art. 235. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS under the specific regime for health assistance plans shall be composed:

        I - of the revenue from the services, comprising:

        a) premiums and consideration, including for co-responsibility assumed, effectively received, on a cash basis; and

        b) financial revenues, in the assessment period, from the assets guaranteeing technical reserves, effectively settled;

        II - with the deduction:

        a) of the indemnities corresponding to events that occurred, effectively paid, on a cash basis;

        b) of amounts relating to cancellations and refunds of premiums and consideration that have been computed as revenue;

        c) of amounts paid for health plan intermediation services; and

       d) of the administration fee paid to the benefits administrators and other amounts paid to other entities provided for in art. 234 of this
  Complementary Law.

         § 1º For purposes of item "a" of item II of the caput of this article, indemnities corresponding to events that occurred means the total assistance costs
  arising from beneficiaries' use of the coverage offered by the health plans, comprising:

        I - goods and services acquired directly by the entity from natural and legal persons; and

        II - reimbursements to insured persons or beneficiaries for goods and services acquired by them from natural and legal persons.

         § 2º Operations by way of co-responsibility ceded between the entities provided for in art. 234 of this Complementary Law shall also be considered assistance
  costs under the terms of § 1º and shall be deducted from the tax base for purposes of the provisions of the caput of this article.

        § 3º Co-responsibility ceded referred to in § 2º of this article means the making available of services by one operator to beneficiaries of another, with
  the corresponding assumption of the risk of the provision.

       § 4º For purposes of item "b" of item I of the caput of this article, financial revenues shall be considered effectively settled when there is,
  cumulatively:

        I - the settlement or redemption of the respective guaranteeing asset; and

        II - the reduction of technical provisions backed by the guaranteeing asset, considering the difference between the total value of technical provisions in the assessment period
  and in the immediately preceding period.

          § 5º Reimbursements to insured persons or beneficiaries referred to in item II of § 1º of this article are not subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS and do not give
  rise to credits.

        § 6º Financial revenues that have no connection with the allocation of funds arising from the
  receipt of premiums and consideration paid by contracting parties of health assistance plans shall not form part of the tax base of the IBS and the CBS.

        Art. 236. Funeral assistance plans are subject to the provisions of arts. 234 to 242 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 237. The rates of IBS and CBS under the specific regime for health assistance plans are nationally uniform and correspond to the reference
  rates of each federative sphere, reduced by 60% (sixty percent).

        Art. 238. Credit for the IBS and the CBS is prohibited for acquirers of health assistance plans.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of the caput of this article do not apply to the case referred to in item "f" of item IV of § 2º of art. 57 of this Complementary Law, in
  which the IBS and CBS credits to be used by the contracting party that is a taxpayer in the regular regime:

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of the caput of this article do not apply to the case referred to in item "f" of item IV of § 3º of art. 57 of this Complementary Law,
  in which the IBS and CBS credits to be used by the contracting party that is a taxpayer in the regular regime: (Wording given by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

        I - shall be equivalent to the multiplication of:

        a) the amounts of the IBS and CBS debits paid by the entity subject to the specific regime referred to in this Chapter in the assessment period; and

        b) the proportion between:
