        1. the total premiums and consideration corresponding to the coverage of the contracting party's employee-holders and their dependents, in the assessment
  period; and

        2. the total premiums and consideration collected by the entity, in the same assessment period;

        II - do not reach the portion of premiums and consideration whose financial burden has been passed on to employees; and

        III - shall be appropriated based on the information provided by suppliers to the IBS Management Committee and the RFB, in the manner provided by the regulation, and shall be subject
  to the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 239. The entities referred to in this Chapter shall submit, as an ancillary obligation, in the manner provided by the regulation, information on the identity
  of the natural persons who are the holder-beneficiaries of the health assistance plans and the amounts of premiums and consideration for each one.

        § 1º In collective plans where there is no individualization of the amount of premiums and consideration per holder natural person, the operator may allocate, in the
  ancillary obligation referred to in the caput of this article, the total amount received to each holder natural person in accordance with criteria to be established in the regulation.

        § 2º In collective plans by adhesion contracted with the participation or intermediation of a benefits administrator, the latter shall be responsible for the
  submission of the information provided for in the caput and in § 1º of this article.

         Art. 240. Health assistance plan intermediation services are subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS on the value of the operation at the same
  rate applicable to the health assistance plan.

        Sole paragraph. Providers of health assistance plan intermediation services that opt for the Simples Nacional:

        I - shall remain taxed in accordance with the Simples Nacional rules, in cases where they do not exercise the option for the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS; and

        II - shall be subject to the same rate of the IBS and the CBS applicable to health assistance plan services, in cases where they exercise the option for the regular
  regime of the IBS and the CBS.


         Art. 241. Should the importation of health assistance plan services come to be permitted, the IBS and the CBS shall be levied at the same
  rate applicable to operations carried out in the Country on the value of the operation, and the regulation may provide for a reduction factor to account for a presumed
  margin, observing the limits established in this Chapter for the tax base deductions of such services.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of Chapter IV of Title I of this Book apply to importations referred to in the caput of this article, insofar as they do not conflict with the
  provisions of this article.

         Art. 242. Should the supply of health assistance plan services to residents or persons domiciled abroad for use
  abroad come to be permitted, such supply shall be considered an export and shall be immune to the IBS and the CBS, for purposes of the provisions of Chapter V of Title I of this Book.

         Art. 243. Pet health assistance plans are subject to the provisions of arts. 234 to 242 of this Complementary Law, with the exception of the
  applicable rates, which shall be nationally uniform and shall correspond to the sum of the reference rates of each federative sphere, reduced by 30% (thirty
  percent), with credit to the acquirer prohibited.

                                                                                  CHAPTER IV

                                                                    OF PROGNOSTIC CONTESTS (LOTTERIES AND BETTING)

                                                                                      Section I

                                                                               General Provisions

       Art. 244. Prognostic contests, in physical or virtual form, comprising all lottery modalities, including fixed-odds betting and
  sweepstakes, horse racing bets and other bets, are subject to a specific regime of incidence of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of this Chapter apply to fantasy sport.

        Art. 245. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS on prognostic contests is the entity's own revenue arising from that activity, corresponding to the
  proceeds of collection, with the deduction of:

        I - prizes paid; and

        II - mandatory allocations by law to a public body or fund and to other beneficiaries.

        Sole paragraph. Prizes paid are not subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS.

        Art. 246. The rates of the IBS and the CBS on prognostic contests are nationally uniform and correspond to the sum of the reference rates of the
  federative spheres.

        Art. 247. Credit for the IBS and the CBS is prohibited for bettors of prognostic contests.

        Art. 248. The company that operates prognostic contests shall submit an ancillary obligation, in the manner provided by the regulation, containing, at a minimum, information
  on the place where the bet is made and the amounts of bets and prizes paid.

        Sole paragraph. If bets are made virtually, in the ancillary obligation referred to in the caput of this article, the
  bettor shall be identified.

                                                                                     Section II

                                                         Of the Importation of Prognostic Contest Services

         Art. 249. Should the importation of prognostic contest services come to be permitted, entities domiciled abroad that provide, by virtual means,
  prognostic contest services referred to in this Chapter to bettors residing or domiciled in the Country shall be subject to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS at the same
  rate provided for prognostic contests in the Country.

       § 1º The supplier of the service referred to in the caput of this article is the taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS, and the bettor may be jointly liable for
  payment in the cases provided for in art. 24 of this Complementary Law.

       § 2º The tax base is the revenue earned by the entity as a result of the operation, with the application of a reduction factor provided for in the regulation, calculated
  based on the tax base deductions of prognostic contest services in the Country.

        § 3º The provisions of Chapter IV of Title I of this Book apply to importations referred to in this Section, insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this article.

                                                                                     Section III

                                                         Of the Exportation of Prognostic Contest Services

        Art. 250. Prognostic contest services provided, by virtual means, to residents or persons domiciled abroad shall be considered exported,
  and shall be immune to the incidence of the IBS and the CBS, for purposes of the provisions of Chapter V of Title I of this Book.

        § 1º The regulation shall provide for the manner of proving residence or domicile abroad for purposes of the caput of this article.

         § 2º Prognostic contest services provided in the physical presence, within national territory, of a resident or person domiciled abroad shall not be considered
  exported.

                                                                                   CHAPTER V

                                                                              OF REAL PROPERTY

                                                                                      Section I

                                                                               General Provisions

         Art. 251. Operations with real property carried out by taxpayers who assess the IBS and the CBS under the regular regime are subject to the specific regime
  provided for in this Chapter.

        § 1º Natural persons who carry out operations with real property shall be considered taxpayers of the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS and subject to the regime
  referred to in this Chapter, in the following cases:

        I - lease, onerous assignment and letting of real property, provided that, in the preceding calendar year:

        a) the total revenue from such operations exceeds R$ 240,000 (two hundred and forty thousand reais); and

        b) they relate to more than 3 (three) distinct real properties;


        II - disposal or assignment of rights to real property, provided they relate to more than 3 (three) distinct properties in the preceding calendar year;

        III - disposal or assignment of rights, in the preceding calendar year, of more than 1 (one) real property built by the disposing party themselves in the 5 (five) years prior to the
  date of disposal.

          § 2º The natural person referred to in the caput of § 1º of this article shall also be considered a taxpayer of the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS in the calendar year itself,
  in relation to the following operations:

        I - the disposal or assignment of rights to properties that exceeds the limits provided for in items II and III of § 1º of this article; and

        II - the lease, onerous assignment or letting of real property in an amount that exceeds by 20% (twenty percent) the limit provided for in item "a" of item I of § 1º
  of this article.

        § 3º For purposes of item II of § 1º of this article, the properties relating to the operations must have been held in the taxpayer's assets for less than 5 (five)
  years counted from the date of their acquisition.

        § 4º In the case of real property received by division of marital property, donation or inheritance, the period referred to in § 3º of this article shall be counted from acquisition
  by the spouse from whom the property was divided, the deceased, or the donor.

         § 5º The amount provided for in item "a" of item I of § 1º shall be updated monthly as from the date of publication of this Complementary Law by the IPCA or by
  another index that comes to replace it.

        § 6º The regulation shall define what constitutes distinct real properties, for purposes of items I and II of § 1º of the caput.

        § 7º The provisions of Title I of this Book apply, insofar as applicable, with respect to other rules not provided for in this Chapter.

        Art. 252. The IBS and the CBS are levied, under the terms of this Chapter, on the following operations with real property:

        I - disposal, including that arising from real estate development and land subdivision;

        II - onerous assignment and transfer or constitutive acts of real rights;

        III - lease, onerous assignment and letting;

        IV - administration and intermediation services; and

        V - civil construction services.

        § 1º The following are subject to taxation by the IBS and the CBS under the same rules as the lease, onerous assignment and letting of real property:

        I - servitude, assignment of use or of space;

        II - the granting of use, the right of passage; and

        III - (VETOED).

        § 2º The IBS and the CBS are not levied in the following cases:

        I - in exchange operations of real property, except on the equalization payment (torna), which shall be taxed under the terms of this Chapter;

       I - in exchange operations between real properties, except on the equalization payment (torna), which shall be taxed under the terms of this Chapter;                     (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - in the constitution or transfer of real security rights; and

         III - in the operations provided for in this article, when carried out by organizations managing endowment funds, constituted under the terms of Law No. 13,800, of
  January 4, 2019, for purposes of investment of the endowment fund.

        § 3º In the case referred to in item I of § 2º of this article, the exchanged amount shall not be considered in the value of the operation for the calculation of the adjustment reducer
  referred to in art. 258 of this Complementary Law.

         § 4º For purposes of this Chapter, operations with real property referred to in item III of § 2º of this article are not considered operations of a
  taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS.

        § 5º In exchanges of properties carried out between taxpayers of the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS:

        § 5º In exchanges between real properties carried out between taxpayers of the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS:              (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        I - the value of the adjustment reducer of the property given in exchange is maintained, and may be used in future operations with the property received in exchange; and

        II - in the case of an exchange for delivery of units to be built, the adjustment reducer shall be applied proportionally to the operation of each party to the exchange, taking
  as a basis the ideal fraction of the exchanged units.

        § 5º-A. In exchanges between properties carried out between a taxpayer of the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS and a non-taxpayer of the regular regime:             (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - no adjustment reducer shall be constituted for the property received in exchange by the non-taxpayer of the regular regime; and          (Included by Complementary Law
  No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the value of the adjustment reducer of the property received in exchange by the taxpayer of the regular regime shall correspond to:             (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

        a) if there is no equalization payment (torna), the value of the adjustment reducer of the property given by them in exchange;          (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) if there is payment of an equalization payment (torna) by the taxpayer of the regular regime, the value of the adjustment reducer of the property given by them in exchange, plus
  the value of the equalization payment; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         c) if there is payment of an equalization payment (torna) by the non-taxpayer of the regular regime, the value of the adjustment reducer of the property given in exchange by the
  taxpayer of the regular regime, less the value of the equalization payment, and the value of the adjustment reducer may not be negative. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

        § 6º The provisions of item I of § 2º and § 5º of this article also apply to settled purchase and sale operations for real property followed by acknowledgment of debt and
  promise of conveyance in lieu of payment of a constructed or to-be-constructed real estate unit, provided that the disposal of the property and the commitment to convey in payment
  are carried out on the same date, by public instrument.
         § 7º The provisions of § 4º of art. 57 of this Complementary Law apply to the operations of disposal, lease, onerous assignment and letting of real property owned
  by a natural person subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS that are not related to the development of their economic activity.

        § 8º The provisions of § 6º of this article do not apply if the quantity and value of the operations with the properties referred to therein characterize economic
  activity of the taxpayer, under the terms of §§ 1º and 2º of art. 251.

       § 8º The provisions of § 7º of this article do not apply if the quantity and value of the operations with the properties referred to therein characterize economic
  activity of the taxpayer, under the terms of §§ 1º and 2º of art. 251. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 9º In the disposal of properties that have been the subject of a guarantee constituted in favor of a creditor subject to the specific regime of this Chapter, whose ownership
  has been consolidated by or transferred to them in payment or amortization of the debt, the provisions of art. 200 of this Complementary Law must be observed.

         Art. 253. The lease, onerous assignment or letting of residential real property by a taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, for a period not
  exceeding 90 (ninety) uninterrupted days, shall be taxed in accordance with the same rules applicable to hotel services, provided for in Section II of Chapter
  VII of Title V of this Book.

         § 1º For purposes of the caput of this article, natural persons who meet the provisions of item I of § 1º and item II of § 2º, both of
  art. 251 of this Complementary Law, are considered taxpayers subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 2º The operations referred to in this article shall be included in the limits referred to in item I of § 1º and item II of § 2º, both of art. 251 of this
  Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                      Section II

                                                                  Of the Moment of Occurrence of the Taxable Event

        Art. 254. The taxable event of the IBS and the CBS is considered to occur:

        I - in the disposal of real property, at the moment of the act of disposal;

         II - in the assignment or in the onerous transfer or constitutive act of real rights over real property, at the moment the act is executed, including any
  subsequent adjustments, except those relating to security;

        III - in the lease, onerous assignment or letting of real property, at the moment of payment;

        IV - in the administration and intermediation service for real property, at the moment of payment; and

        V - in civil construction services, at the moment of supply.

         § 1º For purposes of item I of the caput of this article, disposal means adjudication, execution, including any subsequent adjustments, of the
  disposal contract, even by means of a promise instrument, reservation letter with a beginning of payment, or any other document representing a
  commitment, or when the suspensive condition to which the disposal is subject is fulfilled.

        § 2º In the cases referred to in items III and IV of the caput of this article, the IBS and the CBS levied on the operation shall be due upon each payment.

                                                                                      Section III

                                                                                Of the Tax Base

                                                                                     Subsection I

                                                                                General Provisions

        Art. 255. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS is the value:

        I - of the transaction for the disposal of the real property;

        II - of the lease, onerous assignment or rental of the real property;

        III - of the assignment or the onerous act transferring or constituting real rights over real property;

        IV - of the administration or intermediation transaction;

        V - of the transaction in civil construction services.

        § 1º The value of the transaction referred to in the caput of this article includes:

        I - the value of interest and monetary variations, based on the exchange rate or on an index or coefficient applicable under legal or contractual provision;

         II - monetary restatement, in sales contracted with a clause for monetary restatement of the price's outstanding balance, that come to form part of the values
  actually received from the disposal of real property;

        III - the values referred to in items I to III and VI of § 1º of art. 12 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The following shall not be included in the value of the lease, onerous assignment or rental of real property:

        I - the value of taxes and fees levied on the real property; and

        II - condominium expenses.

        § 3º In real property intermediation services, in the event that the act or transaction relating to real property is concluded through the intermediation of more than one broker,
  natural or legal person, the tax base for the levy of the IBS and the CBS shall be considered to be the portion of the remuneration agreed with each broker for the
  intermediation, excluding:

        I - the amounts paid directly by the parties contracting the intermediation; and

        II - the amounts passed on between real estate brokers.

        § 4º In the case referred to in § 3º of this article, each broker is liable for the IBS and the CBS levied on its respective portion of the remuneration.

        § 5º In the case of the rendering of civil construction services to a non-taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime in which construction
  materials are supplied, the service provider may only appropriate the IBS and CBS credit relating to the acquisition of the construction materials up to the value of the debit relating to
  the rendering of the civil construction service.



         § 6º The provision of § 5º of this article does not apply to the rendering of civil construction services to the direct public administration, agencies and public
  foundations.

        Art. 256. The tax administrations may determine the reference value of the real property, in the manner set out in regulations, by means of a specific methodology to
  estimate the market value of real property, which shall take into account:

         I - analysis of prices practiced in the real estate market;

         II - information sent by the tax administrations of the Municipalities, the Federal District, the States and the Union;

         III - information provided by registry and notarial services; and

         IV - location, typology, use and date, standard and construction area, among other characteristics of the real property.

       § 1º The reference value may be used as a means of proof in cases of arbitration of the transaction value under the terms of art. 13, together with the
  other characteristics of the transaction.

         § 2º The reference value of real property shall be:

         I - disclosed and made available in the National System for the Management of Territorial Information (Sinter);

         II - estimated for all real property comprising the CIB referred to in item III of § 1º of art. 59 of this Complementary Law; and

         III - updated annually.

         § 3º The reference value may be challenged by means of a specific procedure, under the terms of the regulations.

       § 4º For purposes of determining the reference value, the registry and notarial services must share the information on real property transactions
  with the tax administrations through the Sinter.

                                                                                    Subsection II

                                                                                Of the Adjustment Reducer

        Art. 257. As of January 1, 2027, there shall be linked to each real property owned by a taxpayer subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime a value
  corresponding to the respective adjustment reducer, under the terms of the regulations.

         § 1º The adjustment reducer referred to in this article shall be used exclusively to reduce the tax base of transactions for the disposal of real property
  carried out by a taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime.

         § 2º The value of the adjustment reducer is composed of:

         I - its initial value, under the terms of the caput of art. 258; and

         II - the values set out in § 6º of art. 258.

         § 3º The values referred to in items I and II of § 2º of this article shall be adjusted by the IPCA or by another index that may replace it, from the date of its
  constitution until the date on which the IBS and the CBS levied on the disposal of the real property become due.

         § 4º In the disposal of real property, the adjustment reducer:

         I - shall be maintained at the same value and with the same restatement criterion, in the case where the real property is acquired by a taxpayer subject to the IBS and
  CBS regular regime;

         II - shall be extinguished in other cases.

        § 5º In the merger, consolidation or unification of real property, the value of the adjustment reducer of the real property resulting from the merger, consolidation or unification
  shall correspond to the sum of the value of the adjustment reducer of the merged or unified real properties.

         § 6º In the division of real property, including by subdivision, dismemberment and parceling, the value of the adjustment reducer of the real properties resulting from the
  division must be equal to the value of the adjustment reducer of the divided real property, observing the following criteria:

         I - the value of the adjustment reducer shall be allocated to each real property resulting from the division in proportion to its market value; or

        II - where it is not possible to identify the market value of each real property resulting from the division, or in other cases provided for in regulations, the value
  of the adjustment reducer shall be allocated to each real property resulting from the division in proportion to its area.

       § 7º In land subdivision (loteamento) activity carried out by means of a partnership agreement, the adjustment reducer shall be applied proportionally to the transaction of each partner,
  based on the percentages set out in the partnership agreement.

       § 8º The absence of regulations on the manner of use of the adjustment reducer referred to in this article does not prevent its use under the terms of this Complementary
  Law.

         Art. 258. The initial value of the adjustment reducer corresponds to:

         I - in the case of real property owned by the taxpayer on December 31, 2026:

         a) the acquisition value of the real property adjusted under the terms of § 4º of this article; or

         b) at the taxpayer's option, the reference value referred to in art. 256 of this Complementary Law;

         II - in the case of real property under construction on December 31, 2026, the sum of:

         a) the acquisition value of the land, as stated in the instruments referred to in the manner of § 1º of art. 254, adjusted under the terms of § 4º of this article; and

         a) the acquisition value of the real property on which the construction is being carried out, as stated in the instruments referred to in the manner of § 1º of art. 254,
  adjusted under the terms of § 4º of this article; and (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) the value of the goods and services that may be recorded as production cost of the real property or as a direct expense related to the production or
  commercialization of the real property acquired prior to January 1, 2027, evidenced on the basis of valid tax documents, adjusted under the terms of §
  4º of this article;

         III - in the case of real property acquired as of January 1, 2027, the acquisition value of the real property.



       III - in the case of real property acquired from a non-taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime as of January 1, 2027, the acquisition value of the
  real property. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1º The date of constitution of the adjustment reducer is:

        I - in the case of items I and II of the caput of this article, December 31, 2026;

        II - in the case of item III of the caput of this article, the date of the transaction.

         § 2º If the reference value of the real property is not available on December 31, 2026, the taxpayer who does not opt for fixing the adjustment reducer in the
  manner of item I of the caput of this article may calculate it based on an estimate of the market value of the real property made by means of a specific procedure,
  under the terms of the regulations.

        § 3º If the acquisition value referred to in items I, item "a", II, item "a", and III of the caput of this article is based on declarations or documents that
  are not consistent with the market value or that do not merit credence, the tax authority may institute administrative proceedings, observing the right to challenge and
  full defense, to determine the actual acquisition value, under the terms of the regulations.

        § 4º The values referred to in items I, item "a", and II, items "a" and "b", of the caput of this article shall be adjusted until December 31, 2026 by the IPCA
  or by another index that may replace it.

         § 5º In the case referred to in item III of the caput, the value of the adjustment reducer is limited to the acquisition value of the real property by the transferor, adjusted by the IPCA or by
  another index that may replace it, in the event that:

        I - the disposal occurs within a period of less than 3 (three) years, counted from the date of acquisition of the real property;

        II - the real property was acquired from a taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime; and

        III - payment is not evidenced, by the transferor, of:

        a) the Income Tax on capital gains in relation to the transaction; and

        b) the Real Property Transfer Tax, in relation to the acquisition by the transferor.

        § 6º The following are included in the adjustment reducer relating to the real property, as of the date of actual payment:

        I - the value of the Real Property Transfer Tax (ITBI) and of the laudêmio levied on the acquisition of the real property to which the adjustment reducer refers; and

         II - urban planning and environmental consideration payments made or delivered to public entities as a result of federal, state or municipal
  legislation, including, but not limited to, amounts spent as onerous grant of the right to build, onerous grant for change of use, and any
  other considerations owed to public bodies for the execution of the real estate development, provided that they have not been included in the initial value of the adjustment
  reducer referred to in the caput.

        § 7º The following are included in the concept of municipal considerations:

         I - the value corresponding to the percentage allocated for the donation of public areas under the terms of art. 22 of Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979, recorded
  in the subdivision registration and its real property record, applied to the value of the transactions, provided that the respective value has not already been considered in the adjustment
  reducer; and

         II - the considerations established in the development approval act recorded in the real property registry office, under the terms of item V of the caput of
  art. 18 of Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979.

        § 8º The appropriation of credits in relation to the IBS and the CBS levied on the goods and services acquired for carrying out the considerations
  referred to in item II of § 6º of this article that form part of the adjustment reducer is prohibited, under the terms of the said paragraph.

         § 9º The date of constitution of the values included in the adjustment reducer under the terms of § 6º of this article is the date of payment of the taxes and considerations
  or of the transfer to the government of the assets ceded as consideration.

        § 10. In the case of real property acquired from a taxpayer subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime as of January 1, 2027, the maintenance of the value of the adjustment reducer is assured, under the terms of item I of § 4º of art. 257, without prejudice to the right to the IBS and CBS credit levied on the
  transaction. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                   Subsection III

                                                                                Of the Social Reducer

         Art. 259. In the disposal of new residential real property or of a residential lot carried out by a taxpayer subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime, a social reducer of
  R$ 100,000.00 (one hundred thousand reais) per new residential real property and of R$ 30,000.00 (thirty thousand
  reais) per residential lot may be deducted from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS, up to the limit of the tax base value, after deduction of the adjustment reducer.

        § 1º The following are considered:

         I - residential real property: the unit built in an urban or rural zone for residential purposes, in accordance with the building regulations of the
  locality in which it is situated and occupied by a person as a place of residence;

       II - residential lot: the real estate unit resulting from urban land subdivision under the terms of Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979, or subject to a
  condominium of lots, under the terms of art. 1,358-A of Law No. 10,406, of January 10, 2002 (Civil Code); and

        III - new real property: one that has not been occupied or used, under the terms of the regulations.

        § 2º For each real property, the social reducer referred to in this article may be used only once.

         § 3º The value of the social reducer provided for in the caput of this article shall be adjusted monthly as of the publication of this Complementary Law by the IPCA or by another
  index that may replace it.

         § 4º When the land subdivision (loteamento) activity is carried out by means of a partnership agreement, the social reducer shall be applied proportionally to the transaction of each
  partner, based on the percentages set out in the partnership agreement.

        Art. 260. In the transaction of lease, onerous assignment or rental of real property for residential use carried out by a taxpayer subject to the
  IBS and CBS regular regime, a social reducer of R$ 600.00 (six hundred reais) per real property may be deducted from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS, up to the limit of the value
  of the tax base.

         Art. 260. In the transaction of lease, onerous assignment or rental of real property for residential use carried out by a taxpayer subject to the IBS and CBS
  regular regime, a social reducer of R$ 600.00 (six hundred reais), per month, per real property, may be deducted from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS, up to
  the limit of the value of the tax base. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)


         Sole paragraph. The value of the social reducer provided for in the caput of this article shall be adjusted monthly as of the date of publication of this Complementary Law
  by the IPCA or by another index that may replace it.

                                                                                     Section IV

                                                                                    Of the Rate

        Art. 261. The rates of the IBS and the CBS relating to the transactions referred to in this Chapter are reduced by 50% (fifty percent).

         Sole paragraph. The rates of the IBS and the CBS relating to transactions of lease, onerous assignment and rental of real property are reduced by 70%
  (seventy percent).

                                                                                     Section V

                                                            Of Real Estate Development and Land Subdivision

       Art. 262. In real estate development and land subdivision, the IBS and the CBS levied on the disposal of the real estate units shall be due upon each
  payment.

        § 1º The following is considered a real estate unit:

        I - land acquired for sale, with or without construction;

        II - each lot arising from the dismemberment of land;

        III - each plot of land arising from a subdivision;

        IV - each distinct unit resulting from a real estate development; and

        V - the building constructed for sale as an isolated or autonomous unit.

        § 2º Of the amounts of IBS and CBS due in each assessment period, the transferor may offset the appropriated credits relating to the IBS and the CBS
  paid on the acquisition of goods and services.

        § 3º Any credit balance may be the subject of:

         I - a request for reimbursement, provided that the reimbursement is made directly into a current account linked to the segregated estate (patrimônio de afetação), in the manner of
  arts. 31-A to 31-E of Law No. 4,591, of December 16, 1964, and arts. 18-A to 18-E of Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979, until the completion,
  respectively, of the development or of the land subdivision; or

        II - a request for reimbursement or offsetting against the amounts of the IBS and the CBS relating to other taxed transactions of the taxpayer, after the completion of the
  development or of the land subdivision.

        § 4º In the disposal of real property referred to in this article, the adjustment reducer referred to in art. 258 and, where applicable, the social reducer referred to in art. 259 of this
  Complementary Law shall be deducted from the tax base relating to each installment, proportionally to the total value of the real property.

        § 5º In the case of residential lots and new residential real property whose payment began before January 1, 2027, the application of the reducers
  referred to in § 4º of this article shall occur proportionally to the total value of the real property, including installments paid before that date.

                                                                                     Section VI

                                                                                Of Tax Liability

        Art. 263. The following are taxpayers of the transactions referred to in this Chapter:

        I - the transferor of real property, in the disposal of real property or of a right related thereto;

        II - whoever assigns, institutes or transfers real rights over real property, in the assignment or in the onerous act instituting or transferring real rights over real
  property, except security interests;

        III - the lessor, the assignor or the landlord, in the lease, onerous assignment or rental of real property;

        IV - the acquirer, in the case of adjudication, redemption and acquisition at judicial auction of real property;

        V - the provider of construction services;

        VI - the provider of real property administration and intermediation services.

        § 1º In the case of item IV of the caput of this article, the transaction:

        I - shall be taxed as a disposal carried out by a taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime, if there is an adjustment reducer linked to the real property, applying the
  provision of art. 257, § 1º; or

        II - shall be treated as a disposal carried out by a non-taxpayer of the IBS and CBS regular regime, if there is no adjustment reducer linked to the real property.

         § 2º In the case of co-ownership of real property subject to undivided co-ownership (condomínio pro indiviso), the co-owners may, under the terms of the regulations,
  opt for the unified collection of the IBS and the CBS under a single CNPJ.

         § 3º In the case of co-ownership, the IBS and the CBS shall be levied proportionally on the portion of the real property relating to the co-owner who qualifies as a
  taxpayer, under the terms of the caput and of § 1º of art. 251 of this Complementary Law.

       Art. 264. In sociedades em conta de participação (silent partnerships), the ostensible partner is required to make the payment of the IBS and the CBS levied on
  transactions with real property, the exclusion of amounts owed to participating partners being prohibited.

                                                                                     Section VII

                                                                                Final Provisions

        Art. 265. The urban and rural real property referred to in this Section must be registered in the CIB, part of the Sinter, referred to in item III of § 1º of art. 59
  of this Complementary Law.

         § 1º The CIB is the inventory of urban and rural real property constituted with data sent by the source registries, which must meet the criteria for
  assignment of the CIB registration code.

        § 2º The CIB must mandatorily appear on all documents relating to civil construction works issued by the Municipality.
        Art. 266. The following deadlines are established for the registration of all real property in the CIB:      Effective as of

        I - 12 (twelve) months for:

        a) the direct and indirect federal administration bodies to adapt their systems for the adoption of the CIB as the cadastral identification code for
  urban and rural real property;

        b) the notarial and registry services to adapt their systems for the adoption of the CIB as the cadastral identification code for real property;

        c) the state capitals and the Federal District to include the CIB code in their systems;

        II - 24 (twenty-four) months for:

        a) the direct and indirect state administration bodies to adapt their systems for the adoption of the CIB as the cadastral identification code for
  urban and rural real property;

        b) the other Municipalities to include the CIB code in their systems.

        Art. 267. A negative certificate of debts shall be issued for urban and rural real property, under the terms of the regulations.

         Art. 268. The IBS Management Committee and the RFB may establish, by joint act, ancillary obligations in the interest of tax enforcement and administration,
  for third parties related to the transactions referred to in this Chapter, including notaries, real property registrars and boards of trade.

        Art. 269. The civil construction work shall receive a cadastral identification in the registry referred to in art. 265 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 270. The assessment of the IBS and the CBS shall be made for each civil construction development, linked to a specific CNPJ or CPF, including
  real estate development and land subdivision, each civil construction work, development or land subdivision being considered as a distinct cost center.

         Sole paragraph. In the case of assessment of the IBS and the CBS under the terms of the caput of this article, the tax document must indicate the registration number of the work
  on the acquisitions of goods and services used in the civil construction work for which they are intended.

                                                                                   CHAPTER VI

                                                                     OF COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES

         Art. 271. Cooperative societies may opt for a specific IBS and CBS regime under which the rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on the transaction are reduced to zero, in which:

        I - the member supplies a good or service to the cooperative it participates in; and

        II - the cooperative supplies a good or service to a member subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime.

        § 1º The provision of the caput of this article also applies to:

        I - transactions carried out between singular, central cooperatives, federations, confederations and those originating from their respective cooperative banks that
  the cooperatives participate in; and

        II - the transaction of supplying a material good by an agricultural production cooperative to a member not subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime, provided
  that the credits it appropriated relating to the good supplied are cancelled.

        § 2º The provision of item II of the caput of this article also applies to the supply, by cooperatives, of financial services to their members, including
  those charged by way of fees and commissions.

        § 3º The option referred to in the caput of this article shall be exercised by the cooperative in the calendar year prior to that in which effects begin to be produced or at the beginning of
  its operations, under the terms of the regulations.

         § 4º The provision of item II of § 1º does not apply to transactions with agricultural and aquaculture inputs covered by the deferral established by § 3º
  of art. 138.

        Art. 272. The member subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime, including singular cooperatives, that carries out transactions with the rate reduction referred to in item I of the caput of art. 271 may transfer the credits from prior-stage transactions to the transactions in which it supplies goods and services and the presumed
  credits to the cooperative it participates in, the provision of art. 55 of this Complementary Law not applying.

        Sole paragraph. The transfer of credits referred to in the caput of this article covers only the goods and services used for the production of the good or the rendering
  of the service supplied by the member to the cooperative it participates in, under the terms of the regulations.

                                                                                   CHAPTER VII

           OF BARS, RESTAURANTS, HOTEL SERVICES, AMUSEMENT PARKS AND THEME PARKS, COLLECTIVE PASSENGER TRANSPORT AND
                                                        TOURISM AGENCIES

                                                                                     Section I

                                                                          Of Bars and Restaurants

        Art. 273. Transactions for the supply of food by bars and restaurants, including snack bars (lanchonetes), are subject to a specific regime for the levy of the IBS
  and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Section.

        § 1º The specific regime referred to in this Section also applies to the supply of non-alcoholic beverages prepared on the premises.

        § 2º The following supplies are not subject to the specific regime referred to in this Section:

        I - food for a legal entity, under contract, classified under NBS codes 1.0301.31.00, 1.0301.32.00 and 1.0301.39.00 or by a company classified under
  code 5620-1/01 of the National Classification of Economic Activities (CNAE);

        II - food products and non-alcoholic beverages acquired from third parties, not subjected to preparation on the premises; and

        III - alcoholic beverages, even if prepared on the premises.

       Art. 274. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS is the value of the transaction for the supply of food and of the beverages referred to in § 1º of art. 273 of this
  Complementary Law.

        Sole paragraph. The following are excluded from the tax base:

        I - the tip (gorjeta) levied on the supply of food, provided that:
        a) it is passed on in full to the employee, without prejudice to the amounts of the tip that are withheld by the employer pursuant to a legal determination; and

        b) its value does not exceed 15% (fifteen percent) of the total value of the food and beverages supplied;

        II - the amounts not passed on to bars and restaurants by the delivery and food and beverage order intermediation service via digital platform.

        Art. 275. The rates of the IBS and the CBS relating to the transactions referred to in this Chapter are reduced by 40% (forty percent).

        Art. 276. The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by acquirers of food and beverages supplied by bars and restaurants, including
  snack bars, is prohibited.

                                                                                      Section II

                                                              Of Hotel Services, Amusement Parks and Theme Parks

        Art. 277. Hotel services, amusement parks and theme parks are subject to a specific regime for the levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the
  provisions of this Section.

         Art. 278. For purposes of this Complementary Law, hotel service is considered to be the supply of temporary lodging, as well as of other
  services included in the value charged for the lodging, in:

        I - units for the exclusive use of guests, in an establishment intended for that purpose; or

        II - furnished residential real property, even if not for the exclusive use of guests.

         Sole paragraph. The supply of hotel services is not disqualified by the division of the development into hotel units, understood as the
  attribution of autonomous legal status to the residential units comprising it, under the ownership of various persons, provided that their functional purpose is
  exclusively for lodging.

        Art. 279. For purposes of this Complementary Law, the following are considered:

         I - amusement park: the permanent or itinerant establishment or development whose essential activity is to make available attractions intended to
  entertain people and enjoyed in person at the location where they are made available; and

        II - theme park: the amusement park inspired by a historical, cultural, ethnographic, recreational or environmental theme.

        Art. 280. The tax base of the IBS and the CBS is the value of the transaction with hotel services, amusement parks and theme parks.

        Sole paragraph. Transactions for the supply of food and beverages by establishments that render the services referred to in this Section shall
  observe the rules relating to the specific regime for bars and restaurants. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 281. The rates of the IBS and the CBS relating to the transactions referred to in this Chapter are reduced by 40% (forty percent).

         Art. 282. The appropriation and use of IBS and CBS credits on acquisitions of goods and services by suppliers of hotel services, amusement parks and theme parks are permitted, observing the provision of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 283. The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the acquirer of hotel services, amusement parks and theme parks is prohibited.

                                                                                      Section III

        Of Intermunicipal and Interstate Road, Rail, Waterway and Regional Air Collective Passenger Transport and Of Regional Air Cargo
                                                                     Transport

         Art. 284. The following collective passenger transport services are subject to a specific regime for the levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the
  provisions of this Section:

        I - intermunicipal and interstate road transport;

        II - intermunicipal and interstate rail and waterway transport;

        III - urban, semi-urban and metropolitan rail and waterway transport; and

        IV - regional air transport.

        § 1º For purposes of this Complementary Law, the following are considered:

        I - collective passenger transport: the service of moving people that is accessible to the entire population by means of individualized charging;

        II - intermunicipal passenger transport: the service of moving people between Municipalities located within the same State or the Federal District;

        III - interstate passenger transport: the service of moving people between Municipalities of different States or of a State and the Federal District;

        IV - road passenger transport: that defined in accordance with the provision of item II of the sole paragraph of art. 157 of this Complementary Law;

        V - rail passenger transport: the service of moving people carried out by means of the locomotion of trains or convoys on rails;

        VI - waterway passenger transport: the service of moving people carried out by means of routes for water traffic;

       VII - urban, semi-urban and metropolitan transport: that defined in accordance with the provision of items IV to VI of the sole paragraph of art. 157 of this
  Complementary Law, with routes and fares set by the government; and

        VIII - regional air transport: domestic aviation with flights originating in or destined for the Legal Amazon or for regional capitals, sub-regional
  centers, zone centers or local centers, as defined by the IBGE, and in the manner regulated by the Ministry of Ports and Airports.

        § 2º The appropriation and use of IBS and CBS credits by the acquirers of transport services are permitted, observing the provision of arts.
  47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

          § 3º The routes referred to in item VIII of § 1º shall be defined by joint act of the General Committee of the IBS and the Minister of State for Finance, based on
  classification by the National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC), the exclusion of routes within a period of less than 2 (two) years from their inclusion being prohibited.

        § 4º The specific regime referred to in items I to III of the caput applies only to public collective passenger transport, understood as that
  operated under a regime of public authorization, permission or concession.

        Art. 285. In relation to public collective passenger transport services by rail and waterway of an urban, semi-urban and metropolitan nature:


        I - the rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on the supply of these services are reduced by 100% (one hundred percent);

        II - the appropriation of IBS and CBS credits on acquisitions by the transport service supplier is prohibited; and

        III - the appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the acquirer of the transport services is prohibited.

        Art. 286. In relation to intermunicipal and interstate collective passenger transport services by road, rail and waterway, the rates of the IBS
  and the CBS of the specific regime referred to in this Section are reduced by 40% (forty percent).

         Sole paragraph. The appropriation and use of IBS and CBS credits on acquisitions of goods and services by suppliers of the transport
  services referred to in this article subject to the IBS and CBS regular regime are permitted, observing the provision of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 287. The rates of the IBS and the CBS levied on the supply of regional air collective passenger or cargo transport services are reduced by 40% (forty percent).

                                                                                        Section IV

                                                                              Of Tourism Agencies

        Art. 288. Tourism agency services are subject to a specific regime for the levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this Section.

        Art. 289. In the intermediation of tourism services carried out by tourism agencies:

       I - the tax base of the IBS and the CBS is the value of the transaction, less the amounts passed on to the suppliers intermediated by the agency based on the
  document that substantiates the agency transaction; and

        II - the rate is the same one applicable to hotel services, amusement parks and theme parks.

        § 1º The value of the transaction referred to in item I of the caput of this article comprises the total value charged to the user of the agency's service, including all
  the goods and services provided and enjoyed with the intermediation of the agency, added to its margin and other charges collected from the user.

        § 2º The other amounts, commissions and incentives paid by third parties, as a result of the agency's activity, also form part of the tax base and are subject to the provisions of this article.

        Art. 290. The appropriation, by the acquirer, of IBS and CBS credits relating to the intermediation service rendered by the tourism agency is permitted,
  observing the provision of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 291. The appropriation and use of IBS and CBS credits on acquisitions of goods and services by tourism agencies are permitted, the
  crediting of amounts that are deducted from the tax base, under the terms of item I of the caput of art. 289 of this Complementary Law, being prohibited, observing the provision of arts. 47 to
  56 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                     CHAPTER VIII

                                                                   OF THE FOOTBALL CORPORATION - SAF

        Art. 292. Transactions with goods and services carried out by a Sociedade Anônima do Futebol - SAF (Football Corporation) are subject to a specific IBS and CBS regime, in
  accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

         Sole paragraph. An SAF is considered to be the company whose principal activity consists of the practice of football, women's and men's, in professional
  competition, subject to the rules provided for in specific legislation.

        Art. 293. The SAF is subject to the Specific Football Taxation Regime - TEF established in this Chapter.

        § 1º The TEF consists of the monthly payment of the following taxes and contributions, to be assessed following the cash basis:

        I - Corporate Income Tax - IRPJ;

        II - Social Contribution on Net Income - CSLL;

        III - contributions provided for in items I, II and III of the caput and in § 6º of art. 22 of Law No. 8,212, of July 24, 1991;

        IV - CBS; and

        V - IBS.

         § 2º Payment in the manner of this Chapter does not exclude the levy of other federal, state, district or municipal taxes, owed in the capacity of
  taxpayer or party liable, in relation to which the legislation applicable to other legal entities shall be observed.

        § 3º The tax base for the unified monthly payment of the taxes referred to in § 1º of this article shall be the total revenue received in the month, including
  that relating to:

        I - prizes and fan-membership (sócio-torcedor) programs;

        II - assignment of athletes' sporting rights;

        III - assignment of image rights; and

        IV - transfer of the athlete to another sporting entity or their return to activity at another sporting entity.

        § 4º The value of the unified monthly payment of the taxes referred to in § 1º of this article shall be calculated by applying the following rates:

        I - 4% (four percent) for the unified federal taxes referred to in items I to III of § 1º of this article;

        II - 1.5% (one and five-tenths percent) for the CBS; and

        II - 1% (one percent) for the CBS; and       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - 3% (three percent) for the IBS, of which:

        III - 1% (one percent) for the IBS, of which:       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) half of that percentage corresponds to the state rate; and

        b) half of that percentage corresponds to the municipal rate.


        § 5º The SAF may only appropriate and use IBS and CBS credits in relation to transactions in which it is the acquirer of athletes' sporting rights,
  at the same rate owed on those transactions, observing, as applicable, the provision of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         § 6º The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by acquirers of goods and services from the SAF is prohibited, with the exception of the acquisition of athletes' sporting rights,
  at the same rate owed on those transactions, observing, as applicable, the provision of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         § 7º For purposes of the apportionment of tax revenue, the amount collected in the manner of the unified monthly payment referred to in § 4º of this article shall be allocated to the
  taxes specified below, by applying the following percentages to the amount collected:

        I - 43.5% (forty-three and five-tenths percent) to the IRPJ;

        II - 18.6% (eighteen and six-tenths percent) to the CSLL; and

         III - 37.9% (thirty-seven and nine-tenths percent) to the contributions provided for in items I, II and III of the caput and in § 6º of art. 22 of Law No. 8,212, of July
  24, 1991, distributed as governed by an act of the Minister of State for Finance.

        § 8º A joint act of the RFB and the IBS Management Committee shall regulate the manner of payment of the IBS and the CBS owed under this Chapter.

        § 9º (VETOED).         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 10. (VETOED).         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 294. From January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2032, the rates of the taxes comprising the TEF shall be:

        I - as to the federal taxes referred to in items I to III of § 1º of art. 293, the rate defined in item I of § 4º of art. 293 of this Complementary Law;

        II - as to the CBS, the rate defined in item II of § 4º of art. 293 of this Complementary Law, which shall be reduced by 0.1% (one-tenth percent) for the
  calendar years 2027 and 2028; and

        III - as to the IBS:

        a) 0.1% (one-tenth percent) in 2027 and 2028;

        b) 0.3% (three-tenths percent) in 2029;

        c) 0.6% (six-tenths percent) in 2030;

        d) 0.9% (nine-tenths percent) in 2031;

        e) 1.2% (one and two-tenths percent) in 2032; and

        f) the full rate percentage, from 2033 onward.

         Sole paragraph. The provision of items "a" and "b" of item III of § 4º and of § 7º of art. 293 of this Complementary Law applies to the apportionment of the
  tax revenue of the taxes referred to in the caput of this article during the transition period.

        Art. 295. The importation of athletes' sporting rights is subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS at the same rates applicable to transactions carried out
  in the Country, applying the rules for the importation of intangible goods, including rights, and of services provided for in Section II of Chapter IV of Title I of this Book.

         Art. 296. The assignment of athletes' sporting rights to a resident or domiciliary abroad for the carrying out of sporting activities predominantly
  abroad shall be considered an export for purposes of the IBS and CBS immunity, the percentages referred to in items II and III of § 4º of art. 293 of this
  Complementary Law being excluded from the rate applicable for calculation of the unified payment referred to in the said article.

                                                                                     CHAPTER IX

                      OF DIPLOMATIC MISSIONS, CONSULAR OFFICES AND TRANSACTIONS COVERED BY INTERNATIONAL TREATY

        Art. 297. Transactions with goods and services covered by a treaty or international convention entered into by the Union and endorsed by the National
  Congress, under the terms of item VIII of art. 84 of the Federal Constitution, including those relating to diplomatic missions, consular offices, representations of
  international organizations and their respective accredited officials, are subject to a specific regime for the levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of this
  Chapter.

         Art. 298. Amounts of IBS and CBS paid in transactions with goods or services intended for diplomatic missions and consular offices of a
  permanent nature and their respective accredited officials may be reimbursed, under the terms of the regulations, upon approval by the Ministry of Foreign
  Affairs after verification of the tax regime applied to Brazilian diplomatic representations and their respective officials in that country.

        Art. 299. The application of the rules relating to the IBS and the CBS provided for in an internalized treaty or international convention, including those
  relating to international organizations of which Brazil is a member and their respective accredited officials, and those in force on the date of publication of this Complementary Law, shall be
  regulated by joint act of the Minister of State for Finance and the IBS Management Committee, after consulting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

                                                                                     CHAPTER X

                                                              COMMON PROVISIONS FOR THE SPECIFIC REGIMES

        Art. 300. The assessment period of the IBS and the CBS in the specific regimes for financial services, health care plans and prognostic contests
  referred to in Chapters II, III and IV of this Title shall be monthly.

        Art. 301. If the tax base of the IBS and the CBS in the specific regimes for financial services, health care plans and prognostic contests
  referred to in Chapters II, III and IV of this Title is negative in the assessment period, the taxpayer may deduct the negative value from the tax base, without
  any restatement, from the positive tax bases of subsequent assessment periods.

        Sole paragraph. The deduction referred to in the caput may be made within a period of up to 5 (five) years counted from the last business day of the assessment period.

        Art. 302. Taxpayers subject to the specific regimes for financial services, health care plans, prognostic contests and real property referred to in Chapters II, III, IV and V of this Title may appropriate and use the IBS and CBS credit on their acquisitions of goods and services, observing the
  provision of arts. 47 to 56, except where there is a specific rule in a specific regime applicable to the goods and services acquired.

         Sole paragraph. The assessment of the IBS and CBS in the specific regimes referred to in the caput does not entail reversal, partial or full, of the credits relating to
  acquisitions of goods and services.

        Art. 303. The appropriation of IBS and CBS credit on amounts that are deducted from the tax base of the IBS and the CBS in the specific
  regimes, as well as the duplicate deduction of any amount, is prohibited.

        Art. 304. The general rules on the levy of the IBS and the CBS referred to in Title I of this Book apply to transactions, imports and exports with
  goods and services carried out by suppliers subject to specific regimes and that are not the subject of one of those specific regimes.
         Art. 305. The ancillary obligations to be complied with by legal entities subject to specific regimes shall be uniform throughout the national territory and
  may be different from those applicable to the operationalization of the IBS and the CBS on transactions, provided for in the general levy rules referred to in Chapter III
  of Title I of this Book, including in relation to their periodicity, and shall be set by the regulations.

        § 1º The ancillary obligations referred to in the caput must contain the information necessary for the assessment of the tax base, crediting and distribution
  of the proceeds from the collection of the IBS, in addition to the other information required in each specific regime.

        § 2º The data to be reported in the ancillary obligations referred to in the caput may be aggregated by municipality, under the terms of the regulations.

       § 3º The information provided by the taxable person under the terms of this article has a declaratory character, constituting a confession of the amount owed of IBS and
  CBS set out in the ancillary obligation.

         § 4º The regulations shall provide for cases in which compliance with the ancillary obligation referred to in this article shall exempt the issuance of the electronic tax
  document referred to in art. 60 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 306. In the case of financial services and health care plans acquired by the Union, States, the Federal District and Municipalities, the
  same rules provided for in art. 473 of this Complementary Law for other acquisitions of goods and services by the direct public administration, by agencies and by
  public foundations shall apply.

        Art. 307. The general rules on the levy of the IBS and the CBS, in accordance with the provisions of Title I of this Book, apply as to rules not
  expressly provided for the specific regimes in this Title.

                                                                                    TITLE VI

                                                                     OF THE DIFFERENTIATED CBS REGIMES

                                                                                    CHAPTER I

                                                            OF THE UNIVERSITY FOR ALL PROGRAM - PROUNI

        Art. 308. The rate of the CBS levied on the supply of higher education services by a private educational institution, with or without a profit motive,
  is reduced to zero during the period of adherence and participation in the University for All Program - Prouni, established by Law No. 11,096, of January 13,
  2005.

        § 1º The rate reduction referred to in the caput shall be applied:

        I - to revenue arising from the carrying out of higher education activities, arising from undergraduate courses or specific-training sequential
  courses; and

        II - in proportion to the effective occupation of the scholarships owed within the scope of the Prouni, under the terms defined in an act of the Executive Branch of the Union.

        § 2º If the institution is disaffiliated from the Prouni, the CBS shall be required as of the initial term established for requiring the other federal taxes
  covered by the Prouni.

                                                                                    CHAPTER II

                                                                             OF THE AUTOMOTIVE REGIME

        Art. 309. Until December 31, 2032, presumed CBS credit shall be available, under the terms of this Complementary Law, to projects qualified for the benefits
  established by art. 11-C of Law No. 9,440, of March 14, 1997, and by arts. 1º to 4º of Law No. 9,826, of August 23, 1999. Effective as of

        § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput:

         I - shall exclusively incentivize the production of vehicles equipped with an electric motor capable of propelling the vehicle solely with electric power,
  combination with an internal combustion engine that uses biofuels being permitted, alone or simultaneously with petroleum-derived fuels; and

        II - shall be granted exclusively to:

        a) projects approved by December 31, 2024, of legal entities that, on December 20, 2023, were qualified for the benefits
  established by art. 11-C of Law No. 9,440, of March 14, 1997, and by arts. 1º to 4º of Law No. 9,826, of August 23, 1999; and

          b) new projects, approved by December 31, 2025, that expand or restart production at an industrial plant used in active or inactive projects
  qualified for the benefits referred to in item "a" of this item.

         § 2º The benefit referred to in this article shall be extended to projects of legal entities referred to in item "a" of item II of § 1º related to the production of
  vehicles propelled by an internal combustion engine that use biofuels, alone or cumulatively with petroleum-derived fuels, provided that the
  qualified legal entity:

        I - begins production of the vehicles referred to in item I of § 1º by January 1, 2028, at the incentivized establishment; and

        II - assumes, under the terms of the benefit's granting act, commitments relating to:

        a) the minimum volume of investments;

        b) the minimum volume of production;

        c) compliance with the basic production process;

        d) the maintenance of production for a minimum period, including after the termination of the benefit.

        § 3º The benefit referred to in the caput is conditioned on:

         I - the carrying out of investments in research, development and technological innovation in the region, including in the field of automotive engineering,
  corresponding to at least 10% (ten percent) of the value of the presumed credit assessed, under the terms regulated by the Ministry of Development,
  Industry, Trade and Services - MDIC; and

        II - the tax compliance of the legal entity as to federal taxes.

        § 4º An act of the Executive Branch of the Union shall define the requirements and conditions of the requirements contained in item II of § 2º and in item I of § 3º.

        § 5º Compliance with the requirements and conditions referred to in item II of § 2º and item I of § 3º shall be evidenced before the MDIC.

        § 6º The MDIC shall send to the RFB, annually, the results of the audits relating to compliance with the requirements referred to in § 4º.



        Art. 310. The presumed credit referred to in art. 309 may not be enjoyed cumulatively with any other federal CBS tax benefits
  intended for the beneficiary of that presumed credit. Effective as of

        Art. 311. In relation to projects qualified for the benefits established by art. 11-C of Law No. 9,440, of March 14, 1997, the presumed credit
  referred to in art. 309 of this Complementary Law shall be calculated by applying the following percentages to the value of domestic market sales, in
  each month, of the products included in the projects referred to in art. 309, manufactured or assembled at the incentivized establishments: Effective as of

        I - 11.60% (eleven and sixty-hundredths percent) up to the 12th (twelfth) month of enjoyment of the benefit;

        II - 10% (ten percent) from the 13th (thirteenth) to the 48th (forty-eighth) month of enjoyment of the benefit;

        III - 8.70% (eight and seventy-hundredths percent) from the 49th (forty-ninth) to the 60th (sixtieth) month of enjoyment of the benefit.

         § 1º In calculating the presumed credit referred to in the caput, taxes and contributions levied on the sales transaction shall not be included, and
  unconditional discounts granted shall be excluded.

        § 2º The presumed credit referred to in the caput applies only to domestic market sales made with the full charging of the CBS, not including:

       I - sales that are exempt, immune, not covered by the levy of the contribution, at a zero rate, with a reduction of rates or of the tax base, or with
  suspension of the contribution; and

        II - cancelled and returned sales.

         § 3º The percentages referred to in items I to III of the caput shall be reduced at the rate of 20% (twenty percent) of the initial percentage per year, between 2029 and 2032,
  until they are extinguished as of 2033.

        Art. 312. In relation to projects qualified for the benefits established by arts. 1º to 4º of Law No. 9,826, of August 23, 1999, the presumed
  credit referred to in art. 309 of this Complementary Law shall correspond to the product of the multiplication of the following factors: Effective as of

       I - the value of domestic market sales, in each month, of the products included in the projects referred to in art. 309 of this Complementary Law, manufactured or
  assembled at the incentivized establishments;

        II - the rates of the Tax on Industrialized Products - IPI in force on December 31, 2025, in accordance with the Table of Incidence of the Tax on
  Industrialized Products - Tipi, including Supplementary Notes, relating to products classified under headings 8702 to 8704;

        III - the efficiency factor, which shall be the result of the calculation of 1 (one) less the rate referred to in item II, for each heading in the Tipi; and

        IV - the multiplying factor, which shall be:

        a) 32.00% (thirty-two percent) in the years 2027 and 2028;

        b) 25.60% (twenty-five and sixty-hundredths percent) in the year 2029;

        c) 19.20% (nineteen and twenty-hundredths percent) in the year 2030;

        d) 12.80% (twelve and eighty-hundredths percent) in the year 2031; and

        e) 6.40% (six and forty-hundredths percent) in the year 2032.

        Sole paragraph. The provision of §§ 1º and 2º of art. 311 of this Complementary Law applies to this article.

        Art. 313. Credits assessed as a result of the benefits referred to in art. 309 may only be used for:           Effective as of

        I - offsetting against CBS debits; and

        II - offsetting against the entity's own debits relating to taxes administered by the RFB, observing the conditions and limits in force for offsetting as of the date of the
  declaration.

        § 1º The credits referred to in this article:

        I - may not be transferred to another establishment of the legal entity;

        II - must be used only for the deduction and offsetting of the qualified establishment's own debits, located in the incentivized region; and

        III - may not be the subject of reimbursement.

        § 2º The own debits of the qualified establishment located in the incentivized region are considered to be the portion of the legal entity's federal tax and contribution
  debits by way of apportionment established in an Act of the Executive Branch of the Union.

        Art. 314. Failure to comply with the conditions required for enjoyment of the presumed credit may give rise to the following penalties:              Effective as of

        I - cancellation of the qualification with retroactive effects; or

        II - suspension of the qualification.

         Sole paragraph. The suspension of the qualification referred to in item II of the caput may be applied in the event of a finding of non-compliance, by the qualified
  legal entity, with the condition referred to in item II of § 3º of art. 309, the use of the presumed credit referred to in this Chapter remaining suspended until
  the reasons that gave rise to the suspension of the qualification are remedied.
         Art. 315. Cancellation of the authorization may be applied in the event of failure to comply with the requirements and conditions referred to in art. 309, even if
  it occurs after the period of appropriation of the presumed credit. Effective as of publication.

        § 1º Cancellation of the authorization shall result in the return of a portion of the presumed credit calculated for the period, together with the legal additions thereto, which
  shall correspond to the product of the multiplication of the following factors:

        I - total presumed credit calculated for the period fixed in the granting act;

        II - 100% (one hundred percent) reduced by the product of the multiplication of the following percentage values:

        a) F1%: result of dividing the sum of investments made by the establishment during the credit period by the minimum volume of investments in the
  credit period fixed in the act granting the benefit, such that F1% may not exceed 100.0% (one hundred percent);
