        b) F2%: result of dividing the sum of the production volumes achieved by the establishment during the credit period by the minimum production volume
  in the credit period fixed in the act granting the benefit, such that F2% may not exceed 100.0% (one hundred percent); and


         c) F3%: result of dividing the period of maintenance of production at the establishment, including after termination of the benefit, by the minimum
  production period fixed in the act granting the benefit, including the period after termination of the benefit, such that F3% may not exceed 100.0% (one hundred
  percent).

        § 2º The portion of the presumed credit to be returned referred to in § 1º:

        I - shall be calculated by the MDIC, upon closing of the process of cancellation of the authorization, which must be initiated within 5 (five) years counted from the date of
  becoming aware of the failure to comply with the requirements and conditions referred to in art. 309;

        II - shall be subject to late-payment interest calculated in the same manner as that calculated on federal taxes, under the terms of the law, counted from the assessment period in
  which the event that gave rise to the cancellation of the authorization occurs; and

        III - must be paid by the last business day of the month following the cancellation of the authorization.

         § 3º The right of the tax administration to collect the return of the portion of the presumed credit referred to in this article shall be 5 (five) years counted from
  the first day of the month following the one in which the payment should have been made, pursuant to item III of § 2º.

         Art. 316. The IPI benefits established by art. 11-C of Law No. 9,440, of March 14, 1997, and by arts.
  1 to 4 of Law No. 9,826, of August 23, 1999, are extended until December 31, 2026, under the terms set forth in the aforementioned rules and in this article.

         § 1º During the period referred to in the caput, the conditions and requirements for enjoyment of the extended benefits remain enforceable under the same rules
  applicable to the beneficiary legal entity in the year 2025, whether arising from law or from the act granting the benefit.

         § 2º The presumed credit established by art. 11-C of Law No. 9,440, of March 14, 1997, shall be equivalent to the result of applying the rates
  provided for in art. 1 of Law No. 10,485, of July 3, 2002, to the value of domestic market sales, each month, of the products included in the projects
  approved for enjoyment of the benefit, multiplied by 0.75 (seventy-five hundredths).

                                                                                    TITLE VII

                                                                     ADMINISTRATION OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

                                                                                   CHAPTER I

                                                                     OF THE IBS AND CBS REGULATIONS

        Art. 317. It is the responsibility of:    Effective as of publication.

        I - the IBS Management Committee to issue the IBS regulation; and

        II - the Executive Branch of the Union to issue the CBS regulation.

        § 1º Provisions common to the IBS and the CBS, including subsequent amendments thereto, shall be approved by joint act of the IBS Management Committee and the
  Executive Branch of the Union and shall likewise be set out in the IBS regulation and the CBS regulation.

        § 2º All references made to "the regulation" in this Book shall be understood as a reference:

        I - to the IBS regulation, in the case of the IBS; and

        II - to the CBS regulation, in the case of the CBS.

                                                                                   CHAPTER II

                                                                     OF THE HARMONIZATION OF THE IBS AND THE CBS

        Art. 318. The IBS Management Committee, the RFB, and the Attorney General's Office of the National Treasury shall act with a view to harmonizing rules, interpretations, ancillary
  obligations, and procedures relating to the IBS and the CBS.

       Sole paragraph. For purposes of the provisions of the caput, the aforementioned bodies may enter into agreements for purposes of providing mutual assistance and
  sharing information relating to their respective taxes.

        Art. 319. Harmonization of the IBS and the CBS shall be ensured by the following bodies:

        I - Tax Administration Harmonization Committee composed of:

        a) 4 (four) representatives of the RFB; and

        b) 4 (four) representatives of the IBS Management Committee, 2 (two) of whom from the States or the Federal District and 2 (two) from the Municipalities or the Federal District; and

        II - Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices composed of:

        a) 4 (four) representatives of the Attorney General's Office of the National Treasury, appointed by the Union; and

        b) 4 (four) representatives of the Attorney's Offices, appointed by the IBS Management Committee, 2 (two) of whom being State or Federal District Attorneys and 2 (two)
  Municipal or Federal District Attorneys.

        § 1º The Committee provided for in item I of the caput shall be chaired and coordinated alternately by a representative of the RFB and by a representative of the IBS Management
  Committee, as provided for in its internal regulations.

         § 2º The Forum provided for in item II of the caput shall be chaired and coordinated alternately by a representative of the PGFN and by a representative of the attorneys
  appointed by the IBS Management Committee, as provided for in its internal regulations.

        Art. 320. The collegiate bodies referred to in art. 319:

        I - shall hold periodic meetings, subject to a minimum participation quorum of 3/4 (three quarters) of the representatives;

        II - shall decide, as provided in their internal regulations, by unanimity of those present;

        III - shall have their members appointed by the Minister of State for Finance, with respect to the representatives of the Union, and by the President of the IBS Management Committee,
  with respect to the representatives of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities; and

        IV - shall draw up their internal regulations by resolution.

        Art. 321. It is the responsibility of the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee to:

        I - standardize the regulation and interpretation of legislation relating to the IBS and the CBS with respect to common matters;
        II - prevent litigation relating to the common rules applicable to the IBS and the CBS; and

        III - deliberate on ancillary obligations and common procedures relating to the IBS and the CBS.

         Sole paragraph. The resolutions approved by the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee, from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette of the Union,
  shall bind the tax administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities.

        § 1º The resolutions approved by the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee, from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette of the Union, shall bind the
  tax administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º Harmonization of the interpretation of IBS and CBS legislation may be requested by the authorities referred to in § 1º of art. 322 and by any
  of the entities representing economic categories responsible for the nomination of taxpayer representatives on the IBS and CBS administrative
  adjudication bodies. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 3º A request for harmonization of the interpretation of IBS and CBS legislation, under the terms of § 2º of this article, shall be decided within 90 (ninety)
  business days counted from the date the request is submitted. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 4º In exercising the powers provided for in the items of the caput of this article, the decisions of the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee
  must be substantiated. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 322. It is the responsibility of the Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices to:

       I - act as an advisory body to the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee in the activities of standardizing and interpreting the common
  rules relating to the IBS and the CBS; and

        II - analyze significant and widespread legal disputes relating to the IBS and the CBS raised under the terms of § 1º.

        II - analyze legal disputes relating to the IBS and the CBS raised under the terms of § 1º.   (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º The Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices shall examine matters relating to significant and widespread legal disputes relating
  to the IBS and the CBS raised by the following authorities:

         § 1º The Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices shall examine matters relating to legal disputes relating to the IBS and the CBS
  raised by the following authorities: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the President of the IBS Management Committee; and

        II - the Minister of State for Finance.

        § 2º The resolutions approved by the Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices, from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette of the Union, shall bind the
  Attorney General's Office of the National Treasury and the Attorney's Offices of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities.

        Art. 323. A joint act of the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee and the Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices must be
  observed, from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette of the Union, in the administrative, normative, and adjudicatory acts carried out by the tax administrations of the
  Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities and in the acts of the Attorney General's Office of the National Treasury and the Attorney's Offices of the States, the Federal District,
  and the Municipalities.

        Sole paragraph. It is the responsibility of the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee and the Legal Harmonization Forum of the Attorney's Offices, within the scope of
  their respective competencies, to propose the joint act referred to in the caput.

        Art. 323-A. The person liable for a tax obligation is guaranteed the right to submit a written inquiry regarding the application of IBS and
  CBS tax legislation, with respect to a specific matter of interest, which must be completely and exactly described in the petition. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        § 1º The inquiry shall contain: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the identification of the party submitting the inquiry; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - the matter of law that is the subject of the doubt; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        III - the date of the taxable event of the principal or ancillary obligation, if it has already occurred; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        IV - a declaration as to the existence or non-existence of the commencement of a tax procedure with respect to the party submitting the inquiry. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 2º Each inquiry must refer to a single matter, cumulation being admitted only when related questions are involved.                   (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 323-B. The resolution of an inquiry relating to the interpretation and application of IBS and CBS legislation shall be issued by the respective bodies of the CGIBS and the
  RFB, subject to the provisions of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º Once the proposed resolution of the inquiry has been drafted, the consulted body shall make the draft available in a shared virtual environment for evaluation by the other
  body, which may, within 30 (thirty) days counted from the date of availability, extendable, upon justification, once, for an equal period:  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        I - accept the draft and jointly issue the resolution of the inquiry; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       II - forward the proposal for deliberation by the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee, in the event of divergence; or               (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

        III - state that there is no matter common to the IBS and the CBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º Forwarding the proposed resolution for deliberation by the Tax Administration Harmonization Committee shall suspend the processing of the
  inquiry procedure before the consulted body until a resolution is issued under the terms of § 1º of art. 321 of this Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 3º If the period referred to in § 1º of this article elapses without a response from the other body, the shared draft shall be deemed tacitly accepted and a
  joint resolution of the inquiry shall be published, with a statement of tacit acceptance by one of the bodies. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 4º The regulation shall govern the procedure referred to in this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 323-C. The inquiry produces the following effects: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - no tax procedure shall be initiated with respect to the matter inquired about, during the period between the filing of the inquiry request and
  notice of the response, provided that the filing occurred before the due date of the obligation to which it refers; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)
         II - it binds the tax administrations and the taxpayer submitting the inquiry, within the limits of the specific matter that was the subject of the analysis, without binding third parties.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. The tax due in accordance with the response to the inquiry shall be paid without the imposition of a penalty, provided that: (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

       I - payment is made within 15 (fifteen) days counted from the date on which the party submitting the inquiry becomes aware of the response;         (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - the filing of the inquiry petition occurred before the due date of the obligation to which it refers.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        Art. 323-D. The inquiry does not suspend the deadline for payment of the tax, before or after it is submitted, nor the deadline for compliance with
  ancillary obligations to which the party submitting the inquiry is subject. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Sole paragraph. The effects provided for in art. 323-C shall not apply to inquiries that: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - contain inaccurate or untrue data; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - do not describe exactly and completely the matter that gave rise to them; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         III - are merely dilatory, understood as those dealing with provisions clearly stated in the tax legislation or with a question
  of law already resolved by a final administrative or judicial decision; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        IV - fail to observe a formal requirement that is not remedied within the period established by the tax authority;      (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

        V - deal with an allegation of unconstitutionality or with the refusal to apply tax legislation;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

          VI - are submitted after the commencement of a tax procedure with respect to the matter inquired about. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 323-E. The tax that is the subject of the matter inquired about shall not be assessed against the taxpayer who acts in strict accordance with the resolution of the
  inquiry, of which they have been notified, so long as it has not been revoked, in whole or in part. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º A change in guidance does not require payment of the tax deemed due for a taxable event that occurred between the date of notification of the
  amended resolution and the date of the new guidance. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º While a response to an inquiry submitted is pending, the taxpayer shall also be deemed notified of the resolution of the inquiry upon the publication of
  any normative act dealing with the same matter. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 3º The subsequent enactment of a tax legislation rule shall cause the effects of the response to the inquiry to cease insofar as the rule conflicts with the response,
  regardless of communication to the party submitting the inquiry. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Art. 323-F. No appeal or motion for reconsideration shall be admissible against the resolution of the inquiry or the order declaring it ineffective.                (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         Sole paragraph. The resolution of the inquiry shall be final and shall be issued within the period defined in the regulation, counted from the date of its filing.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                 CHAPTER II-A
                                                               (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                             OF THE INTEGRATION OF IBS AND CBS LITIGATION

        Art. 323-G. A special appeal is admissible, within 10 (ten) business days, against a decision of the CGIBS issued by an Appellate Adjudication Chamber or by a First-Instance
  Adjudication Chamber under summary proceedings, or against a decision of a Chamber, panel of a Chamber, extraordinary panel, or special panel of the Administrative Council of Tax Appeals
  (Carf), that gives the common IBS and CBS legislation a legal interpretation diverging from that given to it by another
  decision of those adjudication bodies, with a view to standardizing administrative case law on matters common to the two taxes.          (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 1º The appeal referred to in the caput shall be examined by the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and CBS Administrative Litigation, composed of:
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       I - 4 (four) counselors representing the National Treasury on the Superior Chamber of Tax Appeals of Carf, appointed by the Minister of State for
  Finance; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - 4 (four) members of the Superior Chamber of the CGIBS, 2 (two) of whom from the tax administrations of the States and the Federal District and 2 (two) from the
  tax administrations of the Municipalities and the Federal District, appointed by the CGIBS; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        III - 4 (four) taxpayer representatives, 2 (two) of whom from among the counselors of the Superior Chamber of Tax Appeals of Carf and 2 (two) from among
  the members of the Superior Chamber of the CGIBS, appointed respectively by the Minister of State for Finance and by the CGIBS; (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

          IV - the President, who shall vote only in the event of a tie. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 2º The petition for filing the special appeal must transcribe the headnote and the pertinent excerpts of the paradigm decision, sufficient to demonstrate
  the existence of a divergence regarding the common IBS and CBS legislation. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 3º The following may file a special appeal: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - the representation of the Public Treasury; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - the taxpayer. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 4º The special appeal suspends the enforceability of the tax credit. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 5º Decisions rendered in special appeal proceedings: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       I - are not bound by the grounds presented by the parties and may diverge both from the paradigm ruling and from the decision under appeal;          (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

       II - may not set aside the application of, or fail to observe, tax legislation on the grounds of unconstitutionality or illegality; (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)


           III - are limited to the examination of questions of law, with review of the factual and evidentiary record prohibited; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       IV - shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Union and, from the date of their publication, shall bind the adjudication bodies of the Union and of the CGIBS.                 (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 6º No appeal is admissible against the collegiate decision of the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and CBS Administrative Litigation that denies admission of the special
  appeal. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 7º A joint act of the CGIBS and the Minister of State for Finance shall regulate the provisions of this article, including with respect to the terms of office of the adjudicators
  referred to in § 1º. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 8º The Presidency of the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and CBS Administrative Litigation shall be held, on an alternating basis, by a representative
  of the National Treasury or by a representative of the CGIBS, in the manner established in the joint act referred to in § 7º of this article.            (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Art. 323-H. A motion for a standardization incident before the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and
  CBS Administrative Litigation is admissible: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - for recurring matters, when there are repeated rulings on the same question of law, subject to the provisions of arts. 323-I and 323-J;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       II - for a second-instance decision that fails to apply a binding ruling, subject to the provisions of arts. 323-K and 323-L.                     (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 1º The judgment of the standardization incident for recurring matters shall establish a legal thesis on the matter, and it shall be the responsibility of the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and
  CBS Administrative Litigation to issue a binding precedent that shall have the character of a binding ruling from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette of the Union.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 2º The binding effect referred to in § 1º of this article also extends to all challenges and appeals, pending or future, that deal with an
  identical question of law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 3º Review of the thesis established in the standardization incident may be sought either on the adjudicator's own initiative or upon request by the parties entitled to do so under arts. 323-J and 323-L.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 4º A joint act of the CGIBS and the Minister of State for Finance shall govern the processing of the incident referred to in this article. (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 323-I. The motion for the standardization incident referred to in item I of the caput of art. 323-H must be accompanied by 5 (five) final
  decisions rendered by an Adjudication Chamber of the CGIBS or by a Chamber, panel of a Chamber, extraordinary panel, or special panel of Carf, or by 3 (three)
  decisions rendered by the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and CBS Administrative Litigation, by, at a minimum, a majority vote, in distinct
  adjudication sessions, under penalty of the motion not being admitted. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

           Art. 323-J. The following may raise the standardization incident referred to in item I of the caput of art. 323-H: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

           I - the representation of the Public Treasury; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - the Presidents of an Adjudication Chamber of the CGIBS, the Presidents of a Chamber, panel of a Chamber, extraordinary panel, or special panel of Carf, or the
  President of the National Chamber for the Integration of IBS and CBS Administrative Litigation. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. The standardization incident referred to in item I of the caput of art. 323-H shall not suspend the enforceability of the tax credit. (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 323-K. The motion for the standardization incident referred to in item II of the caput of art. 323-H must be accompanied by an indication of the
  binding ruling that the second-instance decision failed to apply. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

           Art. 323-L. The following may raise the standardization incident referred to in item II of the caput of art. 323-H: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

           I - the representation of the Public Treasury; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

           II - the taxpayer. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. The standardization incident referred to in item II of the caput of art. 323-H shall suspend the enforceability of the tax credit. (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Art. 323-M. A joint act of the CGIBS and the Minister of State for Finance shall regulate the provisions of arts. 323-H to 323-L.                              (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                     CHAPTER III

                                                                DEFICIENCY AUDITS AND EX OFFICIO ASSESSMENT

                                                                                        Section I

                                                                           Of the Power to Audit

           Art. 324. The audit of compliance with principal and ancillary tax obligations, as well as the establishment of the tax credit relating:

           I - to the CBS is the responsibility of the tax authority that is part of the tax administration of the Union;

           II - to the IBS is the responsibility of the tax authorities that are part of the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities.

           Art. 325. The RFB and the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities:

         I - may use in their respective assessments the grounds and evidence arising from the ex officio assessment administrative proceeding carried out by
  another federative entity;

           II - shall share, in the same environment, the records of the commencement and outcome of CBS and IBS audits.

           § 1º The environment referred to in item II of the caput shall be jointly managed by the IBS Management Committee and the RFB.

           § 2º A joint act of the Management Committee and the RFB may provide for other cases of information to be shared in the environment referred to in item II of the
  caput.

        § 3º The use of the grounds and evidence referred to in item I of the caput, even if relating to closed administrative proceedings, does not dispense with the
  opportunity for the taxpayer to exercise adversarial proceedings and a full defense.
          § 4º In the environment referred to in item II of the caput of this article:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - the responses, clarifications, and documents provided in response to the following shall be kept on file:         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        a) an audit procedure of any of the federative entities, it being prohibited to request, in another audit procedure relating to the same
  taxable events and the same period, the same responses, clarifications, and documents; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        b) an administrative tax proceeding of any of the federative entities, which shall be taken into account by the adjudication bodies in other
  administrative tax proceedings relating to the same facts and assessment period; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       II - accesses to and the sharing of the information and documents contained therein shall be recorded, with at least the following being required:                        (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) identification of the permanent public servant responsible for the access;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) date, time, and reason for the access;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          c) a history of accesses and changes made;    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - the following information and documents shall not be shared:         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         a) information obtained on the basis of international treaties, agreements, or conventions for the exchange of tax information whose sharing is prohibited
  by the treaty, agreement, or convention, unless there is consent and it is authorized under the domestic legislation of the reporting country; (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) information protected by judicial secrecy;   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          c) information obtained on the basis of the provisions of art. 6 of Complementary Law No. 105, of January 10, 2001.              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

         Art. 326. The RFB and the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities may enter into an agreement for the reciprocal delegation of the
  activity of auditing the IBS and the CBS in low-value tax proceedings, understood as those in which the assessment does not exceed a single threshold established
  in the regulation.

         Art. 327. The Ministry of Finance and the IBS Management Committee may enter into an agreement for the reciprocal delegation of the adjudication of administrative litigation
  relating to the ex officio assessment of the IBS and the CBS carried out under the terms of art. 326.

         Art. 327-A. In the Manaus Free Trade Zone and in the Free Trade Areas, Suframa shall exercise, exclusively through its permanent staff, the
  activities of auditing compliance with the basic production process or with other commitments undertaken by the taxpayer at the time of approval of the
  economic project, of investments in research, development, and innovation and, without prejudice to the powers of the tax administrations, of the entry of
  goods and services. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º Suframa shall notify the federal, Federal District, State, and Municipal tax administrations that are part of the incentivized areas, whenever
  a failure to comply with the provisions of the caput is found. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º The tax administrations and other interested public bodies may submit a substantiated request for Suframa to institute a proceeding
  to verify compliance with the basic production process or with other commitments undertaken by the taxpayer at the time of approval of the economic
  project and of investments in research, development, and innovation referred to in the caput of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 3º (VETOED).      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                        Section II

                                                                     Of the Audit and the Tax Procedure

          Art. 328. The tax procedure begins with:

        I - notice to the taxpayer, its representative, or agent, of the first ex officio act, carried out by a tax authority that is part of the tax administrations
  of the Union, the states, the Federal District, and the municipalities, aimed at establishing a tax obligation or infraction;

          II - the seizure of goods;

          III - the seizure of documents or books, including in digital form;

          IV - the commencement of customs clearance of imported goods.

       § 1º The commencement of the tax procedure excludes the spontaneity of the taxpayer with respect to prior acts and, regardless of notification, that
  of the other parties involved in the infractions found.

         § 2º For purposes of the provisions of § 1º, the acts referred to in items I to III of the caput shall remain valid for a period of 90 (ninety) days, extendable, successively, for
  an equal period, by any other act that formalizes the continuation of the work.

          Art. 329. The following actions do not exclude the spontaneity of the taxpayer:

        I - data cross-referencing, understood as the comparison of information existing in the databases of the tax administrations or of the IBS Management
  Committee, or between such information and other information provided by the taxpayer or third parties;

         II - monitoring, understood as the evaluation of the tax-fiscal behavior of a taxpayer, individually or by economic sector, through
  ongoing oversight of compliance with obligations and analysis of economic-fiscal data, submitted or obtained by the tax administrations or by the IBS Management
  Committee, including through inspections of the establishment.

                                                                                        Section III

                                                                                Of Ex Officio Assessment

         Art. 330. In order to establish the tax credit arising from a tax procedure, by way of ex officio assessment, the tax authority that is part of the tax
  administration of the Union and the tax authorities that are part of the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities must issue a notice
  of infraction.

          Sole paragraph. The notice of infraction shall necessarily contain:

          § 1º The notice of infraction shall necessarily contain:    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - identification of the person cited;


        II - the place, date, and time of issuance;

        III - a description of the act;

        IV - the legal provision infringed and the applicable penalty;

        V - the determination of the demand and notification to comply with it or challenge it within the legal period;

        VI - the signature of the issuing officer, indication of the position, and registration number;

        VII - identification of the federative entity responsible for the assessment, in the case of a notice of infraction relating to the IBS.

        § 2º The issuance of the ex officio assessment act and its supporting documentation must be implemented electronically.              (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

        § 3º The issuance of the ex officio assessment act does not prevent the adoption of consensual dispute-resolution procedures for tax disputes.             (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 331. The demand for the tax credit and the imposition of a stand-alone penalty shall be the subject of separate notices of infraction for each tax or penalty.

        Sole paragraph. The provisions of the caput of this article also apply in cases in which, upon a violation of tax legislation being found, it does not
  result in a demand for a tax credit.

                                                                                     Section IV

                                                           Of the Electronic Tax Domicile - DTE and of Notifications

        Art. 332. Notifications of acts in the proceeding shall be made through the DTE, including in the case of notification of an attorney-in-fact.

        § 1º Notification made through the DTE is deemed personal, for all legal purposes.

        § 2º (VETOED).

        § 3º The tax administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities may effect notification in person, by the party initiating the
  procedure or by an agent of the body preparing the proceeding, at the office or elsewhere, evidenced by the signature of the taxpayer, its agent, attorney-in-fact, or
  legal representative, or, in the event of refusal, by a written certificate drawn up by the person effecting notification, identifying the person who refused.

         § 4º The bankrupt estate and the legal entity in extrajudicial liquidation shall be notified at the DTE of the legal entity, it being the responsibility of the judicial administrator and the
  liquidator, respectively, to update the physical and electronic address thereof.

         Art. 333. The RFB and the IBS Management Committee may establish an electronic communication system, with shared governance, to be designated as the DTE,
  which shall be used by the RFB and by the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities, for purposes of notice, notification, or advisories
  provided for in the CBS and IBS legislation.

        Art. 334. (VETOED).

                                                                                     Section V

                                                                             Of Legal Presumptions

        Art. 335. The following shall constitute omission of revenue and the occurrence of transactions subject to CBS and IBS incidence:

       I - the occurrence of transactions involving tangible or intangible property, including rights, or involving services, without the issuance of a tax document or without the issuance of a
  proper tax document;

        II - a credit balance in the cash account, shown in the bookkeeping or found in an audit procedure;

        III - maintenance, as a liability, of obligations already paid or whose enforceability is not proven;

        IV - failure to record in the books payments made by the legal entity;

        V - a hidden asset, whose entry does not appear in the accounts for the period covered by the audit procedure;

        VI - failure to make an accounting record of a document relating to transactions involving tangible or intangible property, including rights, or involving services;

        VII - amounts credited to a deposit or investment account maintained at a financial institution, with respect to which the holder, whether a natural person or a legal entity,
  duly notified, does not prove, by means of proper documentation, the origin of the funds used in such transactions;

         VIII - a cash advance provided to the company by a manager, partner, holder of a sole proprietorship, or controlling shareholder of the company, including by third parties,
  if the effectiveness of the delivery and the origin of the funds are not satisfactorily demonstrated;

         IX - a difference found through the quantitative control of the inflows and outflows of transactions involving tangible or intangible property, including rights, or involving
  services during a given period, taking into account the opening and closing balances;

        X - inventory valued in a manner inconsistent with what is provided for in tax legislation, for inventory purposes;

        XI - the write-off of liabilities whose offsetting entry does not correspond to actual debt settlement, reversal of a provision, exchange of amounts within liabilities, or
  a justified conversion of the obligation into revenue or transfer to equity accounts, in accordance with accounting bookkeeping standards;

         XII - amounts received by the taxpayer, reported by financial institutions, credit and debit card administrators, any institution
  participating in a payment arrangement, entities providing commercial intermediation in a virtual environment or related to electronic commerce, commercial
  condominiums, or another legal entity legally holding financial information, in excess of the amount of the transactions declared by the person liable for the tax
  obligation; and

         XIII - net revenue for the period analyzed that is lower than the cost of the goods sold, the cost of the merchandise sold, and the cost of the services rendered.

        § 1º The amount of revenue omitted for purposes of assessing federal taxes and the IBS, including under specific legal presumptions, shall be taken into account in determining the
  tax base for the assessment of the CBS and the IBS.

        § 2º The taxpayer shall bear the burden of proving the rebuttal of the presumptions referred to in this article.

        § 3º Where it is not possible to identify the moment of occurrence of the taxable event, in the cases provided for in this article, it shall be presumed to have occurred,
  observing the following order, on the last day:


        I - of the assessment period;

        II - of the fiscal year; or

        III - of the period audited.

        § 4º Where it is not possible to identify the place of the transaction, it shall be deemed to have occurred at the place of the taxpayer's principal domicile.

                                                                                        Section VI

                                                                         Of Tax and Supporting Documentation

        Art. 336. Bookkeeping records of the legal entity relating to matters that affect accounting entries in future fiscal years shall
  be retained until the right of the Public Treasury to establish the tax credits relating to those fiscal years lapses.

        Art. 337. A taxpayer that uses a data-processing system must maintain complete and up-to-date technical documentation of the system, sufficient
  to allow it to be audited, maintenance in digital form being permitted, without prejudice to its printing, when requested.

                                                                                     Section VII

                                                                      Of the Special Audit Regime - REF

        Art. 338. Without prejudice to other measures provided for in the legislation, the RFB and the tax administrations of the States, the Federal District, and the Municipalities
  may impose a Special Audit Regime - REF for compliance with tax obligations, in the following cases:

        I - obstruction of the audit, characterized by an unjustified refusal to provide documents or information, even if partial, regarding transactions
  involving goods or services, financial movements, business, or activity, whether one's own or that of third parties, when notified, and other cases that authorize a request for
  the assistance of the police force, under the terms of art. 200 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 - National Tax Code;

         II - resistance to the audit, characterized by refusal of access to the establishment, tax domicile, or any other location where the activities of the taxpayer are carried out, or the
  activities related to the goods or services in its possession or ownership;

         III - evidence that the legal entity is constituted through parties standing in for others who are not the true partners or shareholders, or the holder, in the case of a
  sole proprietorship;

        IV - carrying out transactions subject to tax incidence without the proper registration in the appropriate taxpayer register;

        V - repeated commission of violations of tax legislation;

        VI - marketing of goods with evidence of smuggling or contraband;

        VII - conduct that constitutes a crime against the tax order.

        § 1º In the cases provided for in items IV to VII of the caput, application of the REF does not depend on the prior institution of an audit procedure.

        § 2º For purposes of the provisions of item V of the caput, repeated commission shall be understood as:

        I - the second occurrence of identical violations of tax legislation, including of an ancillary nature, found with respect to the last 5 (five) calendar
  years, formalized by means of a notice of infraction; or

          II - the occurrence, in 2 (two) or more assessment periods, consecutive or alternating, of violations of tax legislation, where it is found that a device,
  scheme, or any other fraudulent means was used with a view to suppressing, deferring, or reducing payment of the tax.

         § 3º For purposes of application of the provisions of item I of § 2º, violations of an ancillary nature that do not prejudice the assessment and
  collection of the principal obligations or that are not a requirement for taking advantage of a tax benefit shall not be taken into account, without prejudice to the application of the sanction provided for the
  conduct.

        § 4º Application of the REF must be based on a detailed report prepared by the responsible tax authority, which must contain, at a minimum:

        I - identification of the taxpayer subject to the audit procedure;

        II - the classification under one or more of the cases provided for in the caput;

        III - a description of the facts justifying application of the regime;

        IV - a copy of the notices issued and the notifications made;

        V - the proposed measures provided for in art. 339 to be adopted and the period of validity of the regime; and

        VI - identification of the tax authority responsible for carrying out the audit procedure.

        § 5º The REF shall begin upon notice, to the taxpayer, of a substantiated order, which shall state the grounds, the measures adopted, and the
  duration.

        Art. 339. The special audit regime may consist of:

        I - maintenance of uninterrupted oversight at the taxpayer's establishment;

        II - reduction, by half, of the assessment periods and of the deadlines for payment of the CBS and the IBS;

        III - compulsory use of electronic control of the transactions carried out;

        IV - a requirement of daily payment of the CBS and the IBS levied on the transactions carried out by the taxpayer, without prejudice to the use of the
  credits of those taxes by the taxpayer, under the terms of art. 53 of this Complementary Law;

        V - a requirement of systematic proof of compliance with tax obligations; and

        VI - special control of the issuance of commercial and tax documents and monitoring of financial movements.

        Art. 340. Application of the REF shall be governed:

        I - by the RFB, with respect to the CBS; and

        II - by the IBS Management Committee, with respect to the IBS.


          § 1º In regulating the REF, the RFB and the Management Committee must:

        I - require that the order referred to in § 5º of art. 338 be issued by an authority hierarchically superior to the tax authority responsible for the
  audit procedure, in order to apply the REF; and

         II - provide for a maximum duration for the REF, which may only be renewed, by means of a new substantiated order, in cases where the
  circumstances warranting its application persist.

          § 2º In defining the measures provided for in art. 339 applicable to the taxpayer, the tax authority must:

          I - consider the seriousness and harmfulness of the conduct engaged in; and

          II - limit itself to the measures necessary for the audit activity in the specific situation.

        Art. 341. The imposition of the special audit regime does not preclude the application of penalties provided for in tax legislation, nor does it exempt the taxpayer
  from compliance with other obligations, including ancillary ones, not covered by the regime.

         § 1º Ex officio fines applicable to the CBS and the IBS shall have their percentage doubled for violations committed by the taxpayer during the period in which it
  is subject to the REF, without prejudice to the adoption of other measures provided for in tax, administrative, or criminal legislation.

        § 2º In cases in which the measures referred to in items II to IV of the caput of art. 339 have been applied, the payment deadlines established under the
  REF must be observed for purposes of the ex officio assessment.

                                                                                  CHAPTER IV
                                                               (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                      OF INFRACTIONS AND PENALTIES RELATING TO THE IBS AND THE CBS

         Art. 341-A. Any act or omission, even if involuntary, that results in a failure by the taxpayer to observe a principal
  or ancillary tax obligation constitutes an infraction. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 341-B. Punitive fines shall be calculated after the addition referred to in item II of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.          (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Art. 341-C. The Standard Fiscal Unit for Taxes on Goods and Services (UPF) is hereby established, in the amount of R$ 200.00 (two hundred reais), to be updated
  annually by the change in the IPCA or another index that may replace it. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Sole paragraph. A joint act of the CGIBS and the RFB shall publish the updated amount of the UPF referred to in the caput of this article.                     (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         Art. 341-D. Penalties shall be cumulative when they result from the simultaneous non-compliance with ancillary and principal tax obligations.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. When the amount of tax due has already served as the basis for application of the punitive fine, the late-payment fine provided for in item I of § 2º of art. 29
  of this Complementary Law shall not apply, until the date of notice of the ex officio assessment. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 341-E. Application of the penalties provided for in this Title does not exclude:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the requirement to pay the unpaid tax, together with the applicable legal additions, where applicable; and            (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        II - revocation of licenses, concessions, or authorizations, ex officio deregistration from the CNPJ, the imposition of special audit and
  collection regimes, cancellation of the authorization for tax benefits, exclusion from special taxation regimes, or reports to the authorities for criminal purposes, among
  other administrative measures provided for by law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 341-F. A fine of 75% (seventy-five percent) shall apply in cases of ex officio assessment:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - on the amount of tax not declared or declared at less than its true value and not paid or not collected, in whole or in part; or          (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

          II - on the amount of the improper credit, due to its improper use.   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º In cases of tax evasion, fraud, simulation, or collusion, regardless of other applicable administrative or criminal penalties, the fine shall be
  increased to: (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - 100% (one hundred percent) of the total amount or the difference in the tax that is the subject of the ex officio assessment;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         II - 150% (one hundred and fifty percent) of the total amount or the difference in the tax that is the subject of the ex officio assessment, in cases where the
  taxpayer is found to be a repeat offender. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 2º For purposes of the provisions of this article, the following shall be understood:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - tax evasion: any willful act or omission tending to prevent or delay, in whole or in part, the tax authority's becoming aware of:
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) the occurrence of the taxable event of the principal tax obligation, its nature, or material circumstances;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        b) the personal circumstances of the taxpayer, capable of affecting the principal tax obligation or the corresponding tax credit;      (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - fraud: any willful act or omission tending to prevent or delay, in whole or in part, the occurrence of the taxable event of the principal tax obligation,
  or to exclude or modify its essential characteristics, so as to reduce the amount of tax due, to avoid it, or to defer its payment;       (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - (VETOED);    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        IV - collusion: a willful arrangement between 2 (two) or more natural or legal persons, aimed at any of the effects referred to in items I to III of this
  paragraph; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       V - repeat offense: the commission of a new infraction classified as tax evasion, fraud, simulation, or collusion, by the same legal entity or its
  successors, considering all of its establishments together, or by the same natural person, within 3 (three) years counted from the date on which the
  prior assessment was made. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)



       § 3º The fine referred to in item I of the caput of this article shall be 50% (fifty percent) of the portion of the tax that is the subject of the ex officio assessment,
  provided that the declaration correctly describes the goods or services and the respective quantities, as well as the value of the transaction.                    (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 4º The repeat offense referred to in item V of § 2º of this article is voided if liability for the infraction identified in the prior
  assessment has been set aside by a final decision at the administrative level or a judicial decision that is no longer subject to appeal. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        § 5º Reimbursement of the amount paid in excess is guaranteed, where the repeat offense has been set aside under the terms of § 4º of this article, and the taxpayer
  has paid the increased fine based on item V of § 2º of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 6º The amount to be reimbursed referred to in § 5º of this article shall be adjusted by the Selic rate, from the date of actual payment.             (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)
        Art. 341-G. The fines to be applied due to infractions for non-compliance with ancillary tax obligations of the IBS or the CBS are the
  following: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          I - failing to register in the registry with unique identification referred to in art. 59 of this Complementary Law, within the period set forth in regulation: 10 (ten)
  UPF; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         II - failing to update the principal domicile provided for in item "b" of subsection I of § 3 of art. 11 of this Complementary Law in the registry with unique identification referred to in
  art. 59 of this Complementary Law, when there is a change, observing the form and time limit set forth in regulation: 10 (ten) UPF per infraction; (Incluído
  pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        III - failing to notify the tax administration of the sale or transfer of an establishment and the closure or temporary suspension of activities,
  in the form and within the time limits established in tax legislation: 10 (ten) UPF per infraction; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         IV - delivering late, failing to deliver, to record, to make available or to maintain, or maintaining, recording or delivering in disagreement with tax
  legislation, including with respect to non-compliance with a deadline set in a tax notice, electronic files resulting from the issuance of tax documents or
  their bookkeeping, informational document of economic or tax activity, periodic returns or other information required by legislation necessary
  for bookkeeping or tax assessment: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          a) 20 (twenty) UPF per assessment period, regardless of tax notice; and (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          b) 30 (thirty) UPF per assessment period and for each tax notice; (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         V - installing or keeping installed a program, software, tax application or technological solution that enables the issuance of tax documents with suppression
  or reduction of tax or transaction amounts or that does not meet the requirements established in tax legislation: 100 (one hundred) UPF per equipment;
  (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         VI - developing, supplying or installing a program, software, tax application or technological solution for third parties that enables the issuance of tax
  documents with suppression or reduction of tax or transaction amounts or that does not meet the requirements established in tax legislation: 150 (one hundred and
  fifty) UPF per equipment; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         VII - failing to use or using in disagreement with tax legislation a volume measurement mechanism required and controlled by the tax
  administration: 100 (one hundred) UPF per equipment; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

       VIII - failing to notify or notifying after the deadline set forth in tax legislation the invalidation of a tax document number: 1 (one) UPF per
  number; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         IX - the acquirer or recipient, with respect to a tax document issued by a third party, even under contingency, failing to confirm the transaction, to
  report their lack of knowledge, the cancellation of the deal, to report the return of the goods, in the form and under the conditions set forth in tax
  legislation: 1 (one) UPF per document; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        X - failing to comply with the duty of cooperation with the tax authorities, through obstruction of or resistance to tax enforcement action, under the terms of subsections I and II of the caput of art. 338 of this
  Complementary Law, by any means: 50 (fifty) UPF per event; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         XI - supplying, acquiring, importing, receiving, transporting, delivering, causing entry or exit of, or keeping in storage a good, or providing, making available or receiving a service,
  without cover of a tax document, including declarations of information necessary for the assessment of the IBS and the CBS: 100% (one hundred percent) of the value of the
  reference tax; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XII - covering the transit of a good more than once or providing a transport service more than once, using the same tax document: 100% (one hundred
  percent) of the value of the reference tax; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XIII - issuing or using an invalid tax document, including the auxiliary document linked to it: 66% (sixty-six percent) of the value of the reference tax;
  (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XIV - falsifying, adulterating, losing or destroying a tax document: 100% (one hundred percent) of the value of the reference tax; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar
  nº 227, de 2026)

        XV - unduly appropriating or failing to make the reversal or cancellation of a tax credit in the cases provided for in legislation: 66% (sixty-six percent) of the
  credit; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         XVI - failing to issue a tax document referring to the acquisition or entry of a good or the acquisition of a service, within the time limit and in the cases provided for in tax
  legislation: 100% (one hundred percent) of the value of the reference tax; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          XVII - cancelling a tax document or electronic transaction record information: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          a) after the occurrence of the taxable event: 66% (sixty-six percent) of the value of the reference tax; or (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de
  2026)

         b) after the deadline for cancellation of a tax document set forth in tax legislation: 33% (thirty-three percent) of the value of the reference tax;
  (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XVIII - reporting a Prior Declaration of Issuance under Contingency with a value diverging from that stated in the respective tax document: 33% (thirty-three
  percent) of the value of the difference; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XIX - omitting information relating to import or export transactions, or providing it inaccurately or incompletely, provided that it is necessary to
  determine the tax control procedure: 100 (one hundred) UPF per piece of information; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        XX - violating a security device affixed by the tax authorities to a cargo unit: 10 (ten) UPF per device; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227,
  de 2026)

       XXI - failing to comply with ancillary obligations related to the specific controls for verifying the entry of material goods into the Manaus Free Trade Zone
  (ZFM) or into a Free Trade Area, including customs clearance and inspection: 66% (sixty-six percent) of the value of the reference tax; (Incluído
  pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         XXII - the facility accredited for purposes of specific controls for verifying the entry of material goods into the Manaus Free Trade Zone or into a
  Free Trade Area failing to meet the minimum infrastructure requirements set forth at the time of its accreditation: 20 (twenty) UPF per required requirement.
  (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

       § 1 The penalties referred to in this article shall be increased by 50% (fifty percent) in the case of specific recidivism. (Incluído pela Lei
  Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         § 2 For purposes of the provision in § 1 of this article, specific recidivism is considered to be recurrence of an infraction provided for in the same subsection of the caput of this
  article, by the same legal entity or its successors, considering together all of its establishments, or by the same natural person,
  within 3 (three) years counted from the date on which the prior assessment was made. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          § 3 For purposes of the provision in § 1 of this article, the provisions of §§ 4 to 6 of art. 341-F apply. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        § 4 The penalties provided for in subsection IV of this article do not apply in case of mere failure or material error that does not prejudice
  knowledge of the nature, description, origin and destination of the transaction. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        § 5 For purposes of the provision in subsections XI, XII, XIII, XIV, XVI, XVII and XXI of the caput of this article, the value of the reference tax corresponds to: (Incluído pela
  Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        I - from 2027, for the CBS, and from 2033, for the IBS, the multiplication of the reference rate by the value of the transaction, even if it is an
  immune, exempt transaction, subject to a zero rate, reduced rate or reduced tax base, covered by deferral or suspension; (Incluído pela Lei
  Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        II - in the period from 2027 to 2032, for the IBS, the multiplication of the percentage corresponding to double the CBS reference rate by the value of the
  transaction; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          III - in 2026: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          a) for the CBS, 6% (six percent) of the value of the transaction; and (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          b) for the IBS, 12% (twelve percent) of the value of the transaction. (Incluída pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

       § 6 For purposes of the provision in subsection XIII of the caput of this article, an invalid tax document is considered to be, among others, one:
  (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          I - that does not effectively correspond to a transaction involving a good or service or to the acquisition of a good or service; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de
  2026)

          II - in which a person or establishment other than the one to whom the good or service was in fact intended, or who, in
  fact, acquired the good or service, is listed as recipient or acquirer. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          § 7 For purposes of the provision in subsection XIX of the caput of this article: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

         I - information necessary to determine the tax control procedure is considered to be information that identifies those responsible for the transaction, indicates the
  economic destination of the good or service and the countries of origin, provenance and acquisition, and describes the essential characteristics of the material good;
  (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        II - if more than one of the infractions occurs for the same good or service, the fine applies only once; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº
  227, de 2026)

          III - the amount of the fine may not exceed 1% (one percent) of the total value of the transaction stated in the corresponding tax document, subject to the
  lower limit of 50 (fifty) UPF. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          Art. 341-H. The fines referred to in arts. 341-F and 341-G may be paid with the following reductions: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de
  2026)

       I - 50% (fifty percent) of the penalty applied, if full payment of the tax credit is made within the period provided for filing an
  administrative challenge; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        II - 40% (forty percent) of the penalty applied, if installment payment of the tax credit is arranged within the period provided for filing an administrative
  challenge; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        III - 30% (thirty percent) of the penalty applied, if full payment of the tax credit is made after the period provided for in subsection I of this article and
  before it is entered into active debt; (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        IV - 20% (twenty percent) of the penalty applied, if installment payment of the tax credit is arranged after the period provided for in subsection II of this article and before its
  entry into active debt. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        § 1 The reduction percentages provided for in subsections I to IV of the caput of this article shall be, respectively, 60% (sixty percent), 50% (fifty
  percent), 40% (forty percent) and 30% (thirty percent), in the case of taxpayers that: (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          I - participate in the National Tax Compliance Program (PNCT) referred to in art. 471-A; or (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

          II - have a good tax compliance record, under the terms of the regulation. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        § 2 Termination of the installment plan, motivated by non-compliance with the rules governing it, shall result in reinstatement of the amount of the fine
  proportionally to the value of the tax credit not satisfied. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

                                                                                     TITLE VIII

                                                                    ON THE TRANSITION TO THE IBS AND TO THE CBS

                                                                                     CHAPTER I

                                                             ON THE SETTING OF RATES DURING THE TRANSITION

                                                                                       Section I

                                                              On the Setting of IBS Rates during the Transition

          Art. 342. The transition to the IBS shall meet the criteria established in this Section and in the following provisions:



        I - art. 501 of this Complementary Law, with respect to the reduction of the rates of the tax provided for in art. 155, II, of the Federal Constitution, and the reduction of the
  tax benefits related to this tax between 2029 and 2032;

        II - art. 508 of this Complementary Law, with respect to the reduction of the rates of the tax provided for in art. 156, III, of the Federal Constitution, and the reduction of the
  tax benefits related to this tax between 2029 and 2032;

        III - arts. 361 to 365 of this Complementary Law, with respect to setting the IBS reference rates from 2029 to 2033; and

        IV - arts. 366 and 369 of this Complementary Law, with respect to setting the IBS reference rates in 2034 and 2035.

        Art. 343. With respect to taxable events occurring from January 1 to December 31, 2026, the IBS shall be charged by applying the state rate of
  0.1% (one tenth of one percent).

        Sole paragraph. During the period indicated in the caput of this article, IBS collection shall not observe the earmarking, apportionment and allocation rules provided for in the
  Federal Constitution, and shall instead be applied, fully and successively, to:

        I - the funding of the IBS Management Committee, under the terms of art. 156-B, § 2, III, of the Federal Constitution; and

        II - composing the Fund for Compensation of Tax or Financial-Tax Benefits of the ICMS.

         Art. 344. With respect to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028, the IBS shall be charged at the state rate of 0.05%
  (five hundredths of one percent) and at the municipal rate of 0.05% (five hundredths of one percent).

        Sole paragraph. The rates provided for in the caput:

        I - shall be applied with the respective reduction in the case of transactions subject to a reduced rate, within differentiated taxation regimes;

        II - shall be applied in relation to the specific regimes covered by this Complementary Law, observing the respective tax bases, except in relation
  to fuels subject to the specific regime covered by arts. 172 to 180 of this Complementary Law; and

        III - in relation to fuels subject to the specific regime covered by arts. 172 to 180 of this Complementary Law, the rates referred to in the caput
  of this article shall be applied to the value of the transaction at the time the CBS is levied.

         IV - shall be considered as IBS reference rates for purposes of the provisions of § 2 of art. 189, § 8 of art. 485, § 13 of art. 486 and § 12 of
  art. 487. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

                                                                                     Section II

                                                             On the Setting of CBS Rates during the Transition

        Art. 345. The transition to the CBS shall meet the criteria established in this Section and in the following provisions:

        I - arts. 353 to 359 of this Complementary Law, with respect to setting the CBS reference rate from 2027 to 2033, observing the provisions of art. 368
  for the period from 2030 to 2033; and

        II - arts. 366 and 369 of this Complementary Law, with respect to setting the CBS reference rate in 2034 and 2035.

        Art. 346. With respect to taxable events occurring from January 1 to December 31, 2026, the CBS shall be charged by applying the rate of 0.9%
  (nine tenths of one percent).

         Art. 347. With respect to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028, the CBS rate shall be that set under the terms of
  subsection I of the caput and §§ 2 and 3, all of art. 14, reduced by 0.1 (one tenth) percentage point, except in relation to fuels subject to the specific regime
  covered by arts. 172 to 180 of this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The rate reduction provided for in the caput shall be:

        I - proportional to the respective reduction in the case of transactions subject to a reduced rate, within differentiated taxation regimes;

        II - applied in relation to the specific regimes covered by this Complementary Law, observing the respective tax bases.

        § 2 During the period referred to in the caput of this article, the amount of IBS collected under the terms of subsection III of the sole paragraph of art. 344 may be
  deducted from the amount of CBS payable by taxpayers subject to the specific fuel regime covered by arts. 172 to 180 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                    Section III

                                                                Common Provisions for the IBS and the CBS in 2026

        Art. 348. With respect to taxable events occurring from January 1 to December 31, 2026:

          I - the amount collected of the IBS and the CBS shall be offset against the amount owed, in the same assessment period, of the contributions provided for in art. 195, subsection
  I, item "b", and subsection IV, and of the contribution to the PIS referred to in art. 239, both of the Federal Constitution;

        II - if the taxpayer does not have sufficient debts to carry out the offset referred to in subsection I, the amount collected may be:

        a) offset against any other federal tax, under the terms of legislation; or

        b) refunded within up to 60 (sixty) days, upon request;

        III - the IBS and CBS rates provided for in arts. 343 and 346 of this Complementary Law:

        a) shall be applied with the respective reduction in the case of transactions subject to a reduced rate, within differentiated taxation regimes;

        b) shall be applied in relation to the specific regimes covered by this Complementary Law, observing the respective tax bases, except in relation
  to fuels and biofuels covered by arts. 172 to 180;

        c) shall not be applied in relation to the transactions of taxpayers opting for the Simples Nacional.

        § 1 Collection of the IBS and the CBS relating to taxable events occurring in the period indicated in the caput is waived in relation to taxpayers that
  comply with the ancillary obligations provided for in legislation.

          § 2 The taxpayer exempted from collection under § 1 remains obligated to make full payment of the Contributions provided for in art. 195, subsection
  I, item "b", and subsection IV, and of the contribution to the Social Integration Program referred to in art. 239, both of the Federal Constitution.

        § 3 During the period referred to in the caput of this article, if a notice of infraction is issued for non-compliance with the ancillary obligations relating to the
  IBS and the CBS provided for in art. 341-G of this Complementary Law, the taxpayer shall be notified to, within 60 (sixty) days counted from the notice, remedy
  the omission identified by the tax authorities. (Incluído pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

       § 4 Compliance with the notice referred to in § 3 of this article extinguishes the penalty imposed on the taxpayer. (Incluído pela Lei
  Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

                                                                                       Section IV

                                                             On the Setting of Reference Rates from 2027 to 2035

                                                                                     Subsection I

                                                                                 General Provisions

        Art. 349. Subject to the calculation method and limits provided for in this Section, a resolution of the Federal Senate shall set:

        I - for the years 2027 to 2033, the CBS reference rate;

        II - for the years 2029 to 2033:

        a) the IBS reference rate for the States;

        b) the IBS reference rate for the Municipalities;

        c) the IBS reference rate for the Federal District, which shall correspond to the sum of the reference rates provided for in items "a" and "b" of this subsection;

        III - for the years 2027 to 2033, the reducer to be applied to the CBS and IBS rates on transactions contracted by direct public administration,
  by autarchies and by public foundations, including their imports.

         § 1 The reference rates and the reducer referred to in subsection III of the caput shall be set in the year prior to the one in which they take effect, based on calculations made
  by the Federal Court of Audit (Tribunal de Contas da União), observing the following:

         I - the Federal Court of Audit shall send the Federal Senate the calculations referred to in this paragraph by September 15 of the year prior to the year in which
  the reference rates and the reducer take effect;
