         II - the Federal Senate shall set the reference rates and the reducer by October 31 of the year prior to the year in which they take effect, the provisions of
  art. 150, subsection III, item "c", of the Federal Constitution not applying.

         § 2 If the deadline provided for in subsection II of § 1 extends beyond December 22 of the year prior to the year in which they take effect, while the
  rates have not yet been set by the Federal Senate or taken effect, the reference rates calculated by the Federal Court of Audit shall be used, subject to the following
  conditions:

        I - the rates set by the Federal Senate shall take effect from the beginning of the second month following the one in which they are set;

        II - the provisions of art. 150, subsection III, item "b", of the Federal Constitution shall be observed.

        § 3 The calculations assigned to the Federal Court of Audit under the terms of § 1 shall be carried out based on proposals submitted:

        I - by the Federal Executive Branch, for calculations relating to the CBS reference rate;

        II - by the IBS Management Committee, for calculations relating to the IBS reference rates;

        III - jointly by the Federal Executive Branch and the IBS Management Committee, for the reducer referred to in subsection III of the caput.

        § 4 The Federal Executive Branch and the IBS Management Committee shall act jointly to harmonize the methodology of the calculations referred to in the subsections of §
  3.

        § 5 The proposals referred to in the subsections of § 3:

        I - shall be prepared based on the methodology approved under the terms of § 7;

        II - shall be sent to the Federal Court of Audit by July 31 of the year prior to the year in which the reference rates and the reducer take effect;

        III - shall be accompanied by the data and information necessary for calculating the reference rates and the reducer, which shall be supplemented in
  a timely manner, if so requested by the Federal Court of Audit.

         § 6 If the proposals referred to in the subsections of § 3 are not submitted within the period provided for in subsection II of § 5, the Federal Court of Audit
  shall perform the calculations necessary to set the reference rates and the reducer referred to in subsection III of the caput based on the information to which it has access.

        § 7 The calculation methodology referred to in subsection I of § 5:

         I - shall be prepared by the IBS Management Committee and the Federal Executive Branch, within their respective areas of competence, based on the criteria set forth in
  arts. 350 to 369 of this Complementary Law; and

        II - shall be approved by the Federal Court of Audit.

         § 8 In defining the methodology referred to in § 7, the Federal Executive Branch and the IBS Management Committee may propose adjustments to the criteria set forth in
  arts. 350 to 369 of this Complementary Law, provided such adjustments are justified.

        § 9 In the process of approving the methodology referred to in § 7:

         I - the IBS Management Committee and the Federal Executive Branch shall send the Federal Court of Audit the proposed methodology to be adopted by the
  end of June of the second year prior to the one in which the reference rate calculated based on the methodology to be approved takes effect;

        II - the Federal Court of Audit shall approve the methodology within 180 (one hundred and eighty) days;

          III - the Federal Court of Audit may request adjustments to the methodology from the IBS Management Committee and the Federal Executive Branch, which shall, within
  30 (thirty) days:

        a) implement the adjustments; or

        b) submit to the Federal Court of Audit an alternative to the proposed adjustments.

        § 10. The Federal Court of Audit, and, within their respective areas of competence, the IBS Management Committee and the Federal Executive Branch, may, by mutual
  agreement, implement subsequent adjustments to the approved methodology under the terms of § 9.


        § 11. The federative entities and the IBS Management Committee shall provide the Federal Court of Audit with the information necessary for preparing the calculations
  referred to in this article.

       § 12. The Federal Executive Branch and the IBS Management Committee shall provide the Federal Court of Audit with all the resources necessary for the approval of the
  methodology and for preparing the calculations referred to in this article, by sharing data and information.

         § 13. The sharing of data and information referred to in this article shall observe the provisions of art. 198 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 - National
  Tax Code.

       § 14. In setting the CBS reference rate and the state, district and municipal IBS reference rates, the values calculated under the terms of this
  Section shall be rounded to the nearest tenth of a percentage point, up or down.

                                                                                     Subsection II

                                                                             On Reference Revenue

        Art. 350. In preparing the calculations for setting the reference rates, the following are understood:

        I - Union reference revenue, the sum of revenue, before the offset referred to in subsections I and II of the caput of art. 348 of this Complementary Law:

        a) of the contributions provided for in art. 195, subsection I, item "b", and subsection IV and of the contribution to the PIS referred to in art. 239, all of the Federal Constitution;

        b) of the tax provided for in art. 153, subsection IV, of the Federal Constitution; and

        c) of the tax provided for in art. 153, subsection V, of the Federal Constitution, on insurance transactions;

        II - reference revenue of the States, the sum of the revenue of the States and the Federal District:

        a) from the tax provided for in art. 155, subsection II, of the Federal Constitution;

         b) from the contributions earmarked for funding state funds in operation on April 30, 2023 and established as a condition for
  the application of deferral, a special regime or other differentiated treatment relating to the tax referred to in art. 155, subsection II, of the Federal Constitution;

        III - reference revenue of the Municipalities, the sum of the revenue of the Municipalities and the Federal District from the tax provided for in art. 156, subsection III, of the Federal
  Constitution.

        § 1 For purposes of the provision in this article, the revenue from the taxes referred to in the caput shall be determined so as to include:

        I - revenue obtained under Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006;

        II - revenue obtained under art. 82 of the Transitional Constitutional Provisions Act; and

        III - the total amount collected, including interest and fines, arising from amounts entered or not entered into active debt.

        § 2 The revenue from the contributions referred to in item "b" of subsection II of the caput:

        I - does not include revenue from contributions on primary and semi-processed products replaced by similar contributions, under the terms of art. 136 of the Transitional Constitutional
  Provisions Act;

        II - shall correspond, for each period, to the average value of the contributions effectively collected from 2021 to 2023, adjusted by the variation in revenue from the tax
  referred to in art. 155, subsection II, of the Federal Constitution, of the respective State or Federal District;

        III - shall be calculated according to a methodology to be developed by the IBS Management Committee and approved by the Federal Court of Audit.

        § 3 For purposes of the provision in subsection III of § 2:

       I - the IBS Management Committee shall send the proposed methodology to the Federal Court of Audit by June 31, 2026; and (Revogado pela Lei
  Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        II - the procedures provided for in §§ 9 and 10 of art. 349 shall be observed.

                                                                                     Subsection III

                                                                     On the Calculation of Reference Rates

         Art. 351. Subject to the availability of information, the calculations for setting the reference rate shall consider the IBS and CBS revenue
  broken down between:

        I - revenue from transactions and imports subject to the general incidence rules provided for in Title I of this Book, broken down into:

        a) transactions and imports subject to the standard rate;

        b) transactions and imports subject to a rate reduced by 60% (sixty percent) of the standard rate;

        c) transactions and imports subject to a rate reduced by 30% (thirty percent) of the standard rate;

        II - revenue from transactions and imports taxed on the basis of each of the specific taxation regimes;

        III - revenue from transactions taxed under the Special Unified Regime for the Collection of Taxes and Contributions owed by Micro and Small
  Businesses - Simples Nacional, covered by Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006, broken down if necessary for each of the brackets
  of the tables in the annexes to that Complementary Law;

         IV - revenue obtained by each federative sphere in acquisitions of goods and services in which the revenue is allocated entirely to the acquiring federative entity,
  under the terms of art. 473 of this Complementary Law, broken down for each type of transaction and import referred to in subsections I to III of the caput of this article;

        V - the amount of the revenue reduction resulting from:

        a) the granting of presumed credits, broken down for each type of presumed credit provided for in this Complementary Law;

        b) the general refund of IBS and CBS to individuals, referred to in art. 118 of this Complementary Law, broken down for each type of refund;

        VI - other factors that increase or reduce IBS and CBS revenue not considered in the preceding subsections, broken down by category.

        § 1 The revenues referred to in subsections I to III of the caput of this article:


         I - shall not consider transactions contracted by direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations, including their imports, and
  subject to the regime referred to in art. 473 of this Complementary Law;

        II - shall correspond to the value of the IBS and the CBS levied on transactions that do not give rise to a credit right for acquirers.

        § 2 For purposes of setting the reference rate, the value of IBS and CBS revenue referred to in the caput:

        I - shall be determined so as to include:

        a) revenue obtained under Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14, 2006;

        b) revenue obtained under art. 82 of the Transitional Constitutional Provisions Act; and

        c) the total amount collected, including interest and fines, arising from amounts entered or not entered into active debt;

        II - shall not include IBS amounts withheld for later offset or reimbursement.

        § 3 Calculations by revenue category or revenue reduction category referred to in the subsections of the caput may be carried out based on the values stated
  in tax documents, and adjusted afterward so that their total value corresponds to that determined under the terms of § 2.

                                                                                    Subsection IV

                                                                  On the Calculation of the CBS Reference Rate

       Art. 352. The calculation of the CBS reference rate for each year of effect from 2027 to 2033 shall be carried out, under the terms of arts. 353 to 359 of this Complementary
  Law, based on:

        I - the Union's reference revenue in prior base years;

        II - an estimate of what CBS revenue would be if, in each of the base years, the reference rate, the rates of the specific regimes
  and the CBS legislation for the year of effect were applied; and

        III - estimates of what the revenue of the Selective Tax and the IPI would be, if, in each of the base years, the rates and legislation of those
  taxes for the year of effect were applied.

         § 1 The estimate of CBS revenue referred to in subsection II of the caput shall be calculated, in base-year values, for each revenue or revenue-reduction category
  referred to in the subsections of the caput of art. 351 of this Complementary Law, by applying the reference rate and the other rates provided for in
  CBS legislation for the year of effect, to an estimate of the tax base in the base year.

         § 2 The estimates of the revenue of the taxes referred to in subsection III of the caput shall be calculated, in base-year values, by applying the rates
  provided for in the legislation of those taxes for the year of effect, to an estimate of the tax base in the base year.

        § 3 Subject to the specific criteria provided for in arts. 353 to 359 of this Complementary Law, the estimate of the tax base of each category referred to
  in §§ 1 and 2 of this article may take as reference, among others:

        I - data obtained in the process of collecting taxes on goods and services in the base year;

        II - public data relating to macroeconomic aggregates in the base year and, in case such specific data is unavailable, data relating to macroeconomic
  aggregates of prior years, adjusted to base-year values by the variation in the value of macroeconomic aggregates or of appropriate price and
  quantity indicators;

         III - the tax base of each CBS revenue category in years after the base year, determined from tax documents and CBS bookkeeping,
  adjusted to base-year values by the variation in the value of macroeconomic aggregates or of price and quantity indicators appropriate to each revenue
  category; or

         IV - the tax base of the taxes referred to in subsection III of the caput in years after the base year, determined from tax documents and
  the bookkeeping of those taxes, adjusted to base-year values by the variation in the value of macroeconomic aggregates or of specific price and
  quantity indicators.

        § 4 In the case of specific (ad rem) rates or amounts fixed in the domestic currency in legislation, the amounts provided for in legislation for the year of
  effect shall be adjusted to base-year values so as to reflect the variation in prices between the two periods.

        Art. 353. The CBS reference rate for 2027 shall be set based on the estimate, for each of the base years 2024 and 2025:

         I - of CBS revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the
  rates of the specific regimes and the CBS legislation for 2027;

        II - of Selective Tax revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2027 rates; and

        III - of IPI revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2027 rates.

        § 1 The CBS reference rate for 2027 shall be set so as to bring about equivalence between:

        I - the average of the ratio between the sum of the values referred to in the subsections of the caput and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the base years referred to in the caput; and

        II - the average of the ratio between the Union's reference revenue and GDP in the years 2012 to 2021.

         § 2 For purposes of the provision in subsection III of § 3 of art. 352 of this Complementary Law, in 2026, the deadlines referred to in subsections I and II of § 1 and in subsection II of
  § 5, both of art. 349, shall be extended by 45 (forty-five) days.

        Art. 354. The CBS reference rate for 2028 shall be set based on the estimate, for each of the base years 2025 and 2026:

         I - of CBS revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the
  rates of the specific regimes and the CBS legislation for 2028;

        II - of Selective Tax revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the
  2028 rates; and

        III - of IPI revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2028 rates.

        Sole paragraph. The CBS reference rate for 2028 shall be set so as to bring about equivalence between:

        I - the average of the ratio between the sum of the values referred to in the subsections of the caput and GDP in the base years referred to in the caput; and


        II - the average of the ratio between the Union's reference revenue and GDP in the years 2012 to 2021.

        Art. 355. The CBS reference rate for 2029 shall be set based on the estimate:

         I - of CBS revenue in 2027, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the
  rates of the specific regimes and the CBS legislation for 2029;

        II - of Selective Tax revenue in 2027, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2029 rates; and

        III - of IPI revenue in 2027, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2029 rates.

        Sole paragraph. The CBS reference rate for 2029 shall be set so as to bring about equivalence between:

        I - the ratio between the sum of the values referred to in the subsections of the caput and GDP in 2027; and

        II - the average of the ratio between the Union's reference revenue and GDP in the years 2012 to 2021.

        Art. 356. The CBS reference rate for 2030 shall be set based on the estimate, for each of the base years 2027 and 2028:

         I - of CBS revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the
  rates of the specific regimes and the CBS legislation for 2030;

        II - of Selective Tax revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the
  2030 rates; and

        III - of IPI revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2030 rates.

        Sole paragraph. The CBS reference rate for 2030 shall be set so as to bring about equivalence between:

        I - the average of the ratio between the sum of the values referred to in the subsections of the caput and GDP in the base years referred to in the caput; and

        II - the average of the ratio between the Union's reference revenue and GDP in the years 2012 to 2021.

        Art. 357. The CBS reference rate for 2031 shall be set based on the estimate, for each of the base years 2028 and 2029:

         I - of CBS revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the
  rates of the specific regimes and the CBS legislation for 2031;

        II - of Selective Tax revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the
  2031 rates; and

        III - of IPI revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection III of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the 2031 rates.

        Sole paragraph. The CBS reference rate for 2031 shall be set so as to bring about equivalence between:

        I - the average of the ratio between the sum of the values referred to in the subsections of the caput and GDP in the base years referred to in the caput; and

        II - the average of the ratio between the Union's reference revenue and GDP in the years 2012 to 2021.

         I - of CBS revenue in the base year, calculated under the terms of subsection II of the caput of art. 352 of this Complementary Law based on the reference rate, the

                                                                                  Subsection V

                                                               On the Calculation of IBS Reference Rates

        Art. 360. The calculation of the state and municipal IBS reference rates for each year of effect from 2029 to 2033 shall be carried out, under the terms of arts. 361
  to 365 of this Complementary Law, based on:

        I - the reference revenue of the respective federative sphere in prior base years; and

        II - an estimate of what IBS revenue would be if, in each of the base years, the reference rate, the rates of the specific
  regimes and the IBS legislation for the year of effect were applied.

         § 1 The estimate of IBS revenue referred to in subsection II of the caput shall be calculated, in base-year values, for each revenue or revenue-reduction category
  referred to in the subsections of the caput of art. 351 of this Complementary Law, by applying the reference rate and the other rates provided for in
  IBS legislation for the year of effect, to an estimate of the tax base in the base year.

         § 2 Subject to the specific criteria provided for in arts. 361 to 365 of this Complementary Law, the estimate of the tax base of each category referred to
  in § 1 of this article may take as reference, among others:

         I - the tax base of each CBS revenue and revenue-reduction category in the base year, adjusted so as to reflect the differences between the
  CBS legislation in the base year and the IBS legislation in the year of effect;

        II - the tax base of each IBS revenue and revenue-reduction category in the base year, adjusted so as to reflect the differences in the
  IBS legislation between the base year and the year of effect.

        § 3 In the case of specific (ad rem) rates or amounts fixed in the domestic currency in legislation, the amounts provided for in legislation for the year of
  effect shall be adjusted to base-year values so as to reflect the variation in prices between the two periods.

        Art. 361. The state and municipal IBS reference rates for 2029 shall be set so that:
        I - the estimate of the state share of IBS revenue in 2027, calculated based on the state reference rate, the state rates of the specific
  regimes and the IBS legislation for 2029, under the terms of art. 360 of this Complementary Law, is equivalent to 10% of the reference revenue of the States in 2027;
        II - the estimate of the municipal share of IBS revenue in 2027, calculated based on the municipal reference rate, the municipal rates of the specific
  regimes and the IBS legislation for 2029, under the terms of art. 360 of this Complementary Law, is equivalent to 10% of the reference revenue of the Municipalities in 2027.
        Sole paragraph. In preparing the calculations referred to in this article, the tax base to be used in the estimates shall take as reference:
        I - primarily, CBS revenue in 2027, adjusted so as to reflect differences between the CBS legislation in 2027 and the IBS legislation in 2029;
        II - subsidiarily, IBS revenue in 2027, adjusted so as to reflect differences in IBS legislation between 2027 and 2029, or other sources of
  information.

        Art. 361. The state and municipal IBS reference rates for 2029 shall be set based on the estimate: (Redação dada pela Lei Complementar
  nº 227, de 2026)

  and the IBS legislation for 2029, under the terms of art. 360 of this Complementary Law; (Redação dada pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

        II - of the municipal share of IBS revenue in 2027, calculated based on the municipal reference rate, the municipal rates of the specific
  regimes and the IBS legislation for 2029, under the terms of art. 360 of this Complementary Law; (Redação dada pela Lei Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

       III - of the reference revenue of the States for the year 2027 with the effects of the 10% (ten percent) rate reduction; (Incluído pela Lei
  Complementar nº 227, de 2026)

                                                                                     Subsection VI

                                                              On the Setting of Reference Rates in 2034 and 2035

        Art. 366. Subject to the provisions of arts. 19 and 369 of this Complementary Law, the CBS reference rate and the state and municipal reference rates
  of the IBS in 2034 and 2035 shall be those set for 2033.

                                                                                     Subsection VII

                                                             On the Limit for Reference Rates in 2030 and 2035

           Art. 367. For purposes of the provisions of arts. 368 and 369 of this Complementary Law, the following definitions apply:

         I - Union Reference Ceiling: the average revenue in the period from 2012 to 2021, calculated as a proportion of GDP, of the tax provided for in art. 153, item IV, of the
  contributions provided for in art. 195, item I, subitem "b", and item IV, of the contribution to the PIS referred to in art. 239 and of the tax provided for in art. 153, item V, on
  insurance operations, all under the Federal Constitution;

         II - Total Reference Ceiling: the average revenue in the period from 2012 to 2021, calculated as a proportion of GDP, of the taxes provided for in arts. 153, item IV,
  155, item II, and 156, item III, of the contributions provided for in art. 195, item I, subitem "b", and item IV, of the contribution to the PIS referred to in art. 239 and of the tax
  provided for in art. 153, item V, on insurance operations, all under the Federal Constitution;

           III - Base Revenue of the Union: the revenue of the Union from the CBS and the Selective Tax, calculated as a proportion of GDP;

         IV - Base Revenue of the Subnational Entities: the revenue of the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities from the IBS, deducted of the share referred to in subitem
  "b" of item II of the caput of art. 350 of this Complementary Law, calculated as a proportion of GDP;

           V - Total Base Revenue: the sum of the Base Revenue of the Union with the Base Revenue of the Subnational Entities, the latter being:

           a) multiplied by 10 (ten) in 2029;

           b) multiplied by 5 (five) in 2030;

           c) multiplied by 10 (ten) and divided by 3 (three) in 2031;

           d) multiplied by 10 (ten) and divided by 4 (four) in 2032;

           e) multiplied by 1 (one) in 2033.

           Art. 368. The CBS reference rate in 2030 shall be reduced if the average of the Base Revenue of the Union in 2027 and 2028 exceeds the Union
  Reference Ceiling.

           § 1 The reduction referred to in this article, if any:

           I - shall be defined so that, after its application, the average of the Base Revenue of the Union in 2027 and 2028 equals the Union Reference Ceiling;

           II - shall be set in percentage points;

           III - shall be applied to the Union's reference rate, calculated in the manner set forth in arts. 356 to 359 of this Complementary Law, for the years 2030 to 2033.

        § 2 The amount of the reduction referred to in this article shall be set by the Federal Senate at the time of setting the CBS reference rate for the years
  2030 to 2033, in accordance with the criteria established in art. 349 of this Complementary Law.

           § 3 The revision of the CBS reference rate in accordance with this article shall not entail the collection of or refund of CBS relating to prior years.

        Art. 369. The CBS and IBS reference rates in 2035 shall be reduced if the average Total Base Revenue between 2029 and 2033 exceeds the Total Reference
  Ceiling.

           § 1 The reduction referred to in this article, if any:

           I - shall be defined so that, after its application, the average Total Base Revenue between 2029 and 2033 equals the Total Reference Ceiling;

           II - shall be set in percentage points;

           III - shall be distributed proportionally among the CBS reference rate, and the state and municipal reference rates of the IBS.

         § 2 The amount of the reduction referred to in this article shall be set by the Federal Senate for the year 2035, in accordance with the criteria and deadlines established in
  art. 349 of this Complementary Law.

         § 3 The revision of the CBS and IBS reference rate in accordance with this article shall not entail the collection of or refund of any tax relating to prior years or
  transfer of funds between the federative entities.

                                                                                       Section V
                On the Reducer to be applied to the CBS and IBS Rates on Transactions Contracted by the Public Administration from 2027 to 2033

         Art. 370. The calculation of the reducer to be applied, in each year of validity, to the CBS and IBS rates on transactions contracted by the direct
  public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations, including their imports, shall take as reference:

        I - estimate of the CBS and IBS revenue on the transactions referred to in the caput for each base year from 2024 to 2026, calculated under the terms of arts. 352 and 360
  of this Complementary Law, considering:

        a) estimate of the tax base of those transactions in each base year; and

        b) the CBS and IBS rates of the year of validity; and

        II - estimate of the Union's revenue from the taxes referred to in the subitems of item I of art. 350 of this Complementary Law on the transactions referred to in the
  caput of this article;

        III - estimate of the revenue of the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities from the taxes referred to in subitem "a" of item II and item III of art. 350
  of this Complementary Law on the transactions referred to in the caput of this article.

        § 1 For the year of validity 2027, the reducer referred to in the caput shall be set so that there is equivalence between:

       I - the average of the estimate of the CBS revenue for the base years 2024 and 2025, calculated under the terms of item I of the caput, applying to the CBS rates
  the reducer to be applied in 2027; and

        II - the average of the estimate of the Union's revenue for the base years 2024 and 2025, calculated under the terms of item II of the caput.

        § 2 For the year of validity 2028, the reducer referred to in the caput shall be set so that there is equivalence between:

       I - the average of the estimate of the CBS revenue for the base years 2024 to 2026, calculated under the terms of item I of the caput, applying to the CBS rates
  the reducer to be applied in 2028; and

        II - the average of the estimate of the Union's revenue for the base years 2024 to 2026, calculated under the terms of item II of the caput.

        § 3 For the year of validity 2033, the reducer referred to in the caput shall be set so that there is equivalence between:

         I - the average of the estimate of the CBS and IBS revenue for the base years 2024 to 2026, calculated under the terms of item I of the caput, applying to the
  CBS and IBS rates the reducer to be applied in 2033; and

         II - the average of the estimate of the revenue of the Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities for the base years 2024 to 2026, calculated under the terms of
  items II and III of the caput.

        § 4 For the years of validity 2029 to 2032, the reducer referred to in the caput shall be set based on a weighted average of the calculations made in the manner
  established in §§ 2 and 3 of this article, considering the evolution of the CBS and IBS rates.

                                                                                   CHAPTER II

                                                    ON THE LIMIT FOR REDUCTION OF IBS RATES FROM 2029 TO 2077

        Art. 371. From 2029 to 2077 it is forbidden for the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities to set IBS rates lower than those necessary to guarantee the retentions
  referred to in § 1 of art. 131 and art. 132, both of the Transitional Constitutional Provisions Act of the Federal Constitution.

        § 1 For purposes of the provisions of the caput of this article, the IBS rates set by the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities may not be lower
  than the amount resulting from the application of the percentages established for each year in Annex XVI, to the reference rate of the respective federative sphere.

        § 2 In the event that the entity sets a rate at a level lower than that provided for in § 1, the lower rate limit calculated under the terms of § 1
  of this article shall prevail.

                                                                                   CHAPTER III

                                                DA TRANSITION APPLICABLE TO THE GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REGIME

       Art. 372. The regime of full allocation of the proceeds of the collection of the IBS and the CBS to the contracting federative entity under the terms of art. 473 of this
  Complementary Law:

        I - does not apply:

        a) to the IBS and the CBS, in relation to taxable events occurring from January 1 to December 31, 2026;

        b) to the CBS, in relation to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028;

        II - applies in full:

        a) to the IBS, in relation to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2027 onward;

        b) to the CBS, in relation to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2033 onward.

        Sole paragraph. In relation to taxable events occurring from January 1, 2029 to December 31, 2032, the application of the regime referred to in the caput shall
  occur in the following proportions of the CBS levied on the acquisition of goods and services by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations:

        I - from January 1 to December 31, 2029, 10% (ten percent);

        II - from January 1 to December 31, 2030, 20% (twenty percent);

        III - from January 1 to December 31, 2031, 30% (thirty percent);

        IV - from January 1 to December 31, 2032, 40% (forty percent).

                                                                                   CHAPTER IV

                                                           ON THE REBALANCING OF ADMINISTRATIVE CONTRACTS

        Art. 373. This Chapter provides for the adjustment instruments for contracts entered into prior to the entry into force of this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The provisions of this Chapter apply, as applicable, to administrative contracts entered into after the entry into force of this Complementary Law whose proposal
  was submitted before its entry into force.


          § 2 The provisions of this Chapter do not apply to private contracts, which remain subject to the provisions of the specific legislation.

         Art. 374. Contracts in force at the entry into force of this Complementary Law entered into by the direct or indirect public administration of the Union, the States,
  the Federal District and the Municipalities, including public concessions, shall be adjusted to ensure the restoration of the economic-financial balance due to
  the change in the effective tax burden borne by the contracted party as a result of the impact of the introduction of the IBS and the CBS, in cases in which the imbalance is
  proven.

          § 1 For the purposes of this Chapter, the determination of the effective tax burden borne by the contracted party must consider, including:

        a) the effects of non-cumulativity on the acquisitions and costs incurred by the contracted party, considering the rules for the assessment of credits, and the manner of
  determining the tax base of the taxes referred to in the caput;

          b) the possibility of passing on to third parties, by the contracted party, the financial burden of the taxes referred to in the caput;

          c) the impacts arising from the change of the taxes during the transition period provided for in arts. 125 to 133 of the ADCT; and

          d) the tax or financial benefits or incentives of the contracted party related to the taxes extinguished by Constitutional Amendment No. 132 of December 20,
  2023.

        § 2 The provisions of this Chapter also apply to those contracts that already have a provision in the risk matrix that supervening tax impacts are
  the responsibility of the contracted party.

         Art. 375. The public administration shall carry out, on its own initiative, a review to restore the economic-financial balance when a reduction in the
  effective tax burden borne by the contracted party is found, under the terms of art. 374 of this Complementary Law, with the latter's right to be heard assured.

        Art. 376. The contracted party may seek the restoration of the economic-financial balance referred to in art. 374 of this Complementary Law found in the
  transition period referred to in arts. 125 to 133 of the ADCT by means of a specific and exclusive administrative procedure, under the following terms:

          I - the request for restoration of the economic-financial balance may be made:

          a) at each new tax change that causes a proven imbalance; or

          b) so as to already cover all the changes provided for the period referred to in arts. 342 to 347 of this Complementary Law;

          II - the request for restoration of the economic-financial balance must be made during the term of the contract and before any extension;

          III - the procedure referred to in the caput must proceed on a priority basis;

          IV - the request must be accompanied by a calculation and other elements proving the actual economic-financial imbalance, subject to the provisions of § 3;

          V - the rebalancing may be carried out by means of:

          a) revision of the contracted amounts;

        b) financial compensation, tariff adjustments or other amounts contractually owed to the contracted party, including as capital contribution or
  pecuniary consideration;

          c) renegotiation of terms and conditions for the delivery or provision of services;

          d) increase or reduction of amounts owed to the public administration, including grant rights;

          e) transfer to one of the parties of costs or charges originally attributed to the other; or

          f) other methods deemed acceptable by the parties, subject to the sector legislation or that governing the contract.

         § 1 The request referred to in the caput must be decided definitively within 90 (ninety) days counted from the filing, extendable once for an
  equal period if additional evidentiary instruction is necessary, with said period suspended while the request to the contracted party remains unfulfilled.

        § 2 The economic-financial rebalancing shall preferably be implemented by means of a change in the contract's remuneration or a tariff adjustment,
  as the case may be, with alternative forms only being adopted by the Administration with the agreement of the contracted party, subject, in all
  cases, to the terms of the administrative contract.

          § 3 The legal entities that are part of the public administration with authority to decide on economic-financial rebalancing procedures may
  regulate the manner of submitting the request referred to in the caput and the recommended calculation methodologies for demonstrating the imbalance, without prejudice to the
  right of the contracted party to request it in the absence of such regulation.

        § 4 Under the terms of the regulation, the economic-financial rebalancing may, at the discretion of the public administration, be implemented on a provisional basis in
  cases in which the contracted party demonstrates a relevant financial impact on contract performance arising from the change in the effective tax burden, with the
  economic compensation to be reviewed and adjusted upon the definitive decision on the request.

        § 5 The definitive decision referred to in § 4 must state the manner and instruments for the collection or refund of amounts paid short or in excess
  during the application of the provisional adjustment measure.

          Art. 377. In cases of omission by this Chapter, the provisions of the legislation governing the contract shall apply subsidiarily.

                                                                                      CHAPTER V

                                                             ON THE USE OF THE CREDIT BALANCE OF PIS AND COFINS

         Art. 378. The credits of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and of COFINS, including presumed credits, not appropriated or not used up to the date of extinction of these
  contributions:

          I - shall remain valid and usable in the manner set forth in this Chapter, with the running of the period for their use maintained;

          II - must be duly recorded in the bookkeeping environment for the taxes mentioned in the caput, under the terms of the applicable legislation;

          III - may be used for offsetting against the amount owed of the CBS; and

        IV - may be refunded in cash or offset against other federal taxes, provided that the requirements for use in those modalities established by the legislation of the
  contributions referred to in the caput as of the date of their extinction are met, subject to, on the date of the request or the declaration, the conditions and limits
  in force for the refund or offsetting of credits relating to taxes administered by the RFB.

        Art. 379. Goods received in return as of January 1, 2027, relating to sales made prior to that date, shall entitle the appropriation of a CBS credit
  corresponding to the amount of the contributions referred to in the caput of art. 378 that had been levied on the respective transactions.


        Sole paragraph. The credit referred to in the caput may only be used for offsetting against the CBS, offsetting against other taxes and refund being forbidden.

        Art. 380. The credits of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and of COFINS, which, up to the date of extinction of those taxes, were being appropriated based on
  depreciation, amortization or a monthly amount quota, must remain being appropriated, as presumed credits of the CBS, in the manner provided for:

        I - in item III of § 1 and in § 21 of art. 3 of Law No. 10,637, of December 30, 2002;

        II - in item III of § 1 and in §§ 14, 16 and 29, all of art. 3, and in item II of the caput of art. 15, all of Law No. 10,833, of December 29, 2003;

        III - in §§ 4 and 7 of art. 15 of Law No. 10,865, of April 30, 2004; and

        IV - in art. 6 of Law No. 11,488, of June 15, 2007.

        § 1 The provisions of the caput also apply to credits that are awaiting the fulfillment of requirements to begin appropriation based on
  depreciation, amortization or monthly amount quota on the day immediately prior to the date of extinction of the taxes.

         § 2 The appropriation of the credit referred to in the caput is subject to the legislation in force on the date of extinction of the said taxes, including with respect to
  the rate applicable in calculating its amount, subject to the provisions of art. 378 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3 In the event of disposal of the asset that gives rise to the installment appropriation of credits referred to in the caput before the appropriation is complete, no
  crediting shall be allowed, as of the date of the disposal, with respect to the installments not yet appropriated.

        Art. 381. The taxpayer subject to the regular CBS regime may appropriate a presumed credit on the inventory of material goods existing on January 1,
  2027, in the following situations:

        I - if the taxpayer, on December 31, 2026, was subject to the cumulative assessment regime of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and COFINS,
  established primarily by Law No. 9,718, of November 27, 1998, in relation to goods in inventory on which no credits of the
  Contribution to PIS/Pasep and COFINS were assessed due to being subject to said assessment regime;

        II - in relation to goods in inventory subject, upon acquisition, to tax substitution or single-phase levy referred to in the following provisions:

        a) item I of art. 1 of Law No. 10,147, of December 21, 2000;

        b) caput of art. 1, item II of art. 3 and caput of art. 5 of Law No. 10,485, of July 3, 2002;

        c) art. 43 of Provisional Measure No. 2,158-35, of August 24, 2001;

        d) art. 53 of Law No. 9,532, of December 10, 1997; and

        e) item II of art. 6 of Law No. 12,402, of May 2, 2011;

        III - in relation to the portion of the value of the goods in inventory subject to the partial crediting prohibition established by §§ 7 to 9 of art. 3 of Law No. 10,637, of
  December 30, 2002, and of Law No. 10,833, of December 29, 2003.

        § 1 The right to the presumed credit provided for in the caput:

        I - applies only to new goods acquired from a legal entity domiciled in the Country or imported for resale or for use in the production of goods
  intended for sale or in the provision of services to third parties;

        II - does not apply to products whose acquisition was covered by a zero rate, exemption, suspension, or that were not subject to the levy of the Contribution to
  PIS/Pasep and COFINS;

        III - does not apply to goods considered for personal use and consumption referred to in art. 57 of this Complementary Law;

        IV - does not apply:

        a) to goods incorporated into the taxpayer's fixed assets; and

        b) to real property.

        § 2 An act of the Union's Executive Branch shall regulate the manner of verification of the inventory existing on January 1, 2027, and may determine the conducting
  of an inventory count and valuation, or an alternative method.

        § 3 The amount of the presumed credit referred to in the caput:

         I - in the case of goods acquired domestically, shall be calculated by applying a percentage of 9.25% (nine and twenty-five hundredths percent) to the
  value of the inventory;

        II - in the case of imported goods, shall be equivalent to the amount of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep-Importação and of Cofins-Importação effectively paid on the
  import, with the assessment of a presumed credit in relation to the additional rate referred to in § 21 of art. 8 of Law No. 10,865, of April 30, 2004, being forbidden.

        § 4 The presumed credit referred to in the caput:

        I - must be assessed and appropriated by the last day of June 2027;

        II - must be used in 12 (twelve) equal and successive monthly installments starting from the period following that of appropriation; and

        III - may only be used for offsetting against the CBS, offsetting against other taxes and refund being forbidden.

       § 5 For the purposes of this article, goods with the same nature that, as a result of applicable accounting standards, are recorded by public service
  concessionaires as contract, intangible or financial assets shall also be considered goods incorporated into fixed assets.

          Art. 382. The use of the credits of the contributions referred to in this Chapter for offsetting shall take preference over the CBS credits referred to in
  art. 53 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 383. The right to use the credits referred to in arts. 379 to 381 of this Complementary Law shall be extinguished after a period of 5 (five) years, counted
  from the last day of the assessment period in which the appropriation of the credit occurred.

                                                                                      CHAPTER VI

             ON THE CRITERIA, LIMITS AND PROCEDURES RELATING TO THE OFFSETTING OF ICMS TAX OR FINANCIAL-TAX BENEFITS

                                                                                         Section I


                                                                                 General Provisions

         Art. 384. Individuals or legal entities holding onerous benefits relating to the ICMS, due to the reduction in the level of those benefits provided for in § 1
  of art. 128 of the ADCT, in the period between January 1, 2029 and December 31, 2032, shall be compensated with funds from the Fund for Compensation of Tax
  or Financial-Tax Benefits established by art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, in accordance with the criteria and limits for determining
  the level of benefits and their reduction and with the procedures for analyzing the requirements for the applicant's qualification for compensation established in this Complementary
  Law.

         Art. 384. Individuals or legal entities holding onerous benefits relating to the ICMS, due to the reduction in the level of those benefits arising from the
  provisions of art. 128 of the ADCT, in the period between January 1, 2029 and December 31, 2032, shall be compensated with funds from the Fund for Compensation
  of Tax or Financial-Tax Benefits established by art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, in accordance with the criteria and
  limits for determining the level of benefits and their reduction and with the procedures for analyzing the requirements for the applicant's qualification for compensation
  established in this Complementary Law. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Sole paragraph. The compensation referred to in the caput:

        I - applies to holders of onerous benefits regularly granted up to May 31, 2023, without prejudice to subsequent extensions or renewals,
  subject to the deadline of December 31, 2032 and, if applicable, the registration and deposit requirement established by art. 3, item II, of Complementary Law No. 160, of
  August 7, 2017, who timely complied with the conditions required by the norm granting the benefit;

        II - also applies to other programs or benefits that migrated by virtue of changes in state legislation between May 31, 2023 and the date of
  enactment of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, or that were in the process of migration on the date of enactment of said Constitutional
  Amendment, provided that their granting act is issued by the federated unit within 90 (ninety) days after the publication of this Complementary Law;

        III - does not apply to holders of benefits arising from the provisions of § 2-A of art. 3 of Complementary Law No. 160, of August 7, 2017.

       IV - shall adopt as a parameter for calculating the reduction in the level of tax or financial-tax benefits the legislation in force on May 31, 2023, or,
  where applicable, on the date on which the benefits that migrated under the terms of item II of this paragraph began to take effect.              (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 385. For the purposes of the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, the following are considered:

        I - onerous benefits: the economic repercussions arising from exemptions, incentives and tax or financial-tax benefits granted by the
  federated unit for a fixed term and subject to condition, in the manner provided for in art. 178 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 - National Tax Code;

        II - holders of onerous benefits: persons who hold the right to enjoy onerous benefits by virtue of a granting act or norm, provided they are
  compliant with the conditions required by the norm granting the benefit, subject to the provisions of item III of the sole paragraph of art. 384 of this Complementary
  Law;

        III - fixed term: the term established for obtaining the onerous benefit, subject to the deadline of December 31, 2032, under the terms of the caput of art.
  12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023;

         IV - condition, in the manner provided for in art. 178 of Law No. 5,172, of October 25, 1966 - National Tax Code: the counterparts provided for in the granting act or
  established in state or district legislation required of the benefit holder from which onus or restrictions on its activity result, such as those that:

        a) are aimed at the implementation or expansion of an economic enterprise linked to processes of transformation or industrialization capable of
  adding value;

        b) establish the creation of new jobs; or

        c) impose a limitation on the sale price or the restriction on contracting with certain suppliers;

        V - economic repercussion:

       a) the portion of the ICMS levied on the transaction appropriated by the taxpayer of the tax due to the granting of a tax benefit by the federated unit, such
  as presumed ICMS credit, granted ICMS credit, among others;

         b) the portion corresponding to the discount granted on the ICMS to be collected due to the early payment of the tax whose payment term
  had been extended; or

         c) in the case of the benefit of extending the ICMS payment term, the unrealized financial gain resulting from the reduction of the ICMS rates
  provided for in art. 128 of the ADCT, using as calculation parameters, among others, the Selic Rate accumulated between the month following the ordinary due date of the ICMS
  debt and the month to which the payment was deferred, limited to December 2032;

          VI - granting act of onerous benefits: any administrative act or classification under a legal norm by which the granting of the
  ownership of onerous benefits to an individual or legal entity by the federated unit is effected;

        VII - implementation of an economic enterprise: the establishment of an economic enterprise for the development of the activity to be carried out
  by a legal entity not domiciled in the geographic location of the federated unit that grants the subsidy;

         VIII - expansion of an economic enterprise: the expansion of capacity, the modernization or the diversification of the trade or production of goods or
  services of the economic enterprise, including by means of establishing another unit, by the legal entity domiciled in the geographic location of the
  federated unit that grants the subsidy.

        § 1 For the purposes of the provisions of item IV of the caput, the counterparts provided for in acts or norms granting
  tax benefits that:

        I - amount to the mere fulfillment of duties of mandatory observance for all taxpayers and already previously established in legislation;

        II - constitute a mere declaration of intentions, without the establishment of any actual onus or restrictions; and

        III - require a contribution to a state or district fund linked to the enjoyment of the benefit,

  do not fall within the concept of condition.

         § 2 For the purposes of the compensation referred to in this Chapter, and without applying the provisions of item III of § 1 of this article, a benefit whose
  counterpart is a contribution to a state or district fund whose entire resources are used in public infrastructure works or in
  projects that promote the economic activity of the private sector, including when carried out by state-owned companies, established up to May 31, 2023, is
  considered an onerous benefit.

        § 3 For the calculation of the economic repercussion arising from a tax or financial-tax benefit, all amounts of a tax nature
  corresponding to waived rights and assumed obligations must be deducted, such as ICMS bookkeeping credits that ceased to be used or contributions to funds
  made for the enjoyment of the benefit, including in the case of § 2 of this article.

       § 4 The costs, expenses and investments made as a condition for the enjoyment of onerous benefits shall not be taken into account for the calculation of the economic
  repercussion arising from a tax or financial-tax benefit.



        § 5 The RFB may list other cases with economic repercussions arising from tax or financial-tax benefits relating to the ICMS
  equivalent to those provided for in item V of the caput.

                                                                                        Section II

                                                                          On the Powers Assigned to the RFB

        Art. 386. In relation to the compensation of onerous benefits referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, the RFB is responsible, in observance of this
  Complementary Law, for:

          I - establishing the manner and the information for qualification requests;

          II - issuing complementary norms relating to compliance with the requirements to which applicants are subject for their qualification;

          III - analyzing the qualification requests made by the holders of onerous benefits and, if the legal requirements are met, granting them;

          IV - establishing the information to be provided in the fiscal and tax bookkeeping and the format of the credit assessment demonstration;

         V - processing and reviewing the credit assessments transmitted by the qualified holders of onerous benefits before the body and, if no
  irregularity is found, recognizing the respective credits, authorizing their payment;

          VI - establishing risk parameters for the purpose of automating the recognition of the credit and the authorization of payment;

          VII - establishing analysis criteria to be applied in the review procedures;

          VIII - regulating the manner of rectification of the information provided and the treatment of its consequences;

       IX - regulating the manner of returning improper payment due to an irregularly assessed credit and the withholding of subsequent credits to
  offset improper payments;

          X - regulating the standardization of the representation per federated unit referred to in art. 398 of this Complementary Law;

          XI - regulating deadlines not provided for in this Chapter;

          XII - regulating other procedural aspects not provided for above, especially those concerning the guarantee of the right to a full defense and to adversarial proceedings.

          Sole paragraph. For the purposes of this Chapter, the regulation of the administrative process provided for in Law No. 9,784, of January 29,
  1999, applies subsidiarily.

         Art. 387. Within the scope of the RFB's authority and on an exclusive basis, the Tax Auditor of the Brazilian Federal Revenue Service is responsible, in relation to the right assured
  to holders of onerous benefits to the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, for:

        I - preparing and rendering decisions or participating therein in a process or procedure for analyzing the recognition of the right to the compensation referred to in the caput and of the
  recognition of the credit arising therefrom;

         II - examining the accounting and fiscal bookkeeping of business companies and of business persons for the purpose of reviewing the assessment of the credit
  submitted, without the restrictions provided for in arts. 1,190 and 1,191 of Law No. 10,406, of January 10, 2002 - Civil Code applying to them, and subject to the provisions
  of art. 1,193 of the same statute;

          III - providing guidance to the holders of the right to the compensation referred to in the caput; and

          IV - carrying out the assessment of the credit arising from amounts unduly paid generated by the systematization of the compensation referred to in the caput.

                                                                                        Section III

                                                                    On the Qualification of the Applicant for Compensation

         Art. 388. The holder of an onerous benefit qualified by the RFB may be a beneficiary of the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, except for the
  onerous benefit that, under the terms of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, is covered by the compensation provided for in §§ 2 and 6, all of
  art. 92-B of the ADCT, or, still, by any other form of compensation provided for in the Federal Constitution, even if partial.

         Sole paragraph. The request for the qualification procedure, in the manner to be regulated by the RFB, must be submitted in the period from January
  1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.

          Art. 389. The requirements for granting the qualification to the applicant are:

          I - being the holder of an onerous benefit granted by a federated unit;

          II - there being a granting act of the onerous benefit issued by the federated unit:

          a) up to May 31, 2023, or within the period provided for in the case set forth in item II of the sole paragraph of art. 384 of this Complementary Law, without prejudice to
  subsequent extensions or renewals, as provided for in § 1 of that same article;

          b) that expressly establishes the conditions and counterparts to be observed by the beneficiary;

          c) whose term of enjoyment does not exceed December 31, 2032; and

        d) that is in force in all or part of the period referred to in the caput of art. 384 of this Complementary Law, even by means of an act of extension or
  renewal;

          III - the registration and deposit provided for in item II of art. 3 of Complementary Law No. 160, of August 7, 2017, having been carried out, if such requirement applies;

          IV - timely complying with the conditions required by the granting act of the onerous benefit;

        V - submitting the ancillary obligations with the information necessary to verify the onerous benefit subject to compensation, as well as those in
  which the registration of the benefit itself is recorded, where applicable;

          VI - there being no legal impediment to the enjoyment of tax benefits;

          VII - presenting registration compliance before the national register of legal entities - CNPJ.

        Sole paragraph. For purposes of fulfilling the qualification requirement provided for in item IV of this article, the holder of the onerous benefit must
  submit a declaration that it timely complies with the conditions, with the prior statement of the granting federated unit to the granting of the qualification being mandatory.

          Art. 390. Subject to the right to a full defense and to adversarial proceedings, the qualification shall be:
        I - denied, in the event that the applicant does not meet the requirements referred to in art. 389 of this Complementary Law;

        II - suspended, in the event that the applicant temporarily fails to meet the requirements referred to in art. 389 of this Complementary Law;

        III - cancelled, in the event that the applicant fails to meet the requirements referred to in art. 389 of this Complementary Law.

          Sole paragraph. The suspension provided for in item II of the caput shall be reversed in the event of a change in the elements that led to the suspension, with the same
  previously granted qualification being maintained.

                                                                                        Section IV

                                Da Demonstration and Recognition of the Assessed Credit and of the Review of the Regularity of the Withheld Credit

       Art. 391. The qualified holder of an onerous benefit shall report monthly, in the fiscal bookkeeping, the elements necessary for the quantification of the economic
  repercussion of each tax or financial-tax benefit, in accordance with the regulation to be issued by the RFB.

          § 1 The credit shall be calculated for each competency month based on the amount of the economic repercussion of each tax or financial-tax benefit and of the
  reduction in the level of tax benefits referred to in the caput of art. 384 of this Complementary Law with respect to each granting act and type of qualified tax
  benefit.

        § 2 The assessment of the credit relating to the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law shall be shown in the fiscal bookkeeping, in accordance with the
  RFB's regulation.

        § 3 The right to seek the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law shall be extinguished with the passage of a period of 3 (three) years, counted
  from the expiration of the deadline for transmitting the fiscal bookkeeping established in the regulatory norm to contain the assessment of the corresponding credit.

         Art. 392. The RFB shall process the amount calculated for purposes of compensation, in the manner set forth in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, and, unless there are indications of
  irregularity or the amount falls within risk parameters, shall have its credit automatically recognized and authorized for payment within 60 (sixty) days
  from the expiration of the deadline for transmitting the fiscal bookkeeping containing its demonstration.
         Art. 392. The RFB shall process the amount calculated for offsetting purposes, pursuant to art. 384 of this Complementary Law, and, unless there are indications
  of irregularity or the amount falls within risk parameters, the respective credit shall be automatically recognized and authorized for payment within 60
  (sixty) days counted: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - from the expiration of the deadline for submission of the tax bookkeeping record containing its computation;           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - from the date of submission, if made late; or       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - from the date of the correction made after expiration of the deadline for submission.         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 1 If the RFB does not respond within the deadline set forth in the caput, recognition of the credit and authorization of payment shall be tacitly deemed to occur on the
  final date of the deadline.

        § 2 Delivery of the funds to the beneficiary shall occur within 30 (thirty) days counted from the date of the authorization referred to in the caput.

       § 3 Payment made on a date later than that set forth in § 2 shall be increased by interest, at the SELIC Rate for federal securities, accrued monthly, and by interest of
  1% (one percent) in the month in which the amount is made available to the taxpayer, starting from the month following the end of the deadline set forth in that paragraph.

        § 4 If the monthly amount computed is at a level above the tolerable risk threshold, the excess portion shall be withheld for review of the
  regularity of the computation.

        § 5 If there are indications of irregularity, the entire amount computed shall be withheld for its review.

        § 6 Withholdings made under the circumstances described in §§ 4 and 5 of this article must be notified to the interested party.

        § 7 Interest accrues on the withholdings referred to in §§ 4 and 5, at the same rate established in § 3, starting from the month following the end of the 90
  (ninety)-day period counted from the expiration of the deadline for submission of the tax bookkeeping record containing its computation.

       § 8 Review of the regularity of the computation of withheld credits must be carried out within the following maximum periods counted from the date of full
  submission of the supporting evidence required by the RFB on the date of notice described in § 6 of this article:

        I - 120 (one hundred and twenty) days, in the circumstance provided for in § 4 of this article; and

        II - 1 (one) year, in the circumstance provided for in § 5 of this article.

        § 9 Failure to fully submit the supporting evidence referred to in § 8 of this article within 60 (sixty) days counted from notice
  of the request for submission shall result in non-recognition of the withheld portion of the credit, without prejudice to the examination of the regularity of the portion of the credit
  already paid, if any.

       § 10. If the deadline established in § 8 of this article expires without the computation review having been completed, the withheld credit shall be tacitly authorized
  for payment, which must be made within the period provided for in § 2 of this article, without prejudice to the continuation of the ongoing procedure, if applicable.

        § 11. The criteria for defining the tolerable risk threshold may not result in the withholding of amounts referring to more than 20% (twenty percent) of the
  computations submitted in the respective monthly period, not counting toward this computation the computations regarding which there are objective indications of irregularity or
  well-founded suspicions of fraud.

         § 12. The withholding-limiting percentage set forth in § 11 of this article may be expanded during the period in which the total amount of credits computed indicates
  that the resources originally earmarked to fund the Fund established by the caput of art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 23, 2023, will be
  insufficient to cover the offsets referred to in the caput of art. 384 of this Complementary Law until the end of the year 2032, and provided that the indicative criterion is
  regulated and published by the National Treasury Secretariat.

                                                                                        Section V

                                                               Of the Self-Regularization of Information Provided

        Art. 393. If the interested party finds an irregularity in the computation of the credit submitted for payment, it must immediately proceed to
  correct it, amending the information provided in the tax bookkeeping record, in accordance with the regulation to be issued by the RFB.

        § 1 Having received undue amounts arising from the credit computed in excess in the circumstance described in the caput, the beneficiary must also make its immediate
  return to the Fund referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, subject to § 2 of this article and in the manner to be regulated by the RFB.

        § 2 The amount unduly received must be increased by interest from the first day of the month following the date of its receipt, equivalent to the
  SELIC Rate, accrued monthly, and by interest of 1% (one percent) in the month in which the amount is returned to the Fund referred to in art. 12 of Constitutional
  Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023.


         § 3 If the interested party carries out the regularization referred to in the caput and does not make the immediate full return of the amount unduly received referred to
  in § 1 of this article, the RFB is authorized to ex officio offset the debt against credits of the same nature submitted in subsequent periods until
  they are sufficient to equal the amount of the debt updated pursuant to § 2, without prejudice to the ordinary withholdings relating to the review of the regularity of the
  computation of credits subsequently submitted.

            § 4 The interested party must be notified of the ex officio offsets made in accordance with the provisions of § 3 of this article.

            § 5 The RFB shall be responsible for establishing the credit of the Union pursuant to art. 395, if, before the full return of the debt referred to in § 1 of this article:

        I - the interested party does not submit the computation of credits of the same nature eligible for offsetting in the first period following the
  circumstance described in § 3 of this article; or

            II - for any reason, the credits of the same nature eligible for offsetting cease for three consecutive months; or

            III - one year has elapsed since the first offset authorized in § 3 of this article.

         § 6 The correction of the information provided in the tax bookkeeping record referred to in the caput that imposes on the interested party the immediate duty to return
  amounts unduly received, as provided for in § 1 of this article, constitutes the day of occurrence of the undue receipt referred to in § 1 of art. 395, for purposes of
  fixing the initial term of the statute-of-limitations period with respect to the amount arising from the correction.

                                                                                        Section VI

                                                   Of the Procedures for Review of the Credit Computation and the Procedural Rite

         Art. 394. If an irregularity is found in a procedure for review of the computation of the credit submitted for payment, the competent authority
  shall issue a decision order that shall be notified to the interested party with the grounds and evidence necessary, denying the credit
  submitted in whole or in part.

         § 1 The procedural rite provided for in Law No. 9,784, of January 29, 1999, applies to the provisions of the caput, subject to the specific rules established in this
  chapter.

        § 2 The procedure for review of the computation of the credit may also be carried out after payment to the beneficiary, in accordance with procedural rules
  to be established by an act of the RFB.

        § 3 In the course of the computation review procedure, the competent authority shall carry out investigative activities aimed at ascertaining and verifying the
  necessary data, including carrying out inquiries, if applicable.

         § 4 If payment of amounts has occurred for which a decision order is subsequently issued denying the credit submitted in whole or in part, the
  interested party shall be notified to return, within 30 (thirty) days, the amounts unduly received, increased by interest calculated pursuant to § 2 of art. 393.

        § 5 As an alternative to the provisions of § 4 of this article, the interested party may authorize the offsetting of regular credits of the same nature to be
  submitted in subsequent periods until they are sufficient to equal the amount of the debt updated pursuant to § 2 of art. 393.

        § 6 The authorization provided for in § 5 of this article constitutes an irrevocable confession of debt eligible for registration in the Union's active debt, should, for any
  reason, the offsetting cease for three consecutive months and the interested party fail to make the return of the full remaining balance.

            § 7 The interested party may file an appeal within 30 (thirty) days counted from notice of the decision order.

         § 8 The appeal filed does not prevent the establishment of any credit of the Union referred to in art. 395 of this Complementary Law, including the applicable fine,
  but its enforceability shall be suspended until 30 (thirty) days counted from the interested party's notice of the decision on the appeal, further subject to the provisions of § 7
  of art. 395.

        § 9 If the appeal is decided, in a final and definitive manner, wholly or partly in favor of the interested party, and there being an amount owed to it, in accordance with the
  decision rendered, payment of the withheld amount must be authorized.

        § 10. After the appeal is decided, if the denial in whole or in part of the credit submitted for payment is upheld in final administrative form and it has
  already been made, the interested party shall be notified to make the return of the undue payment increased by interest calculated pursuant to § 2 of art. 393 within
  30 days counted from notice of the decision, under its terms.

                                                                                        Section VII

                                                                         Of the Establishment of the Union's Credit

        Art. 395. In the circumstance of § 5 of art. 393 or upon finding an irregularity in the computation of the credit calculated by the beneficiary after the
  payment has been made by the Union and the full return, with the interest increase provided for in § 2 of art. 393, has not occurred, within the period of § 4 of art. 394, nor the authorization
  referred to in § 5 of art. 394, the RFB shall notify ex officio, in the manner to be established by it, the establishment of the Union's credit composed of:

            I - principal amount: equivalent to the amount unduly received that was not returned or offset;

        II - default interest: principal amount multiplied by the SELIC Rate for federal securities, accrued monthly, starting from the first day of the month following the
  date of the undue receipt until the month preceding the date of the notification;

            III - 20% fine: portion resulting from 0.2 (two tenths) multiplied by the sum of default interest and principal amount.

        § 1 The RFB's right to establish the credit arising from the circumstance provided for in the caput expires after 3 (three) years, counted from the first day of the fiscal year
  following the occurrence of the undue receipt, subject to the provisions of § 6 of art. 393.

         § 2 Default interest accrues on the established credit at the same rate provided for in item II of the caput, accrued monthly starting from the month in which it was
  established, and of 1% (one percent) in the month of its payment.

         § 3 The notification issued, followed by due notice to the debtor, containing all the elements required by law, shall be a suitable instrument for registration in the Union's active
  debt.

            § 4 The procedural rite provided for in Law No. 9,784, of January 29, 1999, applies to the provisions of the caput, subject to the specific rules established in this
  article.

            § 5 The interested party may file an appeal within 30 (thirty) days counted from notice of the notification that established the credit in the circumstance provided for in the
  caput.

         § 6 The appeal filed does not suspend the obligation to pay the established credit, except if the party has also filed the appeal referred to in §
  7 of art. 394 and it is pending judgment, in which case the connection between both appeals must be observed.

         § 7 If the interested party timely complies with the notification referred to in § 10 of art. 394, the Union's credit established pursuant to the caput of this
  article shall be canceled.


         § 8 After notice of the establishment of the Union's credit which is not subject to suspended enforceability, there shall be an ex officio offset of the
