  interested party's credits not yet paid until the amount of the debt is reached.

        § 9 If the appeal referred to in § 5 of this article is decided, in a final and definitive manner, wholly or partly in favor of the interested party, the
  established amount must be reduced or canceled and the amounts possibly offset pursuant to § 7 of this article shall be paid, increased by interest calculated pursuant to § 2 of art. 393, in
  accordance with the decision rendered.

        § 10. The portion of the credit corresponding to the principal amount and the proportional default interest that is collected shall be allocated to the Fund referred to in art. 12
  of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 23, 2023, if the collection occurs by December 31, 2032, and to the Fund referred to in art.
  159-A of the Federal Constitution, if on a later date.

       § 11. The 20% (twenty percent) fine provided for in item III of the caput, increased by the proportional default interest, shall be allocated to the Special Fund for
  Development and Improvement of Tax Enforcement Activities - FUNDAF, established by art. 6 of Decree-Law No. 1,437, of December 17, 1975.

                                                                                     Section VIII

                                                                       Of the Report for Criminal Purposes

        Art. 396. Within 10 (ten) days of the issuance of the infraction notice provided for in art. 395 of this Complementary Law, the corresponding
  criminal report to the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office must be made, in accordance with regulations to be issued by the RFB.

                                                                                      Section IX

                                                   Of the Communication and Tax Reporting by the Federated Units

        Art. 397. If the federated unit finds noncompliance with the conditions required by the rule granting the onerous benefit, it must notify the RFB within
  10 (ten) days, so that the RFB may effect the suspension or cancellation of the qualification.

         Art. 398. In tax proceedings in which the state or Federal District tax administration finds an irregularity in the enjoyment of an onerous benefit granted
  by the corresponding federated unit, when the situation falls within the offsetting circumstance referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law, the
  competent authority must, within 10 (ten) days of the act of finding the irregularity, report the facts accompanied by the evidence to the head of its
  agency, so that the agency may forward the matter to the RFB.

         Sole paragraph. The RFB and the tax administration of a federated unit are permitted, by means of an agreement, to regulate the format of the report, its
  routing, and, if convenient, the frequency of forwarding.

                                                                                      Section X

                                                                                Final Provisions

         Art. 399. By means of a written requisitory act, for purposes of verifying the requirement set forth in item IV of art. 389 of this Complementary Law, the public bodies
  of the Union, States, Federal District and Municipalities and any other entities or persons are required to provide the RFB with all information they have
  relating to compliance with conditions established in the act granting the onerous benefit.

          Art. 400. The RFB shall publish, under active transparency, the monthly list of beneficiaries of the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law,
  identifying the beneficiary, the federative unit granting the onerous benefit, the granting act, the type of tax benefit, the amount paid as compensation and the
  amount of the credit, if any, withheld for verification or compensation.

        Art. 401. Amounts paid to the holder of the onerous benefit as a result of the compensation referred to in art. 384 of this Complementary Law shall receive the same
  tax treatment as the tax benefit granted by the State or the Federal District, for purposes of the incidence of IRPJ, CSLL, PIS and COFINS.

        Art. 402. The State Finance Departments (Secretarias de Fazenda) of the federative units and the RFB shall designate officials to form a working group for the purposes of:

        I - identifying the types of incentives and tax or financial-tax benefits granted for a fixed term and subject to conditions;

        II - identifying the respective methods for calculating the resulting economic repercussions;

        III - proposing adjustments to the ancillary obligations to be submitted by the holders of onerous benefits, so that they include a demonstration of the
  economic repercussion of each tax or financial-tax benefit granted to them.

       Art. 403. The RFB shall specify its own electronic system for the processing and handling of the information, acts and procedures described in this Complementary
  Law, and specific resources must be reserved in the Union budget as of the year 2025. Effects to take place [Produção de efeitos]

         Art. 404. The Union shall supplement the resources referred to in § 1 of art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, in the event of
  insufficient resources for the compensation referred to in § 2 of the same article, limited to the amounts provided for in the annual budget bill.

         Sole Paragraph. The resources referred to in this Chapter shall not be subject to withholding, unlinking or any other restriction on disbursement, nor shall they be
  subject to the spending limitation rules set forth in art. 9 and in item II of § 1 of art. 31 of Complementary Law No. 101, of May 4, 2000.

        Art. 405. The financial balance of the Fund referred to in art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, existing as of December 31,
  2032, shall be provisioned in the amount corresponding to the sum of:

         I - the estimate of the total value of credits in processing and of credits administratively approved and still subject to the legal deadlines for
  authorization and payment;

        II - the estimate of the amount corresponding to the total amount of credits withheld by the RFB under the terms of §§ 4 and 5 of art. 392 of this Complementary Law; and

        III - the amount proportional to the judicial risk relating to any lawsuits whose subject matter is the payment of compensations denied at the
  administrative level.

        § 1 The amount referred to in item III of the caput shall be reviewed annually by joint act of the Attorney General of the Union (Advogado-Geral da União) and the Minister of State for Finance.

       § 2 The balance of the Fund referred to in art. 12 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023, existing as of December 31, 2032 and that
  exceeds the provisioning referred to in the caput shall be transferred to the National Regional Development Fund (Fundo Nacional de Desenvolvimento Regional), established by art. 159-A of the Federal Constitution
  in 120 (one hundred and twenty) equal monthly installments, subject to the adjustment provided for in § 3 of this article, as of July 2033.

        § 3 The balance to be transferred to the National Regional Development Fund and the corresponding installments shall be adjusted as follows:

        I - the return on available funds and any refund of payments to the Tax Benefits Compensation Fund (Fundo de Compensação de Benefícios Fiscais) shall be added to the balance and the
  remaining installments shall be increased proportionally;

        II - any excess provisioning, determined after periodic reviews, shall be added to the balance and the remaining installments shall be increased
  proportionally;

        III - any insufficiency of provisioning shall be deducted from the balance and the remaining installments shall be reduced proportionally.
        § 4 In the absence of a financial balance on the date referred to in the caput, the Tax Benefits Compensation Fund shall be dissolved, whereby:

        I - any need for subsequent compensation shall be met by means of a specific budget allocation;

        II - resources that are subsequently returned to the Tax Benefits Compensation Fund shall be transferred directly to the National Regional
  Development Fund, net of the amounts contributed under item I of this paragraph.

                                                                                  CHAPTER VII

                                                              ON THE TRANSITION APPLICABLE TO CAPITAL GOODS

         Art. 406. The incidence of the IBS and the CBS shall be subject to the rates established in this article on the sale of used machinery, vehicles and equipment acquired
  by December 31, 2032:

        I - whose acquisition was covered by a valid tax document; and

        II - which have remained recorded in the seller's fixed assets for more than 12 (twelve) months.

        § 1 With respect to the CBS, the rates provided for in this article apply only to the sale of the goods referred to in the caput whose acquisition:

        I - occurred by December 31, 2026; and

        II - was subject to the incidence of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins at a positive nominal rate.

        § 2 As of January 1, 2027, the CBS rate applicable to the sale of the goods referred to in the caput and § 1:

        I - is reduced to zero for the portion of the CBS tax base that is equal to or less than the net acquisition value of the good; and

        II - shall be that provided for the transaction, with respect to the portion of the CBS tax base that exceeds the net acquisition value of the good.

        § 3 With respect to the IBS, the rates provided for in this article apply only to the sale of the goods referred to in the caput whose acquisition:

        I - occurred by December 31, 2032; and

        II - was subject to the incidence of the ICMS at a positive nominal rate.

        § 4 As of January 1, 2029, the IBS rate applicable to the sale of the goods referred to in the caput and § 3:

        I - is reduced to zero for the portion of the value of the IBS tax base that is equal to or less than the net acquisition value of the good multiplied by:

        a) 1 (one whole), in the case of goods acquired by December 31, 2028;

        b) 0.9 (nine tenths), in the case of goods acquired in calendar year 2029;

        c) 0.8 (eight tenths), in the case of goods acquired in calendar year 2030;

        d) 0.7 (seven tenths), in the case of goods acquired in calendar year 2031; and

        e) 0.6 (six tenths), in the case of goods acquired in calendar year 2032; and

         II - shall be that provided for the transaction, with respect to the portion of the value of the IBS tax base that exceeds the net acquisition value determined after the
  adjustments provided for in item I of this paragraph.

         § 5 In the sale of the goods referred to in the caput, the provisions of § 3 of art. 380 of this Complementary Law shall be observed with respect to the CBS, and of item V of § 5 of
  art. 20 of Complementary Law No. 87, of September 13, 1996, with respect to the ICMS.

        § 6 For purposes of this article, net acquisition value shall be understood as:

        I - for goods acquired by December 31, 2026, the amount corresponding to the difference between:

        a) the total acquisition value of the good recorded on the tax invoice; and

        b) the value of the ICMS, of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and of the Cofins levied on the acquisition of the good, as recorded on the tax invoice, that have allowed the
  appropriation of credits for the respective taxes; and

        II - for goods acquired from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2032, the tax base of the IBS and the CBS, as recorded on the tax invoice, plus
  the amount of ICMS levied on the acquisition that did not allow the appropriation of credits.

          § 7 For purposes of item I of § 6, if there is no information on the amount of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins levied on the transaction
  in which the good was acquired, the calculation of the difference shall use the amount corresponding to the application of the rates of 1.65% (one point sixty-five percent
  ) for the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and of 7.6% (seven point six percent) for the Cofins on the acquisition value of the good stated on the tax
  invoice.

       § 8 For the purposes of this article, goods of the same nature that, as a result of the applicable accounting standards, are
  recorded by public service concessionaires as contract, intangible or financial assets shall also be considered assets recorded in fixed assets.

       Art. 407. The incidence of the IBS and the CBS shall be subject to the rates established in this article on the resale of used machinery, vehicles and equipment
  acquired used.

        § 1 The provisions of this article apply only to:

        I - resale carried out by a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime; and

        II - machinery, vehicles or equipment whose acquisition and resale are covered by a valid tax document.

        § 2 In the resale of goods referred to in the caput acquired by December 31, 2026 and that did not allow the appropriation of credits of the Contribuição
  para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins, the CBS rate:

        I - is reduced to zero for the portion of the value of the CBS tax base that is equal to or less than the net acquisition value of the good; and

        II - shall be that provided for the transaction, with respect to the portion of the CBS tax base that exceeds the net acquisition value of the good.

        § 3 The provisions of § 2 do not apply to the resale of goods referred to in the caput acquired from an individual.



         § 4 In the resale of goods acquired by the reseller as of January 1, 2027 and whose acquisition was benefited by the reduction to zero of rates
  established provided for by art. 406 of this Complementary Law:

        I - the CBS rate applicable to the resale of the good:

         a) is reduced to zero for the portion of the value of the CBS tax base that was benefited by the reduction to zero of the CBS rate under the terms of
  item I of § 2 of art. 406 of this Complementary Law when the good was acquired; and

        b) shall be that provided for the transaction, with respect to the portion of the CBS tax base that exceeds the amount referred to in item "a" of this item; and

        II - the IBS rate applicable to the resale of the good:

         a) is reduced to zero for the portion of the value of the IBS tax base that was benefited by the reduction to zero of the IBS rate under the terms of
  item I of § 4 of art. 406 of this Complementary Law when the good was acquired; and

        b) shall be that provided for the transaction, with respect to the portion of the IBS tax base that exceeds the amount referred to in item "a" of this item.

                                                                                  CHAPTER VIII

                                                                             FINAL PROVISIONS

        Art. 408. Without prejudice to the other rules established in this Complementary Law, during the transition period to the IBS and the CBS, the provisions
  of this article shall apply.

        § 1 Should the same situation provided for by law constitute, until December 31, 2025, a taxable event of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and of the Cofins or of the
  Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep - Importação and of the Cofins-Importação, and, as of January 1, 2026, a taxable event of the CBS, the following shall be observed:

        § 1 Should the same situation provided for by law constitute, until December 31, 2026, a taxable event of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and of the Cofins or of the
  Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep-Importação and of the Cofins-Importação, and, as of January 1, 2027, a taxable event of the CBS, the following shall be observed:
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - the CBS shall not be required;

        II - the following shall be required, as applicable:

        a) Cofins;

        b) Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep;

        c) Cofins - Importação;

        d) Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep - Importação.

          § 2 The provisions of § 1 of this article shall not apply in cases where the assessment and collection of the CBS are carried out under the terms of optional
  regimes provided for in this Complementary Law, in which case the CBS shall be required and the social contributions referred to in item II of § 1 of this
  article shall not be required.
         § 2 The provision of § 1 of this article shall not apply in cases in which the assessment and collection of the CBS are carried out under the terms of
  optional regimes provided for in arts. 485 to 487 of this Complementary Law, in which case the CBS shall be charged and the social contributions referred to in
  item II of § 1 of this article shall not be charged. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 3 For operations occurring until December 31, 2026, including those constituting a pending taxable event on the date of publication of this Complementary
  Law, in cases in which the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins are charged as revenue is actually received under the cash basis regime:

        I - the taxable event of the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins shall be deemed to have occurred on the date the revenue was earned under the accrual basis regime;

         II - the Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins shall be charged at the time the revenue is received, even if this occurs after the said
  contributions have been extinguished; and

        III - the CBS shall not be charged on the receipt of revenue arising from the operation, except in the case of § 2 of this article, in which case the
  Contribuição para o PIS/Pasep and the Cofins shall not be charged.

        § 4 During the period from 2029 to 2032:

         I - if the same operation constitutes, in different calendar years, taxable events of the Tax on Transactions Relating to the Circulation of Goods and
  on Interstate and Intermunicipal Transportation and Communication Services (ICMS) or of the Tax on Services of Any Nature (ISS) and of the
  IBS, the legislation in force in the calendar year of the first occurrence shall prevail with respect to the said taxes; and

        II - if the temporal element of the taxable-event hypothesis of the ICMS or the ISS has not been completed by December 31, 2032:

        a) the said taxes shall not be levied on the operation; and

        b) only the IBS shall be due on the operation.

        § 5 In the case of item II of § 4, the remaining amount of IBS due shall be assessed based on the legislation in force as of January 1, 2033.

                                                                                     BOOK II

                                                                            OF THE SELECTIVE TAX

                                                                                     TITLE I

                                                                         PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS

        Art. 409. The Selective Tax, referred to in item VIII of art. 153 of the Federal Constitution, is hereby instituted, levied on the production, extraction, marketing
  or importation of goods and services harmful to health or the environment.

        § 1 For purposes of the levy of the Selective Tax, the goods classified under the NCM/SH codes and
  mineral coal, and the services listed in Annex XVII, relating to the following, are considered harmful to health or the environment:

        I - vehicles;

        II - vessels and aircraft;

        III - tobacco products;
        IV - alcoholic beverages;

        V - sugary beverages;

        VI - mineral goods;

        VII - prognostic contests and fantasy sport.

        § 2 The goods referred to in items III and IV of § 1 are subject to the Selective Tax when packaged in primary packaging, understood as
  that which is in direct contact with the product and intended for the final consumer.

        Art. 410. The Selective Tax shall be levied only once on the good or service, and any use of credit of the tax with
  prior operations or generation of credits for subsequent operations is prohibited.

        Art. 411. The RFB is responsible for the administration and inspection of the Selective Tax.

        Sole paragraph. Administrative litigation within the scope of the Selective Tax shall comply with the provisions of Decree No. 70.235, of March 6, 1972.

                                                                                   TITLE II

                                                               OF THE GENERAL RULES OF THE SELECTIVE TAX

                                                                                  CHAPTER I

                                                             OF THE MOMENT OF OCCURRENCE OF THE TAXABLE EVENT

        Art. 412. The taxable event of the Selective Tax shall be deemed to have occurred at the moment of:

       I - the first supply, under any title, of the good, including that arising from the legal transactions mentioned in items I to VIII of § 2 of art. 4 of this Complementary
  Law;

        II - the auction at public sale;

        III - the non-onerous transfer of a produced good;

        IV - the incorporation of the good into fixed assets by the manufacturer;

        V - the extraction of a mineral good;

        VI - the consumption of the good by the manufacturer;

        VII - the supply or payment of the service, whichever occurs first; or

        VIII - the importation of goods and services.

                                                                                 CHAPTER II

                                                                             OF NON-INCIDENCE

        Art. 413. The Selective Tax does not apply to:

        I - (VETOED);

        II - operations with electric energy and telecommunications; and

        III - goods and services whose rates are reduced under the terms of § 1 of art. 9 of Constitutional Amendment No. 132, of December 20, 2023.

                                                                                 CHAPTER III

                                                                            OF THE TAX BASE

        Art. 414. The tax base of the Selective Tax is:

        I - the sale value in marketing;

        II - the auction value in the auction;

        III - the reference value in:

        a) a non-onerous transaction or in the consumption of the good;

        b) extraction of a mineral good; or

        c) marketing of tobacco products;

        c) marketing and importation of tobacco products;      (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        IV - the accounting value of incorporation of the produced good into fixed assets;

        V - the entity's own revenue promoting the activity, in the case referred to in item VII of § 1 of art. 409 of this Complementary Law, calculated under the
  terms of art. 245.

        VI - the market value of the good, in the remaining cases.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1 In cases in which the application of specific rates is provided for, under the terms of this Complementary Law, the tax base is that expressed in a
  unit of measure.

        § 2 An act of the head of the Federal Executive Branch shall define the methodology for calculating the reference value mentioned in item III of the caput of this article, based,
  among other things, on quotations, indices or prices in force on the date of the taxable event, on commodities and futures exchanges, on research agencies or on
  government agencies.

        § 3 In the marketing of tobacco products, the reference value shall take into account the retail sale price.

        Art. 415. In the marketing of a good subject to the ad valorem rate, the tax base is the full amount charged in the operation under any title, including the amount
  corresponding to:
        I - additions arising from adjustment of the value of the operation;

        II - interest, fines, additions and charges;

        III - discounts granted under condition;

        IV - the value of transport charged as part of the value of the operation, whether the transport is carried out by the supplier itself or on its behalf and order;

       V - taxes and public prices, including tariffs, levied on the operation or borne by the supplier, except those provided for in § 2 of art. 12 of this Complementary
  Law; and

        VI - other amounts charged or received as part of the value of the operation, including insurance and fees.

        Sole paragraph. If the value of the operation is expressed in foreign currency, it shall be converted into national currency at the exchange rate assessed
  by the Central Bank of Brazil, under the terms of the regulation.

         Art. 416. In marketing between related parties, in the case of a levy subject to the ad valorem rate and in the absence of the reference value referred to
  in § 2 of art. 414, the tax base shall not be lower than the market value of the goods, understood as the value practiced in comparable operations between
  unrelated parties.

        Sole paragraph. For purposes of the provision in the caput, related parties are considered to be those defined in §§ 2 to 5 of art. 5 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 417. The following do not form part of the tax base of the Selective Tax:

        I - the amount of the CBS, the IBS and the Selective Tax itself levied on the operation; and

        II - unconditional discounts.

       § 1 For purposes of the provision in item II of the caput, an unconditional discount is considered to be the portion reducing the price of the operation that appears in the respective
  tax document and does not depend on a subsequent event.

       § 2 A bonus that meets the same conditions specified in § 1 for the characterization of
  unconditional discounts does not form part of the tax base of the Selective Tax.

        § 3 The provision of § 2 does not apply to taxation by means of a specific rate, in which the tax base, expressed in a unit of measure, must consider
  the goods supplied as a bonus.

        § 4 Until December 31, 2032, the amount of the following does not form part of the tax base of the Selective Tax:

      I - the Tax on Transactions Relating to the Circulation of Goods and on Interstate and Intermunicipal Transportation and
  Communication Services (ICMS), provided for in item II of art. 155 of the Federal Constitution;

        II - the Tax on Services of Any Nature (ISS), provided for in item III of art. 156 of the Federal Constitution.

       Art. 418. The return of goods sold gives rise to the right to deduct the amount of the Selective Tax charged in the respective operation in the assessment period
  in which the return occurred or in subsequent periods.

                                                                                  CHAPTER IV

                                                                                OF THE RATES

                                                                                     Section I

                                                                                  Of Vehicles

        Art. 419. The rates of the Selective Tax applicable to vehicles classified under the NCM/SH codes listed in Annex XVII shall be established by
  ordinary law.

        Sole paragraph. The rates referred to in the caput of this article shall be graduated in relation to each vehicle according to classification under the following criteria, under the
  terms of ordinary law:

        I - vehicle power;

        II - energy efficiency;

        III - structural performance and driving assistance technologies;

        IV - recyclability of materials;

        V - carbon footprint;

        VI - technological density;

        VII - carbon dioxide emissions (energy-environmental efficiency), considering the well-to-wheel cycle;

        VIII - vehicle recyclability;

        IX - performance of manufacturing stages in the Country; and

        X - vehicle category.

        Art. 420. The rate of the Selective Tax is reduced to zero for vehicles intended for acquirers whose right to the benefit of the differentiated regime
  provided for in art. 149 of this Complementary Law has been recognized by the RFB, under the terms of art. 153.

         § 1º In the case of the acquirer being a person referred to in item II of the caput of art. 149 of this Complementary Law, the rate reduction referred to
  in the caput applies to a vehicle whose sale price to the consumer, including taxes levied had there been no reductions, is not higher than R$ 200,000.00 (two hundred thousand reais).

       § 2º Subject to the provisions of § 1º, the provisions applicable to the differentiated regime provided for in Section VII
  of Chapter IV of Title IV of Book I apply to the Selective Tax, as applicable, including with regard to the disposal of the vehicle and the interval for enjoyment of the benefit.

                                                                                     Section II

                                                                          Of Aircraft and Vessels



        Art. 421. The rates of the Selective Tax applicable to aircraft and vessels classified under the NCM/SH codes listed in Annex XVII shall
  be established in ordinary law and may be graduated according to environmental sustainability criteria under the terms of the ordinary law.

        Sole paragraph. The ordinary law may provide for a zero rate for vessels and aircraft with zero carbon dioxide emissions or with high
  energy-environmental efficiency.

                                                                                      Section III

                                                                   Of Other Goods Subject to the Selective Tax

        Art. 422. Subject to the provisions of arts. 419 and 420, the rates of the Selective Tax applicable to transactions with the goods and services referred to in Annex
  XVII are those provided for in ordinary law.

         § 1º Ad valorem rates combined with specific rates shall be applied to:

         I - tobacco products classified under heading 24.02 of the NCM/SH; and

         II - alcoholic beverages, for which the specific rates must consider the product of the alcohol content by the volume of the products.

        § 2º The rates of the Selective Tax established for transactions with extracted mineral goods shall respect the maximum percentage of 0.25% (twenty-five
  hundredths percent).

         § 2º The rates of the Selective Tax shall respect the maximum percentage of 0.25% (twenty-five hundredths percent), for transactions with extracted mineral
  goods. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 3º Ordinary law may establish specific rates for other tobacco products not referred to in item I of § 1º, which shall be applied
  cumulatively with the ad valorem rates.

         § 4º The ad valorem rates established for transactions with alcoholic beverages may be differentiated by product category and progressive based on
  alcohol content.

          § 5º The rates of the Selective Tax levied on alcoholic beverages and tobacco products shall be set in a staggered manner, so as to incorporate, from
  2029 to 2033, progressively, the differential between the ICMS rates levied on alcoholic beverages and tobacco products and the
  standard rates of that tax.

        § 5º The rates of the Selective Tax levied on the products provided for in items III to V of § 1º of art. 409 of this Complementary Law shall be set in
  a staggered manner, so as to incorporate, from 2029 to 2033, progressively, the differential between the ICMS rates levied on
  tobacco products, alcoholic beverages, and sugary beverages and the standard rates of that tax. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 6º The adjustment referred to in § 5º:

         I - in the case of alcoholic beverages may be carried out by estimate for the group of beverages as a whole or be differentiated by beverage category; and

         II - shall not condition the setting of the Selective Tax rates on the maintenance of the tax burden of the sectors or of specific categories.

         § 7º The rates applicable to alcoholic beverages may be established so as to differentiate transactions carried out by small producers,
  as defined in ordinary law.

         § 8º To ensure the provisions of § 7º, the rates may be:

         I - progressive based on production volume; and

         II - differentiated by product category.

        Art. 423. If natural gas is intended for use as input in an industrial process and as fuel for transport purposes, the rate
  established under § 2º of art. 422 of this Complementary Law must be set at zero.

          § 1º For purposes of applying the provisions of the caput, the acquirer or the importer must, in the manner set out in the regulation, declare that the natural gas will be intended for
  use as input in an industrial process.

        § 2º In the event that natural gas acquired or imported with a rate reduction is given a destination other than that provided for in the caput, the acquirer or
  the importer must pay the Selective Tax calculated by applying the rate established under § 2º of art. 422 of this Complementary Law, plus
  penalty and default interest under the terms of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, in the capacity of:

         I - responsible party, for the acquirer; or

         II - taxpayer, for the importer.

                                                                                     CHAPTER V

                                                                                OF TAX LIABILITY

         Art. 424. The taxpayer of the Selective Tax is:

         I - the manufacturer, upon the first sale, upon incorporation of the good into fixed assets, upon transfer of the good in a non-onerous transaction, or upon consumption of the
  good;

         I - the manufacturer, upon the first supply, upon incorporation of the good into fixed assets, upon transfer of the good in a non-onerous transaction, or upon consumption of the
  good;     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         II - the importer upon entry of the good of foreign origin into national territory;

         III - the successful bidder upon the auction;

         IV - the extractive producer that carries out the extraction; or

         V - the service supplier, even if resident or domiciled abroad, in the case referred to in item VII of § 1º of art. 409 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 425. The following are obligated to pay the Selective Tax as responsible parties, without prejudice to the other cases provided for in law and to the application of the penalty of
  forfeiture:

         I - the carrier, in relation to taxed products that it transports unaccompanied by tax documentation proving their origin;

       II - the possessor or holder, in relation to taxed products that it possesses or keeps for sale or industrialization purposes, unaccompanied by the
  tax documentation proving their origin;
        III - the owner, the possessor, the carrier, or any other holder of domestic products that left the manufacturer with immunity for export,
  found in the Country in a different situation, except when the products are in transit:

        a) intended for use or consumption on board, in vessels or aircraft on international routes, with payment in convertible currency;

        b) intended for duty-free shops, in a direct sale transaction, under the terms and conditions established by art. 15 of Decree-Law No. 1,455, of April 7, 1976;

        c) acquired by the export trading company referred to in art. 82 of this Complementary Law, for the specific purpose of export, and sent directly
  from the industrial establishment for export shipment or to bonded facilities, on behalf and by order of the acquirer; or

        d) sent to bonded facilities or to other locations where export customs clearance is processed.

       Sole paragraph. If the manufacturer has in any way contributed to the case provided for in item III of the caput, it shall be jointly and severally liable for
  payment of the tax.

                                                                                     CHAPTER VI

                                                                    OF THE EXPORT TRADING COMPANY

        Art. 426. The Selective Tax does not apply to the supply of goods for the specific purpose of export to an export trading company that meets the requirements
  in the caput and in §§ 1º and 2º of art. 82 of this Complementary Law.

       Art. 427. The export trading company is responsible for the payment of the Selective Tax that was not paid on the supply of goods to the
  export trading company, in the cases referred to in § 5º of art. 82 of this Complementary Law.

       § 1º For the purposes of the provisions of the caput, the Selective Tax is deemed due on the date of occurrence of the taxable event, as defined in art. 412 of this
  Complementary Law.

        § 2º Amounts that are not paid shall be subject to penalty and default interest under the terms of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3º The provisions of § 10 of art. 82 of this Complementary Law apply to the Selective Tax.

                                                                                    CHAPTER VII

                                                                             OF THE PENALTY OF FORFEITURE

        Art. 428. Without prejudice to the other legal cases, the penalty of forfeiture applies in cases of transport, storage, or display for sale of the
  tobacco products listed in Annex XVII unaccompanied by tax documentation proving their origin.

        § 1º The application of the penalty of forfeiture referred to in the caput of this article does not prejudice the collection of the Selective Tax due.

        § 2º In the case of the caput of this article, if the goods are being transported, the penalty of forfeiture also applies to the vehicle used, if the circumstances
  show that the owner of the vehicle, its possessor, or its agents, through action or omission, contributed to the commission of the unlawful act, facilitated its occurrence,
  or benefited from it.

        § 3º For purposes of the provisions of § 2º:

        I - omission by the owner of the vehicle, its possessor, or its agents is deemed to occur when there is failure to require appropriate documentation in situations where the
  characteristics, volume, or quantity of goods transported on behalf and by order of the contracting party or passenger allow inference of the unlawful practice;

         II - contribution by the owner of the vehicle, its possessor, or its agents to the unlawful practice is presumed in situations where adaptation of the
  vehicle structure aimed at concealing the transported goods is found;

        III - ownership of the vehicle and the value of the transported goods are irrelevant; and

        IV - it is incumbent upon vehicle rental companies to take precautions regarding the background of lessees or authorized drivers, under penalty of presumption of their collaboration
  in the unlawful practice.

        Art. 429. Except in the case of export, treated tobacco leaves, wholly or partially de-stemmed, trimmed or not, even if cut into regular shapes
  or shredded, shall only be sold or sent to a company that processes cigars, cigarettes, cigarillos, or shredded, cut, crumbled, or powdered tobacco, in rolls
  or in rope form.

        § 1º The commercialization of the products referred to in the caput of this article between establishments engaged in the activity of processing and
  packaging by baling is permitted.

        § 2º The Federal Executive Branch shall require, for the transactions referred to in this article, the necessary means of control.

        § 3º Goods found in transport, storage, or display for sale in disagreement with the determination of the caput are subject to the penalty provided in art. 428
  of this Complementary Law.

        § 4º (VETOED).

                                                                                    CHAPTER VIII

                                                                                    OF ASSESSMENT

        Art. 430. The assessment period for the Selective Tax shall be monthly and the regulation shall establish:

        I - the deadline for completion of the assessment; and

        II - the due date.

        Art. 431. The assessment relating to the Selective Tax shall consolidate the operations carried out by all establishments of the taxpayer.

                                                                                     CHAPTER IX

                                                                                   OF PAYMENT

        Art. 432. The Selective Tax shall be paid by collection of the amount due by the taxable person.

        Art. 433. Payment of the Selective Tax shall be centralized at a single establishment and, in the manner provided in its regulation, may occur upon the financial
  settlement of the operation (split payment), observing the provisions of arts. 31 to 35 of this Complementary Law.

                                                                                       TITLE III


                                                               OF THE SELECTIVE TAX ON IMPORTS

        Art. 434. The following applies to the Selective Tax, on the import of material goods:

        I - art. 65 of this Complementary Law, in relation to the taxable event;

        II - art. 66 and item III of art. 413 of this Complementary Law, in relation to non-incidence;

        III - art. 67 of this Complementary Law, in relation to the moment of occurrence of the taxable event; and

        IV - arts. 72, 73 and 74 of this Complementary Law, in relation to tax liability.

        § 1º The rates of the Selective Tax levied on imports shall be set by ordinary law.

        § 2º If the rate of the Selective Tax is ad valorem, its tax base, on import, shall be the customs value plus the amount of the Import
  Tax.

         § 2º-A. In the case of import of tobacco products subject to the ad valorem rate of the Selective Tax, the tax base shall be the greater between that provided
  in item "c" of item III of art. 414 and that provided in § 2º of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3º The Selective Tax, on import, must be paid upon registration of the import declaration.

          § 4º Payment of the Selective Tax levied on the import of material goods is suspended when admitted under the regimes referred to in Chapters I
  and II of Title II of Book I, observing the discipline established in customs legislation.

        § 5º In the case of duty-free shops, the suspension referred to in § 4º of this article covers goods imported and goods acquired in the domestic market.

        § 6º In the case of goods temporarily admitted into the Country for economic use, the suspension of payment of the Selective Tax shall be partial, and shall be
  paid proportionally to the length of stay of the goods in the Country, under the terms of art. 89 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 435. Exempt from payment of the Selective Tax on the import of material goods are:

        I - baggage of travelers and crew members, accompanied or unaccompanied, when subject to the special taxation regime; and

        II - international shipments, when subject to the simplified taxation regime.

                                                                                     TITLE IV

                                                                              FINAL PROVISIONS

        Art. 436. The specific rates referred to in this Book shall be updated by the IPCA once a year, under the terms of ordinary law.

        Art. 437. The RFB may establish an electronic communication system to be assigned as DTE, which shall be used for purposes of notification, summons, or
  notices provided for in the legislation of the Selective Tax.

        Art. 438. The regulation of the Selective Tax dealt with in this Book shall be issued by the head of the Federal Executive Branch.

                                                                                     BOOK III

                                                                           OF THE OTHER PROVISIONS

                                                                                     TITLE I

                 OF THE MANAUS FREE TRADE ZONE, THE FREE TRADE AREAS AND THE REFUND OF THE IBS AND THE CBS TO FOREIGN TOURISTS

                                                                                    CHAPTER I

                                                                         OF THE MANAUS FREE TRADE ZONE

        Art. 439. The benefits relating to the Manaus Free Trade Zone established in this Chapter apply until the date established by art. 92-A of the ADCT.

        Art. 440. For purposes of this Chapter, the following are considered:

        I - Manaus Free Trade Zone the area defined and demarcated by specific legislation;

          II - incentivized industry a legal entity that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS and authorized in the manner of art. 442 of this Complementary Law to enjoy
  tax benefits in the industrialization of goods in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, except those referred to in art. 441 of this Complementary Law;

        II - incentivized industry a legal entity that is a taxpayer of the IBS and the CBS and authorized in the manner of item II of art. 442 of this Complementary Law
  to enjoy tax benefits in the industrialization of goods in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, except those referred to in art. 441 of this Complementary Law; (Wording given
  by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - intermediate good:

        a) the industrialized product intended for incorporation or consumption in the industrialization process of other goods, provided the immediate recipient is an
  industrial establishment;

        b) the product intended for packaging by industrial establishments;

        IV - final good, that on which no further value is added in the production process and that is intended for consumption.

       Sole paragraph. For purposes of this Chapter, in all operations between related parties the provisions of § 4º of art. 12 of this Complementary
  Law shall be observed.

        Art. 441. Not covered by the favored regime of the Manaus Free Trade Zone are:

        a) weapons and ammunition;

        b) tobacco and its derivatives;

        c) alcoholic beverages;

        d) passenger automobiles;



         e) petroleum, lubricants and liquid and gaseous fuels derived from petroleum, except for the petroleum refining industry located in the Manaus Free Trade
  Zone, exclusively in relation to internal shipments to that incentivized area, provided the basic production process is complied with, the prohibition remaining
  in place for all other stages; and

        f) perfumery or toiletry products, cosmetic preparations and preparations, except with respect to these (headings 3303 to 3307 of the Mercosul Common
  Nomenclature), if intended exclusively for internal consumption in the Manaus Free Trade Zone or if produced using raw materials of regional fauna and flora,
  in accordance with the basic production process.

        Art. 442. Under terms defined in regulation, it is a condition for qualification for the tax incentives of the Manaus Free Trade Zone:

         I - the specific registration in the registry of the Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus - Suframa, for the legal entity that carries out commercial activity
  or the supply of services; and

        I - the specific registration in the registry of the Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (Suframa), for the legal entity that carries out commercial
  activity or the supply of services or industrial activity not covered by the provision of item II of this article; and (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        II - the specific registration and approval of a technical-economic project by the Administrative Council of Suframa, based on the respective basic
  production processes, for a legal entity that carries out industrial activity.

        II - the specific registration and approval of a technical-economic project by the Administrative Council of Suframa, based on the respective basic
  production processes, for a legal entity that carries out incentivized industrial activity. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Sole paragraph. In the process of approving the projects and the basic production processes referred to in this article, the State of
  Amazonas and the Municipality of Manaus shall be heard.

       Art. 443. The levy of the IBS and the CBS on the importation of material goods carried out by incentivized industry for use in the Manaus Free Trade
  Zone is suspended.

        § 1º The suspension referred to in the caput does not apply to imports of:

        I - goods not covered by the favored regime of the Manaus Free Trade Zone provided for in art. 441 of this Complementary Law; and

         II - goods for personal use and consumption referred to in art. 57 of this Complementary Law, unless it is demonstrated that they are necessary for the
  development of the taxpayer's activity linked to the approved technical-economic project.

        § 2º The suspension referred to in the caput converts into exemption:

        I - when the imported goods are consumed or incorporated into the importer's production process in the Manaus Free Trade Zone;

         II - after the full depreciation of the good or its remaining in the fixed assets of the acquiring establishment for 48 (forty-eight) months, whichever
  occurs first.

        § 3º Should goods imported with the suspension referred to in the caput be sent outside the Manaus Free Trade Zone before the conversion into exemption
  referred to in § 2º of this article, the importer must collect the suspended taxes with the applicable legal additions, in the manner set forth in § 2º of art. 29 of this
  Complementary Law, with the appropriation and use of credits permitted in the manner of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law in relation to amounts actually paid,
  except in relation to the legal additions.

        Art. 444. A presumed credit of IBS relating to the importation of material goods for in-person resale in the Manaus Free Trade Zone is granted to the taxpayer qualified in the manner of art. 442 and subject to the regular regime or to the Simples Nacional. Effective as of a future date

         § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying a percentage corresponding to 50% (fifty percent) of the IBS
  rate applicable on the import.

        § 2º The presumed credit referred to in this article must be deducted from the amount of IBS due on the import.

         § 3º To the importer of the goods referred to in the caput subject to the regular IBS regime, the appropriation and use of the full IBS credits is guaranteed for the
  amount of the tax levied on the import, observing the rules set forth in arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        § 4º The importer must collect IBS corresponding to the amount of the presumed credit deducted from the amount due on the import, with the applicable legal additions,
  in the manner of § 2º of art. 29, from the date of import, if:

        I - the resale does not comply with the requirement set forth in the caput;

        II - the entry of the good into the establishment of destination in the Manaus Free Trade Zone is not proven within the time limits established in regulation; and

        II - the good is resold outside the Manaus Free Trade Zone or transferred outside the Manaus Free Trade Zone.

        § 5º (VETOED).

         Art. 445. The IBS and CBS rates levied on transactions originating outside the Manaus Free Trade Zone that direct industrialized material goods
  of national origin to a taxpayer established in the Manaus Free Trade Zone are reduced to zero, where such taxpayer is:

        I - qualified under the terms of art. 442 of this Complementary Law; and

       II - subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS or an opting member of the Simples Nacional regime referred to in art. 12 of Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14,
  2006.

        § 1º The provision of the caput does not apply to transactions with goods referred to in § 1º of art. 443.

        § 2º The taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS that carries out the transactions referred to in the caput may appropriate and use the credits relating to
  preceding transactions, observing the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3º Specific controls must be instituted for verification of the entry into the Manaus Free Trade Zone of the material goods referred to in the caput, under the terms
  of the regulation.

         § 4º Should there be no proof that the goods destined for the Manaus Free Trade Zone entered their destination, within the time limits established in regulation, the
  taxpayer must collect the amount of IBS and CBS that would be due had there been no reduction of rates to zero, with the applicable legal additions, in the manner
  of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

        § 5º The provision of the caput also applies to transactions with intermediate material goods submitted to industrialization by order.

        Art. 446. The IBS will be levied on the entry, into the state of Amazonas, of material goods that had been covered by the reduction of rates to zero under the
  terms of art. 445 of this Complementary Law, except where destined for incentivized industry for use in the Manaus Free Trade Zone. Effective as of a future date


        § 1º In the case referred to in the caput:

        I - the IBS taxpayer will be the recipient of the transaction referred to in the caput of art. 445 of this Complementary Law;

        II - the tax base will be the value of the transaction referred to in the caput of art. 445 of this Complementary Law;

       III - the IBS will be charged by applying a rate corresponding to 70% (seventy percent) of the rate that would be levied on the respective transaction had there
  been no reduction to zero established by art. 445 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The amount of IBS paid in the manner of item III of § 1º will allow the taxpayer to appropriate and use the tax credit, in the manner of arts. 47 to 56
  of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 447. A presumed credit of IBS relating to the acquisition of industrialized material goods of national origin covered by the reduction to zero of the IBS
  rate under the terms of art. 445 of this Complementary Law is granted to the taxpayer subject to the regular IBS regime and qualified under the terms of art. 442 of this Complementary Law. Effective as of a future date

        § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the following percentages on the value of the transaction covered by the
  reduction to zero of the IBS rate under the terms of art. 445 of this Complementary Law:

        I - 7.5% (seven whole and five tenths percent), in the case of goods originating from the South and Southeast regions, except from the State of Espírito Santo; and

        II - 13.5% (thirteen whole and five tenths percent), in the case of goods originating from the North, Northeast and Center-West regions and from the State of Espírito Santo.

        § 2º The presumed credit must be reversed if:

        I - the entry of the good into the establishment of destination in the Manaus Free Trade Zone is not proven within the time limits established in regulation, requiring
  the applicable legal additions under the terms of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law;

        II - the good is resold outside the ZFM or transferred outside the ZFM, with legal additions not required if the reversal is carried out in a timely manner.

       § 3º When goods submitted to industrialization by order return to the party that ordered them, the presumed credit referred to in the caput applies only
  to the value added in this industrialization process.

        Art. 448. The IBS and CBS rates levied on transactions carried out by incentivized industry that direct intermediate material goods to another incentivized
  industry in the Manaus Free Trade Zone are reduced to zero, provided that the delivery or making available of the goods occurs within said area.

        § 1º The provision of the caput does not apply to transactions with goods referred to in § 1º of art. 443 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The appropriation and use of the credits relating to preceding transactions is assured to the taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS that carries out
  the transactions referred to in the caput, under the terms of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         § 3º The provision of the caput also applies to transactions with intermediate material goods submitted to industrialization by order, in relation to the value
  added in the industrialization.

         Art. 449. A presumed credit of IBS relating to the acquisition of intermediate goods produced in said area is granted to incentivized industry in the Manaus Free Trade
  Zone, subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, provided that the good is covered by the reduction to zero of the rate established by art. 448 of this Complementary
  Law and is used for incorporation or consumption in the production of final goods. Effective as of a future date

        § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the percentage of 7.5% (seven whole and five tenths percent) on the value
  of the transaction covered by the reduction to zero of the IBS rate established by art. 448 of this Complementary Law.

       § 2º At the moment goods submitted to industrialization by order return to the party that ordered them, the presumed credit referred to in the caput applies only
  to the value added in this industrialization process.

          Art. 450. Presumed credits of IBS and CBS relating to transactions that direct to the national territory, including to the Manaus Free Trade Zone itself,
  material goods produced by the incentivized industry itself in said area under the terms of the approved economic project, except in relation to the transactions provided for
  in art. 447 of this Complementary Law, are granted to incentivized industry in the Manaus Free Trade Zone.        Effective as of a future date

          Art. 450. Presumed credits of IBS and CBS relating to transactions that direct to the national territory, including to the Manaus Free Trade Zone itself,
  material goods produced by the incentivized industry itself in said area under the terms of the approved economic project, except in relation to the transactions provided for
  in art. 448 of this Complementary Law, are granted to incentivized industry in the Manaus Free Trade Zone.       (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        § 1º The presumed credit of IBS referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the following percentages on the debit balance of IBS in the assessment
  period:    Effective as of a future date

        I - 55% (fifty-five percent) for final consumption goods;

        II - 75% (seventy-five percent) for capital goods;

        III - 90.25% (ninety whole and twenty-five hundredths percent) for intermediate goods; and

         IV - 100% (one hundred percent) for information technology goods and for products for which the legislation of the State of Amazonas, until December
  31, 2023, established an ICMS incentive credit at this percentage.

       § 2º The presumed credit of CBS referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the following percentages on the value of the transaction recorded on
  a valid tax document:  Effective as of a future date

        I - 6% (six percent) on the sale of products, under the terms of art. 454 of this Complementary Law; or

        II - 2% (two percent) in other cases.

        § 3º The provision of the caput does not apply to transactions:      Effective as of a future date

        I - not subject to levy or covered by cases of exemption, zero rate, suspension or deferral of the IBS and the CBS; and

        II - with goods not covered by the favored regime of the Manaus Free Trade Zone, provided for in art. 441 of this Complementary Law.

         § 4º To acquirers of the goods referred to in the caput subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, the full appropriation and use of the credits
  relating to the IBS and the CBS is guaranteed for the value of said taxes levied on the transaction and recorded on a valid tax document, observing the rules provided for in the
  arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law. Effective as of a future date

        § 5º In the case of sales to the Union in which the IBS rates are subject to the reduction referred to in item "a" of item I of § 1º of art. 473, the presumed
  credit of IBS referred to in § 1º of this article may be appropriated, considering, exclusively for purposes of calculating said presumed credit, the
  assessment of the debit balance of IBS based on the rates that would be applicable to the transaction had there been no reduction to zero. Effective as of a future date
        § 6º The application of the presumed credit of IBS referred to in § 1º of this article will observe the following:        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - the debit balance of the IBS, for each incentive percentage, is considered to be the balance assessed under the terms of the caput and of § 1º of art. 45 of this
  Complementary Law, excluding the presumed credit referred to in § 1º of this article; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         II - the incentive percentages will be applied to each IBS debit to reduce the amounts to be collected or paid under the extinction modes
  provided for in items III to V of the caput of art. 27 of this Complementary Law, with the appropriation of the credit assured;     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

       III - after the assessment of the debit balance of IBS referred to in item I of this paragraph, the presumed credit referred to in § 1º of this article will be deducted and,
  next, the deductions referred to in § 3º of art. 45 of this Complementary Law; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         IV - without prejudice to the other transfers provided for in this Complementary Law, in the event of a recoverable balance, assessed under the terms of § 3º
  of art. 45, the amounts of debits extinguished by the modes provided for in items III to V of the caput of art. 27 in the assessment period will be transferred to the incentivized
  industry, up to the limit of said recoverable balance, within up to 3 (three) business days counted from the date of completion of the assessment. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

        Art. 451. The CBS rates levied on transactions carried out by legal entities established in the Manaus Free Trade
  Zone with material goods of national origin or with services rendered in person, when directed to a natural or legal person located within said
  area, are reduced to zero.

        Sole paragraph. The taxpayer that carries out the transactions referred to in the caput may appropriate and use the credits relating to preceding transactions,
  observing the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

       Art. 452. The presumed credits of IBS and CBS established by arts. 444, 447, 449 and 450 of this Complementary Law may only be used for
  offset, respectively, against the amount of IBS and CBS owed by the taxpayer, with offset against other taxes and cash reimbursement prohibited.

       Sole paragraph. The right to use the presumed credits referred to in the caput extinguishes after 5 (five) years, counted from the first day of the month
  following that in which their appropriation occurs.

        Art. 453. Transactions with goods and services occurring within the Manaus Free Trade Zone or directed to said area, including imports, that are not
  covered by the provisions of arts. 443, 445, 446 and 448 of this Complementary Law are subject to the levy of the IBS and the CBS based on the other rules provided for
  in this Complementary Law.

       Art. 454. As of January 1, 2027, the IPI rates are reduced to zero for products subject to a rate lower than 6.5% (six whole and five
  tenths percent) provided for in the Table of Incidence of the Tax on Industrialized Products - Tipi in force on December 31, 2023, and that have:

        I - been industrialized in the Manaus Free Trade Zone in the year 2024; or

        II - a technical-economic project approved by the Administrative Council of Suframa (CAS) between January 1, 2022 and the date of publication of this Law.

        § 1º The following products will be benefited by a presumed CBS credit, under the terms of item I of § 2º of art. 450 of this Complementary Law:

        I - those referred to in the caput of this article; or

        II - (VETOED).

       § 2º The reduction to zero of the rates referred to in the caput of this article does not reach products classified as information and
  communication technology goods, in accordance with the regulation of art. 16-A of Law No. 8,248, of October 23, 1991.

         § 3º The Executive Branch of the Union will disclose the list of products whose IPI rate has been reduced to zero under the terms of this article and of art. 126, item III,
  subitem "a", of the ADCT.

        Art. 455. In relation to goods without a national equivalent whose production is to be installed in the Manaus Free Trade Zone:

         I - the presumed CBS credit referred to in art. 450 of this Complementary Law will be calculated by applying the percentage established by item I of §
  2º of said article; or

        II - the IPI rate will be at least 6.5% (six whole and five tenths percent), and the head of the Executive Branch of the Union may increase it or
  reinstate it, subject to the following conditions:

        a) the rate increase will be at most thirty percentage points;

        b) the rate resulting from reinstatement may not be lower than that provided for in item II of the caput of this article;

        c) the reduction or reinstatement may not be effected before 60 (sixty) months have elapsed from the setting or increase of the IPI rate;

        d) the reduction must be made gradually, limited to at most five percentage points per year.

         § 1º In the case of goods with a national equivalent whose production is to be installed in the Manaus Free Trade Zone, the tax incentives referred to
  in this Law are assured, except those provided for in items I and II of the caput of this article.

         § 2º The conditions provided for in item II of the caput and its subitems apply to products industrialized in the Manaus Free Trade Zone that have a positive
  IPI rate.

         Art. 456. The reduction in IBS and CBS revenue resulting from the benefits provided for in this Chapter, including as a result of the presumed credits
  provided for in arts. 444, 447, 449 and 450 of this Complementary Law, must be taken into account for the setting of the reference rates.

         Art. 457. The State of Amazonas may institute a matching contribution similar to those existing on December 31, 2023, provided that it is
  destined for financing higher education, promoting micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the interiorization of development, in accordance with the provision of the caput
  of art. 92-B of the ADCT of the Federal Constitution, observing that:

        I - the percentage of the matching contribution provided for in the caput will be 1.5% (one and a half percent), calculated on the revenue of incentivized industries;

        II - the matching contribution referred to in the caput will be charged as of the year 2033, when the transition provided for in arts. 124 to 133 of the Act of
  Transitional Constitutional Provisions ends;

       III - in the year 2033, the collection of the matching contribution provided for in the caput will be equivalent to 10% (ten percent) of the percentage provided for in item I, with the
  remaining 90% (ninety percent) being borne by the recomposition provided for in art. 131, § 1º, II of the Act of Transitional Constitutional
  Provisions;

         IV - from 2034 to 2073, the percentage of the matching contribution collection provided for in the caput will be increased at the rate of 1/45 (one forty-fifth) per year in
  addition to the percentage applied in the year 2033, with the remainder being borne by the recomposition provided for in art. 131, § 1º, III of the Act of Transitional Constitutional
  Provisions.

                                                                                   CHAPTER II
                                                                     ON FREE TRADE AREAS

        Art. 458. The benefits relating to the Free Trade Areas established in this Chapter apply until the date established by art. 92-A of the ADCT.

        Art. 459. For purposes of the provisions of this Complementary Law, the following free trade areas are covered by a favored regime:

        I - Tabatinga, in Amazonas, created by Law No. 7,965, of December 22, 1989;

        II - Guajará-Mirim, in Rondônia, created by Law No. 8,210, of July 19, 1991;

        III - Boa Vista and Bonfim, in Roraima, created by Law No. 8,256, of November 25, 1991;

        IV - Macapá and Santana, in Amapá, created by art. 11 of Law No. 8,387, of December 30, 1991; and

        V - Brasiléia, extending to Epitaciolândia, and Cruzeiro do Sul, in Acre, created by Law No. 8,857, of March 8, 1994.

        Art. 460. Under terms defined in regulation, it is a condition for qualification for the tax incentives of the Free Trade Areas:

         I - the specific registration in the registry of the Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus - Suframa, for the legal entity that carries out commercial activity
  or the supply of services; and

        I - the specific registration in the registry of the Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (Suframa), for the legal entity that carries out commercial
  activity or the supply of services or industrial activity not covered by the provision of item II of this article; and (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

         II - the specific registration and approval of a technical-economic project by the Administrative Council of Suframa for the development of an industrialization
  activity of products whose final composition predominantly consists of raw materials of regional origin, originating from the animal, vegetable,
  mineral segments, except for the ores of Chapter 26 of the NCM/SH, or agro-silvo-pastoral, subject to applicable environmental legislation.

         II - the specific registration and approval of a technical-economic project by the Administrative Council of Suframa for the development of an industrialization
  activity of products whose final composition predominantly consists of raw materials of regional origin, originating from the animal, vegetable,
  mineral segments, except for the ores of Chapter 26 of the NCM/SH, or agro-silvo-pastoral, subject to applicable environmental legislation, for a legal entity that carries out
  incentivized industrial activity. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 1º In the process of approving the projects referred to in this article, the Executive Branch of the State in which the Free Trade Area
  is located shall be heard.

         § 2º Suframa will regulate the criteria for characterizing the predominance of raw material of regional origin in the final composition of the product referred
  to in item II of the caput.

        Art. 461. The levy of the IBS and the CBS on the importation of material goods carried out by industry qualified in the manner of item II of the caput of art.
  460 of this Complementary Law and subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS for incorporation into its production process is suspended. Effective as of a future date

        § 1º The suspension referred to in the caput does not apply to imports of:

        I - goods referred to in art. 441 of this Complementary Law; and

         II - goods for personal use and consumption referred to in art. 57 of this Complementary Law, unless it is demonstrated that they are necessary for the
  development of the taxpayer's economic activity linked to the approved economic project.

        § 2º The suspension referred to in the caput converts into exemption:

        I - when the imported goods are consumed or incorporated into the importer's production process in the respective Free Trade Area;

         II - after the full depreciation of the good or its remaining in the fixed assets of the acquiring establishment for 48 (forty-eight) months, whichever
  occurs first.

         § 3º Should goods imported with the suspension referred to in the caput be sent outside the Free Trade Area before the conversion into exemption
  referred to in § 2º, the importer must collect the suspended taxes with the applicable legal additions, in the manner of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law, with
  the appropriation and use of credits permitted in the manner of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law in relation to amounts actually paid, except in relation to the
  applicable legal additions.

        Art. 462. A presumed credit of IBS relating to the importation of material goods for in-person resale in the Free Trade Area is granted to the taxpayer qualified in the manner of art. 460 and subject to the regular regime or to the Simples Nacional. Effective as of a future date

         § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying a percentage corresponding to 50% (fifty percent) of the IBS
  rate applicable on the import.

        § 2º The presumed credit referred to in this article must be deducted from the amount of IBS due on the import.

         § 3º To the importer of the goods referred to in the caput subject to the regular IBS regime, the appropriation and use of the full IBS credits is guaranteed for the
  amount of the tax levied on the import, observing the rules set forth in arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        § 4º The importer must collect IBS corresponding to the amount of the presumed credit deducted from the amount due on the import, with the applicable legal additions,
  in the manner of § 2º of art. 29, from the date of import, if:

        I - the resale does not comply with the requirement set forth in the caput;

        II - the entry of the good into the establishment of destination in the Free Trade Area is not proven within the time limits established in regulation; and

        II - the good is resold outside the Free Trade Area or transferred outside the Free Trade Area.

        § 5º (VETOED).

         Art. 463. The IBS and CBS rates levied on transactions originating outside the free trade area that direct industrialized material goods
  of national origin to a taxpayer established in the free trade area are reduced to zero, where such taxpayer is:

        I - qualified under the terms of art. 460 of this Complementary Law; and

       II - subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS or an opting member of the Simples Nacional regime referred to in art. 12 of Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14,
  2006.

        § 1º The provision of the caput does not apply to transactions with goods referred to in § 1º of art. 461 of this Complementary Law.



        § 2º The taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS that carries out the transactions referred to in the caput may appropriate and use credits relating to
  preceding transactions, observing the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

        § 3º Specific controls must be instituted for verification of the entry into the Free Trade Areas of the goods referred to in the caput, under the terms of the
  regulation.

         § 4º Should there be no proof that the goods destined for the Free Trade Areas entered their destination, within the time limits established in regulation, the
  taxpayer must collect the amount of IBS and CBS that would be due had there been no reduction of rates to zero, with the applicable legal additions under the
  terms of § 2º of art. 29 of this Complementary Law.

        Art. 464. The IBS will be levied on the entry, into the state in which the free trade area is located, of material goods that had been covered by the
  reduction of rates to zero under the terms of art. 463 of this Complementary Law, except where destined for incentivized industry for use in the Free Trade
  Areas.

        § 1º In the case referred to in the caput:

        I - the IBS taxpayer will be the recipient of the transaction referred to in the caput of art. 463 of this Complementary Law;

        II - the tax base will be the value of the transaction referred to in the caput of art. 463 of this Complementary Law;

       III - the IBS will be charged by applying a rate corresponding to 70% (seventy percent) of the rate that would be levied on the respective transaction had there
  been no reduction to zero established by art. 463 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2º The amount of IBS paid in the manner of item III of § 1º will allow the taxpayer to appropriate and use the tax credit, in the manner of arts. 47 to 56
  of this Complementary Law.

        § 3º The amount of IBS paid in the manner of § 4º of art. 463 of this Complementary Law will allow the taxpayer to appropriate and use the tax credit in the
  manner of arts. 47 to 57 of this Complementary Law, except in relation to legal additions.

        Art. 465. A presumed credit of IBS relating to the acquisition of industrialized material goods of national origin covered by the reduction to zero of the IBS
  rate under the terms of art. 463 of this Complementary Law is granted to the taxpayer subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS and qualified in the manner of art. 460 of this
  Complementary Law.       Effective as of a future date
