        § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the following percentages on the value of the transaction covered by the
  reduction to zero of the IBS rate under the terms of art. 463 of this Complementary Law:

        I - 7.5% (seven whole and five tenths percent), in the case of goods originating from the South and Southeast regions, except from the State of Espírito Santo; and

        II - 13.5% (thirteen whole and five tenths percent), in the case of goods originating from the North, Northeast and Center-West regions and from the State of Espírito Santo.

        § 2º The presumed credit must be reversed if:

        I - the entry of the good into the establishment of destination in the Free Trade Area is not proven within the time limits established in regulation, requiring the
  applicable legal additions under the terms of § 2º of art. 29;

        II - the good is resold outside the Free Trade Area or transferred outside the Free Trade Area, with legal additions not required if the
  reversal is carried out in a timely manner.

       Art. 466. The CBS rates levied on transactions carried out by legal entities established in the Free Trade Area
  with material goods of national origin or services rendered in person, when directed to a natural or legal person located within said area, are reduced to zero.

        Sole paragraph. The taxpayer that carries out the transactions referred to in the caput may appropriate and use the credits relating to preceding transactions,
  observing the provisions of arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

         Art. 467. Presumed credits of CBS relating to transactions that direct to the national territory material goods produced by the industry itself in said area under
  the terms of the approved economic project are granted to industry subject to the regular regime of IBS and CBS and qualified in the manner of item II of the caput of art. 460 of this
  Complementary Law. Effective as of a future date            Effective as of a future date

       § 1º The presumed credit referred to in the caput will be calculated by applying the percentage of 6% (six percent) on the value of the transaction recorded on a
  valid tax document.

        § 2º The provision of the caput does not apply to transactions:

        I - not subject to levy or covered by cases of exemption, zero rate, suspension or deferral of the CBS;

        II - with goods referred to in art. 441 of this Complementary Law.

         § 3º To acquirers of the goods referred to in the caput, if subject to the regular regime of the IBS and the CBS, the full appropriation of the credits
  relating to the CBS is guaranteed for the amount levied on the transaction recorded on a valid tax document, observing the rules provided for in arts. 47 to 56 of this Complementary Law.

       Art. 468. The presumed credits of IBS and CBS established by arts. 462, 465 and 467 of this Complementary Law may only be used for
  offset, respectively, against amounts of IBS and CBS owed by the taxpayer, with offset against other taxes and cash reimbursement prohibited.

       Sole paragraph. The right to use the presumed credits referred to in the caput extinguishes after 5 (five) years, counted from the first day of the month
  following that in which their appropriation occurs.

        Art. 469. For purposes of this Chapter, in all transactions between related parties, the provision of § 4º of art. 12 of this Complementary Law will be observed.

         Art. 470. The reduction in IBS and CBS revenue resulting from the benefits provided for in this Section, including as a result of the presumed credits
  provided for in arts. 462, 465 and 467 of this Complementary Law, must be taken into account for the setting of the reference rates.

                                                                                 CHAPTER III

                                                      ON THE REFUND OF THE IBS AND THE CBS TO FOREIGN TOURISTS

                                                                                   BOOK III
                                                              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                        ON THE OTHER PROVISIONS

                                                                                   TITLE I

         ON THE MANAUS FREE TRADE ZONE, THE FREE TRADE AREAS, THE REFUND OF THE IBS AND THE CBS TO FOREIGN TOURISTS, THE
  NATIONAL TAX COMPLIANCE PROGRAM AND THE NON-TAX ADMINISTRATIVE PENALTIES RELATING TO THE COLLECTION
                                   OF TAXES IN FINANCIAL SETTLEMENT (SPLIT PAYMENT)
        Art. 471. A Joint Act of the Ministry of Finance and the IBS Management Committee may provide that the amount of the IBS and the CBS levied on the supply of
  material goods to a person domiciled or resident abroad, carried out in the Country during a stay of less than 90 (ninety) days, will be refunded to that person at the moment
  their departure from national territory occurs.

          § 1º The refund of the IBS and the CBS referred to in the caput will observe the following:

         I - it will apply only to goods acquired that are part of accompanied baggage, during the period of stay of the resident or person domiciled
  abroad, supplied by qualified taxpayers;

          II - it will apply only to departures by air or sea;

      III - physical proof may be requested that the good subject to the tax refund is included in the baggage of the person domiciled or resident abroad at the
  moment of their departure from national territory; and

          IV - a portion may be deducted from the refund amount for payment of the administrative costs related to the benefit referred to in this article.

          § 2º The Ministry of Finance and the IBS Management Committee will regulate the provisions of this article, including in relation to:

          I - other conditions to be observed for requesting the refund referred to in this article;

          II - the manner of qualification of IBS and CBS taxpayers referred to in item I of § 1º;

          III - the exchange rate applicable for purposes of the provision of item IV of this paragraph;

          IV - the limit of the refund, which may not be lower than US$ 1,000.00 (one thousand US dollars);

          V - the refund, which will have as a parameter the total value of goods acquired per person.

                                                                                     CHAPTER IV
                                                                  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                         ON THE NATIONAL TAX COMPLIANCE PROGRAM

         Art. 471-A. The National Tax Compliance Program (PNCT) is instituted, intended to integrate the tax compliance regimes of the IBS and the
  CBS, with a view to promoting legal certainty, predictability, transparency and the improvement of the relationship between tax administrations and taxpayers.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1º Adherence to the PNCT will be voluntary and will depend on compliance with objective criteria provided for in regulation.             (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

        § 2º The PNCT will be regulated by a joint act of the CGIBS and the RFB, subject to the provisions of this Complementary Law.                   (Included by Complementary Law
  No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 471-B. The PNCT will have as objectives:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - to encourage tax regularity of taxpayers through guidance and prevention mechanisms;           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        II - to promote the self-regularization of tax obligations, allowing taxpayers to regularize their situation before assessment; and          (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - to establish differentiated treatment for taxpayers with a compliance history.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Art. 471-C. For participating taxpayers, the PNCT may provide for:        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - an extended period for compliance with ancillary obligations, as regulated;             (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         II - prioritization of the analysis of IBS and CBS refund requests, as defined in item I of § 3º of art. 39 of this Complementary Law;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         III - reduction of penalties for non-compliance with a principal or ancillary obligation, under the terms of § 1º of art. 341-H of this Complementary Law;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          IV - priority analysis of requests for rulings and tax guidance;   (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          V - reduction of documentary requirements and administrative procedures;          (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       VI - flexibility of the requirement to verify market value in transactions between related parties, under the terms of § 7º of art. 5º of this Complementary
  Law; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          VII - other incentives established in the regulation referred to in § 2º of art. 471-A.       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          Sole paragraph. The provision of items II, III and V applies, in relation to the IBS and the CBS, exclusively within the scope of the PNCT."                    (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                                                                                     CHAPTER V
                                                                  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          ON THE NON-TAX ADMINISTRATIVE PENALTIES RELATING TO THE COLLECTION OF TAXES IN FINANCIAL SETTLEMENT (SPLIT
                                                              PAYMENT)

        Art. 471-D. The electronic payment service provider and the operating institution of payment systems are subject to the following non-tax
  administrative penalties relating to the execution and control of the collection of the IBS and the CBS in financial settlement (split payment): (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        I - failing to segregate or segregating in disagreement with the legislation the amounts relating to the IBS and the CBS: 0.1 (one tenth) of UPF per transaction;              (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - failing to collect or collecting late, or in a smaller amount, the segregated amounts of IBS and CBS: a late-payment fine corresponding to the application of 3% (three
  percent) per month or fraction thereof on the amount not collected, collected late or collected in a smaller amount; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       III - communicating late or in disagreement with the legislation the information relating to segregation and collection carried out: 0.001 (one thousandth) of
  UPF per transaction, per day or fraction of a day of delay. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)



        § 1º The liability of the payment service provider and the operating institution of payment systems is excluded when the infraction was
  caused by information not provided or provided incorrectly by the supplier, the acquirer, the digital platform or another person or
  entity without legal personality that receives the payment, under the terms of § 2º of art. 32 of this Complementary Law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

        § 2º The fines provided for in this article will be increased by late-payment interest equivalent to the Selic rate, accumulated monthly, calculated from the first
  day of the month following that of the occurrence of the infraction, until the month prior to that of payment, and by 1% (one percent) in the month of payment. (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 3º A joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS will establish, for each of the penalties referred to in items I and III of the caput of this article, a tolerance
  limit for the percentage of nonconforming transactions each month, which may not be lower than 0.01% (one hundredth of one percent) nor higher than:
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - 1% (one percent) in the first 24 (twenty-four) months counted from January 1, 2027; and         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

          II - 0.5% (five tenths of one percent) after the period referred to in item I of this paragraph.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 4º The penalties referred to in items I and III of the caput of this article will be reduced by 100% (one hundred percent) if the percentage of
  nonconforming transactions is lower than the tolerance limit defined by the joint act referred to in § 3º of this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       Art. 471-E. The repeated practice of the infractions referred to in art. 471-D constitutes a violation of the rules regulating the financial and
  payment system and gives rise to the application of penalties by the competent regulatory body, without prejudice to the fines referred to in art. 471-D. (Included
  by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 1º For purposes of the provision of this article, the following characterize repeated practice of infractions:     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       I - non-compliance with the provisions of items I, II or III of the caput of art. 471-D in relation to 10% (ten percent) or more of the total number of transactions
  in the month, in 2 (two) successive or alternating months, in each 12 (twelve)-month period; or (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        II - non-compliance with the provisions of items I or II of the caput of art. 471-D in relation to 10% (ten percent) or more of the total value of the transactions in the month,
  in 2 (two) successive or alternating months, in each 12 (twelve)-month period. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 2º In the case of this article:    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - the regulatory body referred to in the caput may apply the following penalties:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) temporary suspension of authorization to provide financial or payment services;           (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) revocation of the authorization to operate;        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - the CGIBS and the RFB may, by joint act:       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          a) declare the CNPJ registration inapt; or      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          b) suspend the CNPJ.      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        Art. 471-F. The payment service provider or the operating institution of the payment system may challenge the penalty applied, within a period of
  up to 20 (twenty) business days, counted from notification of the infraction, in a petition addressed to the RFB, in relation to the CBS, and to the CGIBS, in relation to the
  IBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         § 1º From the decision of the reviewing body referred to in the caput of this article, a hierarchical appeal may be filed a single time, within a period of 10 (ten) business
  days, counted from notice of the appealed decision, to the hierarchical authority immediately above, which will decide definitively. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2º In the event the appeal is considered unfounded, the payment service provider or the operating institution of the payment system
  has a period of up to 20 (twenty) business days, counted from the decision, to make payment of the fines provided for in art. 471-D. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

                                                                                      TITLE II

                                                                        ON GOVERNMENT PURCHASES

        Art. 472. In acquisitions of goods and services by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations, the IBS and CBS rates will be
  reduced, uniformly, in proportion to the reducer set:

        Art. 472. In acquisitions of goods and services by a legal entity governed by internal public law, the IBS and CBS rates will be reduced, uniformly,
  in proportion to the reducer set: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          I - from 2027 to 2033, under the terms of art. 370 of this Complementary Law; and

          II - as of 2034, at the level set for 2033.

          Sole paragraph. The provision of this article does not apply to acquisitions that, cumulatively, are made in person and are exempt from
  competitive bidding, under the terms of specific legislation.

          Sole paragraph. The provision of this article does not apply in the following cases:         (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - acquisitions that, cumulatively, are made in person and are exempt from competitive bidding, under the terms of specific legislation;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         II - acquisitions subject to the nationally uniform rates referred to in arts. 174, 175, 189, 212, 236, 237, 243, 246, items II and III of § 4º of
  art. 293, items II and III of the caput of art. 294, items I and II of the caput of art. 485, § 1º of art. 486 and § 2º of art. 487, all of this Complementary Law; or (Included by the
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       III - acquisitions subject to the regimes of the Simples Nacional or the Individual Micro-Entrepreneur (MEI), referred to in Complementary Law No. 123, of December 14,
  2006. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         Art. 473. The proceeds from the collection of the IBS and the CBS on acquisitions of goods and services by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public
  foundations will be fully allocated to the contracting federative entity, by reducing to zero the IBS and CBS rates owed to the other federative entities and
  equivalently increasing the rate of the tax owed to the contracting entity.

          § 1º For purposes of compliance with the provision of the caput of this article:

          I - in acquisitions by the Union:


          a) the IBS rates of the other federative entities will be reduced to zero; and

         b) the CBS rate will be set at an amount equivalent to the sum of the IBS and CBS rates levied on the transaction, after the reduction referred to in
  art. 472 of this Complementary Law;

          II - in acquisitions by a State:

          a) the CBS rate and the municipal IBS rate will be reduced to zero; and

         b) the state IBS rate will be set at an amount equivalent to the sum of the IBS and CBS rates levied on the transaction, after the reduction referred to
  in art. 472 of this Complementary Law;

          III - in acquisitions by a Municipality:

          a) the CBS rate and the state IBS rate will be reduced to zero;

         b) the municipal IBS rate will be set at an amount equivalent to the sum of the IBS and CBS rates levied on the transaction, after the reduction
  referred to in art. 472 of this Complementary Law; and

          IV - in acquisitions by the Federal District:

          a) the CBS rate will be reduced to zero;

         b) the district IBS rate will be set at an amount equivalent to the sum of the IBS and CBS rates levied on the transaction, after the reduction referred to
  in art. 472 of this Complementary Law.

          § 2º The provision of the caput and of § 1º of this article does not apply to acquisitions that, cumulatively, are made in person and are exempt
  from competitive bidding, under the terms of specific legislation.

        § 3º The provision of this article applies to imports made by the direct public administration, by autarchies and by public foundations, ensuring
  equal treatment in relation to acquisitions within the Country.

          § 4º In acquisitions made by a public consortium with legal personality under public law:      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         I - the rates will be set in the manner of § 1º of this article, treating the acquisition as equivalent to one made by the Municipality of the consortium's seat;
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

         II - the proceeds from the collection of the IBS and the CBS will be fully allocated to the federative entities that are members of the public consortium, in proportion to
  their participation in the financing of the acquisition made; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - the tax document will be issued in the name of the public consortium.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 5º Subject to the criteria established in a joint act of the CGIBS and the RFB, for purposes of the provision of item II of § 4º of this article, the public
  consortium must inform the CGIBS and, where applicable, the RFB of the proportion of each federative entity's participation in the financing of the acquisition made. (Included by
  Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 6º For purposes of the provision of this article, the treatment given to public consortiums applies to the CGIBS.         (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

                                                                                         TITLE III

                                                                             TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

         Art. 474. During the period between 2027 and 2032, the percentages for the levy or crediting of IBS and CBS provided for in arts. 447, § 1º,
  449, § 1º, and 465, § 1º, of this Complementary Law will be reduced in the following proportions: Effective as of a future date

          I - 9/10 (nine tenths), in 2029;

          II - 8/10 (eight tenths), in 2030;

          III - 7/10 (seven tenths), in 2031; and

          IV - 6/10 (six tenths), in 2032.

                                                                                        CHAPTER I

                                                                              ON THE FIVE-YEAR REVIEW
       Art. 475. The Executive Branch of the Union and the IBS Management Committee shall carry out a five-year assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and
  results, as social, environmental and economic development policies, of:

        I - the application to the IBS and to the CBS of the special customs regimes, of the export processing zones and of the capital goods regimes of Reporto,
  of Reidi and of Renaval, dealt with in Title II of Book I;

          II - the personalized refund of the IBS and of the CBS, dealt with in Chapter I of Title III of Book I;

          III - the National Basic Food Basket, dealt with in Chapter II of Title III of Book I;

          IV - the differentiated regimes of the IBS and of the CBS, dealt with in Title IV of Book I; and

          V - the specific regimes of the IBS and of the CBS, dealt with in Title V of Book I.

        § 1 The assessment referred to in the caput must consider, including, the impact of the IBS and CBS legislation on the promotion of equality between men and
  women and ethnic-racial equality.

          § 2 For purposes of the provision in item II of the caput, the assessment referred to in the caput must consider the impact on income inequalities.

        § 3 For purposes of the provision in item III of the caput, the composition of the products that make up the National Basic Food Basket must have as its
  objective to guarantee healthy and nutritionally adequate food, in observance of the social right to food, and must satisfy the following criteria:

          I - to favor fresh or minimally processed foods; and

          II - to favor foods consumed mostly by low-income families.

          § 4 For purposes of the provision in § 3, the following are considered:
         I - fresh or minimally processed foods, those obtained directly from plants, animals or fungi and acquired for consumption without having
  undergone alterations after leaving nature or having been subjected to minimal processing without the addition of salt, sugar, fat and oils and other
  additives that modify the characteristics of the product, and substances of rare culinary use;

        II - foods consumed mostly by low-income families, those that present the highest ratios between:

        a) the share of spending on the respective food in the total food spending of low-income families; and

        b) the share of spending on the respective food in the total food spending of other families.

         § 5 For purposes of calculating the ratio referred to in item II of § 4, the information from the POF (Household Budget Survey) of the IBGE shall be used and,
  for the delimitation of low-income families, the reference shall be the limit of monthly per capita family income of up to half a minimum wage.

        § 6 For purposes of the provision in item IV of the caput, for purposes of the differentiated taxation regime, the definition of foods intended for human
  consumption must favor fresh or minimally processed foods, except those consumed mostly by high-income families.

        § 7 The Federal Audit Court (Tribunal de Contas da União) and the State and Municipal Audit Courts may, as a result of the exercise of their duties, offer
  input for the five-year assessment referred to in this article.

        § 7 The Federal Audit Court and the State, Federal District and Municipal Audit Courts, as a result of the exercise of
  their duties, and civil society, through its sectoral entities, may offer input for the five-year assessment referred to in this article.
  (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8 If the five-year assessment results in recommendations to revise the regimes and policies dealt with in the items of the caput, the Executive Branch of the
  Union must send to the National Congress a complementary bill proposing:

        I - changes in the scope and manner of application of the regimes and policies dealt with in the items of the caput; and

        II - a transition regime to the standard rate, in relation to the differentiated regimes referred to in item IV of the caput.

          § 9 The first five-year assessment shall be carried out based on the data available in the 2030 calendar year and may result in the submission of a
  complementary bill by the Executive Branch of the Union, taking effect starting in 2032, to be sent by the last business day of March 2031.

        § 10. In the five-year assessment referred to in § 9, the reference rates of the IBS and CBS to be applied from 2033 shall be estimated,
  taking into account the collection data of these taxes in relation to the years 2026 to 2030.

       § 10. In the five-year assessment referred to in § 9, the reference rates of the IBS and CBS in 2033 shall be estimated.               (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 11. If the sum of the estimated reference rates referred to in § 10 results in a percentage higher than 26.5% (twenty-six point five
  percent), the Executive Branch of the Union, having heard the IBS Management Committee, must send to the National Congress a complementary bill proposing measures
  to reduce the percentage to a level equal to or lower than 26.5% (twenty-six point five percent).

        § 12. The complementary bill referred to in § 11 must:

        I - be sent to the National Congress within 90 (ninety) days after the conclusion of the five-year assessment;

        II - be accompanied by the data and calculations that supported its submission; and

        III - change the scope and manner of application of the regimes and policies dealt with in the items of the caput.

        § 13. Subsequent assessments shall take place every 5 (five) years, counted from the deadlines set forth in § 9.

         Art. 476. The Executive Branch of the Union shall carry out a five-year assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and results, as a social, environmental and health
  policy, of the levy of the Selective Tax dealt with in Book II.

        § 1 The assessment referred to in this article shall be carried out simultaneously with the assessment referred to in art. 475 of this Complementary Law.

        § 2 The provision in art. 475 of this Complementary Law applies to the assessment referred to in this article, as applicable.

                                                                                  CHAPTER II

         ON THE COMPENSATION FOR ANY REDUCTION IN THE AMOUNT DELIVERED UNDER ART. 159, ITEMS I AND II, OF THE FEDERAL CONSTITUTION
                                      DUE TO THE REPLACEMENT OF THE IPI BY THE SELECTIVE TAX

          Art. 477. Starting in 2027, the Union shall compensate, in the manner set forth in this Title, any reduction in the amount of the amounts delivered under art. 159, items I and
  II, of the Federal Constitution, due to the replacement of IPI collection by Selective Tax collection, as provided in this Complementary Law.

        § 1 The compensation referred to in the caput shall be calculated monthly, starting in January 2027, by the difference between:

        I - the reference value for the month, calculated under the terms of art. 478 of this Complementary Law; and

        II - the amount delivered, in the month, as a result of the application of the provisions of items I and II of the caput of art. 159 of the Federal Constitution to the proceeds of the
  collection of the IPI and of the Selective Tax.

        § 2 The amount calculated under the terms of § 1:

        I - when negative, shall be deducted from the amount calculated under § 1 in the subsequent month;

        II - when positive, shall be delivered in the second month following the calculation, in the manner provided for in items I and II of the caput of art. 159 of the Federal
  Constitution.

         § 3 The amount referred to in item II of § 2 shall be delivered on the same dates set for the delivery of the funds referred to in items I and II of the caput of
  art. 159 of the Federal Constitution, observing its distribution in equal amounts for each of the installments delivered in the month.

        Art. 478. The reference value referred to in item I of § 1 of art. 477 of this Complementary Law shall be calculated as follows:

        I - for the months of January to December 2027, it shall correspond to the average monthly value for 2026, calculated under the terms of § 1 of this article, adjusted for the
  variation of the IPCA up to the month of calculation and increased by 2% (two percent);

       II - starting in January 2028, it shall be set at a value equivalent to the reference value of the twelfth prior month, adjusted for the 12-month (twelve)
  variation of the proceeds of CBS collection, calculated based on the reference rate.

         § 1 The average monthly value at 2026 prices corresponds to the sum of the amounts delivered from 2022 to 2026 as a result of the application of the provisions of items I
  and II of the caput of art. 159 of the Federal Constitution to the proceeds of IPI collection, adjusted to 2026 prices by the variation in IPI collection and divided
  by 60 (sixty).

        § 2 The adjustment for the IPCA variation referred to in item I of the caput shall be made based on:

        I - the IPCA index for the respective month of calculation; and

        II - the average IPCA index for 2026.

        § 3 The Federal Audit Court shall publish, by the last business day of the month following the calculation, the reference value referred to in the caput.

         Art. 479. The amount to be delivered as compensation referred to in art. 477 of this Complementary Law shall observe the same criteria, deadlines and guarantees
  applicable to the delivery of funds referred to in art. 159, items I and II, of the Federal Constitution.

        § 1 It is prohibited to earmark the compensation funds referred to in the caput to any agency, fund or expense, except:

        I - the performance of tax administration activities;

        II - the provision of guarantees for credit operations secured by anticipated revenue;

        III - the payment of debts owed to the Union and to provide it with guarantee or counter-guarantee;

        IV - the minimum percentages for health actions and services provided for in art. 198, § 2, of the Federal Constitution;

        V - the minimum percentages to be applied to the maintenance and development of education under art. 212 of the Federal Constitution; and

        VI - the portion earmarked for the maintenance and development of basic education and for the fair compensation of its professionals, under art.
  212-A of the Federal Constitution.

       § 2 It is prohibited to withhold or place any restriction on the delivery and use of the compensation funds referred to in the caput to the States, the Federal District and
  the Municipalities, under art. 160 of the Federal Constitution.

                                                                                 CHAPTER III

                                                                          ON THE IBS MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE

                                                                                    Section I

                                                                              General Provisions

         Art. 480. The Management Committee of the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS Management Committee, CGIBS) is hereby established, by December 31, 2025, a public entity with a technical and
  operational character under a special regime, with headquarters and jurisdiction in the Federal District, endowed with technical, administrative, budgetary and financial independence. Taking effect

        § 1 The CGIBS, under the terms of the Federal Constitution and of this Complementary Law, shall have its actions characterized by the absence of any binding, guardianship or
  hierarchical subordination to any public administration body.

        § 2 The single IBS regulation shall define the maximum time limit for carrying out administrative collection activities, provided it does not exceed 12 (twelve)
  months, counted from the definitive constitution of the tax credit, after which the tax administration shall forward the matter to the respective attorney's office, for the applicable
  judicial or extrajudicial collection measures, under the terms defined in said regulation.

         § 3 The CGIBS, the Special Secretariat of the Brazilian Federal Revenue Service and the Attorney General's Office of the National Treasury may implement integrated solutions for
  the future administration and collection of the IBS and CBS.

        § 4 The rules common to the IBS and CBS contained in the single IBS regulation shall be approved by joint act of the CGIBS and of the federal Executive Branch.

         § 5 The single IBS regulation shall provide for uniform rules on tax compliance, guidance, self-regularization and differentiated treatment for
  taxpayers who meet the IBS compliance programs established by the federative entities.

         § 6 The biddings and contracting carried out by the CGIBS shall be governed by the general rules on bidding and contracting applicable to the direct, autarchic
  and foundational public administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities.

         § 7 The CGIBS shall observe the principle of publicity, through the disclosure of its normative acts, preferably by electronic means, made available on the
  internet.

                                                                                    Section II

                                                                       On the CGIBS Superior Council

        Art. 481. The CGIBS Superior Council, the highest deliberative body of the CGIBS, has the following composition:           Taking effect

        I - 27 (twenty-seven) members and their respective alternates, representing each State and the Federal District; and

        II - 27 (twenty-seven) members and their respective alternates, representing the Municipalities and the Federal District as a whole.

        § 1 The members and their respective alternates referred to:

        I - in item I of the caput of this article shall be appointed by the Head of the Executive Branch of each State and of the Federal District; and

        II - in item II of the caput of this article shall be appointed by the Heads of the Executive Branches of the Municipalities and of the Federal District, as follows:

        a) 14 (fourteen) representatives elected based on the votes of each Municipality and of the Federal District, with equal weight for all; and

        b) 13 (thirteen) representatives elected based on the votes of each Municipality and of the Federal District, weighted by their respective populations.

          § 2 The selection of the representatives of the Municipalities on the CGIBS Superior Council, referred to in item II of the caput of this article, shall be carried out by
  holding separate elections to determine the members and respective alternates of each of the groups referred to in items "a" and "b" of item II of § 1 of this
  article.

        § 2 The selection of the representatives of the Municipalities on the CGIBS Superior Council, referred to in item II of the caput of this article, shall be carried out,
  exceptionally for purposes of the installation of the provisional CGIBS referred to in the caput of art. 480 of this Complementary Law, by appointment by the National
  Confederation of Municipalities (CNM) and by the National Front of Mayors (FNP). (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3 The election referred to in § 2 of this article: (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
        I - shall be carried out electronically, it being observed that only the sitting Head of the Municipal Executive Branch shall have the right to vote;


          II - shall guarantee the representation of at least 1 (one) Municipality from each region of the Country, and the Federal District may represent the Center-
  West Region;
        III - shall be governed by the democratic principle, guaranteeing the participation of all Municipalities, without prejudice to the observance of minimum requirements for
  candidacy, under the terms of this Complementary Law and of the electoral regulation;
        IV - shall be carried out through a single electoral process, organized by the nationwide municipal representation associations, recognized
  under Law No. 14,341, of May 18, 2022, whose members represent at least 30% (thirty percent) of the Country's population or 30% (thirty percent)
  of the Country's Municipalities, by means of their own electoral regulation drawn up jointly by the entities.

        § 3 (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 4 The Municipalities may only appoint, among the members referred to in item II of the caput of this article, 1 (one) single sitting or alternate
  member, including for the electoral process.

        § 4 The Municipalities may only appoint, among the members referred to in item II of the caput of this article, 1 (one) single sitting or
  alternate member. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 5 Each association, referred to in item IV of § 3, for the election provided for in § 2, in relation to the representatives referred to in item "a" of item II of § 1
  of this article, shall submit up to one slate, which must have the minimum support of 20% (twenty percent) of the total Municipalities of the Country, containing 14
  (fourteen) sitting names, observing the following:

        § 5 The CNM shall appoint the representatives referred to in item "a" of item II of § 1 of this article, and the FNP the representatives referred to in item "b" of item II
  of § 1 of this article, observing the following: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        I - the names appointed and the respective Municipalities shall make up a single slate, and may not appear on another slate;

        II - each sitting member shall have 2 (two) alternates, necessarily from distinct Municipalities and observing the provision in item I of this paragraph;

        III - in the event the sitting member is unable to act, the first alternate shall immediately replace him;

        IV - the slate that obtains more than 50% (fifty percent) of the valid votes shall win the election;

       V - if none of the slates reaches the percentage of votes indicated in item IV of this paragraph, a second round of voting shall be held with the 2 (two)
  most-voted slates, in which case the slate that obtains the majority of the valid votes shall be considered the winner.

        VI - the appointments of each entity shall be approved in advance by the highest deliberative body of the respective municipal representation
  association, with broad publicity, respecting the right of participation of non-member Municipalities. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 5-A. If one of the municipal representation associations fails to submit the appointments as provided for in § 5 of this article by October 31,
  2025, the other association may appoint the representatives in its place. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 6 Each association, referred to in item IV of § 3, for the election provided for in § 2, in relation to the representatives referred to in item "b" of item II of § 1
  of this article, shall submit up to one slate, which must have the support of Municipalities representing at least 20% (twenty percent) of the total
  population of the Country, containing 13 (thirteen) sitting names, observing the provisions of the items of § 5 of this article.         (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of
  2026)

        § 6 (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 7 The member elected under §§ 5 and 6 of this article may be: (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)
          I - replaced, in the manner defined by the CGIBS, by decision of the majority:
          a) of the votes of the Municipalities of the Country, when it concerns the representatives referred to in item "a" of item II of § 1 of this article; or
          b) of the votes of the Municipalities of the Country weighted by their respective populations, when it concerns the representatives referred to in item "b" of
  item II of § 1 of this article;
          II - removed by act of the Head of the Executive Branch of the Municipality that appointed him.

        § 7 (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 8 In the event of removal of the sitting member and the respective alternates, a new election shall be held to fill the respective vacancies, within the period provided
  for by the internal rules of the CGIBS. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 8 (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 9 Except in the first election, provided for in § 2 of this article, the other elections shall be monitored throughout the entire electoral process by 4 (four)
  members of the CGIBS Superior Council, chosen by the 27 (twenty-seven) representatives of the Municipalities referred to in item II of the caput of this article.
  (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 9 (Repealed).     (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 10. The electoral regulation may define other duties of the members referred to in § 9 of this article for monitoring the electoral process.
  (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 10. (Repealed).    (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 11. It is prohibited to appoint representatives of the same Municipality simultaneously to the group of 14 (fourteen) representatives referred to in item "a"
  of item II of § 1 of this article and to the group of 13 (thirteen) representatives referred to in item "b" of said item.

        § 12. The competent venue to resolve judicial actions related to the electoral processes referred to in this article is that of the judicial district of Brasília, in the Federal
  District.

         Art. 482. The members of the CGIBS Superior Council shall be chosen from among citizens of unblemished reputation and notorious knowledge of tax
  administration, observing the following: Taking effect

         I - the sitting representation of the States and of the Federal District shall be exercised by the holder of the office of Secretary of Finance, Treasury, Taxation or a
  similar office corresponding to the highest tax administration authority of the said federative entities; and

         II - the representation of the Municipalities and of the Federal District shall be exercised by a member who does not maintain, during the representation, a hierarchical
  subordination relationship with a federative sphere different from the one that appointed him and who meets at least one of the following requirements:

        a) holding the office of Secretary of Finance, Treasury, Taxation or a similar office corresponding to the highest tax administration authority of the
  Municipality or of the Federal District;

        b) having at least 10 (ten) years of experience in the tax administration of the Municipality or of the Federal District;

       c) having at least 4 (four) years of experience holding senior management, leadership or advisory positions in the tax administration
  of the Municipality or of the Federal District.


        § 1 The members referred to in the caput of this article must, cumulatively:

        I - hold higher education qualifications compatible with the office for which they were appointed;

        II - not fall within the cases of ineligibility provided for in items "a" to "q" of item I of the caput of art. 1 of Complementary Law No. 64, of May 18,
  1990.

        § 2 The members of the CGIBS Superior Council shall be appointed and inducted to hold office for the period referred to in the caput of art. 480 and
  may be replaced or removed:

        I - in relation to the representation of the States and of the Federal District, by the Head of the Executive Branch;    (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       II - in relation to the representation of the Municipalities and of the Federal District, in the manner provided for in § 7 of art. 481 of this Complementary Law; and       (Repealed by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - due to resignation, a final and unappealable court conviction or a dismissal penalty resulting from a disciplinary administrative proceeding.

        § 3 The alternate shall replace the sitting member in his absences and impediments, in the manner set forth in the internal rules.

        § 4 In the event of a vacancy, the office shall be held by the respective alternate for the remaining period, except in cases of replacement.

        § 5 The member of the CGIBS Superior Council inducted into office based on item "a" of item II of the caput of this article who ceases to hold
  the office of Secretary of Finance, Treasury, Taxation or similar must be replaced or removed within 10 (ten) days, counted from the date of dismissal,
  if he does not meet another requirement to be a member of the CGIBS Superior Council. (Repealed by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        Art. 482-A. The provisions of arts. 480 to 482 apply only to the provisional CGIBS provided for in the caput of art. 480.        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

       § 1 The terms of office of the representatives appointed under §§ 2, 5 and 5-A of art. 481 shall extend until March 31, 2027.                  (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 2 In the event the electoral regulation has not been approved and published by joint act of the CNM and of the FNP by January 31, 2027, it shall fall to the
  CGIBS to regulate and conduct the first election. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                   Section III

                                                                    On the Installation of the Superior Council

         Art. 483. The CGIBS Superior Council shall be installed within 120 (one hundred and twenty) days counted from the date of publication of this Complementary Law.        Taking
  effect

        § 1 For purposes of the provision in the caput of this article:

       I - the sitting and alternate members of the CGIBS Superior Council must be appointed within 90 (ninety) days counted from the date of publication of this
  Complementary Law, through publication in the Federal Official Gazette:

        a) by the Heads of the respective Executive Branches, in the case of the States and of the Federal District; or

        b) under the terms of the electoral process provided for in this Complementary Law, in the case of the Municipalities and of the Federal District;

       b) under the terms provided for in §§ 2, 4 and 5 of art. 481 of this Complementary Law, in the case of the Municipalities and of the Federal District;           (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - for the first term of the CGIBS Superior Council, the sitting and alternate members appointed shall be considered inducted:

        a) on the first business day of the second week following publication in the Federal Official Gazette of the appointment of all members; or

        b) on the date referred to in the caput of this article, if the appointment of all members has not been published;

        III - the sitting members of the CGIBS Superior Council shall elect among themselves the President and the 2 (two) Vice-Presidents of the CGIBS; and

        IV - the President of the CGIBS shall notify the Minister of State for Finance of the installation of the CGIBS Superior Council, indicating the bank account intended
  to receive the initial contribution from the Union through the credit operation referred to in art. 484 of this Complementary Law.

       § 2 Until the contribution from the Union referred to in art. 484 of this Complementary Law is made, the expenses necessary for the operation of the Superior Council of the
  CGIBS shall be borne by the entities of origin of the respective members.

        § 2 Until the contribution from the Union referred to in art. 484 of this Complementary Law is made, the expenses necessary for the operation of the Superior Council of the
  CGIBS shall be borne by the entities of origin of the respective members, and shall be reimbursed by the CGIBS, starting in fiscal year 2026, increased by
  remuneration based on the Selic rate from the dates the expenses were paid until their respective reimbursement to the federative entities.         (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 3 After receiving the contribution from the Union referred to in art. 484 of this Complementary Law, the CGIBS Superior Council shall adopt the measures necessary
  for the installation and operation of the CGIBS.

        § 4 The internal rules of the CGIBS shall establish the means to carry out its financial and accounting management while its own budget execution system
  is not made available.

         § 5 For purposes of enabling budgetary, financial, accounting, operational and asset management, while its own Unified and
  Integrated Budget Execution, Financial Administration and Control System (Siafic) is not structured, the CGIBS may enter into a technical cooperation agreement with 1 (one) or more
  federative entities, aimed at making available, developing, customizing, maintaining and hosting the Siafic, as well as other
  structuring systems necessary for the performance of its functions, and the costs arising from said technical cooperation agreements shall be reimbursed by the CGIBS, increased by
  remuneration based on the Selic rate from the dates the expenses were paid until their respective reimbursement to the federative entities.
  (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         Art. 484. The Union shall fund, through a credit operation in 2025, the amount of R$ 600,000,000.00 (six hundred million reais), reduced by 1/12 (one-twelfth)
  per month elapsed up to, and including, the month in which the notification referred to in item IV of § 1 of art. 483 of this Complementary Law is given. Taking
  effect

        Art. 484. The Union shall fund, through a credit operation, the expenses necessary for the installation of the CGIBS, in the period from 2025 to 2028, in the amount of
  up to R$ 3,800,000,000.00 (three billion eight hundred million reais), distributed as follows: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       I - in 2025, in the amount of R$ 600,000,000.00 (six hundred million reais), reduced by 1/12 (one-twelfth) per month elapsed up to, and including, the
  month in which the notification referred to in item IV of § 1 of art. 483 of this Complementary Law is given; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)


        II - in 2026, in the amount of R$ 800,000,000.00 (eight hundred million reais);     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        III - in 2027, in the amount of R$ 1,200,000,000.00 (one billion two hundred million reais); and     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        IV - in 2028, in the amount of R$ 1,200,000,000.00 (one billion two hundred million reais).       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       § 1 The amounts to be financed by the Union shall be distributed in equal and successive monthly installments, from January 2025 or the month following the
  notification referred to in item IV of § 1 of art. 483 of this Complementary Law until the last month of the year.

        § 1 The amounts to be financed by the Union shall be distributed in equal and successive monthly installments:         (Wording given by Complementary Law No.
  227 of 2026)

       I - in 2025, from January 2025 or the month following the notification referred to in item IV of § 1 of art. 483 of this Complementary Law until the last
  month of the year; and (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - from 2026 to 2028, in 12 (twelve) installments.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

          § 2 The monthly installments referred to in this article shall be credited by the tenth day of each month, observing, in the case of the first installment, the minimum period of
  30 (thirty) days between the notification made under item IV of § 1 of art. 483 of this Complementary Law and the date of the credit.

        § 3 The Union's financing to the CGIBS carried out under this article shall be remunerated based on the Selic rate from the date of disbursement until its
  reimbursement to the Union.

        § 4 The CGIBS shall reimburse the Union for the amounts financed under this article in 20 (twenty) successive semiannual installments, starting in June
  2029.

        § 5 The CGIBS shall provide a guarantee in favor of the Union in an amount equal to or greater than the amount owed as a result of the credit operation referred to in this article, which
  may consist of the proceeds of IBS collection earmarked for its financing.

        § 5 The CGIBS shall provide a guarantee in favor of the Union in an amount equal to or greater than the amount owed as a result of the credit operation referred to in this article,
  which may consist of: (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         I - the proceeds of IBS collection earmarked for the financing of the CGIBS, allowing, for fiscal years 2029 to 2038, the additional earmarking of the
  proceeds of IBS collection of each federative entity, exclusively for the payment of the reimbursement referred to in § 4 of this article, at percentages of
  up to:(Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        a) 1% (one percent) in fiscal year 2029;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        b) 0.5% (five tenths of a percent) in fiscal year 2030;      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        c) 0.33% (thirty-three hundredths of a percent) in fiscal year 2031;    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        d) 0.25% (twenty-five hundredths of a percent) in fiscal year 2032; and     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        e) 0.1% (one tenth of a percent) in the period from 2033 to 2038; and       (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the yields from financial investments of the CGIBS's own revenues.     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 6 The CGIBS shall be subject to oversight by the Federal Audit Court exclusively in relation to the funds referred to in this article, until its
  full reimbursement.

                                                                                CHAPTER IV

                                                  ON THE TRANSITION PERIOD FOR TRANSACTIONS INVOLVING REAL ESTATE

                                                                                   Section I

                                                          On Transactions Initiated before January 1, 2029

                                                                                 Subsection I

                                                                              On Development (Incorporação)

        Art. 485. The taxpayer who carries out a real estate development (incorporação imobiliária) subject to the segregated estate (patrimônio de afetação), under the terms of articles 31-A to 31-E of Law No. 4,591, of December 16,
  1964, who has requested the option for the specific regime established by art. 1 and has had the request made effective under the terms of art. 2, both
  of Federal Law No. 10,931 of 2004, before January 1, 2029, may opt for the payment of CBS, as follows:

        Art. 485. The taxpayer who carries out a real estate development subject to the segregated estate, under the terms of arts. 31-A to 31-E of Law No. 4,591, of December 16,
  1964, who has requested the option for the specific regime established by art. 1 and has had the request made effective under the terms of art. 2,
  both of Law No. 10,931 of August 2, 2004, before January 1, 2029, may opt for the payment of IBS and of CBS, as follows:         (Wording
  given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

       I - the real estate development subject to the special taxation regime provided for in arts. 4 and 8 of Federal Law No. 10,931/2004 shall be subject to the payment
  of CBS in an amount equivalent to 2.08% of the monthly revenue received;

       I - the real estate development subject to the special taxation regime provided for in arts. 4 and 8 of Law No. 10,931, of August 2, 2004, shall be subject to the
  payment of IBS and of CBS in an amount equivalent to 2.08% (two point zero eight percent) of the monthly revenue received; (Wording given by Complementary
  Law No. 227 of 2026)

        II - the real estate development subject to the special taxation regime provided for in § 6 and § 8 of art. 4 and the sole paragraph of art. 8 of Federal Law No.
  10,931/2004 shall be subject to the payment of CBS in an amount equivalent to 0.53% of the monthly revenue received.

        II - the real estate development subject to the special taxation regime provided for in §§ 6 and 8 of art. 4 and in the sole paragraph of art. 8 of Law No. 10,931,
  of August 2, 2004, shall be subject to the payment of IBS and of CBS in an amount equivalent to 0.53% (fifty-three hundredths of a percent) of the monthly revenue
  received. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 1 The option for the special regime set forth in the caput excludes any other form of levy of IBS and CBS on the respective development, being subject to
  the levy of these taxes exclusively in the manner set forth in this article.

        § 2 The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the taxpayer subject to the special regime referred to in the caput is prohibited in relation to the acquisitions
  intended for the real estate development subject to the segregated estate.

         § 3 The option for the special regime set forth in the caput prevents the deduction of the adjustment reducers provided for in art. 257 and of the social reducer provided for in art. 259 in the
  disposal of real estate arising from the real estate development.


         § 4 The taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime who acquires real estate arising from a real estate development subject to the specific regime referred to
  in the caput may not appropriate IBS and CBS credits relating to the acquisition of the real property.

         § 5 In the case of acquisition by a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime, transactions taxed under the optional regime referred to in the caput
  shall constitute an adjustment reducer equivalent to what would be constituted had the real property been acquired from a non-taxpayer of the regular IBS and CBS regime, under the terms
  of item III of the caput of art. 258.

         § 6 The IBS and CBS credits arising from the indirect costs and expenses paid by the developer and appropriated to each development in the manner provided in
  § 4 of art. 4 of Federal Law No. 10,931 of 2004 must be reversed by the developer.

            § 7 In the case of the option referred to in this article, Federal Law No. 10,931 of 2004 applies insofar as it does not contradict the provisions of this article.

        § 8 The amount paid under items I and II of the caput of this article shall be distributed among the state, district and municipal shares of the IBS and the CBS in
  proportion to their respective reference rates. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                       Subsection II

                                                                                On Land Subdivision (Parcelamento do Solo)

        Art. 486. The taxpayer who disposes of real estate arising from a land subdivision, whose subdivision registration request, under the terms of
  Federal Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979, was made effective before January 1, 2029, may opt for the payment of CBS based on the gross
  revenue received.

        Art. 486. The taxpayer who disposes of real estate arising from a land subdivision, whose subdivision registration request, under the terms
  of Law No. 6,766, of December 19, 1979, was made effective before January 1, 2029, may opt for the payment of IBS and of CBS based on the gross
  revenue received. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 1 Transactions subject to the regime referred to in this article shall be subject to the payment of CBS in an amount equivalent to 3.65% of the gross revenue
  received.

         § 1 Transactions subject to the regime referred to in this article shall be subject to the payment of IBS and of CBS in an amount equivalent to 3.65% (three
  point sixty-five percent) of the gross revenue received. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 2 The option for the payment set forth in the caput excludes any other form of levy of IBS and CBS on the respective land subdivision, being
  subject to the tax levy of these taxes exclusively in the manner set forth in the caput.

            § 3 The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the taxpayer who exercises the option referred to in the caput is prohibited.

         § 4 The option for the payment set forth in the caput prevents the deduction of the adjustment reducers provided for in art. 257 and of the social reducer provided for in art. 259 in the
  disposal arising from the land subdivision.

         § 5 The taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime who acquires real estate arising from a land subdivision subject to the taxation regime referred to
  in the caput may not appropriate IBS and CBS credit relating to the acquisition of the real property.

         § 6 In the case of acquisition by a taxpayer subject to the regular IBS and CBS regime, transactions taxed under the optional regime referred to in the caput
  shall constitute an adjustment reducer equivalent to what would be constituted had the real property been acquired from a non-taxpayer of the regular IBS and CBS regime, under the terms
  of item III of the caput of art. 258.

         § 7 Gross revenue is considered to be the total revenues earned from the sale of the real estate units that make up the land subdivision, as well as the
  financial revenues and monetary variations arising from this transaction.

       § 8 The payment of CBS in the manner set forth in the caput of this article shall be considered final, giving rise, under no circumstances, to any right to restitution or to
  offset, except in the case of rescission of the transaction.

          § 8 The payment of IBS and of CBS in the manner set forth in the caput of this article shall be considered final, giving rise, under no circumstances, to any right to
  restitution or offset, except in the case of rescission of the transaction. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 9 The revenues, costs and expenses of the land subdivision subject to taxation under this article shall not be included in the calculation of the
  tax base of the CBS owed by the taxpayer as a result of its other business activities.

        § 9 The revenues, costs and expenses of the land subdivision subject to taxation under this article shall not be included in the
  calculation of the tax base of the IBS and of the CBS owed by the taxpayer as a result of its other business activities.           (Wording given by
  Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

        § 10. For purposes of the provision in § 7 of this article, the indirect costs and expenses paid by the taxpayer in the month shall be appropriated to each land subdivision,
  in the same proportion represented by the direct costs of the operations arising from the land subdivision, in relation to the taxpayer's total direct cost,
  understood as the sum of all direct costs of all activities carried out by the taxpayer.

         § 11. The IBS and CBS credits arising from the indirect costs and expenses paid by the taxpayer and appropriated to each land subdivision in the manner
  provided for in § 10 must be reversed by the taxpayer.

            § 12. The taxpayer is required to maintain segregated accounting records for each land subdivision subject to the taxation regime provided for in this
  article.

        § 13. The amount paid under § 1 of this article shall be distributed among the state, district and municipal shares of the IBS and the CBS in proportion to the
  respective reference rates. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                       Subsection III

                                                        On the Leasing, Onerous Assignment and Renting of Real Property

         Art. 487. The taxpayer who carries out the leasing, onerous assignment or renting of real property arising from contracts entered into for a fixed term may
  opt for the payment of IBS and CBS based on the gross revenue received.

            § 1 The option provided for in the caput shall apply exclusively:

            I - to contracts for non-residential purposes, for the original term of the contract, provided that it:

            a) is entered into by the date of publication of this Complementary Law, with the date evidenced by a notarized signature or by electronic signature; and

        b) is registered with the Real Estate Registry Office or with the Registry of Titles and Documents by December 31, 2025, or is made available to the RFB
  and to the IBS Management Committee, under the terms of the regulation;

        II - to contracts for residential purposes, for the original term of the contract or until December 31, 2028, whichever occurs first, provided that it was entered into by the
  date of publication of this Complementary Law, with the date evidenced by a notarized signature, by electronic signature, or by proof of payment
  of the rent by the last day of the month following the first month of the contract.

        § 2 Transactions subject to the regime referred to in this article shall be subject to the payment of IBS and CBS in an amount equivalent to 3.65% of the gross revenue
  received.

         § 2 Transactions subject to the regime referred to in this article shall be subject to the payment of IBS and of CBS in an amount equivalent to 3.65% (three
  point sixty-five percent) of the gross revenue received. (Wording given by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

         § 3 The option for the payment set forth in the caput excludes any other form of levy of IBS and CBS on the respective transaction, being subject to the
  levy of these taxes exclusively in the manner set forth in the caput.

        § 4 The appropriation of IBS and CBS credits by the taxpayer who exercises the option referred to in the caput is prohibited, in relation to the transactions related
  to the real property subject to the optional regime referred to in this article.

         § 5 The option for the payment set forth in the caput prevents the use of the social reducer provided for in art. 260.

       § 6 Gross revenue is considered to be the total revenues earned in the transactions referred to in the caput, as well as the financial revenues and monetary
  variations arising from this transaction.

          § 7 The payment of IBS and CBS in the manner set forth in the caput of this article shall be considered final, giving rise, under no circumstances, to any right to
  restitution or offset.

        § 8 The revenues, costs and expenses of the transactions referred to in the caput shall not be included in the calculation of the tax base of the IBS and of the CBS
  owed by the taxpayer as a result of its other business activities.

        § 9 The indirect costs and expenses paid by the taxpayer in the month shall be appropriated to each transaction, in the same proportion represented by the revenues
  of those transactions, in relation to the taxpayer's total revenue.

        § 10. The IBS and CBS credits arising from the indirect costs and expenses appropriated by the taxpayer and allocated to the transactions subject to the optional regime
  referred to in this article under § 9 must be reversed.

        § 11. The taxpayer is required to maintain segregated accounting records identifying the transactions subject to the taxation regime provided for
  in this article.

        § 12. The amount paid under § 2 of this article shall be distributed among the state, district and municipal shares of the IBS and the CBS in proportion to the
  respective reference rates. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227 of 2026)

                                                                                       Section II

                                                            On Transactions Initiated from January 1, 2029

         Art. 488. Starting January 1, 2029, the taxpayer may deduct from the IBS tax base levied on the disposal of real property the amount paid on the
  acquisition of goods and services carried out between January 1, 2027 and December 31, 2032 that are used for the development, land subdivision and
  construction of the property.

         § 1 The deduction referred to in the caput corresponds to the value of the acquisitions of goods and services:

         I - subject to the levy of the tax provided for in art. 155, II, or the tax provided for in art. 156, III, both of the Federal Constitution;

         II - recorded as a direct production cost of the real property; and

         III - whose acquisition was supported by a valid tax document.

         § 2 In the disposal of real property arising from a development or land subdivision, the indirect costs and expenses paid by the taxpayer that are subject to ICMS or ISS may
  be deducted from the IBS tax base, which shall be allocated to the project in the same proportion represented by the direct costs
  of the project in relation to the taxpayer's total direct cost, understood as the sum of the direct costs of all activities carried out by the
  taxpayer.

       § 3 The amounts to be deducted correspond to the IBS and CBS tax base relating to the acquisition of the goods and services, as recorded in the
  tax document, multiplied by:

         I - 1 (one whole), in the case of goods and services acquired between January 1, 2027 and December 31, 2028;

         II - 0.9 (nine tenths), in the case of goods and services acquired in the 2029 calendar year;

         III - 0.8 (eight tenths), in the case of goods and services acquired in the 2030 calendar year;

         IV - 0.7 (seven tenths), in the case of goods and services acquired in the 2031 calendar year; and

         V - 0.6 (six tenths), in the case of goods and services acquired in the 2032 calendar year.

        § 4 The deduction referred to in the caput does not exclude the right to appropriate the IBS and CBS credits paid by the taxpayer, nor the application of the
  adjustment reducers provided for in art. 257 and of the social reducer provided for in art. 259.

         § 5 The provision in this article does not apply if the taxpayer has opted for the special regime referred to in art. 485 or exercised the option referred to in art.
  486.

       § 6 The amounts to be deducted from the tax base may be used to adjust the IBS tax base of prior periods or of
  subsequent periods relating to the same real property or to the same project, when they exceed the value of the IBS tax base of the respective period.

                                                                                       Section III

                                                                                 Final Provisions

        Art. 489. The total revenue of the IBS and of the CBS collected under art. 487 shall be distributed between the CBS and the state and municipal shares of the IBS in proportion
  to their respective reference rates at the time the taxable event occurred.

        Art. 490. The provision in § 2 of art. 6 does not apply to the Rental Housing Fund - FAR (Fundo de Arrendamento Residencial), referred to in Law No. 10,188, of February 12, 2001, which
  may retain the full amount of the IBS and CBS credits relating to the goods or services acquired by the FAR, even in the case of donation.

                                                                                      TITLE IV

                                                                                FINAL PROVISIONS



       Art. 491. In the event of a merger, extinction or incorporation of any of the ministries, secretariats and other public administration bodies referred to in this Complementary
  Law, an act of the Head of the Executive Branch of the Union shall define the body responsible for assuming the respective responsibilities provided for in this Complementary
  Law.     Taking effect

          Art. 492. For purposes of the provisions of this Complementary Law:                                Taking effect

          I - the Mercosur Common Nomenclature/Harmonized System - NCM/SH corresponds to that approved by Gecex Resolution No. 272, of November 19,
  2021;

          II - the Brazilian Nomenclature of Services - NBS corresponds to that approved by Joint Ordinance RFB/SECEX No. 2,000, of December 18, 2018.

          § 1 The codes contained in this Complementary Law are in accordance with the NCM/SH and with the NBS referred to in items I and II of the caput.

        § 2 Any future changes to the NCM/SH and NBS referred to in the caput that result in a change in the tax classification of the products mentioned in this
  Complementary Law shall not affect the provisions applied to them based on the prior classification.

        Art. 493. References made in this Complementary Law to the SELIC rate, to the DI rate, to the IPCA and to other indices or rates apply to the respective indices and
  rates that come to replace them.     Taking effect

        Art. 493-A. A special public association is instituted, composed of the Union - represented by the RFB - and by the CGIBS, headquartered and domiciled in the Federal District, with
  the objective of developing, implementing, managing and operationalizing, in a shared manner, modules, systems and components relating to the administration of the IBS and the
  CBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 1 The association referred to in the caput of this article qualifies as a public entity of a special nature and is subject to the legal regime of public
  law. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 2 The association's activity is characterized by the absence of hierarchical linkage, tutelage or subordination to any public administration
  body. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 3 The association has its own legal personality, distinct from the Union, the CGIBS, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities, and is guaranteed
  administrative, patrimonial, technical and financial autonomy, within the limits established in regulation and in this article. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of
  2026)

        § 4 A joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS shall provide for the association's internal regiment, especially regarding:                                                    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

          I - the delimitation of the objectives, competences and purposes;                                      (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       II - the rules of structure, governance, management and operation, ensuring shared governance on an equal footing among the associates, as
  well as transparency, administrative efficiency and accountability in management; (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          III - the internal control mechanisms and the rules on accountability to the associates; and                                             (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          IV - provisions on assets, revenues and expenses.                               (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)
