        § 5 The association's governance rules, defined in a joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS, shall ensure:                                                        (Included by Complementary Law No. 227,
  of 2026)

          I - the equal participation of the associates in the deliberative bodies;                                     (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          II - the principle of shared governance, with collegiate deliberations; and                                              (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       III - observance of the principles of legality, impersonality, morality, publicity, efficiency, cost-effectiveness and transparency.                                               (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 6 Biddings and contracting carried out by the association shall be governed by the general bidding and contracting rules applicable to the direct, autarchic
  and foundational public administrations of the Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 7 The association may be contracted by the associated parties, with bidding waived.                                             (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

       § 8 The association may enter into agreements, cooperation accords and other arrangements with bodies and entities of the direct and indirect Public Administration,
  as well as with international organizations, subject to legal and regulatory limits. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 9 The appropriations necessary to cover the association's expenses shall be included in the budget proposal of the Union and of the CGIBS, in the form
  established in a specific joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 10. The Union and the CGIBS are subsidiarily liable for the association's obligations.                                                 (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 11. The association is subject to accounting, operational and patrimonial oversight by the Court of Accounts competent to review the accounts of its
  legal representative. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 12. It is incumbent upon the Federal Court of Accounts (Tribunal de Contas da União) to oversee the application of resources transferred by the Union to the association.                                                 (Included by Complementary
  Law No. 227, of 2026)

          § 13. The Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities may second civil servants to the association, in the form and under the conditions of each
  entity's legislation.    (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

        § 14. The association shall be governed by this article, by the complementary rules approved in a joint act of the RFB and the CGIBS and, subsidiarily,
  insofar as not incompatible with its special nature, by Law No. 11,107, of April 6, 2005, and its regulation. (Included by Complementary Law No.
  227, of 2026)

       § 15. The provisions of this article do not preclude the execution of technical cooperation agreements between the RFB and the CGIBS for the non-onerous transfer of
  modules, systems and technological solutions developed by either party. (Included by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

                     § 11. The option referred to in § 10 shall be exercised for the semesters beginning in January and July of each year, being irrevocable
               for each of those periods, and must be exercised in the months of September and April immediately preceding each semester." (NR)

               given by Complementary Law No. 227, of 2026)

               centavos) per cubic meter of fuel ethanol.

                     ..........................................................................................................

                     § 4º-C. In the case of sale of gasoline by the distributor, with respect to the percentage of anhydrous alcohol added thereto, the
               rates of the Contribution to PIS/Pasep and Cofins are hereby reduced to zero.

                     ..........................................................................................................

                     § 4º-D. .....................................................................................

                     I - in the case of a cooperative not opting for the special regime referred to in § 4º of this article, the amounts of the Contribution to
               PIS/Pasep and Cofins owed shall be obtained by applying the rate set forth in the caput of art. 5º.

                     ..........................................................................................................

                      § 10. The application of the coefficients referred to in § 8º of this article may not result in rates of the Contribution to
               PIS/Pasep and Cofins higher than, respectively, 1.65% (one and sixty-five hundredths percent) and 7.6% (seven and
               six tenths percent) of the average retail sale price.

                      § 11. The average price referred to in § 10 of this article shall be determined from data collected by suitable institutions, weighted
               based on the volumes of ethanol traded in the States and the Federal District in the 12 (twelve) months preceding
               the setting of the coefficients referred to in § 8º of this article.

                     § 12. In the calendar year in which the legal entity begins alcohol production or import activities, the option for the special
               regime may be exercised on any date, taking effect from the first day of the month in which it is exercised.

                     ................................................................................................. " (NR)
